◆ appendTemplateArgumentsToName()

SgName SageBuilder::appendTemplateArgumentsToName ( const SgName & name,
const SgTemplateArgumentPtrList & templateArgumentsList )

Constructs a fully qualified template name string by appending a formatted list of template arguments to a base name.

This function takes a base identifier name and a list of template arguments and produces a combined name of the form "name < arg1 , arg2 , ... > " that can be used as a key in symbol tables for template instantiations. The function is critical for ensuring consistent name generation across multiple locations in the ROSE infrastructure, including the unparsing phase and declaration statement name reset support.

The function iterates over each element in the provided template argument list and handles the following argument types defined by SgTemplateArgument:

  • type_argument: Strips modifier, reference, rvalue reference, pointer, array, and pointer-to-member type layers from the argument type, then resolves the underlying named type to its fully qualified name. Supported underlying declaration kinds include SgClassDeclaration, SgTemplateInstantiationDecl, SgTemplateClassDeclaration, SgTypedefDeclaration and its template variants, SgEnumDeclaration, and SgNonrealDecl.
  • nontype_argument: Handles expression-based template arguments, specifically SgVarRefExp nodes, by resolving the referenced variable to its fully qualified name. Template arguments backed by SgInitializedName are not yet supported and will trigger an assertion failure.
  • template_template_argument: Partially handled; sets an internal flag but does not append a name component. The associated SgTemplateDeclaration is expected to be null in this path.
  • start_of_pack_expansion_argument: Silently skipped.
  • argument_undefined and any unrecognized type: Trigger an immediate abort.

When a fully qualified name cannot be determined through the above logic, the function falls back to calling the argument's unparseToString() method with an SgUnparse_Info object configured for C++ language output with global name qualification enabled, class and enum definition output suppressed, and generated names used for template arguments.

Template arguments of kind start_of_pack_expansion_argument are skipped before any separator or name logic is applied. Arguments are separated by " , " (with surrounding spaces) to match the formatting required by other name-generation sites in the ROSE framework. If the argument list is empty, no angle brackets are appended and the base name is returned unchanged.

This function is one of three locations in the ROSE infrastructure where template argument names must be assembled identically. The other two are Unparse_ExprStmt::unparseTemplateArgumentList() and SgDeclarationStatement::resetTemplateNameSupport(). Divergence between these sites can cause symbol table collisions.

An SgUnparse_Info object is allocated on the heap during execution and is deleted before the function returns.

Parameters
nameThe base name to which the formatted template argument list will be appended.
templateArgumentsListThe list of template argument pointers to be formatted and appended to the base name. Each element must be a valid, non-null SgTemplateArgument pointer. Pack expansion sentinel entries (start_of_pack_expansion_argument) are silently skipped.
Returns
An SgName representing the base name with the formatted template argument list appended, for example "MyClass < ::ns::TypeA , ::ns::TypeB > ". If the argument list is empty, the original name is returned without modification.
Warning
This function calls ROSE_ABORT() if an argument of type argument_undefined or any unrecognized SgTemplateArgument type is encountered.
Nontype template arguments backed by SgInitializedName (rather than SgExpression) are not yet supported. Encountering such an argument will trigger an assertion failure.
The name formatting, including the use of " , " and " < " / " > " with surrounding spaces, must remain consistent with the other two name-generation sites in the ROSE framework. Any change here must be mirrored in those locations to avoid symbol table collisions.
The function asserts that each SgTemplateArgument pointer in the list is non-null. Passing a list containing null pointers results in undefined behavior or an assertion failure.
Precondition
The parameter name may be empty or non-empty; both cases are handled correctly.
Each pointer in templateArgumentsList must be non-null and must point to a valid SgTemplateArgument node in the AST.
For type_argument entries whose stripped type is an SgNamedType, the associated declaration must be non-null and must be one of the supported declaration kinds (SgClassDeclaration, SgTemplateInstantiationDecl, SgTemplateClassDeclaration, SgTypedefDeclaration, SgTemplateTypedefDeclaration, SgTemplateInstantiationTypedefDeclaration, SgEnumDeclaration, or SgNonrealDecl).
For nontype_argument entries backed by an SgExpression, the expression must be non-null. If the expression is an SgVarRefExp, its associated symbol and initialized name must be non-null.
Postcondition
The returned SgName is of the form "name < arg1 , arg2 , ... > " when the argument list is non-empty, or equal to name when the argument list is empty.
The internal SgUnparse_Info object allocated during execution is deleted before the function returns; no memory is leaked by this allocation.
Note
The conditional debug output controlled by the preprocessor macros DEBUG_APPEND_TEMPLATE_ARGUMENT_LIST and DEBUG_TEMPLATE_ARGUMENT_NAMES is compiled out by default (both macros are define'd to 0). Enable them at compile time for diagnostic tracing of name construction.
This function is partially redundant with SgTemplateArgumentList::unparseToStringSupport() introduced as of March 2018.
The SgUnparse_Info object is configured with set_SkipClassDefinition() and set_SkipEnumDefinition() to prevent inline expansion of class and enum bodies within template argument strings.

◆ buildAbstractHandle()

AbstractHandle::abstract_handle * SageBuilder::buildAbstractHandle ( SgNode * n)

Builds an AbstractHandle from a given SgNode, avoiding duplicate creation.

This function constructs an AbstractHandle::abstract_handle object corresponding to the provided SgNode. To prevent redundant allocations, it maintains a static internal map (keyed by SgNode pointer) that caches previously created handles. If a handle for the given node already exists in the cache, the cached handle is returned directly. Otherwise, a new AbstractHandle::abstract_node is built from the SgNode using AbstractHandle::buildroseNode(), and a new abstract_handle is constructed wrapping that node. The newly created handle is then stored in the cache for future lookups.

The static map persists across calls to this function for the lifetime of the program, ensuring that each SgNode is associated with at most one abstract handle instance.

Parameters
nA pointer to the SgNode for which an abstract handle is to be built. Must not be NULL.
Returns
A pointer to the AbstractHandle::abstract_handle corresponding to the given SgNode. The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-NULL.
Warning
The returned handle pointer is owned by the internal static cache and should not be deleted by the caller, as doing so would corrupt the cache and cause undefined behavior on subsequent calls with the same node.
This function uses a static local map, which is not thread-safe. Concurrent calls from multiple threads without external synchronization may lead to data races.
Precondition
n must not be NULL. An assertion failure will occur if a NULL pointer is passed.
Postcondition
The returned abstract_handle pointer is non-NULL and is associated with the provided SgNode in the internal cache.
Note
The static map caches handles for the entire program lifetime. In long-running or memory-sensitive applications, this may contribute to persistent memory usage proportional to the number of unique SgNode pointers processed.
The function currently contains a TODO comment questioning whether a NULL handle should ever be returned. At present, a NULL handle triggers an assertion failure, so callers can rely on a valid non-NULL return value under normal conditions.

◆ buildActualArgumentExpression()

SgActualArgumentExpression * SageBuilder::buildActualArgumentExpression ( SgName arg_name,
SgExpression * arg )

Builds an SgActualArgumentExpression node representing a named actual argument in a function call.

This function constructs a new SgActualArgumentExpression AST node that associates a named argument label with an expression used as an actual argument in a function or subroutine call. This is particularly relevant for languages such as Fortran, which support keyword (named) arguments in procedure calls.

The function allocates a new SgActualArgumentExpression object using the provided argument name and expression, sets the parent pointer of the argument expression to the newly created node to maintain proper AST parent-child relationships, and assigns a default source position indicating that the node was introduced by a transformation rather than originating from user source code.

The source position is set via setOneSourcePositionForTransformation, which marks the node as compiler-generated or transformation-introduced, ensuring that downstream processing and unparsing handle the node appropriately.

Parameters
arg_nameThe name (label) of the actual argument, used in keyword argument passing conventions. This corresponds to the formal parameter name in the callee's definition.
argA pointer to the SgExpression node representing the value or variable being passed as the actual argument. Must not be NULL.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgActualArgumentExpression node with its argument name and expression properly initialized and its source position set for transformation.
Warning
The caller is responsible for managing the lifetime of the returned node within the AST. Improper deletion or reuse of the arg expression pointer after this call may lead to dangling pointer issues, since the parent of arg is updated to point to the new node.
Precondition
arg must not be NULL. An assertion failure will occur at runtime if arg is NULL.
arg_name should be a valid SgName instance representing the intended argument label.
Postcondition
The returned SgActualArgumentExpression node is fully initialized with the given argument name and expression.
The parent pointer of arg is set to the returned SgActualArgumentExpression node.
The source position of the returned node is set to indicate a compiler transformation.
Note
This builder function follows the standard SageBuilder convention of marking newly created nodes with a transformation source position, distinguishing them from nodes parsed directly from source code.
In languages that do not support named actual arguments, the arg_name may be left as an empty SgName, though usage conventions may vary depending on the target language and frontend.

◆ buildActualArgumentExpression_nfi()

SgActualArgumentExpression * SageBuilder::buildActualArgumentExpression_nfi ( SgName arg_name,
SgExpression * arg )

Builds an SgActualArgumentExpression node representing a named actual argument in a function call.

This function constructs a new SgActualArgumentExpression AST node using the provided argument name and expression. It is the "no file info" (nfi) variant, meaning source position information is explicitly set to null rather than being derived from an existing source location. After allocating the node, the function sets the parent pointer of the argument expression to the newly created node, ensuring proper parent-child linkage within the AST. Source position is then initialized to null via setOneSourcePositionNull.

This function is typically used when constructing AST nodes programmatically where no corresponding source file location is available or applicable, such as during code generation or transformation passes.

Parameters
arg_nameThe name of the actual argument, used in named argument passing conventions (e.g., Fortran keyword arguments). May be an empty SgName if no explicit argument name is required.
argA pointer to the SgExpression node representing the value of the actual argument. Must not be NULL.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgActualArgumentExpression node with its argument name and expression set, its parent link established, and source position information set to null.
Warning
The caller is responsible for managing the lifetime of the returned SgActualArgumentExpression node. Passing a NULL pointer for arg will trigger an assertion failure and abort execution.
Precondition
arg must not be NULL; this is enforced by an internal ROSE_ASSERT.
arg must be a valid, fully constructed SgExpression node prior to being passed to this function.
Postcondition
The returned SgActualArgumentExpression node has its argument name set to arg_name.
The parent pointer of arg is set to the returned SgActualArgumentExpression node.
The source position of the returned node is set to null.
Note
The "nfi" suffix in the function name stands for "no file info", indicating that this builder does not attach source file location data to the created node.
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface for programmatic AST construction.

◆ buildAggregateInitializer()

SgAggregateInitializer * SageBuilder::buildAggregateInitializer ( SgExprListExp * initializers,
SgType * type )

Builds an aggregate initializer node for use in the ROSE AST.

This function constructs a new SgAggregateInitializer node, which represents an aggregate initializer expression (e.g., a brace-enclosed list used to initialize arrays, structs, or unions in C and C++). The function accepts an optional expression list containing the initializer values and an optional type for the aggregate being initialized.

Internally, the function allocates a new SgAggregateInitializer object, sets the parent pointer of the provided initializer list to the newly created node (if the list is non-NULL), marks the node as requiring explicit braces in the output, and assigns a default source position suitable for compiler-generated (transformation) nodes via setOneSourcePositionForTransformation.

This builder is typically used during AST construction or transformation passes where aggregate initialization syntax must be synthesized programmatically.

Parameters
initializersA pointer to an SgExprListExp node representing the list of initializer expressions enclosed in braces. May be NULL if no initializer expressions are provided at construction time.
typeA pointer to an SgType node representing the type of the aggregate being initialized. May be NULL if the type is not known or not required at construction time.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgAggregateInitializer node. The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-NULL; an assertion failure will occur if allocation fails.
Warning
The caller is responsible for managing the lifetime of the returned SgAggregateInitializer node. Improper deletion or double-freeing of AST nodes can lead to undefined behavior within the ROSE framework.
If a non-NULL initializers list is passed, its parent pointer will be set to the newly created aggregate initializer. Passing an SgExprListExp that already has a parent set elsewhere may corrupt the AST structure.
Precondition
If initializers is non-NULL, it must point to a valid, well-formed SgExprListExp node that is not already owned by another AST node.
If type is non-NULL, it must point to a valid SgType node within the current ROSE IR context.
Postcondition
The returned SgAggregateInitializer node has its need_explicit_braces flag set to true.
If initializers is non-NULL, its parent is set to the returned SgAggregateInitializer node.
The returned node has a source position assigned appropriate for transformation-generated nodes.
Note
The default values for both parameters are NULL, making both arguments optional at the call site.
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface, which provides factory functions for constructing ROSE AST nodes during program analysis and transformation.

SgAggregateInitializer * SageBuilder::buildAggregateInitializer_nfi ( SgExprListExp * initializers,

Builds an aggregate initializer node without file information.

This function constructs a new SgAggregateInitializer AST node using the provided expression list and type. After allocation, the function sets the parent pointer of the initializer list to the newly created node (if the list is non-null) and enables explicit braces on the aggregate initializer by calling set_need_explicit_braces(true). This function is part of the SageBuilder interface for programmatically constructing ROSE IR nodes.

typeA pointer to an SgType node representing the type of the aggregate being initialized. May be NULL if the type is not yet known or not applicable.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgAggregateInitializer node. The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-null, as the function asserts successful allocation.
Warning
The caller is responsible for managing the lifetime of the returned SgAggregateInitializer node. Passing ownership to an appropriate parent node in the AST is expected to avoid memory leaks.
Precondition
If initializers is non-null, it must be a valid, fully constructed SgExprListExp node before being passed to this function.

The "nfi" suffix in the function name stands for "no file info", distinguishing this builder from variants that attach source location information to the created node.

◆ buildAliasedType()

SgModifierType * SageBuilder::buildAliasedType ( SgType * base_type)

Builds an aliased modifier type wrapping a given base type.

This function constructs an SgModifierType node that applies the "aliased" type modifier to the provided base type. Aliased types are used in the ROSE abstract syntax tree (AST) to represent types that may be accessed through multiple pointers or references, indicating that the compiler should not assume strict aliasing rules for the underlying type.

Internally, the function defines a lambda operation that calls setAliased() on the type modifier of the newly created SgModifierType node, and then delegates construction to the internal helper _buildModifierType, which handles the allocation and initialization of the SgModifierType node before applying the provided modifier operation.

Parameters
base_typeA pointer to the SgType node that will serve as the underlying base type for the aliased modifier type. This pointer must not be null and should point to a valid, fully initialized type node within the AST.
Returns
A pointer to a newly constructed SgModifierType node with the aliased modifier set, wrapping the given base type.
Warning
Passing a null pointer for base_type results in undefined behavior. The caller is responsible for ensuring that base_type is a valid and properly initialized AST node.
Precondition
base_type must be a non-null pointer to a valid SgType node.
The ROSE AST infrastructure must be properly initialized before calling this function.
Postcondition
The returned SgModifierType node has its aliased modifier set via setAliased() on its type modifier.
The returned node wraps base_type as its underlying base type.
Note
The returned SgModifierType is managed by the ROSE memory pool allocator. Callers should not manually delete the returned pointer.
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface, which provides factory functions for constructing ROSE AST nodes in a consistent and well-formed manner.

◆ buildAlignOfOp() [1/2]

SgAlignOfOp * SageBuilder::buildAlignOfOp ( SgExpression * exp)

Builds an __alignof__() expression node with an expression parameter.

This function constructs a new SgAlignOfOp AST node representing a __alignof__() expression that takes an expression as its operand. The __alignof__ operator is a GCC extension that returns the alignment requirement, in bytes, of a given expression or type.

The function allocates a new SgAlignOfOp node, sets the provided expression as its operand, and establishes the parent-child relationship in the AST by calling set_parent() on the operand. If the expression is non-null, left-hand side value marking is also applied via markLhsValues(). Finally, the source position of the resulting node is set to indicate it was introduced by a transformation, using setOneSourcePositionForTransformation().

Parameters
expA pointer to the SgExpression node to be used as the operand of the __alignof__() expression. May be NULL, in which case the resulting node is created without an operand expression, and no parent or LHS value marking is applied.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgAlignOfOp AST node representing the __alignof__() expression.
Precondition
If exp is non-null, it must be a valid, fully constructed SgExpression node that is not already owned by another part of the AST, or its parent relationship must be safe to reassign.
Postcondition
The returned SgAlignOfOp node is non-null (asserted internally).
If exp is non-null, its parent pointer is set to the returned SgAlignOfOp node.
The source position of the returned node is set to reflect a compiler-generated transformation rather than an original source location.
Warning
Passing a NULL expression results in an SgAlignOfOp node without a valid operand. Ensure that downstream AST processing or code generation can handle this case appropriately.
Note
This function is intended for use with the expression form of __alignof__(). A separate builder function should be used when constructing the type-based form of the __alignof__ operator.
The function uses ROSE_ASSERT to verify that the allocated node is non-null. If memory allocation fails, the assertion will trigger before returning.

If dim_info is NULL, the function delegates to the overloaded version of buildArrayType that accepts a single SgExpression pointer (set to NULL) instead of an SgExprListExp. This handles the degenerate case gracefully without asserting or crashing.

The left-hand side expression is marked as an lvalue, and both operands have their parent pointers set to the newly created assignment operator. rhs must not be NULL.

The SgAssignOp has its parent pointer set to the returned SgExprStatement.

Instead, it calls setOneSourcePositionForTransformation only on the directly created nodes (SgAssignOp and SgExprStatement), preserving any pre-existing source position data on the provided lhs and rhs expressions.

The returned SgExprStatement contains an SgAssignOp as its expression.
The parent pointer of lhs is set to the SgAssignOp.
The parent pointer of rhs is set to the SgAssignOp.
The parent pointer of the SgAssignOp is set to the returned SgExprStatement.

This function constructs a new SgAtStmt abstract syntax tree node, which represents an "at" statement as used in certain parallel or distributed programming language extensions supported by ROSE. The function allocates a new SgAtStmt object using the provided expression and body block, sets the source position information on the newly created node via SageInterface::setSourcePosition, and establishes the correct parent-child relationships by setting the parent of both the expression and the body to the newly created statement node.

This builder function follows the standard ROSE SageBuilder pattern: it creates the AST node, initializes its source position, and wires up parent pointers before returning the completed node.

expressionA pointer to the SgExpression node that specifies the target or location clause of the "at" statement. Must not be null.
bodyA pointer to the SgBasicBlock node representing the body of the "at" statement. Must not be null.

A pointer to the newly constructed SgAtStmt node with source position information set and parent pointers established for both the expression and the body.
Warning
Both the expression and body pointers must be valid, non-null pointers. Passing null for either argument will trigger an assertion failure and abort the program.
Precondition
expression must be a non-null pointer to a valid SgExpression node.
body must be a non-null pointer to a valid SgBasicBlock node.
Postcondition
The returned SgAtStmt node has its source position initialized.
The parent of expression is set to the returned SgAtStmt node.
The parent of body is set to the returned SgAtStmt node.
Note
This function was added to support the "at" statement construct (added on 6/11/2014). It is part of the SageBuilder interface, which provides factory functions for constructing ROSE AST nodes in a consistent manner.
Ownership of the returned SgAtStmt node is transferred to the caller, who is responsible for inserting it into the AST or managing its lifetime.

◆ buildAttributeSpecificationStatement()

SgAttributeSpecificationStatement * SageBuilder::buildAttributeSpecificationStatement ( SgAttributeSpecificationStatement::attribute_spec_enum kind)

Builds and returns a new SgAttributeSpecificationStatement AST node for a given Fortran attribute specification kind.

This builder function constructs a new SgAttributeSpecificationStatement node representing a Fortran attribute specification statement. The function sets both the defining and first non-defining declaration pointers to the newly created node itself, making it a self-referential declaration as is conventional for such nodes in the ROSE AST.

The attribute kind is set on the node, and then a switch statement dispatches on the kind to perform any kind-specific initialization. For the kinds e_parameterStatement, e_externalStatement, e_dimensionStatement, and e_allocatableStatement, a new SgExprListExp parameter list is created using the no-file-info variant of the builder (buildExprListExp_nfi), attached to the statement, and its parent pointer is set accordingly. Source position information is also set for the parameter list via setSourcePositionForTransformation.

For the e_dataStatement kind, no additional initialization is performed. Any unrecognized kind value results in an error message printed to standard error followed by an abort via ROSE_ABORT.

After kind-specific initialization, source position information for transformation is applied to the statement node itself before it is returned.

Parameters
kindThe attribute specification kind, expressed as a value of the enumeration SgAttributeSpecificationStatement::attribute_spec_enum. Supported values include e_parameterStatement, e_externalStatement, e_dimensionStatement, e_allocatableStatement, and e_dataStatement. Any other value will cause an error message and program abort.
Returns
A pointer to the newly allocated and initialized SgAttributeSpecificationStatement node. The caller is responsible for integrating this node into the AST.
Warning
Passing an unsupported or unrecognized attribute_spec_enum value will cause an error message to be written to standard error and the program to abort via ROSE_ABORT. Ensure that only valid, handled enum values are passed to this function.
The returned pointer points to a heap-allocated object. Ownership and lifetime management of this node are governed by the ROSE AST memory management conventions. Do not manually delete the returned pointer unless you are certain it has not been inserted into the AST.
Precondition
kind must be one of the enumeration values explicitly handled by this function: e_parameterStatement, e_externalStatement, e_dimensionStatement, e_allocatableStatement, or e_dataStatement.
Postcondition
The returned SgAttributeSpecificationStatement node has its defining declaration and first non-defining declaration pointers set to itself.
The attribute kind of the returned node is set to the value of kind.
For kinds e_parameterStatement, e_externalStatement, e_dimensionStatement, and e_allocatableStatement, the node has a non-null parameter list (SgExprListExp) with its parent pointer set to the returned statement node.
Source position information for transformation is set on the returned node and, where applicable, on the parameter list.
Note
This function uses ROSE_ASSERT to verify that the newly allocated node is non-null immediately after construction.
The parameter list for applicable kinds is built using buildExprListExp_nfi, which creates the list without file information, suitable for compiler-generated or transformation nodes.
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface, which provides factory functions for constructing ROSE AST nodes programmatically.

◆ buildAutoType()

SgAutoType * SageBuilder::buildAutoType ( )

Builds and returns a new SgAutoType node representing the C++ auto type.

This function constructs a new SgAutoType object on the heap, which represents the C++ auto type keyword used in type deduction contexts. The function allocates the node dynamically using the default constructor of SgAutoType and verifies successful allocation via an assertion before returning the pointer. This is part of the ROSE SageBuilder interface, which provides factory functions for constructing nodes in the ROSE Abstract Syntax Tree (AST).

The auto type is commonly used in C++11 and later standards to allow the compiler to automatically deduce the type of a variable from its initializer. The returned SgAutoType node can be used when constructing variable declarations or other AST constructs that require an auto-deduced type.

Returns
A pointer to the newly allocated SgAutoType node representing the C++ auto type. The caller is responsible for managing the lifetime of this object within the AST.
Precondition
The system must have sufficient heap memory available to allocate a new SgAutoType object.
Postcondition
A valid, non-null SgAutoType pointer is returned. The returned node is freshly allocated and ready to be inserted into a ROSE AST.
Warning
The returned pointer is heap-allocated. Improper management of this pointer outside of the AST infrastructure may lead to memory leaks. It is expected that the returned node will be managed by the ROSE memory pool or AST ownership mechanisms.
Note
This function uses ROSE_ASSERT to verify that the allocation succeeded. If memory allocation fails and the assertion is disabled, behavior is undefined. In debug builds, a failed allocation will trigger an assertion failure.

◆ buildBaseClass()

SgBaseClass * SageBuilder::buildBaseClass ( SgClassDeclaration * classDeclaration,
SgClassDefinition * classDefinition,
bool isVirtual,
bool isDirect )

Constructs and registers an SgBaseClass node representing a base class relationship.

This function creates a new SgBaseClass AST node that encodes the inheritance relationship between a derived class and one of its base classes. It is part of the SageBuilder API, which provides factory functions for constructing ROSE AST nodes in a consistent and well-formed manner.

The function accepts a class declaration and a class definition that together describe the base class being inherited. The declaration provided does not need to be the defining declaration; it is typically the first non-defining declaration, though this is not strictly enforced in all cases. The class definition must have a valid associated declaration.

After allocating the SgBaseClass node, the function optionally marks it as virtual if the isVirtual flag is set. It then sets the parent of the newly created SgBaseClass to the provided class definition and appends the base class entry to the class definition's inheritance list via append_inheritance().

Note that SgBaseClass nodes are not traversed during standard ROSE AST traversals, so their parent pointers must be set explicitly, which this function handles.

Parameters
classDeclarationA pointer to the SgClassDeclaration representing the base class. This should generally be the first non-defining declaration of the base class, though this is not strictly required in all cases. Must not be NULL.
classDefinitionA pointer to the SgClassDefinition of the derived class into which the base class entry will be inserted. Must not be NULL, and its associated declaration must also not be NULL.
isVirtualA boolean flag indicating whether the base class is inherited virtually. If true, the virtual modifier is set on the base class modifier object of the newly created SgBaseClass node.
isDirectA boolean flag indicating whether the base class is a direct base class of the derived class. This value is passed directly to the SgBaseClass constructor.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed and registered SgBaseClass node. This pointer is guaranteed to be non-NULL upon successful return.
Precondition
classDeclaration must not be NULL.
classDefinition must not be NULL.
classDefinition->get_declaration() must not be NULL.
Postcondition
A new SgBaseClass node has been allocated and initialized.
If isVirtual is true, the virtual modifier has been set on the SgBaseClass node.
The parent of the returned SgBaseClass node is set to classDefinition.
The returned SgBaseClass node has been appended to classDefinition's inheritance list.
Warning
The returned SgBaseClass node is owned by the classDefinition's inheritance list after this call. Callers should not manually delete the returned pointer unless they also remove it from the inheritance list to avoid dangling references.
Note
SgBaseClass nodes are not traversed during standard ROSE AST traversals. As a result, their parent pointers are not set automatically and must be assigned explicitly, which this function does on behalf of the caller.
The access specifier (e.g., public, protected, private) of the base class is not set by this function and must be configured separately if needed, using the base class modifier's access modifier interface.

◆ buildBasicBlock()

SgBasicBlock * SageBuilder::buildBasicBlock ( SgStatement * stmt1,

Builds an SgBasicBlock node containing up to ten optional statements.

This function constructs a new SgBasicBlock AST node and populates it with up to ten optional SgStatement children. Each statement parameter is checked for a non-null value before being appended to the block; null parameters are silently skipped. This allows callers to build a basic block with a variable number of statements without needing separate overloads for each count.

After allocation, the function checks whether the current language uses case-insensitive symbol table semantics (for example, Fortran) via SageInterface::is_language_case_insensitive(), and if so, marks the block as case-insensitive. A single source position is then set on the block to indicate it was introduced by a transformation rather than originating from user source code.

Statements are appended in order from stmt1 to stmt10 using SageInterface::appendStatement, which properly sets parent pointers and updates the block's symbol table as needed.

Parameters
stmt1The first statement to append to the block, or null to skip.
stmt2The second statement to append to the block, or null to skip.
stmt3The third statement to append to the block, or null to skip.
stmt4The fourth statement to append to the block, or null to skip.
stmt5The fifth statement to append to the block, or null to skip.
stmt6The sixth statement to append to the block, or null to skip.
stmt7The seventh statement to append to the block, or null to skip.
stmt8The eighth statement to append to the block, or null to skip.
stmt9The ninth statement to append to the block, or null to skip.
stmt10The tenth statement to append to the block, or null to skip.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgBasicBlock node containing all non-null statements provided as arguments, in order. The returned pointer is never null.
Precondition
Each non-null statement pointer must point to a valid, well-formed SgStatement node that is not already attached to another parent in the AST, unless the caller intends to re-parent it.
Postcondition
The returned SgBasicBlock is a valid AST node with its source position marked as a transformation site.
All non-null statement arguments have been appended to the returned block in parameter order, with their parent pointers updated accordingly.
If the current language uses case-insensitive semantics, the returned block has its case-insensitive flag set to true.
Warning
Passing more than ten statements requires a different approach, such as calling SageInterface::appendStatement directly on the returned block after construction.
Passing a statement that is already owned by another AST node may result in an inconsistent AST with multiple parents referencing the same child node.
Note
All parameters default to null, so the function may be called with fewer than ten arguments when default arguments are supported by the calling context.
The case-insensitivity check replaces an older mechanism that relied on a global flag named symbol_table_case_insensitive_semantics.

T * SageBuilder::buildBinaryExpression ( SgExpression * lhs,

Builds a binary expression node of the specified type from two operand expressions.

This template function constructs a new binary expression AST node of type T, which must be a subclass of SgBinaryOp or a compatible binary expression type in the ROSE compiler framework. The function accepts left-hand side and right-hand side operand expressions, allocates a new node of type T, and wires up the parent pointers so that the resulting subtree is properly linked within the AST.

After construction, if the left-hand side operand is non-null, its parent pointer is set to the newly created node and the lvalue marking pass is applied via markLhsValues() to correctly annotate lvalue semantics. If the right-hand side operand is non-null, its parent pointer is similarly updated. Finally, SageInterface::setOneSourcePositionForTransformation() is called on the result to assign a default source position, indicating that the node was introduced by a transformation rather than parsed from source code.

lhsPointer to the left-hand side operand expression. May be NULL, in which case no parent assignment or lvalue marking is performed for this operand.
rhsPointer to the right-hand side operand expression. May be NULL, in which case no parent assignment is performed for this operand.

Precondition
The template parameter T must be a concrete binary expression type compatible with a two-operand constructor of the form T(SgExpression*, SgExpression*, SgType*).
If lhs or rhs are non-null, they must be valid, fully constructed SgExpression nodes that are not already attached to another parent in a live AST, or the caller must be prepared to update the original parent accordingly.

If rhs is non-null, rhs->get_parent() returns the newly created node.
The returned node has a transformation source position assigned.
Warning
The third argument passed to the T constructor is NULL, meaning no explicit type is provided at construction time. The type of the resulting expression may need to be set separately if the specific binary expression type requires it.
Passing expression nodes that are already children of other AST nodes will silently overwrite their parent pointers, potentially corrupting the original AST structure.
The caller is responsible for managing the lifetime of the returned node and for inserting it into the AST to avoid memory leaks.
Note
This function is a convenience builder intended for use during AST transformations. The source position is set to a transformation marker rather than a real file location, which is the expected behavior for programmatically generated nodes.
The template parameter T is typically one of the SgBinaryOp-derived classes such as SgAddOp, SgSubtractOp, SgMultiplyOp, and similar types defined in the ROSE AST node hierarchy.

This function constructs a new SgBoolValExp node initialized with the given integer value, which is interpreted as a boolean (zero for false, non-zero for true). Unlike its counterpart that attaches source file information, this function uses the "no file info" (nfi) variant, meaning the source position of the resulting node is explicitly set to null via setOneSourcePositionNull. This is typically used when building AST nodes programmatically that do not correspond to any location in the original source file.

After allocation, the function asserts that the node was successfully created before returning it, ensuring that memory allocation did not fail silently.

Parameters
valueAn integer representing the boolean value to store in the node. A value of zero corresponds to false, and any non-zero value corresponds to true.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgBoolValExp node initialized with the specified boolean value and a null source position.
Warning
The caller is responsible for managing the lifetime of the returned node. Improper handling may result in memory leaks if the node is not properly inserted into or managed by the AST.
Precondition
The ROSE infrastructure must be properly initialized before calling this function.
Postcondition
The returned SgBoolValExp node has its source position set to null, indicating it does not correspond to any location in the original source file.
Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface for constructing AST nodes without associated source file information. The "nfi" suffix in the function name stands for "no file info", distinguishing it from builder functions that attach source location metadata to the created node.

◆ buildBracedInitializer()

SgBracedInitializer * SageBuilder::buildBracedInitializer ( SgExprListExp * initializers,
SgType * expression_type )

Constructs and returns a new SgBracedInitializer AST node.

This function creates a braced initializer node (corresponding to C++11 brace-enclosed initializer lists, e.g., {1, 2, 3}) in the ROSE Abstract Syntax Tree (AST). It allocates a new SgBracedInitializer object using the provided expression list and optional type information. If a non-null initializer list is provided, its parent pointer is set to the newly created node to maintain correct parent-child relationships within the AST. The source position of the resulting node is marked as a transformation, indicating that it was programmatically generated rather than parsed from source code.

Parameters
initializersA pointer to an SgExprListExp node representing the list of initializer expressions enclosed in the braces. May be NULL if no initializer expressions are present.
expression_typeA pointer to an SgType node representing the type associated with the braced initializer. May be NULL if the type is not explicitly specified or is to be inferred.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgBracedInitializer node. The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-null.
Precondition
If initializers is non-null, it must be a valid, well-formed SgExprListExp node.
If expression_type is non-null, it must be a valid, well-formed SgType node.
Postcondition
The returned SgBracedInitializer node is fully constructed and has its source position set to reflect a programmatic transformation.
If initializers is non-null, its parent pointer is set to the returned SgBracedInitializer node.
Warning
The caller is responsible for inserting the returned node into the AST at the appropriate location. Failing to do so may result in memory leaks or an inconsistent AST structure.
Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface, which provides utilities for programmatically constructing ROSE AST nodes during source-to-source transformations. The created node corresponds to C++11 braced-init-list syntax.

Builds a braced initializer node without file information (nfi variant).

The "nfi" suffix indicates that no file information is attached to the resulting node; instead, source position data is explicitly set to null via setOneSourcePositionNull().

The function allocates a new SgBracedInitializer on the heap, optionally associates an expression list as its child initializers, and sets the parent pointer of the initializer list to the newly created node if the list is non-null. The resulting node is suitable for insertion into a ROSE AST where source location tracking is not required or not yet available.

Parameters
initializersA pointer to an SgExprListExp node representing the list of initializer expressions enclosed in braces. May be NULL, in which case no parent assignment is performed.
expression_typeA pointer to an SgType representing the type associated with the braced initializer expression. May be NULL if the type is not yet known or not applicable.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgBracedInitializer node. This pointer is guaranteed to be non-null; the function asserts successful allocation.
Warning
The returned node is heap-allocated and must be managed appropriately within the ROSE AST memory model. Failing to attach it to a parent node or to manage its lifetime may result in memory leaks.
Precondition
If initializers is non-null, it must be a valid, fully constructed SgExprListExp node prior to being passed to this function.
expression_type, if non-null, must point to a valid SgType instance.
Postcondition
The returned SgBracedInitializer node has its source position set to null.

Note

It is the low-level "nfi" (no file info) variant, intended for use in contexts where source location information is not available or not meaningful, such as during code generation or transformation passes.

◆ buildBreakStmt()

SgBreakStmt * SageBuilder::buildBreakStmt ( )

Builds and returns a new SgBreakStmt AST node representing a break statement.

This function constructs a new SgBreakStmt node, which corresponds to a C/C++ break statement in the Abstract Syntax Tree (AST). After allocating the node, it sets a single source position marker appropriate for compiler-generated (transformation) code, indicating that this node was not derived from original source text but was introduced programmatically. This is consistent with the ROSE infrastructure convention for builder functions used in AST transformations.

The function uses setOneSourcePositionForTransformation to mark the node as a transformation artifact, which helps downstream tools and analyses distinguish between original and synthesized AST nodes.

Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgBreakStmt node with its source position set for transformation. The caller is responsible for inserting this node into a valid location within the AST.
Warning
The returned pointer must be inserted into the AST in a syntactically valid context (e.g., inside a loop or switch statement body). Inserting a break statement outside of such a context will result in an ill-formed AST that may cause errors during subsequent processing or code generation.
Precondition
The ROSE infrastructure must be properly initialized before calling this function.
Postcondition
A valid SgBreakStmt node is allocated and its source position is set for transformation. The node is not yet attached to any parent in the AST.
Note
This function follows the standard ROSE builder pattern. The returned node should be managed in accordance with ROSE memory management conventions. The internal assertion (ROSE_ASSERT) ensures that memory allocation succeeded; if allocation fails, the program will abort.

The suffix "_nfi" stands for "no file information", meaning that the source position associated with the resulting node is explicitly set to null rather than being populated with real source location data. This is useful when constructing synthetic or compiler-generated break statements that do not correspond to any particular location in a source file.

Internally, the function allocates a new SgBreakStmt object on the heap, asserts that the allocation succeeded, and then calls setOneSourcePositionNull to mark the node as having no associated source position before returning it.

Returns
A pointer to the newly allocated and initialized SgBreakStmt node with a null source position. The caller is responsible for managing the lifetime of the returned object.
Warning
The caller is responsible for inserting the returned node into a valid AST. Failing to do so may result in memory leaks or an inconsistent AST state.
Because source position information is set to null, this node should not be used in contexts where valid source location data is required for correct analysis or code generation.
Precondition
The ROSE infrastructure must be properly initialized before calling this function.
Postcondition
The returned SgBreakStmt pointer is non-null and has its source position set to null via setOneSourcePositionNull.
Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface, which provides factory functions for constructing ROSE AST nodes programmatically. It is intended for use in AST transformations and code generation scenarios where synthetic statements are needed.

◆ buildCaseOptionStmt()

SgCaseOptionStmt * SageBuilder::buildCaseOptionStmt ( SgExpression * key,
SgStatement * body )

Builds and returns a new SgCaseOptionStmt node representing a case option statement.

This function constructs an AST node of type SgCaseOptionStmt, which corresponds to a case label statement in a C or C++ switch construct (e.g., "case <expr>: <statement>"). The function allocates a new SgCaseOptionStmt object using the provided key expression and body statement, then sets a default source position appropriate for compiler-generated (transformation) nodes. If the key expression or body statement are non-null, their parent pointers are updated to reference the newly created case option statement node, ensuring proper parent-child relationships within the AST.

The function uses setOneSourcePositionForTransformation to mark the resulting node as a transformation artifact, which is the standard practice when building AST nodes programmatically rather than parsing them from source code.

Parameters
keyA pointer to the SgExpression representing the case label value (the expression following the "case" keyword). May be null, in which case no parent assignment is performed for the key.
bodyA pointer to the SgStatement representing the body of the case option (the statement or block executed when this case is matched). May be null, in which case no parent assignment is performed for the body.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgCaseOptionStmt node. This pointer is guaranteed to be non-null; an assertion failure will occur if allocation fails.
Warning
The caller is responsible for inserting the returned node into the appropriate location within the AST. Failing to do so may result in memory leaks or an inconsistent AST structure.
If key or body are already attached to another part of the AST, reassigning their parent pointers here may corrupt the existing AST structure. Ensure that these nodes are not already owned by another parent before passing them to this function.
Precondition
key, if non-null, must be a valid, heap-allocated SgExpression node.
body, if non-null, must be a valid, heap-allocated SgStatement node.
Postcondition
The returned SgCaseOptionStmt node has its source position set for transformation.
If key is non-null, key->get_parent() == result.
If body is non-null, body->get_parent() == result.
Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface, which provides factory functions for programmatic construction of ROSE AST nodes during source-to-source transformation.
The resulting node is marked as a transformation node and will not have a valid source file location from the original input source.

Builds a SgCaseOptionStmt AST node without file information (nfi variant).

This function constructs a new SgCaseOptionStmt node representing a case option statement (e.g., a case label within a switch statement) in the ROSE Abstract Syntax Tree (AST). The "nfi" suffix indicates that no file information is attached to the resulting node; source position information is explicitly set to null via setOneSourcePositionNull.

The function allocates a new SgCaseOptionStmt using the provided key expression and body statement. If either the key or the body is non-null, the parent pointer of that child node is updated to point to the newly created SgCaseOptionStmt, ensuring proper parent-child linkage within the AST.

This function is part of the SageBuilder interface, which provides factory functions for constructing ROSE IR (Intermediate Representation) nodes.

Parameters
keyA pointer to the SgExpression representing the case label value (e.g., the constant expression following the case keyword). May be null, in which case no parent assignment is performed for this parameter.
bodyA pointer to the SgStatement representing the body of the case option. May be null, in which case no parent assignment is performed for this parameter.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgCaseOptionStmt node with null source position information and properly set parent pointers for any non-null child nodes.
Warning
The caller is responsible for managing the lifetime of the returned SgCaseOptionStmt node. Improper deletion or reuse of the key or body nodes after passing them to this function may result in dangling pointers or undefined behavior, since their parent pointers will have been modified.
This function asserts (via ROSE_ASSERT) that the newly allocated node is non-null. If memory allocation fails, the assertion will trigger and the program will abort.
Precondition
If key is non-null, it must be a valid, fully constructed SgExpression node.
If body is non-null, it must be a valid, fully constructed SgStatement node.
Postcondition
The returned SgCaseOptionStmt node is non-null.
The source position of the returned node is set to null (no file information).
If key is non-null, key->get_parent() returns the newly created SgCaseOptionStmt.
If body is non-null, body->get_parent() returns the newly created SgCaseOptionStmt.
Note
This is the "no file information" (nfi) variant of the case option statement builder. Use the standard builder variant when source location information is available and should be preserved in the AST node.

Builds a cast expression node in the ROSE Abstract Syntax Tree (AST).

This function constructs a new SgCastExp node representing a type cast operation in the AST. It allocates a new SgCastExp object using the provided operand expression, target type, and cast kind. After construction, it sets the parent pointer of the operand to the newly created cast expression node, marks any left-hand side values within the expression as appropriate, and assigns a default source position suitable for compiler-generated (transformation) nodes.

The function uses setOneSourcePositionForTransformation to mark the resulting node as a transformation artifact, which is the standard practice when building AST nodes programmatically rather than parsing them from source code.

Parameters
operand_iThe expression to be cast. If non-null, its parent pointer will be set to the newly created SgCastExp node, and left-hand side value marking will be applied.
expression_typeThe target type to which the operand is being cast. This type is stored directly in the resulting SgCastExp node.
cast_typeAn enumeration value of type SgCastExp::cast_type_enum that specifies the kind of cast to perform (e.g., C-style cast, static_cast, reinterpret_cast, dynamic_cast, etc.).
Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgCastExp node representing the cast expression. This pointer is guaranteed to be non-null, as the function asserts successful allocation.
Warning
The caller is responsible for ensuring that expression_type is a valid, non-null SgType pointer. Passing a null expression_type may lead to undefined behavior or assertion failures in downstream AST processing.
The returned SgCastExp node is heap-allocated. Ownership and lifetime management of this node are governed by the ROSE AST memory management conventions. Do not manually delete this node unless following the appropriate ROSE AST cleanup procedures.
Precondition
operand_i, if non-null, must be a valid SgExpression node that is not already attached to another parent in a way that would conflict with reassignment of its parent pointer.
expression_type should be a valid SgType pointer representing the desired target type for the cast.
cast_type must be a valid value from the SgCastExp::cast_type_enum enumeration.
Postcondition
The returned SgCastExp node has its operand, type, and cast kind set as specified by the input parameters.
If operand_i is non-null, its parent pointer is set to the returned SgCastExp node upon return.
The returned node is marked with a transformation source position, indicating it was generated programmatically rather than parsed from source code.
Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface, which provides factory functions for constructing ROSE AST nodes during source-to-source transformation tasks.
The internal call to markLhsValues ensures that any sub-expressions that appear in a left-hand side context within the cast are properly annotated in the AST.

◆ buildCatchOptionStmt()

SgCatchOptionStmt * SageBuilder::buildCatchOptionStmt ( SgVariableDeclaration * condition,
SgStatement * body )

Builds a catch statement node for use in an abstract syntax tree.

This function constructs an SgCatchOptionStmt node, which represents a single catch clause in a C++ try-catch construct. The node is initialized with the provided condition (the exception variable declaration) and body (the handler block). The parent pointers of both the condition and body nodes are updated to point to the newly created catch statement, ensuring proper tree linkage. The associated SgTryStmt parent is set to NULL at construction time and is expected to be assigned later when the catch option is attached to a try statement. A source position transformation marker is applied to the result to indicate that the node was introduced by a transformation rather than parsed from source code.

Parameters
conditionA pointer to an SgVariableDeclaration representing the exception variable caught by this handler. May be NULL to represent a catch-all handler (i.e., catch(...)).
bodyA pointer to an SgStatement representing the body of the catch clause. May be NULL, though a valid catch clause typically requires a non-NULL body.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgCatchOptionStmt node. The caller is responsible for attaching this node to an appropriate SgTryStmt.
Warning
The returned node has its associated SgTryStmt pointer set to NULL. Failing to attach the catch option to a try statement may result in an incomplete or invalid AST.
If body is NULL, the resulting AST node may be considered malformed by subsequent analysis or code generation passes.
Precondition
If condition is non-NULL, it must be a valid, heap-allocated SgVariableDeclaration node not already owned by another parent in the AST.
If body is non-NULL, it must be a valid, heap-allocated SgStatement node not already owned by another parent in the AST.
Postcondition
The returned SgCatchOptionStmt is heap-allocated and non-NULL.
If condition is non-NULL, its parent pointer is set to the returned SgCatchOptionStmt node.
If body is non-NULL, its parent pointer is set to the returned SgCatchOptionStmt node.
The source position of the returned node is marked as a transformation position via setOneSourcePositionForTransformation.
Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface for programmatic AST construction. It is intended for use during source-to-source transformation tasks where new catch clauses must be introduced into an existing or newly built AST.
The caller must ensure that the returned node is eventually inserted into a valid SgTryStmt to produce a well-formed AST.

If the provided pointer is null, an empty catch statement sequence is returned. If catch_option_stmt is non-null, it must point to a valid, properly initialized SgCatchOptionStmt object.

The returned SgCatchStatementSeq pointer is non-null and has its source position information set to default values.

This function is intended as a builder utility within the SageBuilder interface, following the standard ROSE AST construction patterns. The resulting node should typically be attached to a try statement or similar enclosing construct to form a complete and valid AST.

This function is part of the SageBuilder interface, which provides a unified set of builder routines for constructing ROSE IR (Intermediate Representation) nodes programmatically.

The char16_t type is a character type capable of holding a UTF-16 code unit, as defined by the C99 and C++11 standards. Support for this type was added to ROSE to allow correct representation and manipulation of source code that uses char16_t.

The caller is responsible for ensuring that the returned type node is properly integrated into the AST or managed according to ROSE memory management conventions. Failing to do so may result in memory leaks or dangling references.

Support for char32_t was introduced as part of C99 and C++11 language standards. The newly created node is allocated on the heap, initialized with the provided unsigned integer value and an empty string representation, and then assigned a transformation source position to indicate that it was synthetically generated rather than parsed from source code.

The function uses setOneSourcePositionForTransformation to mark the node as a compiler-generated (transformation) construct, which is the standard practice when building AST nodes programmatically via the SageBuilder interface.

Parameters
valueThe unsigned integer value representing the char32_t character literal. Defaults to 0 if not specified.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgChar32Val AST node initialized with the given value and an empty string representation.
Warning
The caller should not manually delete the returned pointer if the node is inserted into the AST, as the AST memory management infrastructure will handle cleanup. Deleting the node while it is part of the AST may lead to undefined behavior.
Precondition
The ROSE infrastructure must be properly initialized before calling this function.
The provided value must be a valid unsigned integer representable as a char32_t character code point.
Postcondition
A valid SgChar32Val node is created and returned with its source position set to a transformation position.
The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-null; an assertion failure will terminate the program if allocation fails.
Note
This function was added to support char16_t and char32_t types introduced in C99 and C++11. It follows the same construction pattern used by other scalar literal builder functions in the SageBuilder interface.
The string representation of the literal is initialized to an empty string and may need to be set separately if a textual representation is required.

Builds a class declaration node and inserts it into the given scope.

This is a convenience wrapper that ensures a valid defining declaration is always returned.

The function is part of the SageBuilder interface, which provides factory-style construction routines for building ROSE AST (Abstract Syntax Tree) nodes programmatically. The resulting node can be used to represent a C++ class, struct, or union declaration within the AST.

The parameter scope must not be NULL and must point to a valid, initialized SgScopeStatement within the AST.
The parameter name must represent a valid, non-empty class identifier.

A defining SgClassDeclaration node is created and associated with the given scope.
The returned pointer is non-NULL and points to a valid SgClassDeclaration node.

◆ buildClassDeclaration_nfi()

SgClassDeclaration * SageBuilder::buildClassDeclaration_nfi ( const SgName & XXX_name,
SgClassDeclaration::class_types kind,
SgScopeStatement * scope,
SgClassDeclaration * nonDefiningDecl,
bool buildTemplateInstantiation,
SgTemplateArgumentPtrList * templateArgumentsList )

Builds both the non-defining and defining C++ class declarations and links them together in the ROSE AST.

This function constructs a pair of class declarations (non-defining and defining) for a given class name and class kind, and properly wires them together within the ROSE intermediate representation (IR). It is the primary internal builder function for C++ class declarations within the SageBuilder interface.

The function proceeds through several major phases:

  1. Scope resolution: If no scope is provided, the top of the SageBuilder scope stack is used as the enclosing scope.
  2. Name computation: Depending on whether a template instantiation is being built, the function computes both a name without template arguments and a name with template arguments (using appendTemplateArgumentsToName() when applicable).
  3. Symbol table lookup: The function attempts to locate an existing SgClassSymbol in the given scope using the computed name. For template instantiations, it uses lookup_class_symbol() with the template argument list. If a symbol is found, the existing non-defining declaration is reused. If not, a new non-defining declaration is constructed.
  4. Non-defining declaration construction: If no existing symbol is found, a new non-defining declaration is built. For template instantiations, an SgTemplateInstantiationDecl is created; otherwise, a plain SgClassDeclaration is created. The template name and template arguments are set as appropriate. A new SgClassType (or SgJavaParameterType for Java parameter kinds) is created and associated with the non-defining declaration. A new SgClassSymbol is inserted into the scope's symbol table.
  5. Defining declaration construction: A new defining declaration is built using either SgTemplateInstantiationDecl, SgTemplateClassDeclaration, or SgClassDeclaration depending on the flags. A new SgClassDefinition is created and attached to the defining declaration.
  6. Cross-linking: The non-defining and defining declarations are linked via set_definingDeclaration() and set_firstNondefiningDeclaration(). Both declarations are set to share the same SgClassType. Template arguments are set on the defining declaration if applicable.
  7. Fixup: Source position information is set for both declarations using setOneSourcePositionForTransformation(). The fixStructDeclaration() helper is called to finalize scope and parent relationships. Template argument parent pointers are validated via testTemplateArgumentParents().

The function explicitly asserts that this path must NOT be used to build SgTemplateClassDeclaration nodes (i.e., buildTemplateDeclaration must be false). If the input nonDefiningDecl is already a template class declaration, an error is reported and execution is aborted.

Parameters
XXX_nameThe name of the class to be declared. For non-template classes, this is the plain class name. For template instantiations, this should be the base name without template argument syntax; the function appends template arguments internally.
kindThe class kind, specifying whether the declaration represents a class, struct, union, or other supported class type as defined by SgClassDeclaration::class_types.
scopeThe enclosing scope in which the class declaration is to be inserted. If NULL, the top of the SageBuilder scope stack is used. When a scope is provided, the new SgClassSymbol is inserted into its symbol table.
nonDefiningDeclAn optional pointer to an existing non-defining class declaration. If non-NULL, it may be used to retrieve the associated symbol when the symbol table lookup fails. This parameter is currently used only in limited cases and may be NULL.
buildTemplateInstantiationA boolean flag indicating whether the declaration being built represents a template instantiation. When true, SgTemplateInstantiationDecl nodes are constructed and template arguments are attached.
templateArgumentsListA pointer to the list of template arguments to be associated with the declaration when buildTemplateInstantiation is true. Must be non-NULL when buildTemplateInstantiation is true. May be NULL otherwise.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed defining SgClassDeclaration (or SgTemplateInstantiationDecl if building a template instantiation). The returned node has its firstNondefiningDeclaration and definingDeclaration pointers properly set, and shares its SgClassType with the non-defining declaration.
Warning
This function must not be called to build SgTemplateClassDeclaration nodes. If the input nonDefiningDecl is an SgTemplateClassDeclaration, an error is printed and an assertion failure is triggered. Use the appropriate template class builder function in that case.
If no scope is provided and the SageBuilder scope stack is empty, behavior is undefined. Callers should ensure a valid scope is available either explicitly or via the scope stack.
When buildTemplateInstantiation is true, templateArgumentsList must not be NULL. Passing NULL in that case will trigger an assertion failure.
The parent pointers of the returned defining declaration are not set by this function; callers are responsible for setting the parent after insertion into the AST.
Precondition
If buildTemplateInstantiation is true, templateArgumentsList must be non-NULL.
The input nonDefiningDecl, if non-NULL, must not be an SgTemplateClassDeclaration.
The SageBuilder scope stack must be non-empty if scope is NULL.
The class name XXX_name should not contain template argument syntax when buildTemplateInstantiation is false.
Postcondition
The returned defining declaration has get_definingDeclaration() pointing to itself.
The returned defining declaration has get_firstNondefiningDeclaration() pointing to a valid non-defining declaration that is distinct from the defining declaration.
Both the defining and non-defining declarations share the same SgClassType instance.
If a scope was provided or resolved from the stack, a corresponding SgClassSymbol has been inserted into that scope's symbol table (unless the symbol already existed).
The non-defining declaration has its forward flag set via setForward().
Source position information has been set on both declarations via setOneSourcePositionForTransformation().
Template argument parent pointers are valid as verified by testTemplateArgumentParents().
Note
This function is intended for internal use within the SageBuilder infrastructure. It could in principle be refactored to call buildNondefiningClassDeclaration() and buildDefiningClassDeclaration() directly, but currently performs both steps inline.
The DEBUG_CLASS_DECLARATION define controls verbose diagnostic output within this function. It is set to 0 by default and can be enabled at compile time for debugging purposes.
For Java parameter types (kind == SgClassDeclaration::e_java_parameter), an SgJavaParameterType is created instead of a plain SgClassType.
When a template instantiation's defining declaration already has a NULL templateDeclaration pointer but the non-defining declaration has a valid one, this function propagates the templateDeclaration pointer from the non-defining to the defining declaration automatically.

◆ buildClassDefinition()

SgClassDefinition * SageBuilder::buildClassDefinition ( SgClassDeclaration * d,
bool buildTemplateInstantiation )

Builds and returns a new SgClassDefinition node, optionally as a template instantiation definition.

This function constructs a new class definition node in the ROSE abstract syntax tree (AST). Depending on the arguments provided, it creates either a plain SgClassDefinition or an SgTemplateInstantiationDefn. If a non-NULL SgClassDeclaration pointer is supplied, the newly created definition node is associated with that declaration. If the declaration pointer is NULL, the definition is created without an associated declaration.

When buildTemplateInstantiation is true and a non-NULL declaration is provided, the declaration must be an SgTemplateInstantiationDecl; this is enforced by an assertion. If buildTemplateInstantiation is true and the declaration is NULL, an SgTemplateInstantiationDefn is created without an associated declaration.

After construction, the function checks whether the current language uses case-insensitive symbol table semantics (for example, Fortran). If so, it sets the case-insensitive flag on the resulting definition node. Finally, a single source position is assigned to the new node to mark it as a transformation artifact.

Parameters
dA pointer to the SgClassDeclaration with which the new class definition should be associated. May be NULL, in which case the definition is created without an associated declaration. Passing NULL avoids a segmentation fault that would occur if the underlying constructor received a NULL pointer directly.
buildTemplateInstantiationA boolean flag indicating whether to create an SgTemplateInstantiationDefn instead of a plain SgClassDefinition. When true and d is non-NULL, d must be an SgTemplateInstantiationDecl.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgClassDefinition (or SgTemplateInstantiationDefn) node. The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-NULL.
Precondition
If buildTemplateInstantiation is true and d is non-NULL, then d must be an instance of SgTemplateInstantiationDecl; this is enforced by an internal assertion.
Postcondition
The returned SgClassDefinition pointer is non-NULL.
If the current language uses case-insensitive symbol table semantics, the case-insensitive flag is set on the returned node.
The returned node has a source position set to indicate it is a transformation artifact.
Warning
Passing a non-NULL d that is not an SgTemplateInstantiationDecl while setting buildTemplateInstantiation to true will trigger an assertion failure at runtime.
The underlying SgClassDefinition constructor does not guard against a NULL declaration pointer; always use this builder function rather than constructing SgClassDefinition directly with a potentially NULL pointer.
Note
The default value of d is NULL and the default value of buildTemplateInstantiation is false, so calling this function with no arguments produces a plain SgClassDefinition with no associated declaration.
Case sensitivity behavior is determined by SageInterface::is_language_case_insensitive(), which reflects the language currently being processed (for example, Fortran is case-insensitive).
