Builds an SgClassType representing an instantiation of a class template from a given template declaration and a list of template arguments.

This function constructs a fully formed SgClassType node corresponding to a specific instantiation of a C++ class template. The process involves several coordinated steps:

  1. The base name of the template is retrieved from the provided SgTemplateClassDeclaration.
  2. A list of SgTemplateArgument nodes is generated from the raw SgNode template argument list using a helper function.
  3. The canonical form of the template declaration is resolved to ensure consistency across multiple references to the same template.
  4. An SgTemplateInstantiationDecl node is created to represent the specific instantiation of the template with the provided arguments.
  5. An SgClassType is generated from the instantiation declaration.
  6. The instantiation declaration is updated with the newly created type, and its definition pointer is set to null (as the definition may not yet be available at this stage).
  7. The parent pointer of each template argument is set to the instantiation declaration using a functor applied via std::for_each.

This function is part of the SageBuilder interface, which provides utilities for programmatically constructing ROSE IR (Intermediate Representation) nodes.

Parameters
template_declA pointer to the SgTemplateClassDeclaration that represents the class template to be instantiated. Must not be null.
template_argsA reference to a container of SgNode pointers representing the template arguments to be used for the instantiation. Each element is expected to be a valid template argument node.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgClassType representing the template instantiation. The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-null upon successful completion.
Warning
The definition field of the resulting SgTemplateInstantiationDecl is explicitly set to null. Callers that require a fully defined instantiation must set the definition separately after this function returns.
The canonical template declaration is resolved internally. If the provided template_decl is not properly linked within the AST, the canonical resolution may produce unexpected results.
Precondition
template_decl must not be null; an assertion will be triggered if it is.
template_args must contain valid SgNode pointers that are appropriate template argument nodes for the given template declaration.
Postcondition
The returned SgClassType is associated with a valid SgTemplateInstantiationDecl.
The SgTemplateInstantiationDecl has its type field set to the returned SgClassType.
Each template argument in the generated argument list has its parent pointer set to the SgTemplateInstantiationDecl.
The definition field of the SgTemplateInstantiationDecl is set to null.
Note
The definition of the SgTemplateInstantiationDecl is intentionally left as null in this function. This is noted in the source as an unresolved design decision regarding what value is appropriate for this field.
This function relies on several internal helper utilities including genTemplateArgumentList, getCanonicalTemplateDecl, genTemplateInstantiationDecl, genTemplateClass, and the TemplateArgumentParentSetter functor.

◆ buildColonShapeExp()

SgColonShapeExp * SageBuilder::buildColonShapeExp ( )

Builds and returns a new SgColonShapeExp AST node representing a colon shape expression.

This function constructs a SgColonShapeExp node, which represents a colon-shaped array subscript or shape expression commonly found in Fortran array syntax (e.g., the colon operator used to denote a full array dimension or range). Internally, it delegates the core node allocation and initialization to buildColonShapeExp_nfi(), which performs the construction without setting source position information. After the node is created, setOneSourcePositionForTransformation() is called to assign a synthetic source position to the node, marking it as a compiler-generated (transformation) construct rather than one originating from user source code.

Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgColonShapeExp AST node with transformation source position information set.
Precondition
The SageBuilder infrastructure must be properly initialized before calling this function.
Postcondition
The returned SgColonShapeExp pointer is non-null and has its source position set to indicate a compiler transformation origin.
Note
The caller is responsible for inserting the returned node into the AST at an appropriate location. The node is allocated on the heap and its lifetime is managed by the AST memory pool.
Warning
Do not use the returned node outside of a valid AST context. Improper insertion or use of the node may result in undefined behavior or malformed AST structures.

◆ buildColonShapeExp_nfi()

SgColonShapeExp * SageBuilder::buildColonShapeExp_nfi ( )

Builds and returns a new SgColonShapeExp node using the no-frills interface (nfi).

This function allocates a new SgColonShapeExp AST node on the heap, verifies that the allocation succeeded, and initializes its source position information to null before returning the constructed node. The "nfi" suffix indicates that this is a no-frills interface variant, meaning it performs minimal setup and leaves most node attributes at their default values, giving the caller full control over subsequent configuration.

The function uses ASSERT_not_null to guard against failed memory allocation, ensuring that a null pointer is never silently returned. Source position data is explicitly set to null via setOneSourcePositionNull, which is the standard practice for programmatically constructed nodes that do not correspond to any location in the original source file.

Returns
A pointer to the newly allocated and minimally initialized SgColonShapeExp node.
Warning
The caller is responsible for managing the lifetime of the returned pointer. Failing to attach the returned node to a parent AST node or to otherwise manage its memory may result in memory leaks.
Precondition
Sufficient heap memory must be available to allocate a new SgColonShapeExp object.
Postcondition
The returned pointer is non-null and points to a valid SgColonShapeExp node whose source position information has been set to null.
Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface for constructing ROSE intermediate representation (IR) nodes. It is intended for use when building AST nodes programmatically rather than parsing source code. Nodes created through the nfi variant typically require additional manual setup compared to their higher-level counterparts.

◆ buildComment()

PreprocessingInfo * SageBuilder::buildComment ( SgLocatedNode * target,
const std::string & content,
PreprocessingInfo::RelativePositionType position,
PreprocessingInfo::DirectiveType dtype )

Builds and attaches a comment to a specified located node in the AST.

This function creates a comment associated with a given AST node and attaches it at the specified relative position. Internally, it delegates to SageInterface::attachComment, which handles the actual construction of the PreprocessingInfo object and its attachment to the target node's preprocessing information list.

The comment can be placed before or after the target node depending on the value of the position parameter. The directive type parameter allows the caller to specify what kind of C preprocessor directive or comment construct is being represented. By default, the comment is placed before the target node and the directive type is set to CpreprocessorUnknownDeclaration.

This is a convenience builder function in the SageBuilder interface that wraps the corresponding SageInterface utility, following the standard builder pattern used throughout the ROSE compiler infrastructure.

Parameters
targetPointer to the SgLocatedNode to which the comment will be attached. Must not be null and must be a valid node in the AST.
contentThe text content of the comment to be attached. This is the raw string that will be stored as the comment body.
positionThe relative position of the comment with respect to the target node. Defaults to PreprocessingInfo::before, meaning the comment will appear before the target node in the output.
dtypeThe directive type of the comment, indicating what kind of preprocessor or comment construct this represents. Defaults to PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorUnknownDeclaration.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created PreprocessingInfo object representing the attached comment. Returns null if the attachment fails.
Warning
Passing a null pointer for target results in undefined behavior. Ensure the target node is valid and properly initialized before calling this function.
Precondition
target must be a non-null pointer to a valid SgLocatedNode within a well-formed AST.
content should be a properly formatted comment string consistent with the specified directive type.
Postcondition
The returned PreprocessingInfo object is attached to the target node's preprocessing information list at the specified relative position.
The target node's preprocessing info list is updated to include the new comment entry.
Note
This function is a thin wrapper around SageInterface::attachComment and does not perform any additional validation or transformation of its arguments beyond what that function provides.
The caller is generally not responsible for managing the memory of the returned PreprocessingInfo object, as it becomes owned by the AST node to which it is attached.

◆ buildCommonBlock()

SgCommonBlock * SageBuilder::buildCommonBlock ( SgCommonBlockObject * first_block)

Builds and returns a new SgCommonBlock AST node, optionally initialized with a first block object.

This function constructs a new SgCommonBlock node, which represents a Fortran COMMON block declaration in the ROSE abstract syntax tree (AST). If a non-null SgCommonBlockObject is provided, it is appended to the block's internal block list and its parent pointer is set to the newly created SgCommonBlock node. The resulting node is configured as both its own defining declaration and its own first non-defining declaration, which is the standard self-referential setup used for this kind of declaration node in ROSE. Source position information is also set to indicate that this node was introduced by a transformation rather than parsed from source code.

Parameters
first_blockAn optional pointer to an SgCommonBlockObject to be added as the first entry in the COMMON block's block list. If NULL (the default), the resulting SgCommonBlock is created with an empty block list.
Returns
A pointer to the newly allocated and initialized SgCommonBlock node. The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-null.
Precondition
If first_block is non-null, it must point to a valid, fully constructed SgCommonBlockObject instance.
Postcondition
The returned SgCommonBlock node has its definingDeclaration and firstNondefiningDeclaration both set to itself.
If first_block was non-null, it has been appended to the block list of the returned node and its parent pointer has been updated to point to the returned node.
The source position of the returned node is marked as a transformation-generated position.
Warning
The caller is responsible for managing the lifetime of the returned SgCommonBlock pointer. Failure to insert it into the AST or to delete it appropriately may result in memory leaks.
Note
This function is intended for use in Fortran AST construction or transformation contexts within the ROSE compiler framework. It is part of the SageBuilder interface for programmatically building AST nodes.

◆ buildCommonBlockObject()

SgCommonBlockObject * SageBuilder::buildCommonBlockObject ( std::string name,
SgExprListExp * exp_list )

Builds and returns a new SgCommonBlockObject AST node representing a Fortran COMMON block object.

This function constructs a new SgCommonBlockObject node intended for use in the ROSE abstract syntax tree (AST), typically when building or transforming Fortran code that uses COMMON blocks. The function allocates a new SgCommonBlockObject on the heap, sets its block name to the provided string, and optionally associates a variable reference list with it. If a non-NULL expression list is supplied, the function sets it as the variable reference list of the new node and establishes the parent-child relationship by setting the parent of the expression list to the newly created object. After construction, source position information is set on the result node using setSourcePositionForTransformation to mark it as a transformation-generated node rather than one derived from original source code.

Parameters
nameThe name of the COMMON block. Defaults to an empty string if not provided, which corresponds to an unnamed (blank) COMMON block in Fortran.
exp_listA pointer to an SgExprListExp node representing the list of variable references belonging to this COMMON block. May be NULL if no variable list is to be associated at construction time.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgCommonBlockObject node. The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-NULL; the function asserts this condition internally.
Warning
The returned SgCommonBlockObject is heap-allocated. The caller or the AST infrastructure is responsible for managing the lifetime of this node. Failing to attach it to the AST or to free it appropriately may result in memory leaks.
Precondition
If exp_list is non-NULL, it must be a valid, fully constructed SgExprListExp node that is not already attached to another parent node, as this function will reassign its parent pointer.
Postcondition
The returned SgCommonBlockObject has its block name set to the value of name.
If exp_list is non-NULL, the returned node's variable reference list is set to exp_list, and exp_list's parent pointer is set to the returned node.
The source position of the returned node is marked as a transformation using setSourcePositionForTransformation.
Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface, which provides factory functions for constructing ROSE AST nodes programmatically during code generation or transformation passes.
The default value of name is an empty string and the default value of exp_list is NULL, making both parameters optional at the call site.

◆ buildComplexType()

SgTypeComplex * SageBuilder::buildComplexType ( SgType * base_type)

Builds a complex type node in the ROSE AST.

This function constructs and returns a new SgTypeComplex node representing a complex number type, using the provided base type as the underlying element type. Complex types in ROSE correspond to C99 and C++ complex number types (e.g., _Complex float, _Complex double). The function allocates a new SgTypeComplex object on the heap, associates it with the given base type, and returns the resulting node. An assertion ensures that the base type pointer is non-null before construction proceeds.

Parameters
base_typeA pointer to the SgType representing the base (element) type of the complex type (e.g., float, double). Must not be NULL.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgTypeComplex node representing the complex type built from the given base type.
Warning
The caller is responsible for ensuring that the returned SgTypeComplex node is properly integrated into the AST. Failing to do so may result in memory leaks or an inconsistent AST state.
Precondition
base_type must not be NULL. Passing NULL will trigger an assertion failure and abort execution.
Postcondition
A valid SgTypeComplex object is allocated and returned. The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-NULL.
Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface, which provides factory functions for constructing ROSE AST nodes. The default parameter value of NULL for base_type is declared in the interface but is effectively disallowed at runtime due to the internal assertion check.

◆ buildComplexVal()

SgComplexVal * SageBuilder::buildComplexVal ( SgValueExp * real_value,
SgValueExp * imaginary_value )

Builds an SgComplexVal AST node representing a complex number literal from separate real and imaginary value expressions.

This function constructs a new SgComplexVal node in the ROSE Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) by combining a real part and an imaginary part, both provided as SgValueExp pointers. The type of the resulting complex value node is derived from the type of the imaginary value expression. After construction, the parent pointers of both the real and imaginary child nodes are set to point to the newly created SgComplexVal node, establishing the correct parent-child relationships within the AST. A source position transformation marker is applied to the result to indicate that this node was introduced via a builder transformation rather than parsed from source. Assertions are used throughout to verify that the node was successfully allocated and that parent pointers are correctly assigned for any non-NULL child nodes.

Parameters
real_valuePointer to an SgValueExp node representing the real component of the complex number. May be NULL, in which case no parent assignment is performed for this component.
imaginary_valuePointer to an SgValueExp node representing the imaginary component of the complex number. The type of this node is used as the type of the resulting SgComplexVal node. May be NULL, in which case no parent assignment is performed for this component.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgComplexVal AST node representing the complex number formed by the given real and imaginary parts.
Warning
Passing NULL for imaginary_value will cause a null pointer dereference when attempting to call get_type() on it during construction of the SgComplexVal node. Callers should ensure imaginary_value is a valid, non-NULL pointer.
The function uses ROSE_ASSERT to verify successful allocation and correct parent pointer assignment. If assertions are disabled and allocation fails, behavior is undefined.
Precondition
real_value, if non-NULL, must be a valid, heap-allocated SgValueExp node.
imaginary_value must be a valid, non-NULL, heap-allocated SgValueExp node with a valid type accessible via get_type().
Postcondition
The returned SgComplexVal node is heap-allocated and non-NULL.
If real_value is non-NULL, its parent pointer is set to the returned SgComplexVal node.
If imaginary_value is non-NULL, its parent pointer is set to the returned SgComplexVal node.
The returned node has its source position marked as a transformation.
Note
The type of the resulting SgComplexVal is taken directly from the imaginary_value expression's type. If a different or more specific complex type is required, the caller may need to adjust the type after construction.
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface, which provides utilities for programmatically constructing ROSE AST nodes during source-to-source transformations.

◆ buildComplexVal_nfi()

SgComplexVal * SageBuilder::buildComplexVal_nfi ( SgValueExp * real_value,
SgValueExp * imaginary_value,
const std::string & str )

Builds an SgComplexVal AST node representing a complex number value without file information.

This function constructs a new SgComplexVal node in the ROSE Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) using the provided real and imaginary value expressions and an optional string representation. The suffix "_nfi" indicates that no file information is attached to the resulting node; instead, the source position is explicitly set to null via setOneSourcePositionNull().

The type of the resulting complex value node is derived from the type of the imaginary_value expression. After constructing the node, the function sets the parent pointers of both the real and imaginary child nodes to point to the newly created SgComplexVal node, provided they are non-null. Assertions are used throughout to verify that the imaginary value is non-null, that the result node was successfully allocated, and that parent pointers are correctly established after assignment.

Parameters
real_valuePointer to an SgValueExp representing the real part of the complex number. May be NULL, in which case no parent assignment is performed for this component.
imaginary_valuePointer to an SgValueExp representing the imaginary part of the complex number. Must not be NULL; an assertion will fire if it is. Its type is used as the type of the resulting SgComplexVal node.
strA string representation of the complex value, typically used for unparsing or display purposes.

A pointer to the newly constructed SgComplexVal AST node with its real and imaginary child nodes set and parent pointers established. The source position of the returned node is set to null.
Warning
The imaginary_value parameter must not be NULL. Passing a NULL imaginary_value will trigger an assertion failure and abort execution.
The type of the resulting SgComplexVal node is taken from imaginary_value's type. Ensure that this type accurately reflects the intended complex number type.
Precondition
imaginary_value must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgValueExp node.
Both real_value and imaginary_value, if non-null, should not already be owned by another parent node in the AST, as their parent pointers will be overwritten.
Postcondition
The returned SgComplexVal node is non-null and has been allocated on the heap.
If real_value is non-null, its parent pointer is set to the returned SgComplexVal node.
imaginary_value's parent pointer is set to the returned SgComplexVal node.
The source position of the returned node is set to null (no file information attached).
Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface for programmatically constructing ROSE AST nodes. The "_nfi" suffix convention is used throughout SageBuilder to distinguish node-building functions that do not attach source file information.

Builds a compound initializer node for vector type initialization.

This function constructs an SgCompoundInitializer AST node, which represents a compound initializer expression typically used in C and C++ to initialize aggregate or vector types (e.g., array or struct initializers of the form { expr1, expr2, ... }). The function allocates a new SgCompoundInitializer, optionally associates an expression list of initializer values and a type, sets the parent pointer of the initializer list if one is provided, and marks the resulting node with a transformation source position to indicate it was synthetically generated rather than parsed from source code.

The returned SgCompoundInitializer node has been allocated and initialized.

The node is initialized using the provided SgVariableSymbol, which carries type and name information for the compound literal. Builds an AST node representing a C/C++ conditional (ternary) expression.

This function constructs a new SgConditionalExp node, which corresponds to the ternary conditional operator of the form test ? a : b in C and C++. The three sub-expressions provided are attached as children of the newly created node, and each non-null sub-expression has its parent pointer set to the resulting node. A source position is assigned to the node via setOneSourcePositionForTransformation, marking it as a compiler-generated transformation rather than originating from user source code. This function is part of the SageBuilder interface used for programmatic AST construction during source-to-source transformation.

Parameters
testA pointer to the condition expression (the part before the ?). May be NULL, in which case no parent assignment is performed for this operand.
aA pointer to the true-branch expression (the part between ? and :). May be NULL, in which case no parent assignment is performed for this operand.
bA pointer to the false-branch expression (the part after :). May be NULL, in which case no parent assignment is performed for this operand.
Returns
A pointer to the newly allocated SgConditionalExp node representing the ternary expression. The caller is responsible for inserting this node into the AST and managing its lifetime appropriately.
Warning
Passing NULL for test, a, or b will result in an incomplete AST node. While the function handles NULL gracefully by skipping parent assignment, the resulting node may not represent a semantically valid conditional expression and could cause issues during later AST traversal or analysis.
The caller must ensure that the returned node is properly inserted into the AST. Failing to do so may result in memory leaks or dangling nodes.
Precondition
Each non-null expression pointer passed as test, a, or b should not already be attached to another parent node in the AST, as this function will overwrite the parent pointer of each provided sub-expression.
Postcondition
The returned SgConditionalExp node has its condition, true-branch, and false-branch set to test, a, and b respectively.
Each non-null sub-expression has its parent pointer set to the returned node.
The returned node has a source position assigned that marks it as a compiler-generated transformation.
Note
The type of the resulting SgConditionalExp node is set to NULL at construction time and may need to be resolved or set explicitly depending on the context in which the node is used.
This function is intended for use within the SageBuilder API for AST construction during ROSE-based source-to-source transformations.

◆ buildConditionalExp_nfi()

SgConditionalExp * SageBuilder::buildConditionalExp_nfi ( SgExpression * test,
SgExpression * a,
SgExpression * b,
SgType * t )

Builds an SgConditionalExp node (ternary conditional expression) without file information.

This function constructs an SgConditionalExp AST node representing a C/C++ ternary conditional expression of the form test ? a : b. The suffix _nfi indicates that this builder does not attach source file information to the resulting node; instead, the source position is explicitly set to null via setOneSourcePositionNull().

After allocating the SgConditionalExp node, the function sets the parent pointers of the provided sub-expressions (test, a, and b) to point back to the newly created node, provided each sub-expression is non-null. Additionally, markLhsValues() is called on both the true-branch expression a and the false-branch expression b to properly annotate any left-hand side value semantics within those sub-trees.

This function is typically used when building synthetic AST nodes that do not correspond to any location in the original source file.

Parameters
testThe condition expression evaluated to determine which branch is taken. May be null, in which case no parent assignment is performed for this argument.
aThe expression evaluated and returned when test is true (the true branch). May be null, in which case no parent assignment or lhs marking is performed.
bThe expression evaluated and returned when test is false (the false branch). May be null, in which case no parent assignment or lhs marking is performed.
tThe type of the resulting conditional expression. This type is associated directly with the constructed SgConditionalExp node.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgConditionalExp node representing the ternary conditional expression test ? a : b with type t.
Warning
The caller is responsible for ensuring that the provided sub-expressions and type are compatible and semantically valid. No type-checking or semantic validation is performed by this function.
The source position of the returned node is set to null. If source location information is required, use an alternative builder or set the position manually after construction.
Precondition
If test, a, or b are non-null, they must be valid, heap-allocated SgExpression objects that are not already owned by another parent node in the AST, or their parent pointers must be safely reassignable.
t should be a valid SgType pointer representing the intended result type of the conditional expression.
Postcondition
The returned SgConditionalExp node is heap-allocated and has its source position set to null.
Any non-null sub-expression among test, a, and b will have its parent pointer set to the returned SgConditionalExp node.
The true-branch expression a and false-branch expression b, if non-null, will have had markLhsValues() applied to them.
Note
This is the "no file info" (_nfi) variant of the conditional expression builder. It is intended for use when constructing artificial or compiler-generated AST nodes that do not originate from a specific location in the source file.

◆ buildConstructorInitializer()

SgConstructorInitializer * SageBuilder::buildConstructorInitializer ( SgMemberFunctionDeclaration * declaration,
SgExprListExp * args,
SgType * expression_type,
bool need_name,
bool need_qualifier,
bool need_parenthesis_after_name,
bool associated_class_unknown )

Builds and returns a new SgConstructorInitializer AST node.

This function constructs an SgConstructorInitializer node, which represents a constructor initializer expression in the ROSE abstract syntax tree (AST). Such nodes appear in constructor initializer lists (e.g., the colon-separated list of member initializations following a constructor declaration).

The function allocates a new SgConstructorInitializer object using the provided arguments and configures its source position for transformation purposes via setOneSourcePositionForTransformation. If a non-NULL argument list (args) is provided, its parent pointer is set to the newly created initializer node, and its source position is also configured for transformation.

The declaration parameter may be NULL to support implicit constructors, in which case the associated class declaration check is skipped. If a non-NULL declaration is provided, it must have a valid associated class declaration, enforced by an internal assertion.

Parameters
declarationA pointer to the SgMemberFunctionDeclaration representing the constructor being called. May be NULL to represent an implicit constructor. If non-NULL, must have a valid associated class declaration.
argsA pointer to an SgExprListExp representing the argument list passed to the constructor. May be NULL if no arguments are provided.
expression_typeA pointer to the SgType representing the type of the constructor initializer expression.
need_nameA boolean flag indicating whether the constructor initializer requires a name.
need_qualifierA boolean flag indicating whether the constructor initializer requires a qualifier.
need_parenthesis_after_nameA boolean flag indicating whether parentheses are required after the name in the constructor initializer.
associated_class_unknownA boolean flag indicating whether the associated class is unknown at the time of construction.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgConstructorInitializer node. The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-NULL.
Precondition
If declaration is non-NULL, it must have a valid associated class declaration (i.e., declaration->get_associatedClassDeclaration() must not return NULL).
Postcondition
The returned SgConstructorInitializer node is non-NULL and has its source position set for transformation.
If args is non-NULL, its parent pointer is set to the returned SgConstructorInitializer node and its source position is set for transformation.
Warning
Passing a non-NULL declaration that lacks an associated class declaration will trigger a failed assertion and abort the program.
Note
This function was modified to allow a NULL declaration parameter in order to support implicit constructors, as noted in the original implementation (George Vulov, 05/24/2011).
All default parameter values are NULL or false, allowing partial specification of the constructor initializer's properties.

◆ buildConstructorInitializer_nfi()

SgConstructorInitializer * SageBuilder::buildConstructorInitializer_nfi ( SgMemberFunctionDeclaration * declaration,
SgExprListExp * args,
SgType * expression_type,
bool need_name,
bool need_qualifier,
bool need_parenthesis_after_name,
bool associated_class_unknown )

Builds and returns a new SgConstructorInitializer node without file information (nfi).

This function allocates and initializes a new SgConstructorInitializer AST node using the provided member function declaration, argument expression list, and type information. It is the "no file info" (nfi) variant of the constructor initializer builder, meaning source position information is set to null rather than derived from an actual source location.

After allocating the node, the function performs the following steps:

  • Asserts that the result is non-null.
  • Sets the source position of the new node to null via setOneSourcePositionNull.
  • If the argument list is non-null, sets its parent pointer to the newly created node.
  • If the argument list's start-of-construct source position is null, sets it to null explicitly via setOneSourcePositionNull to ensure consistent initialization.

This builder is symmetric with similar nfi builder functions in the SageBuilder interface and is intended for programmatic AST construction where no corresponding source file location exists.

Parameters
declarationA pointer to the SgMemberFunctionDeclaration representing the constructor being initialized. May be NULL, but if non-NULL, its associated class declaration must also be non-NULL (enforced by an internal assertion).
argsA pointer to the SgExprListExp representing the arguments passed to the constructor initializer. May be NULL if no arguments are provided.
expression_typeA pointer to the SgType representing the type of the constructor initializer expression. May be NULL.
need_nameA boolean flag indicating whether the constructor initializer requires a name.
need_qualifierA boolean flag indicating whether the constructor initializer requires a qualifier.
need_parenthesis_after_nameA boolean flag indicating whether parentheses are required after the name in the constructor initializer.
associated_class_unknownA boolean flag indicating whether the associated class is unknown at the time of construction.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgConstructorInitializer node. The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-NULL.
Precondition
If declaration is non-NULL, then declaration->get_associatedClassDeclaration() must also be non-NULL. This is enforced by an internal ROSE_ASSERT.
Postcondition
The returned SgConstructorInitializer node has its source position set to null.
If args is non-NULL, its parent pointer is set to the returned node.
The argument list's start-of-construct source position is initialized (set to null if it was previously unset).
Warning
Passing a non-NULL declaration whose associated class declaration is NULL will trigger an assertion failure and abort execution.
Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface for constructing AST nodes without source file information. It should be used when building AST fragments programmatically rather than parsing from source code.
The caller is responsible for integrating the returned node into the broader AST and ensuring proper memory management within the ROSE IR framework.

◆ buildConstType()

SgModifierType * SageBuilder::buildConstType ( SgType * base_type)

Builds a const-qualified modifier type wrapping a given base type.

This function constructs an SgModifierType node that applies the const qualifier to the provided base type. Internally, it allocates a new SgModifierType object initialized with the given base type, then sets the const flag on the type's constVolatile modifier. To ensure uniqueness within the AST, the newly created type is submitted to the global type table via SgModifierType::insertModifierTypeIntoTypeTable. If an equivalent const-qualified type already exists in the type table, the pre-existing type is returned and the newly allocated object is deleted. This deduplication mechanism prevents redundant type nodes from accumulating in the AST and ensures that structurally identical types share a single representation.

Parameters
base_typeA pointer to the SgType that will serve as the underlying type for the const modifier. This parameter must not be NULL and must point to a valid, fully constructed type node.
Returns
A pointer to an SgModifierType representing the const-qualified version of the given base type. The returned pointer is either a newly allocated SgModifierType or an existing equivalent type retrieved from the type table. The returned type is guaranteed to be distinct from the base_type pointer itself.
Warning
Passing NULL as base_type will trigger an assertion failure and abort the program. Always ensure the base type is a valid, non-null pointer before calling this function.
The caller must not delete the returned pointer, as the type table manages the lifetime of deduplicated type nodes. Deleting the returned pointer may corrupt the AST type table.
Precondition
base_type must not be NULL.
base_type must point to a fully initialized and valid SgType node within the current AST context.
Postcondition
The returned SgModifierType has its const qualifier set.
The returned type is registered in the global SgModifierType type table.
The returned pointer is not equal to base_type.
If an equivalent const-qualified type already existed in the type table, the newly allocated intermediate type has been freed and the pre-existing type is returned instead.
Note
This function uses the ROSE type table infrastructure to deduplicate modifier types. Multiple calls with structurally equivalent base types will return the same SgModifierType pointer.
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface, which provides factory functions for constructing ROSE AST nodes.

◆ buildConstVolatileModifier()

SgConstVolatileModifier * SageBuilder::buildConstVolatileModifier ( SgConstVolatileModifier::cv_modifier_enum mtype)

Builds a const/volatile type qualifier node for the AST.

This function constructs and returns a new SgConstVolatileModifier node, which represents a const, volatile, or combined const/volatile type qualifier in the ROSE Abstract Syntax Tree (AST). The function allocates a new SgConstVolatileModifier object on the heap, sets its modifier type to the specified value, and returns a pointer to the newly created node. If no modifier type is provided, the default value SgConstVolatileModifier::e_unknown is used, indicating an unspecified qualifier.

The function uses a runtime assertion to verify that memory allocation was successful before proceeding to set the modifier type.

Parameters
mtypeThe const/volatile modifier enumeration value to assign to the new node. Valid values are members of the SgConstVolatileModifier::cv_modifier_enum enumeration, such as e_unknown, e_const, e_volatile, or e_const_volatile. Defaults to SgConstVolatileModifier::e_unknown if not specified.
Returns
A pointer to the newly allocated and initialized SgConstVolatileModifier node. The caller is responsible for managing the lifetime of the returned object.
Warning
The returned pointer refers to heap-allocated memory. The caller must ensure that the returned object is properly inserted into the AST or otherwise managed to avoid memory leaks.
Precondition
Sufficient heap memory must be available for the allocation of a new SgConstVolatileModifier object.
Postcondition
The returned SgConstVolatileModifier node is non-null and has its modifier type set to the value specified by mtype.
Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface, which provides factory functions for constructing ROSE AST nodes. The default parameter value SgConstVolatileModifier::e_unknown can be used when the specific qualifier type is not yet known or will be set later.

◆ buildConstVolatileType()

SgModifierType * SageBuilder::buildConstVolatileType ( SgType * base_type)

Builds a const volatile modifier type wrapping a given base type.

This function constructs a new SgModifierType node that applies both the const and volatile qualifiers to the provided base type. The resulting modifier type is inserted into the global type table via SgModifierType::insertModifierTypeIntoTypeTable(). If an equivalent const volatile modifier type already exists in the type table, the pre-existing type is returned and the newly allocated SgModifierType is deleted to avoid duplication in the memory pool. This deduplication strategy ensures that identical types share a single representation within the ROSE IR, which is important for type comparison and consistency across the abstract syntax tree.

The function sets both the const qualifier and the volatile qualifier on the type modifier of the newly created SgModifierType before attempting insertion into the type table.

Parameters
base_typePointer to the SgType that serves as the underlying type to be wrapped with const and volatile qualifiers. Must not be NULL.
Returns
A pointer to an SgModifierType representing the const volatile qualified version of base_type. This may be a newly created node or an existing node retrieved from the type table if an equivalent type was already registered.
Warning
The returned pointer may differ from the internally allocated SgModifierType if a matching type already exists in the type table. Callers must not assume the returned pointer is the same object that was initially allocated during the call.
A diagnostic printf statement is currently active in this function (guarded by a preprocessor if 1 block), which will produce output to stdout during every invocation. This may affect performance or log verbosity in production builds.
Precondition
base_type must not be NULL. An assertion will trigger at runtime if a NULL pointer is passed.
Postcondition
The returned SgModifierType has both its const and volatile qualifiers set.
The returned SgModifierType is registered in the global ROSE type table, ensuring uniqueness of the const volatile qualified type for the given base_type.
If a duplicate type was found in the type table, the intermediate SgModifierType allocated during this call is deleted and the canonical type from the table is returned instead.
Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface for constructing ROSE IR nodes. It follows the standard ROSE pattern of deduplicating types through the type table to maintain a canonical representation of each unique type within the AST.

This marks the node as compiler-generated or transformation-introduced rather than originating from user source code. The resulting node can be inserted into an AST to represent a continue statement within a loop construct.

The returned SgContinueStmt pointer is non-null.

Warning

Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface, which provides factory functions for constructing ROSE AST nodes. The source position assigned by setOneSourcePositionForTransformation distinguishes this node from nodes parsed directly from source code.

◆ buildCpreprocessorDefineDeclaration()

PreprocessingInfo * SageBuilder::buildCpreprocessorDefineDeclaration ( SgLocatedNode * target,
const std::string & content,
PreprocessingInfo::RelativePositionType position )

Builds and attaches a C preprocessor define declaration as a PreprocessingInfo node to a target AST node.

This function creates a new PreprocessingInfo object representing a C preprocessor define directive (e.g., #define xxx yyy) and attaches it to the specified target located node in the ROSE Abstract Syntax Tree (AST). The directive is marked as transformation-generated, meaning it was not present in the original source file but was introduced programmatically during a source-to-source transformation.

The function performs basic validation to ensure the provided content string begins with the #define prefix after trimming leading and trailing whitespace. The resulting PreprocessingInfo node is attached to the target node at the specified relative position (before or after the node by default).

The created PreprocessingInfo object uses the directive type PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorDefineDeclaration and records the source location as "transformation-generated" with line, column, and file index values set to zero, indicating a synthetic (non-file-based) origin.

Parameters
targetA pointer to the SgLocatedNode to which the define directive will be attached. Must not be NULL, as dangling define directives are not permitted in the ROSE AST.
contentA string containing the full text of the define directive, including the #define prefix. Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed before validation. The string must begin with #define after trimming.
positionThe relative position at which the directive is attached to the target node. Defaults to PreprocessingInfo::before, meaning the directive appears before the target node in the output source.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created and attached PreprocessingInfo object representing the define directive. The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-NULL upon successful completion.
Precondition
target must not be NULL.
content, after trimming whitespace, must begin with the string #define.
Postcondition
A new PreprocessingInfo node of type CpreprocessorDefineDeclaration is created and attached to the target node's preprocessing info list at the specified position.
The returned PreprocessingInfo pointer is non-NULL.
Warning
Passing a NULL target pointer will trigger a failed assertion and abort execution.
Passing a content string that does not begin with #define (after trimming) will trigger a failed assertion and abort execution.
The caller should not attempt to manage the lifetime of the returned PreprocessingInfo object directly, as it is owned by the AST node to which it is attached.
Note
The PreprocessingInfo object is tagged as transformation-generated, with source file, line, and column information set to zero, distinguishing it from directives parsed from actual source files.
This function uses the Boost string algorithm trim to remove leading and trailing whitespace from the content string before validation.

The function allocates the node on the heap, asserts successful allocation, and initializes its defining declaration pointer to NULL while setting its first non-defining declaration pointer to itself. Source position is then nullified via setOneSourcePositionNull.

This builder follows the ROSE SageBuilder pattern for constructing AST nodes independently of any particular source file context, which is useful when programmatically generating or transforming code without a corresponding source location.

Returns

The returned pointer must not be used after the enclosing AST or memory management context has been destroyed. Failing to attach the returned node to a valid AST may result in memory leaks or dangling pointers.
Precondition

Postcondition

The "nfi" suffix in the function name stands for "no file info," indicating that this builder intentionally omits source file location data. ◆ buildCudaKernelCallExp_nfi()

SgCudaKernelCallExp * SageBuilder::buildCudaKernelCallExp_nfi ( SgExpression * kernel,
SgExprListExp * parameters,
SgCudaKernelExecConfig * config )

Builds a CUDA kernel call expression of the form kernel<<<config>>>(parameters).

This function constructs a new SgCudaKernelCallExp AST node representing a CUDA kernel launch expression. The kernel launch syntax in CUDA extends standard C++ function call syntax with an execution configuration enclosed in triple angle brackets (e.g., myKernel<<<gridDim, blockDim>>>(arg1, arg2)).

The function performs several validation steps before constructing the node:

  1. It verifies that the kernel expression refers directly to a function via either an SgFunctionRefExp or an SgTemplateFunctionRefExp. If neither is found, a warning is emitted to standard error. Experimental support exists for non-real reference expressions (SgNonrealRefExp) encountered in RAJA/CUDA codes such as Lulesh; in such cases, construction proceeds rather than aborting.
  2. If a valid function or template function reference is found, the function checks that the referenced declaration carries the CUDA kernel modifier (i.e., the global attribute). If this check fails, an error message is printed and the program aborts.

After validation, the SgCudaKernelCallExp node is allocated and its child nodes (kernel expression, parameter list, and execution configuration) are linked by setting their parent pointers accordingly. Source position information is set to null via setOneSourcePositionNull.

Parameters
kernelA pointer to the SgExpression representing the kernel function being called. This is expected to be an SgFunctionRefExp or SgTemplateFunctionRefExp pointing to a function declared with the global CUDA modifier. Must not be null.
parametersA pointer to the SgExprListExp containing the list of arguments to pass to the kernel function. Must not be null.
configA pointer to the SgCudaKernelExecConfig node representing the execution configuration (grid and block dimensions, shared memory, and stream) for the kernel launch. Must not be null.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgCudaKernelCallExp AST node representing the complete CUDA kernel call expression.
Warning
If the kernel expression is neither an SgFunctionRefExp nor an SgTemplateFunctionRefExp, a warning is printed to standard error but construction may still proceed (experimental behavior for certain RAJA/CUDA code patterns). If the referenced function does not have the global CUDA kernel modifier, the program will abort via ROSE_ABORT().
Precondition
kernel must be a non-null pointer to a valid SgExpression node.
parameters must be a non-null pointer to a valid SgExprListExp node.
config must be a non-null pointer to a valid SgCudaKernelExecConfig node.
The function referenced by kernel should be declared with the global CUDA modifier for the construction to succeed without aborting.
Postcondition
The returned SgCudaKernelCallExp node has its parent pointers for kernel, parameters, and config set to itself.
The source position of the returned node is set to null.
The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-null (asserted internally).
Note
This function uses the "no file info" (nfi) convention, meaning the resulting AST node does not carry source file location information.
Template function references (SgTemplateFunctionRefExp) are supported in addition to plain function references (SgFunctionRefExp) to handle templated CUDA kernel calls.
The type of the resulting SgCudaKernelCallExp is taken from the kernel expression's own type via kernel->get_type().

SgCudaKernelExecConfig * SageBuilder::buildCudaKernelExecConfig_nfi ( SgExpression * grid,

Builds a CUDA kernel execution configuration node representing the triple-angle-bracket syntax (<<<grid, blocks, shared, stream>>>).

This function constructs an SgCudaKernelExecConfig AST node that encapsulates the four configuration parameters used when launching a CUDA kernel. The resulting node represents the execution configuration that appears between the triple angle brackets in a CUDA kernel call expression.

The function requires that both the grid and blocks expressions are non-null, as these are mandatory fields for any valid CUDA kernel launch configuration. If either is missing, an error message is printed to standard error and the program is aborted via ROSE_ABORT(). The shared memory and stream parameters are optional and may be null pointers.

After allocating the configuration node, the function sets the parent pointer of each non-null child expression to the newly created configuration node, ensuring proper parent-child relationships within the AST. Source position information is initialized to null via setOneSourcePositionNull().

Note: Type checking for the provided expressions is not yet implemented (marked as a TODO in the implementation).

Parameters
gridPointer to an SgExpression representing the grid dimension of the CUDA kernel launch. Must not be null.
blocksPointer to an SgExpression representing the block dimension of the CUDA kernel launch. Must not be null.
sharedPointer to an SgExpression representing the amount of shared memory to allocate per block. May be null if not specified.
streamPointer to an SgExpression representing the CUDA stream on which the kernel will execute. May be null if not specified.
Returns
A pointer to a newly allocated SgCudaKernelExecConfig node representing the complete CUDA kernel execution configuration. The caller is responsible for managing the lifetime of this node within the AST.
Warning
If either grid or blocks is a null pointer, the function prints an error message to standard error and calls ROSE_ABORT(), terminating the program. Ensure both are valid non-null expressions before calling this function.
Precondition
grid must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgExpression node.
blocks must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgExpression node.
shared, if non-null, must be a valid pointer to an SgExpression node.
stream, if non-null, must be a valid pointer to an SgExpression node.
Postcondition
The returned SgCudaKernelExecConfig node is fully initialized with all provided expressions set as children.
The parent pointer of each non-null expression argument is set to the returned configuration node.
The source position of the returned node is set to null via setOneSourcePositionNull().
Note
The suffix _nfi indicates this is a "no file info" variant, meaning source position information is not derived from a source file location but is instead set to null.
Type validation of the provided expressions is not currently performed and is listed as a pending TODO in the implementation.

SgDeclarationScope * SageBuilder::buildDeclarationScope ( )

Builds and returns a new SgDeclarationScope node for use in constructing SgNonrealDecl and SgNonrealType entities.

This function allocates a new SgDeclarationScope object on the heap and initializes its source position information using SageInterface::setSourcePosition. Both the start and end of the construct are marked as compiler-generated, indicating that this scope statement does not correspond to any user-written source code. The resulting node is intended to serve as a scope container when building nonreal declarations (SgNonrealDecl) and nonreal types (SgNonrealType), which are used internally by ROSE to represent template parameters and other abstract type constructs that do not map directly to concrete source-level declarations.

Returns

The caller is responsible for managing the lifetime of the returned SgDeclarationScope pointer. Failing to attach the returned node to the AST or to properly manage its memory may result in memory leaks or dangling pointers.
Precondition
The ROSE AST infrastructure must be properly initialized before calling this function, as it relies on SageInterface::setSourcePosition to set valid source position data on the new node.
Postcondition
A new SgDeclarationScope object is allocated on the heap with its source position initialized and both its start and end of construct nodes marked as compiler-generated.
Note
This function is typically used internally by the SageBuilder library when constructing nonreal declarations and types. It is not generally intended for direct use in typical AST-building workflows unless working with template-related or abstract type constructs.

Builds and returns an SgDeclType node representing a decltype expression.

This function constructs an SgDeclType AST node, which corresponds to the C++11 decltype specifier. The construction path depends on the nature of the provided base expression. If the base expression is an SgFunctionParameterRefExp (a reference to a function parameter), the SgDeclType node is created directly via its constructor, and the supplied base type is explicitly set on the result. In all other cases, the type is created through the static factory method SgDeclType::createType, which handles the standard decltype construction logic internally.

After construction, the parent pointer of the base expression is set to the newly created SgDeclType node to maintain proper AST parent-child relationships.

base_typeA pointer to the SgType that serves as the explicit base type when the base expression is an SgFunctionParameterRefExp. May be unused if the base expression is not of that kind.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgDeclType node. This pointer is guaranteed to be non-NULL upon successful return.
Precondition
base_expression must not be NULL; an assertion will fire if it is.
Postcondition
The returned SgDeclType pointer is non-NULL.
The parent of base_expression is set to the returned SgDeclType node.
If base_expression is an SgFunctionParameterRefExp, the base type of the result is set to base_type.
Warning
Passing a NULL base_expression will trigger a failed ROSE_ASSERT and terminate the program.
Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface, which provides factory functions for constructing ROSE AST nodes. The special handling for SgFunctionParameterRefExp is required because the standard createType path may not correctly handle function parameter references in all contexts.

◆ buildDefaultConstructor()

SgMemberFunctionDeclaration * SageBuilder::buildDefaultConstructor ( SgClassType * classType)

Builds a default constructor declaration for a given class type.

This function constructs both a non-defining and a defining member function declaration representing a default constructor for the class identified by the provided SgClassType. The resulting constructor has no parameters, uses void as its internal return type (as is conventional in ROSE's AST representation of constructors), and is marked with the constructor special function modifier and public access.

The implementation proceeds in the following steps:

  1. Resolves the SgClassDeclaration and its defining declaration from the provided SgClassType, then retrieves the associated SgClassDefinition.
  2. Builds an empty SgFunctionParameterList (no parameters, since this is a default constructor).
  3. Builds a void return type, which is used internally for constructors even though it is not emitted in generated source.
  4. Calls buildNondefiningMemberFunctionDeclaration to create the forward declaration (prototype) of the constructor, then marks it as a constructor and ensures its firstNondefiningDeclaration pointer is self-referential.
  5. Calls buildDefiningMemberFunctionDeclaration to create the defining declaration of the constructor, linking it to the non-defining declaration.
  6. Marks the defining declaration as a constructor and sets its access modifier to public.

The caller is responsible for inserting the returned declaration into the appropriate class definition or scope. This function does not automatically insert the constructor into the class definition.

Parameters
classTypeA pointer to the SgClassType representing the class for which the default constructor is to be built. Must not be null and must have an associated defining class declaration with a valid class definition.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created defining SgMemberFunctionDeclaration representing the default constructor. The returned declaration is marked as a constructor and has public access. It is not yet inserted into any class definition.
Warning
The returned constructor declaration is not automatically inserted into the class definition. The caller must explicitly insert it into the appropriate SgClassDefinition if it is to appear in the AST.
Internally, constructors use void as their return type in the ROSE AST. This void return type is not emitted during code generation but is required for correct internal representation.
Precondition
classType must not be null.
classType must have a valid associated SgClassDeclaration obtainable via get_declaration().
The SgClassDeclaration associated with classType must have a defining declaration with a non-null SgClassDefinition.
Postcondition
The returned SgMemberFunctionDeclaration has its special function modifier set to constructor (isConstructor() returns true).
The returned SgMemberFunctionDeclaration has its access modifier set to public (isPublic() returns true).
The firstNondefiningDeclaration of the non-defining declaration is self-referential.
The defining declaration is linked to the non-defining declaration via the firstNondefiningDeclaration pointer.
Note
The const-volatile flags and template instantiation flag are both set to zero or false, as these do not apply to a default constructor built in this context.
The decorator list is set to null and the template arguments list is empty, reflecting that this builds a plain, non-templated default constructor.

Builds an SgDefaultOptionStmt AST node representing a default option statement.

This function constructs a new SgDefaultOptionStmt node, which is used in the ROSE abstract syntax tree (AST) to represent a default option statement, such as the default case in a SELECT CASE construct in Fortran or similar language constructs.

The function allocates a new SgDefaultOptionStmt object with the provided body statement, asserts that allocation was successful, and then sets a single source position on the node to indicate it was introduced by a transformation rather than parsed from source code. If a body statement is provided, its parent pointer is updated to point to the newly created SgDefaultOptionStmt node, maintaining proper parent-child relationships within the AST.

Source position information is set via setOneSourcePositionForTransformation, marking the node as a compiler-generated or transformation-introduced construct.

bodyA pointer to the SgStatement that serves as the body of the default option statement. May be a null pointer, in which case no parent assignment is performed.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgDefaultOptionStmt node with source position information set and parent linkage established for the body, if provided.
Precondition
If body is non-null, it must be a valid, fully constructed SgStatement node.
Postcondition
The returned SgDefaultOptionStmt node has its source position set to indicate a transformation-introduced construct.
If body is non-null, body->get_parent() returns the newly created SgDefaultOptionStmt node.
Warning
The caller is responsible for managing the lifetime of the returned SgDefaultOptionStmt node and integrating it into the AST appropriately. Failure to insert the node into the AST may result in memory leaks or dangling pointers.
Note
This function uses ROSE_ASSERT to verify that the allocation of the new SgDefaultOptionStmt node succeeded. If memory allocation fails, the assertion will terminate the program.
The function contains disabled debug output (guarded by if 0 / endif) that was used during development to trace the body pointer value.

This function constructs a new SgDefaultOptionStmt node, which represents a default option statement (such as the "default" case in a SELECT or switch-like construct) in the ROSE abstract syntax tree (AST). The "nfi" suffix indicates that this is the "no file information" variant, meaning the source position of the resulting node is explicitly set to null rather than being derived from actual source location data.

The function allocates a new SgDefaultOptionStmt object with the provided body statement, asserts that allocation succeeded, sets the source position to null via setOneSourcePositionNull, and, if a body statement is provided, sets the parent pointer of the body to point to the newly created node. This ensures proper parent-child linkage within the AST.

bodyA pointer to the SgStatement that serves as the body of the default option statement. May be null, in which case no parent linkage is established. If non-null, its parent pointer will be updated to reference the newly created SgDefaultOptionStmt node.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgDefaultOptionStmt node. This pointer is guaranteed to be non-null, as an assertion is performed immediately after allocation.

If body is non-null, it must be a valid, heap-allocated SgStatement object whose ownership can be transferred to the resulting SgDefaultOptionStmt node.

◆ buildDefiningClassDeclaration()

SgClassDeclaration * SageBuilder::buildDefiningClassDeclaration ( SgName name,

Builds a defining class declaration node in the ROSE AST.

This function constructs a defining SgClassDeclaration along with its associated SgClassDefinition, linking them together with a previously created non-defining class declaration. The function first builds a non-defining class declaration via buildNondefiningClassDeclaration(), then constructs a class definition via buildClassDefinition(), and finally creates the defining SgClassDeclaration node of kind e_class. The resulting nodes are cross-linked so that the defining and non-defining declarations reference each other correctly, and the class definition is attached to the defining declaration.

The semantics of this function differ from those of buildDefiningFunctionDeclaration(). In particular, this function internally creates the non-defining declaration as part of its operation, whereas the function declaration counterpart expects the non-defining declaration to already exist before being called. This behavioral difference is noted by a runtime warning printed to standard output.

Note that this function currently calls ROSE_ABORT() unconditionally after printing diagnostic information, meaning it is not intended for production use in its current state. It exists as a placeholder or work-in-progress implementation.

The input name must not contain template argument syntax (e.g., names of the form "X<Y>" are not permitted). This is enforced via a runtime assertion using SageInterface::hasTemplateSyntax().

Source position information is set on the defining declaration using setOneSourcePositionForTransformation(), marking it as a transformation node.

Parameters
nameThe name of the class to be declared. Must not contain template argument syntax (i.e., angle-bracket template parameters).
scopeThe scope in which the class declaration will be placed. May be NULL, in which case the scope is not set on the resulting declaration. If non-NULL, the scope is assigned to the defining declaration.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed defining SgClassDeclaration node, with its associated class definition and non-defining declaration properly linked. Returns a valid non-NULL pointer on success.
Warning
This function unconditionally calls ROSE_ABORT() in its current implementation and will terminate the program at runtime. It is not suitable for use in production code without modification.
The semantics of this function differ from buildDefiningFunctionDeclaration(). A runtime warning message is printed to standard output to alert callers of this difference.
The input name must not contain template syntax. Passing a name such as "X<Y>" will trigger a failed assertion and abort the program.
Precondition
The parameter name must not contain template argument syntax as determined by SageInterface::hasTemplateSyntax(name) returning false.
If scope is non-NULL, it must point to a valid SgScopeStatement node.
Postcondition
The returned defining SgClassDeclaration has a non-NULL class definition attached via get_definition().
The returned defining declaration and the internally created non-defining declaration are cross-linked: each references the other via get_definingDeclaration() and get_firstNondefiningDeclaration().
The class definition's parent pointer is non-NULL.
The defining declaration's type is non-NULL and matches the type of the non-defining declaration.
If scope is non-NULL, the defining declaration's scope is set to the provided scope.
Note
This function is considered deprecated in its current form. Future development may provide a replacement that separates the construction of non-defining and defining declarations, or a higher-level function that builds both together.
The class kind is hardcoded to SgClassDeclaration::e_class regardless of the intended class type (struct, union, etc.).

Builds a defining function declaration node in the ROSE AST.

For non-template functions, the template argument list is passed as NULL.

The function asserts that first_nondefining_declaration is non-null in both branches. When building a template instantiation, it further asserts that the resulting node is a valid SgTemplateInstantiationFunctionDecl with a non-null template name. For the non-template case, it asserts that the resulting node is a valid SgFunctionDeclaration.

Warning
If buildTemplateInstantiation is true, first_nondefining_declaration must be an SgTemplateInstantiationFunctionDecl; passing an incompatible type will cause assertion failures or undefined behavior.

Precondition
first_nondefining_declaration must not be NULL.
If buildTemplateInstantiation is true, first_nondefining_declaration must point to a valid SgTemplateInstantiationFunctionDecl node with a non-null template name.
return_type must point to a valid SgType node.

Builds a defining function declaration node in the ROSE AST.

This function constructs a defining function declaration (i.e., a function definition that includes a body) for use in the ROSE Abstract Syntax Tree (AST). A defining declaration differs from a non-defining declaration in that it provides the actual implementation body of the function.

Internally, the function first resolves the target scope: if the provided scope is NULL, the top of the current scope stack is used instead. It then constructs a function type from the given return type and parameter list, and searches the scope for an existing function symbol matching the name and type. If a matching symbol is found, its associated non-defining declaration is reused; otherwise, a new non-defining declaration is built via buildNondefiningFunctionDeclaration().

Once a valid non-defining declaration is established, the function delegates to the overloaded buildDefiningFunctionDeclaration() variant that accepts additional arguments including the non-defining declaration pointer, ensuring proper linkage between the defining and non-defining declarations in the AST.

Note that this function is not used in the AST construction within the EDG/ROSE interface itself. It is intended as a public API for programmatic AST construction.

scopeA pointer to the SgScopeStatement representing the scope in which the function declaration is to be placed. If NULL, the top of the current scope stack is used.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgFunctionDeclaration node representing the defining declaration. The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-NULL and properly linked to its corresponding non-defining declaration.
Warning
Passing a NULL value for return_type or parameter_list will trigger an assertion failure and abort execution. Callers must ensure these arguments are valid before invoking this function.
Precondition
return_type must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid SgType node.
parameter_list must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid SgFunctionParameterList node.
If scope is non-NULL, it must point to a valid SgScopeStatement within the AST.
If scope is NULL, the scope stack must be non-empty so that topScopeStack() returns a valid scope.
Postcondition
The returned SgFunctionDeclaration is a defining declaration linked to a non-defining declaration, with get_firstNondefiningDeclaration() returning a non-NULL value equal to the non-defining declaration.
If no prior function symbol existed in the scope, a new non-defining declaration is inserted into the scope before the defining declaration is created.
Note
This function does not directly participate in AST construction during the EDG/ROSE frontend translation phase. It is intended for use in back-end or programmatic AST manipulation contexts.
The overloaded variant of buildDefiningFunctionDeclaration() that accepts additional parameters (including the non-defining declaration) is ultimately responsible for the actual node construction.

◆ buildDefiningFunctionDeclaration_T()

actualFunction * SageBuilder::buildDefiningFunctionDeclaration_T ( const SgName & XXX_name,
SgType * return_type,
SgFunctionParameterList * paralist,
bool isMemberFunction,
SgScopeStatement * scope,
SgExprListExp * decoratorList,
unsigned int functionConstVolatileFlags,
