SgTemplateArgumentPtrList * templateArgumentsList )

Builds a defining function declaration node of the templated type actualFunction within the ROSE AST.

This function is a template-based builder for defining function declarations in the ROSE intermediate representation (IR). It is parameterized on actualFunction, which may be one of several concrete function declaration types such as SgFunctionDeclaration, SgMemberFunctionDeclaration, SgTemplateFunctionDeclaration, SgTemplateMemberFunctionDeclaration, SgTemplateInstantiationFunctionDecl, or SgTemplateInstantiationMemberFunctionDecl.

The semantics of this function differ from those of the defining class declaration builder. In particular, this function requires that a non-defining declaration already exist before it is called. The non-defining declaration is passed explicitly via the first_nondefining_declaration parameter. The function reuses the function type from the non-defining declaration rather than constructing a new one, which is essential for correctness when handling templates, where independently constructed types may differ in their levels of instantiation.

The function performs the following major steps:

  1. Validates all input parameters and resolves the scope if none is provided.
  2. For template instantiations, verifies that the provided template argument list matches that of the first non-defining declaration.
  3. For template declarations, retrieves the template parameter list from the first non-defining declaration.
  4. Optionally appends template arguments to the function name when building a template instantiation.
  5. Looks up the function symbol in the scope's symbol table using the resolved name and function type.
  6. Allocates a new actualFunction node and links it to the first non-defining declaration as the defining declaration.
  7. Constructs an SgFunctionDefinition (or SgTemplateFunctionDefinition for template declarations) along with an empty SgBasicBlock as the function body.
  8. Attaches the parameter list and inserts variable symbols for each parameter into the function definition's scope, including special handling for variable-length array (VLA) parameter types.
  9. Sets parent and scope pointers, source position information, and marks the result as a transformation.
  10. Applies template arguments or template parameters to the defining declaration as appropriate.
  11. Handles the restrict qualifier from functionConstVolatileFlags if applicable.
  12. Clears modification flags on the resulting subtree before returning.

For Python-specific support, a decorator list may be attached to the defining declaration.

Under the ifdef ROSE_DEBUG_NEW_EDG_ROSE_CONNECTION, a warning message is printed to standard output noting the semantic difference between this builder and the defining class declaration builder.

Parameters
XXX_nameThe name of the function being declared. Must not be null. For template instantiations, template argument syntax will be appended to produce the full instantiated name.
return_typeThe return type of the function. Must not be null.
paralistThe parameter list for the function. Must not be null. Each parameter's scope and associated variable symbol will be set within the newly created function definition.
isMemberFunctionA boolean flag indicating whether the function being built is a member function. If true, the resulting declaration is asserted to be an SgMemberFunctionDeclaration.
scopeThe enclosing scope in which the defining declaration is placed. If null, the top of the scope stack is used via SageBuilder::topScopeStack().
decoratorListAn optional list of decorator expressions (used in Python). If non-null, it is attached to the defining declaration and its parent pointer is set accordingly.
functionConstVolatileFlagsA bitmask of flags encoding const/volatile/restrict qualifiers for the function type. If the e_restrict bit is set, the restrict modifier is applied to the defining declaration.
first_nondefining_declarationA pointer to the already-existing first non-defining declaration for this function. Must not be null and must satisfy the invariant that its get_firstNondefiningDeclaration() returns itself. The function type is reused from this node.
templateArgumentsListA pointer to the list of template arguments. Required and must not be null when building a template instantiation. Must be null when building a template declaration. For instantiations, the list must be equivalent to the template argument list of first_nondefining_declaration.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed defining function declaration of type actualFunction*. The returned node has its function definition, body, parameter list, scope, parent, and symbol table entries fully initialized.
Warning
This function aborts (via ROSE_ABORT()) if the function symbol cannot be found in the scope's symbol table. This indicates that the required non-defining declaration was not properly registered before calling this function.
The semantics of this function differ from those of the defining class declaration builder. A non-defining declaration must already exist before this function is called. Calling this function without a pre-existing non-defining declaration is an error.
For template instantiations, the template argument list passed via templateArgumentsList must be equivalent to the one stored in first_nondefining_declaration. A mismatch will trigger an assertion failure.
Precondition
first_nondefining_declaration must not be null.
first_nondefining_declaration->get_firstNondefiningDeclaration() must equal first_nondefining_declaration itself.
XXX_name must not be a null SgName.
return_type must not be null.
paralist must not be null.
If scope is non-null, it must be a valid SgScopeStatement. If null, the scope stack must be non-empty so that SageBuilder::topScopeStack() returns a valid scope.
If the language does not allow non-declarations in scope (as determined by SageInterface::language_may_contain_nondeclarations_in_scope()), the scope must contain only declarations.
When building a template instantiation, templateArgumentsList must not be null and must match the template arguments of first_nondefining_declaration.
When building a template declaration, templateArgumentsList must be null.
The function symbol corresponding to the name and type must already be present in the symbol table of the resolved scope.
Postcondition
The returned actualFunction* node is fully constructed with a valid SgFunctionDefinition and an empty SgBasicBlock as its body.
The firstNondefiningDeclaration of the returned node is set to the first non-defining declaration found via the symbol table lookup.
The definingDeclaration of both the returned node and first_nondefining_declaration is set to the returned defining declaration.
Variable symbols for all named parameters in paralist are inserted into the function definition's symbol table.
Source position information for the returned node and all its children is set as transformation-generated.
No nodes in the returned subtree are marked as modified (modification flags are cleared).
If isMemberFunction is true, the returned node is a valid SgMemberFunctionDeclaration.
If building a template instantiation, template arguments are set on the defining declaration.
If building a template declaration, template parameters are set on the defining declaration.
Note
This function is intended to be called only after the corresponding non-defining declaration has been constructed and its symbol registered in the target scope. A higher-level builder function may be used to construct both the non-defining and defining declarations together.
The function type is deliberately reused from first_nondefining_declaration rather than constructed anew. This ensures type identity between the defining and non-defining declarations, which is critical for correct symbol table lookups, especially in the presence of templates.
VLA (variable-length array) parameter types receive special handling: variable reference expressions in their index expressions are resolved against the function definition's symbol table, and their symbols are updated accordingly.
For case-insensitive languages (e.g., Fortran), the function definition and body are marked as case-insensitive via setCaseInsensitive(true).

A defining declaration is the declaration that includes the function body, as opposed to a non-defining (forward) declaration.

When the parameter buildTemplateInstantiation is true, the function expects first_nondefining_declaration to be a SgTemplateInstantiationMemberFunctionDecl. It then constructs the template name with appended template arguments by calling appendTemplateArgumentsToName(), performs a symbol lookup in the given scope via find_symbol_by_type_of_function, and delegates to the templated helper buildDefiningFunctionDeclaration_T instantiated with SgTemplateInstantiationMemberFunctionDecl. If the symbol lookup fails, diagnostic error messages are printed to standard output before proceeding.

When buildTemplateInstantiation is false, the function verifies that first_nondefining_declaration is non-null and that its first non-defining declaration pointer is properly self-referential, then delegates to buildDefiningFunctionDeclaration_T instantiated with SgMemberFunctionDeclaration, passing a NULL template arguments list.

After the defining declaration is built, the function retrieves the associated SgCtorInitializerList and sets both its defining declaration and first non-defining declaration pointers to itself, satisfying AST consistency requirements checked by AstConsistencyTests. Finally, it verifies that the associated class declaration is non-null before returning.

Parameters
nameThe name of the member function to be declared.
return_typeA pointer to the SgType representing the return type of the member function.
paralistA pointer to the SgFunctionParameterList describing the formal parameters of the member function.
scopeA pointer to the SgScopeStatement representing the enclosing scope (typically a class definition) in which the member function is declared.
decoratorListA pointer to an SgExprListExp holding any decorator expressions associated with the member function declaration. May be NULL if no decorators are present.
buildTemplateInstantiationA boolean flag indicating whether to build a SgTemplateInstantiationMemberFunctionDecl (true) rather than a plain SgMemberFunctionDeclaration (false).
functionConstVolatileFlagsAn unsigned integer encoding the const and volatile qualifiers of the member function (e.g., whether the function is const-qualified).
first_nondefining_declarationA pointer to the first non-defining (forward) declaration of this member function. Must be non-null. When buildTemplateInstantiation is true, this must be a valid SgTemplateInstantiationMemberFunctionDecl.
templateArgumentsListA pointer to an SgTemplateArgumentPtrList supplying the template arguments when building a template instantiation. Must be non-null when buildTemplateInstantiation is true. Passed as NULL when buildTemplateInstantiation is false.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgMemberFunctionDeclaration (or SgTemplateInstantiationMemberFunctionDecl) defining declaration node. The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-null.
Warning
If buildTemplateInstantiation is true and the symbol lookup for the template instantiation member function fails (returns NULL), error diagnostic messages are printed to standard output. The function continues execution in this case, which may lead to an inconsistent AST state.
This function uses ROSE_ASSERT for internal consistency checks. Violations of preconditions will cause assertion failures at runtime in debug builds.
Precondition
name must represent a valid, non-empty function name.
return_type must be a non-null pointer to a valid SgType node.
paralist must be a non-null pointer to a valid SgFunctionParameterList node.
scope must be a non-null pointer to a valid SgScopeStatement node.
first_nondefining_declaration must be non-null and must be the first non-defining declaration of the member function (i.e., first_nondefining_declaration->get_firstNondefiningDeclaration() == first_nondefining_declaration).
When buildTemplateInstantiation is true, first_nondefining_declaration must be a valid SgTemplateInstantiationMemberFunctionDecl and templateArgumentsList must be non-null.
The scope must contain a valid associated class declaration accessible via the resulting declaration's get_associatedClassDeclaration().
Postcondition
The returned SgMemberFunctionDeclaration is a defining declaration with a non-null function body.
The SgCtorInitializerList of the result has its definingDeclaration and firstNondefiningDeclaration pointers set to itself.
When buildTemplateInstantiation is true, the result is a valid SgTemplateInstantiationMemberFunctionDecl with a non-null, non-empty template name.
result->get_associatedClassDeclaration() is non-null.
Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface for programmatically constructing ROSE AST nodes. It internally delegates to the templated helper buildDefiningFunctionDeclaration_T with the appropriate template parameter.
The isMemberFunction flag is always passed as true to the underlying helper, reflecting that this builder is exclusively for member function declarations.
The SgCtorInitializerList self-referential setup is required to satisfy the AST consistency tests enforced by AstConsistencyTests checking for properly set defining and non-defining declarations.

◆ buildDefiningTemplateFunctionDeclaration()

SgTemplateFunctionDeclaration * SageBuilder::buildDefiningTemplateFunctionDeclaration ( const SgName & name,
SgType * return_type,
SgFunctionParameterList * paralist,
SgScopeStatement * scope,
SgExprListExp * decoratorList,
SgTemplateFunctionDeclaration * first_nondefining_declaration )

Builds a defining template function declaration node in the ROSE AST.

This function constructs a defining SgTemplateFunctionDeclaration node, which represents the definition (i.e., the body-containing declaration) of a C++ template function within the ROSE intermediate representation (IR). It delegates the actual construction to the internal template helper function buildDefiningFunctionDeclaration_T<SgTemplateFunctionDeclaration>, passing the provided name, return type, parameter list, scope, decorator list, and the associated first non-defining declaration.

The function enforces that the provided first_nondefining_declaration is non-null, that it has a valid first non-defining declaration pointer, and that it is itself the first non-defining declaration (i.e., it is not a subsequent redeclaration). These invariants are checked via assertions before construction proceeds.

The constructed node is linked to the given first_nondefining_declaration, allowing the ROSE AST to properly represent the relationship between the non-defining and defining declarations of the same template function.

Parameters
nameThe name of the template function to be declared.
return_typePointer to the SgType node representing the return type of the template function.
paralistPointer to the SgFunctionParameterList node representing the parameter list of the template function.
scopePointer to the SgScopeStatement representing the scope in which the template function declaration is to be placed.
decoratorListPointer to an SgExprListExp representing any decorator expressions associated with the template function. May be NULL if no decorators are present.
first_nondefining_declarationPointer to the existing first non-defining SgTemplateFunctionDeclaration that corresponds to this defining declaration. Must not be NULL, and must be its own first non-defining declaration.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed defining SgTemplateFunctionDeclaration node representing the template function definition in the ROSE AST.
Warning
This function will trigger assertion failures and abort if first_nondefining_declaration is NULL, if its internal first non-defining declaration pointer is NULL, or if it is not equal to itself as the first non-defining declaration. Callers must ensure these preconditions are satisfied before invoking this function.
Precondition
first_nondefining_declaration must not be NULL.
first_nondefining_declaration->get_firstNondefiningDeclaration() must not be NULL.
first_nondefining_declaration->get_firstNondefiningDeclaration() must equal first_nondefining_declaration (i.e., it must be the canonical first non-defining declaration, not a subsequent one).
return_type should be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an SgType node.
paralist should be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an SgFunctionParameterList node.
Postcondition
A new defining SgTemplateFunctionDeclaration node is created and associated with the provided first_nondefining_declaration.
The returned node represents the defining declaration of the template function within the ROSE AST.
Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface for programmatically constructing ROSE AST nodes. It specifically handles the non-member template function case (the isMemberFunction flag is set to false internally).
Support for template declarations in the AST was added in December 2011.
The const/volatile flags for the function are set to 0 (none) by default in this builder function.

◆ buildDefiningTemplateMemberFunctionDeclaration()

SgTemplateMemberFunctionDeclaration * SageBuilder::buildDefiningTemplateMemberFunctionDeclaration ( const SgName & name,
SgType * return_type,

Builds a defining template member function declaration node in the ROSE AST.

This function constructs a defining SgTemplateMemberFunctionDeclaration node, which represents a template member function that includes a function body (i.e., a defining declaration). It is intended to be used when constructing template member functions within a class or struct scope in the ROSE intermediate representation (IR).

Internally, the function delegates to the templated helper buildDefiningFunctionDeclaration_T<SgTemplateMemberFunctionDeclaration>, passing the provided arguments along with a flag indicating that the function is a member function. The resulting declaration is linked to the provided first_nondefining_declaration, which must itself be the first non-defining declaration (i.e., its own first non-defining declaration must point back to itself).

After construction, the function asserts that the resulting node is non-null and that it contains a valid function definition body (get_definition() != NULL).

Parameters
nameThe name of the template member function to be declared.
return_typeA pointer to the SgType node representing the return type of the template member function.
paralistA pointer to the SgFunctionParameterList node representing the parameter list of the template member function.
scopeA pointer to the SgScopeStatement representing the enclosing scope (typically a class or struct body) in which the declaration is placed.
decoratorListA pointer to an SgExprListExp node representing any decorator expressions associated with the function declaration. May be NULL if no decorators are present.
functionConstVolatileFlagsAn unsigned integer encoding the const and volatile qualifiers for the member function. Specific bit values correspond to const and volatile attributes.
first_nondefining_declarationA pointer to the existing SgTemplateMemberFunctionDeclaration that serves as the first non-defining declaration for this function. This must be a valid, non-null pointer whose own first non-defining declaration is itself.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed defining SgTemplateMemberFunctionDeclaration node, which is guaranteed to be non-null and to contain a valid function definition.
Warning
This function uses ROSE_ASSERT to enforce critical invariants. If first_nondefining_declaration is not its own first non-defining declaration, or if the resulting declaration or its definition is null, the program will abort at runtime.
Precondition
first_nondefining_declaration must be non-null.
first_nondefining_declaration->get_firstNondefiningDeclaration() must equal first_nondefining_declaration itself.
name, return_type, paralist, and scope must be valid and properly initialized before being passed to this function.
Postcondition
The returned SgTemplateMemberFunctionDeclaration pointer is non-null.
The returned declaration contains a non-null function definition (i.e., result->get_definition() != NULL).
Note
This function was introduced to support template declarations in the AST. It is part of the SageBuilder interface for programmatically constructing ROSE AST nodes representing C++ template member functions.

◆ buildDeleteExp() [1/2]

SgDeleteExp * SageBuilder::buildDeleteExp ( SgExpression * target,
bool is_array,
bool need_global_specifier,
SgFunctionDeclaration * deleteOperatorDeclaration )

Builds an SgDeleteExp AST node representing a C++ delete expression.

This function constructs a new SgDeleteExp node for use in the ROSE abstract syntax tree (AST). It represents a C++ delete or delete[] expression, which is used to deallocate memory previously allocated with new or new[].

The function allocates a new SgDeleteExp object using the provided target expression, array flag, global specifier flag, and an optional custom delete operator declaration. After construction, the target expression's parent pointer is updated to point to the newly created SgDeleteExp node. The source position of the resulting node is then set using setOneSourcePositionForTransformation, which marks it as a transformation node rather than one originating from user source code.

This builder is typically used when programmatically constructing or transforming AST nodes that correspond to memory deallocation operations in C++ programs.

Parameters
targetA pointer to the SgExpression representing the operand of the delete expression, i.e., the pointer to the memory to be freed. Must not be null. Its parent pointer will be set to the newly created SgDeleteExp node.
is_arrayA boolean flag indicating whether this is a delete[] (array delete) expression. Pass true for delete[] and false for scalar delete.
need_global_specifierA boolean flag indicating whether the global scope resolution operator (::) should be used before delete, as in ::delete. Pass true to use the global specifier, false otherwise.
deleteOperatorDeclarationA pointer to an SgFunctionDeclaration representing a custom operator delete function, if one is associated with this delete expression. May be null if no custom delete operator is specified.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgDeleteExp node with its parent and source position information properly initialized.
Precondition
target must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgExpression node.
deleteOperatorDeclaration may be null if no custom delete operator is needed; otherwise it must point to a valid SgFunctionDeclaration.
Postcondition
The returned SgDeleteExp node is fully initialized with the given parameters.
target->get_parent() returns the newly created SgDeleteExp node.
The source position of the returned node is set to a transformation position via setOneSourcePositionForTransformation.
Warning
The caller is responsible for inserting the returned SgDeleteExp node into the AST. Failure to do so may result in memory leaks or an inconsistent AST.
Passing a null pointer for target will result in undefined behavior or a crash when the parent pointer is set.
Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface, which provides factory functions for constructing ROSE AST nodes during source-to-source transformations.

The returned SgDerivedTypeStatement has a valid first non-defining declaration (i.e., get_firstNondefiningDeclaration() returns non-NULL).
Both the defining declaration and the first non-defining declaration have their source position set to a transformation source position.

The function uses ROSE_ASSERT to verify that the first non-defining declaration is not NULL. If this invariant is violated due to an internal error, the program will abort at runtime.

◆ buildDoWhileStatement_nfi()

void SageBuilder::buildDoWhileStatement_nfi ( SgDoWhileStmt * result,

Initializes an existing SgDoWhileStmt node with a body and condition for top-down AST construction.

This function is a "non-from-scratch" initializer (nfi) designed to populate an already-allocated SgDoWhileStmt node with its required child nodes: a loop body and a loop condition. It was introduced to support top-down AST construction scenarios where an SgDoWhileStmt node may be pre-allocated and pushed onto a construction stack before its children are known.

The need for this function arose from a behavioral change between EDG versions 4.7 and 4.8 in how block constructs and end-of-construct entries are handled. Rather than building the entire do-while statement in a single step, this function allows the statement to be finalized after the body and condition subtrees have been constructed.

The function sets the body and condition on the provided result node, establishes parent pointers for both child nodes, and sets a null source position on the result node. All pointer assignments are verified with assertions before and after modification to ensure structural integrity of the AST.

Parameters
resultA non-null pointer to an existing SgDoWhileStmt node that has not yet been assigned a body or condition. Both get_body() and get_condition() must return nullptr prior to calling this function.
bodyA non-null pointer to the SgStatement that will serve as the loop body. Its parent pointer will be set to result upon completion.
conditionA non-null pointer to the SgStatement that will serve as the loop condition. Its parent pointer will be set to result upon completion.
Precondition
result must not be null.
body must not be null.
condition must not be null.
result->get_body() must be nullptr (the node must not already have a body assigned).
result->get_condition() must be nullptr (the node must not already have a condition assigned).
Postcondition
result->get_body() is equal to body and is not null.
result->get_condition() is equal to condition and is not null.
body->get_parent() is equal to result.
condition->get_parent() is equal to result.
The source position of result is set to a null/invalid position via setOneSourcePositionNull.
Warning
This function must only be called on an SgDoWhileStmt node whose body and condition have not yet been set. Calling it on a node that already has a body or condition assigned will trigger assertion failures.
Note
This function is intended for use by the ROSE frontend infrastructure, particularly in conjunction with EDG 4.8 and later, where top-down AST construction requires pre-allocation of statement nodes. It is not intended for general use in user-level AST construction; prefer the standard buildDoWhileStatement builder functions in typical usage scenarios.

◆ buildDoWhileStmt()

SgDoWhileStmt * SageBuilder::buildDoWhileStmt ( SgStatement * body,

Builds a do-while statement node in the ROSE abstract syntax tree.

This function constructs and returns a new SgDoWhileStmt node representing a do-while loop. Two overloads are provided: one that accepts the condition as an SgStatement (typically an SgExprStatement wrapping a boolean expression), and a convenience inline overload that accepts the condition directly as an SgExpression, automatically wrapping it in an expression statement via buildExprStatement() before delegating to the primary overload.

The primary overload (marked ROSE_DLL_API) performs the actual construction of the SgDoWhileStmt node, setting the provided body and condition as child nodes and establishing the appropriate parent-child relationships within the AST.

The inline overload is a convenience wrapper that accepts an SgExpression for the condition parameter. It calls buildExprStatement() to convert the expression into a statement, then forwards both arguments to the primary overload.

Both the body and the condition must be valid, non-null SgStatement pointers before this function is called. Internal assertions enforce this requirement at runtime. After construction, the parent of both the body and the condition is set to the newly created SgDoWhileStmt node. A transformation source position is assigned to the resulting node to indicate that it was generated programmatically rather than parsed from source code.

Parameters
bodyThe statement representing the loop body. This is the block of code that will be executed at least once before the condition is evaluated. Must be a valid, non-null SgStatement pointer.
conditionThe condition controlling loop iteration. In the primary overload, this is an SgStatement (typically an SgExprStatement). In the inline overload, this is an SgExpression that is automatically wrapped in an expression statement. Must be a valid, non-null pointer.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgDoWhileStmt AST node representing the complete do-while loop construct.
Precondition
body must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgStatement node.
condition must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgStatement or SgExpression node (depending on the overload used).
The ROSE AST infrastructure must be properly initialized before calling this function.
Postcondition
A new SgDoWhileStmt node is created and returned with body and condition set as its children.
Parent pointers of the body and condition nodes are updated to reference the newly created SgDoWhileStmt node.
The returned node has a transformation source position assigned via setOneSourcePositionForTransformation.
Warning
Passing a null pointer for either body or condition will trigger a failed assertion and abort the program at runtime.
Passing null pointers for either body or condition results in undefined behavior.
The caller is responsible for inserting the returned SgDoWhileStmt node into the AST at the appropriate location; the node is not automatically attached to any existing tree.
Ownership of the body and condition nodes is transferred to the returned SgDoWhileStmt node. Avoid using or deleting these nodes independently after passing them to this function.
Note
The inline overload accepting SgExpression for the condition is provided as a convenience to avoid manually calling buildExprStatement() at the call site.
This function is part of the ROSE SageBuilder interface for programmatic AST construction. The constructed node is intended for use in transformation contexts and will carry a transformation marker rather than an original source location.

◆ buildEmptyDeclaration()

SgEmptyDeclaration * SageBuilder::buildEmptyDeclaration ( )

Builds and returns a new SgEmptyDeclaration node for use in the ROSE AST.

This function constructs an SgEmptyDeclaration AST node, which represents an empty declaration statement. Empty declarations are particularly useful when adding precision to comment placement and handling C preprocessor directives (such as define, ifdef, endif, and similar constructs) under token-based unparsing in the ROSE compiler framework.

The newly created node is initialized with a single source position suitable for transformed (synthesized) AST nodes via setOneSourcePositionForTransformation. Both the defining declaration and the first non-defining declaration pointers are set to point back to the node itself, establishing it as a self-referential declaration. The parent of the node is set to the current top of the scope stack, if one is available, so that the node is properly integrated into the surrounding scope context.

Returns
A pointer to the newly allocated and initialized SgEmptyDeclaration node. The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-null.
Precondition
The internal scope stack managed by SageBuilder must be in a valid state. If the scope stack is non-empty, its top element must be a valid, non-null SgScopeStatement pointer.
Postcondition
The returned SgEmptyDeclaration node has its defining declaration and first non-defining declaration pointers set to itself.
If the scope stack is non-empty at the time of the call, the returned node's parent pointer is set to the top scope on the stack and is guaranteed to be non-null.
The returned node has a valid source position set for transformation.
Warning
The caller is responsible for inserting the returned node into the AST at an appropriate location. Failing to do so may result in memory leaks or an inconsistent AST.
Note
This function uses an assertion (ROSE_ASSERT) to verify that the allocated SgEmptyDeclaration pointer is non-null immediately after allocation, and also to verify the parent pointer consistency when the scope stack is non-empty.
Class declarations and enum declarations are noted as exceptions that cannot always have their parent set, since they may be non-autonomous declarations. SgEmptyDeclaration does not share this limitation.

◆ buildEnumDeclaration_nfi()

SgEnumDeclaration * SageBuilder::buildEnumDeclaration_nfi ( const SgName & name,
SgScopeStatement * scope )

Builds a defining enum declaration node and its associated non-defining declaration in the ROSE AST.

This function constructs a new SgEnumDeclaration node that serves as the defining declaration for an enumeration type with the given name in the specified scope. The function follows the ROSE AST convention of maintaining both a defining declaration and a non-defining (forward) declaration, along with the appropriate linkage between them.

The implementation performs the following steps:

  1. It first searches the given scope for an existing SgEnumSymbol with the specified name. If found, the associated SgEnumType is reused so that enum types can be shared across declarations rather than duplicated.
  2. A new SgEnumDeclaration is allocated as the defining declaration, using the reused or newly created enum type. Its source position is set to null (indicating a compiler-generated node), and it is marked as its own defining declaration.
  3. The function then checks whether an SgEnumSymbol already exists in the scope. If one is found, its associated declaration is used as the non-defining declaration. Otherwise, a new non-defining declaration is built by calling buildNondefiningEnumDeclaration_nfi(), which also inserts the enum symbol into the scope's symbol table.
  4. The defining and non-defining declarations are cross-linked via set_definingDeclaration() and set_firstNondefiningDeclaration(). If the first non-defining declaration differs from the non-defining declaration itself, its defining declaration pointer is also updated.
  5. Both declarations have their scope set to the provided scope. The parent pointer of the defining declaration is intentionally left as NULL at this stage, because for non-autonomous declarations (such as unnamed enums embedded in variable or typedef declarations), the parent must be set later by the enclosing declaration builder.
  6. A series of assertions verify the integrity of the declaration linkage before returning.

The suffix "_nfi" stands for "no front-end interaction," indicating that this builder does not invoke the front-end parser and is intended for programmatic AST construction.

Parameters
nameThe name of the enumeration to be declared. May be an empty name for unnamed (anonymous) enumerations.
scopeThe scope in which the enum declaration is to be placed. Must not be NULL. The scope is used for symbol table lookups and for setting the declaration's enclosing scope.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgEnumDeclaration node representing the defining declaration of the enumeration. The returned node has its defining declaration pointer set to itself and its first non-defining declaration pointer set to the associated non-defining declaration.
Warning
The parent pointer of the returned defining declaration is NULL upon return. Callers are responsible for setting the parent pointer appropriately, especially when the enum is embedded within another declaration such as a variable declaration or a typedef declaration.
The symbol table entry for the enum is managed by buildNondefiningEnumDeclaration_nfi() when a new non-defining declaration is created. Callers must not insert an additional SgEnumSymbol into the scope, as this would result in duplicate symbol table entries.
Precondition
scope must not be NULL.
The ROSE AST infrastructure must be properly initialized before calling this function.
Postcondition
The returned SgEnumDeclaration is the defining declaration and has get_definingDeclaration() pointing to itself.
The returned declaration has get_firstNondefiningDeclaration() set to a valid non-defining declaration node.
The non-defining declaration's get_definingDeclaration() points to the returned defining declaration.
The scope's symbol table contains an SgEnumSymbol for the given name.
Both the defining and non-defining declarations have their scope set to the provided scope.
The source position of the defining declaration is set to null (compiler-generated).
Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder API for programmatic ROSE AST construction without invoking the front-end parser.
Enum type sharing is attempted by looking up an existing SgEnumSymbol in the scope before allocating a new SgEnumType, which helps maintain type identity consistency across multiple declarations of the same enum.
For unnamed enumerations, the parent of the defining declaration must be set by the caller after this function returns, typically by the builder for the enclosing variable or typedef declaration.

Builds a new SgEnumVal node by copying the value associated with a given enum field symbol.

This function constructs a new SgEnumVal expression node from an existing SgEnumFieldSymbol. It navigates the symbol's associated declaration to retrieve the underlying SgEnumVal expression stored within the initializer of the enum field. Specifically, it retrieves the SgInitializedName from the symbol, extracts the SgAssignInitializer from the initialized name, and then obtains the SgEnumVal operand from that initializer. A deep copy of the retrieved SgEnumVal is made using SageInterface::copyExpression to ensure that the returned node is a fresh, independent copy suitable for insertion into an AST without aliasing the original node.

Warning
This function uses ROSE_ASSERT to validate intermediate results. If the symbol's declaration, its initializer, or the operand of the initializer is NULL or of an unexpected type, the program will abort at runtime.

The declaration associated with sym must be a non-NULL SgInitializedName.
The initializer of the SgInitializedName must be a non-NULL SgAssignInitializer.
The operand of the SgAssignInitializer must be a non-NULL SgEnumVal.
Postcondition
The returned SgEnumVal is a deep copy of the original enum value node and is independent of the original AST node, safe for insertion into a new AST location.
The original AST structure associated with sym is not modified.

The returned node has a transformation source position set on it.

Builds a new SgExprStatement node wrapping a given expression.

This function constructs an expression statement node (SgExprStatement) in the ROSE abstract syntax tree (AST) from a provided SgExpression pointer. Expression statements are a fundamental construct in C and C++, representing a statement that consists solely of an expression followed by a semicolon (e.g., a function call or an assignment used as a statement).

The function allocates a new SgExprStatement on the heap, sets the parent pointer of the provided expression to point to the newly created statement node (if the expression is non-null), and assigns a default source position suitable for compiler-generated (transformation) nodes via setOneSourcePositionForTransformation. The returned SgExprStatement is heap-allocated. The caller is responsible for ensuring the node is properly inserted into the AST or otherwise managed to avoid memory leaks.

If exp is non-null, it should be a valid, well-formed SgExpression node.

The returned SgExprStatement is non-null (enforced by an internal assertion).

The returned node has its source position set to a default transformation position indicating it is a compiler-generated node.
Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface, which provides factory functions for constructing ROSE AST nodes during source-to-source transformation tasks.
The source position assigned by setOneSourcePositionForTransformation marks the node as transformation-generated, which affects how downstream tools and pretty-printers handle the node.

◆ buildFile()

SgFile * SageBuilder::buildFile ( const std::string & inputFileName,
const std::string & outputFileName,
SgProject * project,
bool clear_globalScopeAcrossFiles )

Builds and returns a new SgFile AST node by parsing the specified input file and associating it with a project.

This function constructs a new SgFile IR node corresponding to the given input source file and integrates it into the provided SgProject (or creates a new SgProject if none is supplied). The function handles a wide range of scenarios including:

  • If the input file does not exist on disk, a temporary placeholder file is created so that path resolution utilities can operate correctly. The placeholder contains a comment explaining its purpose.
  • If a project is provided, the existing file list is inspected to detect whether the input file is already present. If it is, the new file is treated as a copy of an existing file, and shared IR nodes between the two ASTs are identified and marked accordingly using set intersection on the global scope declaration lists, followed by a call to fixupSharingSourcePosition().
  • If no project is provided, a minimal SgProject is constructed on the fly with a synthesized command line.
  • The function builds an argument list from the project's original command line, appending the source filename and, if specified, the output filename using the -rose:o option. Redundant filenames are filtered from the argument list before file type determination.
  • The file type is determined via determineFileType(), which may produce an SgSourceFile or SgBinaryComposite depending on the input.
  • The ROSE frontend is invoked explicitly via result->runFrontend() after the SgFile has been added to the project's file list.
  • AstPostProcessing() is called on the result to finalize the AST.
  • To preserve the isModified state of IR nodes that existed before this call (which may be reset during frontend processing of the new file due to shared nodes), the set of modified located nodes is collected before the frontend is run and restored afterward via resetModifiedLocatedNodes().
  • If the global scope of the resulting SgSourceFile has its isModified flag set after construction, it is explicitly cleared to support correct behavior of token-based unparsing when building a dynamic library.
  • The global mangled name map is cleared if it is non-empty after post-processing.
  • Transformation detection suppression (EDG_ROSE_Translation::suppress_detection_of_transformations) is enabled before the frontend is run to avoid false positives when outlining to a separate file.
  • Optionally, the global scope symbol table shared across files (globalScopeAcrossFiles) can be cleared before processing by setting clear_globalScopeAcrossFiles to true. This is useful when a tool reads the same input file more than once.

This function is conditionally compiled and will return NULL if the macro ROSE_USE_INTERNAL_FRONTEND_DEVELOPMENT is defined, which enables a reduced ROSE build for front-end-only development environments.

Parameters
inputFileNameThe path to the source file to be parsed. Must not be empty. If the file does not exist on disk, a temporary placeholder file will be created at this path.
outputFileNameThe desired output file name for the ROSE translator. If non-empty, it is appended to the argument list using the -rose:o flag. May be an empty string to indicate no explicit output file.
projectAn optional pointer to an existing SgProject to which the new SgFile will be added. If NULL, a new SgProject is created internally. Defaults to NULL.
clear_globalScopeAcrossFilesIf true and a project is provided, the symbol table of the project's globalScopeAcrossFiles is cleared before processing the new file. This is useful for tools that process the same file multiple times. Defaults to false.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgFile IR node representing the parsed input file, or NULL if ROSE_USE_INTERNAL_FRONTEND_DEVELOPMENT is defined.
Precondition
inputFileName must not be an empty string.
If project is non-NULL, its globalScopeAcrossFiles and associated symbol table must be valid (non-NULL) pointers.
If project is non-NULL and clear_globalScopeAcrossFiles is true, the symbol table's internal hash table must be accessible and support element deletion.
Postcondition
The returned SgFile is added to the project's file list (either the supplied project or the newly created one).
The parent of the returned SgFile is set to the associated SgProject.
AstPostProcessing() has been called on the returned SgFile.
The isModified state of all previously modified located nodes in the project is restored to their state prior to this call.
The global mangled name map is cleared if it was non-empty after post-processing.
If the result is an SgSourceFile and its global scope was marked as isModified after construction, that flag is reset to false.
The project's frontendErrorCode is updated to reflect the maximum of its previous value and the error code returned by the frontend.
result->get_preprocessorDirectivesAndCommentsList() is non-NULL.
Warning
If ROSE_USE_INTERNAL_FRONTEND_DEVELOPMENT is defined at compile time, this function unconditionally returns NULL and performs no work.
If the input file does not exist, a placeholder file is created at the specified path. The caller is responsible for being aware that this side effect occurs on the filesystem.
When Outliner::use_dlopen is true, the new SgFile is inserted at the beginning of the project's file list rather than appended to the end. This is a workaround for a known issue with object file overwriting when the original command line specifies a combined compile-and-link invocation.
Shared IR nodes between the new file and an existing copy of the same file are detected and marked via fixupSharingSourcePosition(). Failure to handle shared nodes correctly can cause incorrect behavior during unparsing.
Note
This function sets EDG_ROSE_Translation::suppress_detection_of_transformations to true before invoking the frontend. This global flag is not restored afterward.
The inputFileName is added to the project's source file name list as a side effect, regardless of whether the file previously existed.
The function explicitly calls result->runFrontend() because the construction of SgFile IR nodes has been separated from frontend invocation in the ROSE infrastructure.

Builds and returns a new SgFinishExp AST node representing a finish expression.

This function constructs a finish expression node for use in the ROSE abstract syntax tree (AST). A finish expression encapsulates an expression and an associated body block, representing the X10-style "finish" construct, which ensures that all asynchronous activities spawned within the body have completed before execution continues past the finish expression.

The function allocates a new SgFinishExp node, sets its source position using SageInterface::setSourcePosition, and establishes the parent-child relationships between the finish expression node and both the expression and body arguments. This ensures that the resulting AST node is properly connected and consistent with the rest of the tree structure.

expressionA pointer to the SgExpression node that forms the expression part of the finish construct. Must not be null.
bodyA pointer to the SgBasicBlock node that forms the body of the finish construct. Must not be null.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgFinishExp AST node with its source position set and parent pointers correctly established for both the expression and body children.
Warning
Both the expression and body parameters must be valid, non-null pointers. Passing null for either parameter will trigger an assertion failure and terminate the program.
Ownership of the returned SgFinishExp node is transferred to the caller. The caller is responsible for integrating the node into the AST or managing its lifetime appropriately to avoid memory leaks.
Precondition
expression must be a non-null pointer to a valid SgExpression node.
body must be a non-null pointer to a valid SgBasicBlock node.
Postcondition
The returned SgFinishExp node has its source position initialized via SageInterface::setSourcePosition.
The parent pointer of expression is set to the returned SgFinishExp node.
The parent pointer of body is set to the returned SgFinishExp node.
Note
This function was added to support finish expression constructs, originally introduced for X10 language support within ROSE. It follows the standard SageBuilder pattern of constructing AST nodes and wiring parent-child relationships immediately upon creation.

Builds and returns a new SgFinishStmt node wrapping the given basic block body.

This function constructs an SgFinishStmt AST node representing a finish statement, which is used in parallel and concurrent programming constructs (such as X10-style finish blocks) to denote a region where all spawned activities must complete before execution continues. The provided SgBasicBlock is set as the body of the finish statement, and the parent pointer of the body is updated to point to the newly created SgFinishStmt node. A single source position transformation marker is applied to the resulting node to indicate that it was introduced by a transformation rather than originating from user source code.

◆ buildFloat80Type()

SgTypeFloat80 * SageBuilder::buildFloat80Type ( )

Builds and returns an SgTypeFloat80 node representing the 80-bit extended precision floating-point type.

This function constructs a new SgTypeFloat80 instance using the static factory method SgTypeFloat80::createType(). The 80-bit extended precision floating-point type corresponds to the long double type on x86 architectures that support the Intel 80-bit extended precision format (also known as "double-extended" precision). This type provides an 80-bit representation with a 64-bit mantissa and a 15-bit exponent, offering greater precision than the standard 64-bit double type.

The function is part of the ROSE SageBuilder interface, which provides a collection of builder functions for constructing nodes in the SAGE III Abstract Syntax Tree (AST). The returned node can be used as a type specifier when constructing variable declarations, function return types, or other type-bearing AST constructs.

An assertion (ROSE_ASSERT) is performed to verify that the created type node is non-null before returning it, ensuring that memory allocation succeeded.

Returns
A pointer to a newly created SgTypeFloat80 node representing the 80-bit extended precision floating-point type. The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-null.
Warning
The availability and size of the 80-bit extended precision type may vary depending on the target platform and compiler. On platforms that do not support 80-bit extended precision, this type may be treated differently or may not be meaningful.
Precondition
The ROSE infrastructure must be properly initialized before calling this function, as it relies on the internal type creation mechanisms of the SAGE III AST.
Postcondition
A valid, non-null SgTypeFloat80 node is returned and can be safely used in subsequent AST construction operations.
Note
This function always creates a new SgTypeFloat80 node via the SgTypeFloat80::createType() factory method. Callers should be aware of memory management responsibilities for the returned node within the context of the ROSE AST memory pool.

The suffix _nfi stands for "no file info", indicating that the constructed node does not carry source file location information (i.e., it is built without associating it with a specific source position).

As a result, error handling for malformed input strings is limited, since atof returns 0.0 on failure without signaling an error.

Builds and returns a new SgForStatement AST node representing a for-loop construct.

This function constructs a for-loop statement node (SgForStatement) in the ROSE Abstract Syntax Tree (AST). It accepts the individual components of a for-loop, including the initialization statement, the loop test condition, the increment expression, the loop body, and an optional else body (used in language constructs such as Python-style for-else).

The function handles two cases for the initialization statement:

  1. If the provided initialize_stmt is already an SgForInitStatement, it is directly assigned to the for-loop node. Any SgForInitStatement previously created internally by the SgForStatement post-constructor initialization is deleted to avoid AST consistency errors.
  2. If the provided initialize_stmt is any other type of statement (e.g., a variable declaration or an expression statement), a new SgForInitStatement wrapper is created, the initialize_stmt is appended into it, and the wrapper is assigned to the for-loop node. This avoids the double-semicolon issue that would otherwise arise during unparsing.

When the initialization statement is a variable declaration (SgVariableDeclaration), the function additionally calls fixVariableDeclaration() to insert the declared symbols into the symbol table attached to the SgForStatement scope, and calls fixVariableReferences() to repair any variable reference expressions used in the increment or test expressions.

Source position information is set using setOneSourcePositionForTransformation() on both the resulting SgForStatement and any newly created SgForInitStatement, marking the nodes as transformation-generated.

If the language is case-insensitive (as determined by SageInterface::is_language_case_insensitive()), the resulting node is marked accordingly via setCaseInsensitive(true).

Parent pointers for all provided child nodes (test, loop_body, increment, else_body, and the init statement) are set to point to the newly created SgForStatement.

initialize_stmtThe initialization statement for the for-loop. May be an SgForInitStatement, a variable declaration, or another statement. May be NULL if no initialization is needed.
testThe loop condition statement evaluated before each iteration. May be NULL.
incrementThe increment expression evaluated after each iteration. May be NULL.
loop_bodyThe body of the for-loop to be executed on each iteration. May be NULL.
else_bodyAn optional else body, used in languages that support for-else constructs (e.g., Python). May be NULL.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgForStatement AST node. The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-NULL.

Constructs a new SgForStatement AST node using the "no file info" (nfi) convention.

This function allocates and initializes a new SgForStatement node representing a for-loop construct in the ROSE abstract syntax tree (AST). It follows the "nfi" (no file info) builder pattern, which creates AST nodes without attaching source file location information, making it suitable for compiler-generated or transformation-generated code.

The construction is performed in two stages. First, a new SgForStatement object is allocated directly using its constructor with the provided initialization statement, test expression, increment expression, and loop body. This early construction step is necessary to establish the proper enclosing scope for any types that may be declared within the SgForInitStatement. Second, a refactored overload of buildForStatement_nfi is called with the newly created node along with all original arguments to complete the initialization, including attaching the optional else body (used in Python-style for-else constructs).

loop_bodyPointer to the SgStatement representing the body of the for-loop executed on each iteration.
else_bodyPointer to the SgStatement representing an optional else clause associated with the for-loop (e.g., for Python-style for-else semantics). May be NULL if no else clause is present.

A pointer to the newly constructed and initialized SgForStatement AST node.
Precondition
init_stmt must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgForInitStatement node.
test must be a valid pointer to an SgStatement node representing the loop condition.
increment must be a valid pointer to an SgExpression node representing the loop increment.
loop_body must be a valid pointer to an SgStatement node representing the loop body.
else_body may be NULL if no else clause is needed, or a valid SgStatement pointer otherwise.
Postcondition
The returned SgForStatement pointer is non-null and fully initialized.
The SgForStatement node has been further configured by the delegated overload of buildForStatement_nfi, including attachment of the else body if provided.
Warning
The function asserts that the allocated SgForStatement pointer is non-null immediately after construction. If memory allocation fails, the assertion will terminate the program.
Note
This function was refactored to separate early node construction from full initialization. The early construction is required so that the SgForStatement can serve as an enclosing scope for types defined within the SgForInitStatement before the rest of the node is fully configured.
The "nfi" suffix indicates that this builder does not attach Sg_File_Info (source location) data to the created node, which is the standard convention for programmatically generated AST nodes in ROSE transformations.

void SageBuilder::buildForStatement_nfi ( SgForStatement * result,

SgStatement * test,
SgExpression * increment,
SgStatement * loop_body,

Populates an existing SgForStatement node with its constituent child components in a non-failing, in-place initialization style.

This function is a refactored helper (nfi = non-failing initialization) that fills in the sub-components of a pre-allocated SgForStatement AST node. It was introduced to support scenarios where the SgForStatement node must be constructed early, before its children are fully available, in order to establish the correct scope for types that may be declared inside the SgForInitStatement.

The function performs the following steps:

  1. Validates that the result node is non-null.
  2. For each child slot (for_init_stmt, test, increment, loop_body, else_body), if the slot already holds a different node than the one being assigned, the existing node is deleted and the slot is cleared before the new value is assigned. This prevents memory leaks when replacing existing subtrees.
  3. Assigns the provided child nodes to their respective slots on the result node.
  4. If the current language is case-insensitive (as determined by SageInterface::is_language_case_insensitive()), the case-insensitive flag is set on the result node.
  5. Sets all source position information on the result node to null via setOneSourcePositionNull.
  6. Sets the parent pointer of each non-null child node to point back to the result node.
  7. Assigns the else_body slot last, after parent pointers have been established.
  8. Asserts that the mandatory fields (for_init_stmt, test, increment, loop_body) are non-null upon completion.

resultA pointer to the pre-allocated SgForStatement node to be populated. Must not be NULL.
init_stmtA pointer to the SgForInitStatement representing the initialization clause of the for loop. Must not be NULL upon function exit (enforced by assertion).
testA pointer to the SgStatement representing the loop condition (test clause). Must not be NULL upon function exit (enforced by assertion).
incrementA pointer to the SgExpression representing the increment expression of the for loop. Must not be NULL upon function exit (enforced by assertion).
loop_bodyA pointer to the SgStatement representing the body of the for loop. Must not be NULL upon function exit (enforced by assertion).
else_bodyA pointer to the SgStatement representing an optional else clause (used in language extensions such as Python-style for-else). May be NULL.
Precondition
result must be a valid, non-null pointer to an already-allocated SgForStatement node.
init_stmt, test, increment, and loop_body must be non-null pointers to valid AST nodes.
Any child nodes already attached to result that differ from the incoming arguments must be safe to delete (i.e., not shared or referenced elsewhere in the AST).
Postcondition
result->get_for_init_stmt() returns init_stmt and is non-null.
result->get_test() returns test and is non-null.
result->get_increment() returns increment and is non-null.
result->get_loop_body() returns loop_body and is non-null.
result->get_else_body() returns else_body (which may be null if none was provided).
The parent pointer of each non-null child node is set to result.
Source position information on result is set to null.
If the language is case-insensitive, the case-insensitive flag is set on result.
Warning
If any of the existing child nodes on result are shared with other parts of the AST and differ from the incoming arguments, they will be unconditionally deleted, which may cause dangling pointers elsewhere in the AST.
This function asserts (via ROSE_ASSERT) that result, init_stmt, test, increment, and loop_body are all non-null at the end of execution. Passing null for any of these mandatory parameters will cause an assertion failure at runtime.
Note
This function is intended as a low-level builder utility and is typically called from higher-level SgForStatement construction functions within the SageBuilder interface.
The else_body parameter supports language constructs such as the for-else statement found in Python and is expected to be NULL for standard C/C++ for loops.
The source position of the result node is explicitly nulled out by this function; callers are responsible for setting meaningful source position information afterward if required.

Builds a new SgForStatement AST node without file information (nfi).

This function constructs a new SgForStatement node representing a for-loop in the ROSE abstract syntax tree (AST). It allocates a new SgForStatement object using the provided test condition, increment expression, and loop body, then configures the node by setting parent pointers for all child nodes, assigning null source position information, and optionally attaching an initialization statement and an else body (used in languages such as Python that support for-else constructs).

If an initialization statement is provided, it is appended to the SgForInitStatement child of the newly created SgForStatement, and its parent pointer is set to that SgForInitStatement node. loop_bodyPointer to the statement representing the body of the for-loop. May be NULL. If non-null, its parent is set to the new SgForStatement.

The caller is responsible for managing the lifetime of the returned SgForStatement node and ensuring it is properly inserted into a valid AST to avoid memory leaks or dangling pointers.
Passing invalid or already-parented AST nodes as arguments may result in an inconsistent AST state, as this function unconditionally overwrites parent pointers of all non-null child nodes.

All pointer arguments that are non-null must point to valid, fully constructed AST nodes of the appropriate types.
The ROSE infrastructure must be properly initialized before calling this function.

All non-null child nodes (test, increment, loop_body, else_body, initialize_stmt) have their parent pointers set to the appropriate parent node within the new SgForStatement subtree.
If the active language is case-insensitive, the returned node has its case-insensitive flag set to true.

This function is the "no file info" (nfi) variant of buildForStatement. It is intended for use when constructing AST nodes that do not correspond to a specific source location, such as compiler-generated or transformed code.
The else_body parameter supports for-else semantics found in languages such as Python and is not applicable to standard C/C++ for-loops.

Postcondition
A new SgFortranContinueStmt node is allocated and its source position is set to reflect a transformation origin. The returned pointer is non-null.
Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface, which provides factory functions for constructing ROSE AST nodes programmatically. The created node represents the Fortran CONTINUE statement and can be used in AST transformations or code generation tasks targeting Fortran source code.

Builds and returns a new SgFortranDo AST node representing a Fortran DO construct.

This function constructs a Fortran DO loop node (SgFortranDo) for use in the ROSE abstract syntax tree (AST). It accepts optional expressions for the loop control components (initialization, bound, and increment) and an optional loop body block. If any of these arguments are null pointers, the function substitutes appropriate default nodes: null expressions are built for missing control expressions, and an empty basic block is built for a missing loop body.

After constructing the SgFortranDo node, the function sets the parent pointers of all child nodes to point to the newly created DO node, ensuring correct tree linkage. If the current language context is case-insensitive (as determined by SageInterface::is_language_case_insensitive()), the node is marked accordingly. A single source position is assigned to the node to indicate it was created by a transformation rather than parsed from source.

boundA pointer to the SgExpression representing the loop upper bound (e.g., the "n" part of a DO loop). If null, a null expression node is created and used in its place.
incrementA pointer to the SgExpression representing the loop step or increment value. If null, a null expression node is created and used in its place.
loopBodyA pointer to the SgBasicBlock representing the body of the DO loop. If null, an empty basic block is created and used in its place.

A pointer to the newly constructed SgFortranDo node. This pointer is guaranteed to be non-null; the function asserts that allocation succeeded.
Warning
The caller is responsible for managing the lifetime of the returned SgFortranDo node and integrating it into the AST. Failing to attach the returned node to a parent in the AST may result in memory leaks or an inconsistent tree structure.
If non-null expression or block arguments are passed in, their parent pointers will be reassigned to the newly created SgFortranDo node. Callers should not rely on the previous parent associations of these nodes after this call.
Precondition
The ROSE IR and SageBuilder infrastructure must be properly initialized before calling this function.
Any non-null pointer arguments passed in must point to valid, fully constructed SgExpression or SgBasicBlock nodes that are not already owned by another part of the AST in a way that would conflict with reparenting.
Postcondition
The returned SgFortranDo node has its initialization, bound, increment, and loopBody children set, with each child's parent pointer pointing back to the returned node.
The returned node has a source position assigned indicating it is a transformation-generated node.
If the language context is case-insensitive, the returned node has its case-insensitive flag set to true.
Note
This function was added to support construction of Fortran DO constructs programmatically within the ROSE AST builder framework.
Null pointer arguments are silently replaced with default-constructed nodes rather than causing an error, making all four parameters effectively optional.

◆ buildFortranImplicitType()

SgType * SageBuilder::buildFortranImplicitType ( SgName sg_name)

Determines and builds the implicit Fortran type for a variable based on the first letter of its name.

In Fortran, when no explicit type declaration is provided for a variable, the language applies default implicit typing rules based on the first letter of the variable name. This function implements those default Fortran implicit typing rules as follows:

  • Letters A through H: the variable is implicitly typed as REAL (floating-point).
  • Letters I through N: the variable is implicitly typed as INTEGER.
  • Letters O through Z: the variable is implicitly typed as REAL (floating-point).

The function converts the first character of the given name to lowercase before performing the comparison, making the lookup case-insensitive. It then calls either buildFloatType() or buildIntType() to construct and return the appropriate ROSE IR type node corresponding to the implicit Fortran type.

Parameters
sg_nameThe Fortran variable name whose implicit type is to be determined. The first character of this name must be an ASCII letter (A-Z or a-z).
Returns
A pointer to an SgType node representing the implicitly determined Fortran type. Returns a float type (SgTypeFloat) for names starting with A-H or O-Z, and an integer type (SgTypeInt) for names starting with I-N. The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-NULL.
Precondition
The first character of sg_name must be a valid ASCII alphabetic letter (A-Z or a-z). Violating this precondition will trigger a failed ROSE_ASSERT and abort execution.
Postcondition
The returned SgType pointer is non-NULL and points to a valid ROSE IR type node corresponding to the Fortran implicit typing rule for the given variable name.
Warning
This function only implements the DEFAULT Fortran implicit typing rules. It does not account for any user-specified IMPLICIT statements that may override the default rules in a given Fortran program unit.
If sg_name is empty or its first character is not an alphabetic letter, the internal ROSE_ASSERT calls will fail and the program will abort.
Note
Fortran's default implicit typing convention (sometimes called the "I-N rule") has been part of the Fortran standard since early versions of the language. Variables whose names begin with I, J, K, L, M, or N are implicitly INTEGER; all others are implicitly REAL.
The case of the first letter in sg_name does not affect the result, as the function normalizes the character to lowercase before applying the typing rules.

SgFunctionCallExp * SageBuilder::buildFunctionCallExp ( const SgName & name,

Builds a function call expression node in the ROSE AST given a function name, return type, parameters, and scope.

This function constructs a complete SgFunctionCallExp AST node by resolving or creating all necessary intermediate nodes. The construction proceeds through the following steps:

  1. If no scope is provided, the current top of the scope stack is used via SageBuilder::topScopeStack().
  2. If no parameter expression list is provided, an empty SgExprListExp is created using buildExprListExp().
  3. A SgFunctionParameterTypeList is derived from the supplied or constructed parameter list.
  4. A SgFunctionType is built from the return type and the parameter type list.
  5. A SgFunctionRefExp is built using the function name, the constructed function type, and the resolved scope.
  6. A new SgFunctionCallExp is allocated, combining the function reference expression, the parameter list, and the type from the function reference.
  7. The parent pointer of the parameter list is set to the newly created call expression.
  8. Source position information is set to indicate a transformation node.

This builder is intended for use during AST transformation or construction phases where a function call to a named function must be synthesized programmatically.

return_typeThe return type of the function being called. Must not be null.
parametersAn optional pointer to an SgExprListExp representing the argument list. If null, an empty argument list is automatically created.
scopeAn optional pointer to the SgScopeStatement in which the function reference is to be resolved. If null, the top of the current scope stack is used.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgFunctionCallExp node representing the function call expression. The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-null.
Warning
The caller is responsible for ensuring that the provided return_type is valid and consistent with the actual function being called. Providing an incorrect return type may result in a malformed or semantically incorrect AST.
If both scope and the scope stack are unavailable or empty, an assertion failure will occur at runtime.

return_type must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgType node.
If scope is provided, it must point to a valid SgScopeStatement node.
The scope stack must be non-empty if scope is null, so that topScopeStack() can return a valid scope.

The returned SgFunctionCallExp node has its parent pointer and source position information set appropriately for a transformation-generated node.
The parameters expression list has its parent pointer set to the returned SgFunctionCallExp node.
Note
This function creates new AST nodes for the function parameter type list, function type, and function reference expression as intermediate artifacts. These nodes become part of the AST subtree rooted at the returned call expression.
The source position of the resulting node is marked as a transformation, indicating it was synthetically generated rather than parsed from source code.

◆ buildFunctionCallExp() [2/3]

SgFunctionCallExp * SageBuilder::buildFunctionCallExp ( SgExpression * f,
SgExprListExp * parameters )

Builds a function call expression node from a given function expression and an optional argument list.

This builder function constructs an SgFunctionCallExp AST node representing a function call in the ROSE intermediate representation. It takes a function expression (which may be a function reference, a member function reference, or any callable expression) and an optional list of arguments encapsulated in an SgExprListExp node.

The function performs the following steps:

  1. Asserts that the provided function expression is non-null.
  2. Allocates a new SgFunctionCallExp node, using the type of the function expression as the type of the call expression.
  3. Sets the parent pointer of the function expression to the newly created call expression.
  4. If a parameter list is provided, sets its parent pointer to the newly created call expression.
  5. Marks the resulting node with a default transformation source position via setOneSourcePositionForTransformation, indicating this node was introduced by a transformation rather than parsed from source.

This function is part of the SageBuilder interface, which provides factory functions for constructing well-formed ROSE AST nodes during program transformation or code generation.

Parameters
fA pointer to the SgExpression representing the function (or callable) being invoked. This expression also provides the type for the resulting call expression. Must not be NULL.
parametersA pointer to an SgExprListExp representing the list of arguments to the function call. May be NULL if the function is called with no arguments.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgFunctionCallExp node representing the complete function call expression.
Warning
The caller is responsible for ensuring that the function expression and the parameter list are compatible in terms of types and argument count. No type-checking or arity validation is performed by this builder.
Passing a NULL value for f will trigger an assertion failure and abort execution.
Precondition
f must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgExpression node.
If parameters is non-null, it must be a valid pointer to an SgExprListExp node.
Both f and parameters (if provided) should not already have a parent set to an incompatible node, as their parent pointers will be overwritten.
Postcondition
The returned SgFunctionCallExp node is non-null and fully initialized.
The parent of f is set to the returned SgFunctionCallExp node.
If parameters is non-null, its parent is set to the returned SgFunctionCallExp node.
The returned node has its source position marked as a transformation location.
Note
The type of the resulting SgFunctionCallExp is derived directly from the type of the function expression f via f->get_type(). Callers should ensure this type accurately reflects the return type of the function being called.
This function is intended for use during AST transformation and code generation phases. It does not perform semantic analysis or symbol table lookups.

◆ buildFunctionCallExp() [3/3]

SgFunctionCallExp * SageBuilder::buildFunctionCallExp ( SgFunctionSymbol * sym,
SgExprListExp * parameters )

Builds an SgFunctionCallExp node from a function symbol and an optional argument list.

This builder function constructs a function call expression node in the ROSE AST given a function symbol and an optional expression list representing the call arguments. The function distinguishes between regular functions and member functions: if the provided symbol is an SgMemberFunctionSymbol, a member function reference expression (SgMemberFunctionRefExp) is created and used as the callee; otherwise, a standard SgFunctionRefExp is created. In both cases, an SgFunctionCallExp is constructed with the appropriate reference expression, the argument list, and the return type derived from the reference expression.

For member function calls, the virtual call flag and name qualification flag are both set to false by default, as virtual dispatch and name qualification are handled separately through other mechanisms. Parent pointers are set appropriately for both the callee reference expression and the parameter list. The resulting node is also annotated with a transformation source position via setOneSourcePositionForTransformation.

If the parameters argument is NULL, an empty SgExprListExp is automatically created using buildExprListExp(), so callers do not need to supply an explicit empty argument list.

This function preserves the distinction between member function calls and regular function calls, which is important for correct analysis of object-oriented languages such as C++ and Java.

Parameters
symA non-null pointer to the SgFunctionSymbol representing the function to be called. If the symbol is an SgMemberFunctionSymbol, a member function reference expression will be built instead of a plain function reference expression.
parametersAn optional pointer to an SgExprListExp containing the call arguments. If NULL, an empty expression list is automatically constructed and used.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgFunctionCallExp node representing the function call expression. The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-null.
Precondition
sym must not be NULL.
If parameters is non-NULL, it must point to a valid SgExprListExp node.
Postcondition
The returned SgFunctionCallExp has its callee reference expression and parameter list set with correct parent pointers.
The returned node has a transformation source position assigned.
The returned pointer is non-null.
Warning
Virtual function dispatch and name qualification for member function calls are not handled by this function. They must be managed separately after the node is constructed.
Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder API for programmatic AST construction during source-to-source transformation. The caller is responsible for inserting the returned node into the AST and managing memory as appropriate.
The default value of the parameters argument is NULL, meaning callers may omit it when building a zero-argument function call.

SgFunctionCallExp * SageBuilder::buildFunctionCallExp_nfi ( SgExpression * f,
