Builds a function call expression node without file information (nfi).

This function constructs a new SgFunctionCallExp AST node representing a function call expression. It takes a function expression and an optional argument list, creates the corresponding AST node, and sets up the parent-child relationships within the AST. The type of the resulting function call expression is derived directly from the type of the provided function expression node. Source position information for the newly created node is explicitly set to null, which is the distinguishing characteristic of the "nfi" (no file information) variant of this builder function.

After creating the SgFunctionCallExp node, the function sets the parent pointer of the function expression to the new call expression node. If a parameter list is provided, its parent pointer is also updated accordingly. The source position of the resulting node is then nullified via setOneSourcePositionNull to indicate that no source location is associated with this synthetically created node.

Parameters
fA pointer to the SgExpression node representing the function (or function pointer) being called. Must not be NULL. Its type is used as the type of the resulting SgFunctionCallExp node.
parametersA pointer to an SgExprListExp node representing the list of arguments passed to the function call. May be NULL if the function call has no arguments.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgFunctionCallExp node representing the function call expression, with parent pointers and source position properly initialized.
Warning
The caller is responsible for ensuring that the provided SgExpression pointer f is valid and non-NULL. Passing a NULL value for f will trigger an assertion failure and abort execution.
The type assigned to the resulting SgFunctionCallExp is taken directly from the type of f. If f does not carry an appropriate type (e.g., a function type or pointer-to-function type), the resulting AST node may be semantically incorrect.
Precondition
f must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid SgExpression node.
If parameters is non-NULL, it must point to a valid SgExprListExp node.
Postcondition
The returned SgFunctionCallExp node is non-NULL.
The parent of f is set to the returned SgFunctionCallExp node.
If parameters is non-NULL, the parent of parameters is set to the returned SgFunctionCallExp node.
The source position of the returned node is set to null (no file information).
Note
This function is the "nfi" (no file information) variant of the function call expression builder. It is intended for use when constructing synthetic AST nodes that do not correspond to any location in a source file.
The type of the resulting SgFunctionCallExp is set to f->get_type() at construction time. Callers may need to adjust this type if a more specific return type is required.

◆ buildFunctionCallStmt() [1/2]

SgExprStatement * SageBuilder::buildFunctionCallStmt ( const SgName & name,

Builds a function call expression statement for a named function.

This function constructs an SgExprStatement node that wraps a function call expression (SgFunctionCallExp) targeting a function identified by the given name. It first resolves the active scope by consulting the top of the scope stack if no explicit scope is provided. It then delegates to buildFunctionCallExp to construct the underlying call expression, and finally wraps that expression in an SgExprStatement using buildExprStatement. The resulting statement node can be inserted directly into an abstract syntax tree (AST) as a standalone function call statement, which is the common form of a function call used purely for its side effects rather than its return value.

Parameters
nameThe name of the function to be called. This is used to look up or construct the appropriate function reference within the given scope.
return_typeThe return type of the function being called. This type information is used when constructing the function call expression node.
parametersAn optional list of argument expressions to pass to the function call. If NULL, the function call is constructed with no arguments.
scopeAn optional pointer to the enclosing scope statement in which the function call is to be resolved. If NULL, the top of the current scope stack is used automatically.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgExprStatement node wrapping the function call expression.
Precondition
The scope stack must be non-empty if scope is NULL, so that a valid enclosing scope can be obtained from the top of the stack.
name must refer to a valid function name that can be resolved within the provided or inferred scope.
return_type must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an SgType node representing the return type of the target function.
Postcondition
The returned SgExprStatement contains a valid SgFunctionCallExp child node constructed from the provided name, return type, parameters, and scope.
The returned node is suitable for insertion into the AST as a statement.
Warning
If scope is NULL and the scope stack is also empty, an assertion failure will be triggered at runtime. Ensure that a valid scope is available either explicitly or via the scope stack before calling this function.
Note
This function is a convenience wrapper that combines buildFunctionCallExp and buildExprStatement into a single call, simplifying the construction of function call statements during AST transformation or generation tasks.

Builds an expression statement wrapping a function call expression.

This function constructs a complete function call statement (SgExprStatement) from a given function expression and an optional list of arguments. Internally, it first creates a function call expression node (SgFunctionCallExp) by invoking buildFunctionCallExp with the provided function expression and parameter list. The resulting function call expression is then wrapped in an expression statement node (SgExprStatement) via buildExprStatement, producing a statement-level AST node suitable for insertion into a statement list or compound statement body.

This builder is useful when the callee is represented as a raw SgExpression (for example, a function pointer expression or a member function expression) rather than a named function symbol or declaration.

Parameters
function_expA pointer to the SgExpression representing the function or callable entity to be invoked. This expression becomes the callee of the generated function call. Must not be NULL.
parametersA pointer to an SgExprListExp node containing the actual argument expressions to pass to the function call. May be NULL if the function takes no arguments, in which case an empty argument list is used by default.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgExprStatement node that wraps the function call expression. The returned node is a valid AST statement ready for insertion into the ROSE intermediate representation.
Precondition
function_exp must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an SgExpression node that represents a callable entity (e.g., a function reference or function pointer expression).
If parameters is non-NULL, it must point to a properly constructed SgExprListExp node whose child expressions are consistent with the expected parameter types of the target function.
Postcondition
The returned SgExprStatement contains an SgFunctionCallExp child node whose function expression is function_exp and whose argument list corresponds to parameters.
Parent pointers within the newly created AST nodes are set appropriately by the underlying builder functions.
Warning
Passing a NULL function_exp may result in undefined behavior or an assertion failure within the underlying builder functions.
The caller is responsible for inserting the returned statement into the AST at an appropriate location; the node is not automatically attached to any parent scope.
Note
This overload accepts a raw SgExpression for the callee, which is convenient when working with function pointers or complex call targets. For calls to named functions, consider using the overloads of buildFunctionCallStmt that accept a function name string or an SgFunctionSymbol directly.

◆ buildFunctionParameterList() [1/2]

SgFunctionParameterList * SageBuilder::buildFunctionParameterList ( SgFunctionParameterTypeList * paraTypeList)

Builds an SgFunctionParameterList from a given SgFunctionParameterTypeList.

This function constructs a new SgFunctionParameterList node by iterating over the type entries contained within the provided SgFunctionParameterTypeList. For each type found in the type list, an SgInitializedName node is created with an empty name and the corresponding type, and then appended to the resulting parameter list. This is useful when constructing function declarations or definitions where only the parameter types are known and named parameters are not required, such as in function pointer types or forward declarations that omit parameter names.

If the provided SgFunctionParameterTypeList pointer is NULL, the function returns an empty SgFunctionParameterList without adding any parameters.

The internal algorithm proceeds as follows:

  1. An empty SgFunctionParameterList is created via the no-argument overload of buildFunctionParameterList.
  2. If the input type list is NULL, the empty list is returned immediately.
  3. Otherwise, the argument types are retrieved from the type list.
  4. For each type in the list, an SgInitializedName with an empty SgName and the given type is created and appended to the parameter list.
  5. The fully populated parameter list is returned.
Parameters
paraTypeListA pointer to an SgFunctionParameterTypeList containing the sequence of parameter types to be used when constructing the parameter list. May be NULL, in which case an empty SgFunctionParameterList is returned.
Returns
A pointer to a newly constructed SgFunctionParameterList containing one unnamed SgInitializedName entry for each type found in the provided SgFunctionParameterTypeList. Returns an empty SgFunctionParameterList if paraTypeList is NULL.
Warning
The returned SgFunctionParameterList is heap-allocated. The caller or the enclosing AST structure is responsible for managing the lifetime of this node. Failing to attach it to a valid parent node in the AST may result in memory leaks.
All generated SgInitializedName nodes are created with empty names. If named parameters are required, a different overload or a manual construction approach should be used.
Precondition
If paraTypeList is non-NULL, it must point to a valid, well-formed SgFunctionParameterTypeList node whose internal type pointer list contains only valid, non-NULL SgType pointers.
Postcondition
The returned SgFunctionParameterList contains exactly as many SgInitializedName children as there are types in paraTypeList, or zero children if paraTypeList is NULL.
Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface, which provides factory functions for constructing ROSE AST nodes. It relies on the no-argument overload of buildFunctionParameterList to create the initial empty list, and on appendArg to populate it.
The generated parameter names are empty (represented by SgName("")), which is consistent with abstract function type signatures where parameter names are not semantically significant.

The newly created node is configured with its defining declaration pointer set to NULL and its first non-defining declaration pointer set to itself, which is the standard initialization pattern for standalone declaration nodes in the ROSE IR. This function follows the ROSE SageBuilder naming convention where the "_nfi" suffix indicates that no source file information is associated with the resulting node.

SgType * type5,
SgType * type6,

Builds an SgFunctionParameterTypeList node from up to eight optional parameter types.

This function constructs and returns a new SgFunctionParameterTypeList object, which represents the list of parameter types associated with a function type in the ROSE intermediate representation (IR). Up to eight SgType pointers may be supplied as arguments. Each non-null type pointer is appended in order to the internal SgTypePtrList maintained by the newly created node. Parameters that are passed as NULL are silently skipped and do not contribute to the resulting type list. This allows callers to build parameter type lists of varying lengths (zero through eight) using a single overloaded interface without needing to manage the list manually.

The function allocates the SgFunctionParameterTypeList on the heap and asserts that the allocation succeeded before proceeding. The caller receives ownership of the returned node and is responsible for integrating it into the AST or managing its lifetime appropriately.

Parameters
type0Pointer to the first parameter type, or NULL to indicate no type at this position. All subsequent non-null types are ignored once a NULL is encountered only if no later non-null types are intended; however, non-null types at any position are always appended.
type1Pointer to the second parameter type, or NULL to skip.
type2Pointer to the third parameter type, or NULL to skip.
type3Pointer to the fourth parameter type, or NULL to skip.
type4Pointer to the fifth parameter type, or NULL to skip.
type5Pointer to the sixth parameter type, or NULL to skip.
type6Pointer to the seventh parameter type, or NULL to skip.
type7Pointer to the eighth parameter type, or NULL to skip.
Returns
A pointer to the newly allocated SgFunctionParameterTypeList node containing all non-null type pointers appended in the order they were supplied. The returned pointer is never NULL.
Precondition
Each non-null SgType pointer supplied must point to a valid, fully constructed SgType node that is part of or compatible with the current ROSE AST context.
Memory allocation for the new SgFunctionParameterTypeList must succeed; the function asserts this condition internally.
Postcondition
The returned SgFunctionParameterTypeList contains exactly as many entries as there are non-null type arguments among type0 through type7, in the same relative order.
The internal SgTypePtrList of the returned node reflects all non-null type arguments appended sequentially.
Warning
Passing more than eight parameter types is not supported by this overload. For functions with more than eight parameters, use an alternative overload or build the SgFunctionParameterTypeList manually.
The caller takes ownership of the returned heap-allocated node. Failing to attach it to the AST or otherwise manage its lifetime may result in a memory leak.
NULL gaps between non-null type arguments are permitted syntactically but may produce unexpected type list orderings if the intent was to represent a contiguous parameter sequence. Ensure that non-null types are provided in the intended positional order.
Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface, which provides factory functions for constructing ROSE AST nodes.
An overload of this function accepting an SgExpressionPtrList or SgFunctionParameterList may be available for alternative construction strategies.

Builds a function reference expression node given a C-style string name, a function type, and an optional scope.

This function serves as a convenience overload that accepts a C-style character string as the function name. Internally, it converts the provided C-style string into an SgName object and delegates the actual construction to the corresponding overload of buildFunctionRefExp that accepts an SgName. This allows callers to pass raw string literals or character pointers directly without manually constructing an SgName beforehand.

The resulting SgFunctionRefExp node represents a reference to a named function within the AST (Abstract Syntax Tree) of a ROSE-based program transformation or analysis tool. The optional scope parameter can be used to guide symbol lookup when resolving the function reference within a particular scope.

scopeAn optional pointer to an SgScopeStatement indicating the scope in which the function reference should be resolved. May be NULL, in which case a default or global scope may be used during symbol lookup.

name must be a valid, non-null, null-terminated C-style string.
funcType must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgType that describes the function's type.

Postcondition
The returned SgFunctionRefExp node, if non-null, is a valid AST node representing a reference to the named function with the specified type.
Warning
Passing a null pointer for name or funcType may result in undefined behavior or an assertion failure.
The caller is responsible for ensuring that the returned node is properly inserted into the AST to avoid memory leaks or dangling nodes.
Note
This function is a thin wrapper and performs no additional validation beyond what is done in the SgName-based overload of buildFunctionRefExp.
The scope parameter defaults to NULL if not provided.

◆ buildFunctionRefExp() [3/6]

SgFunctionRefExp * SageBuilder::buildFunctionRefExp ( const SgFunctionDeclaration * func_decl)

Builds a function reference expression node from a given function declaration.

This function constructs an SgFunctionRefExp AST node by resolving the appropriate function symbol from the provided SgFunctionDeclaration. The resolution process follows a priority order: it first attempts to retrieve the symbol from the non-defining declaration (i.e., a forward prototype declaration). If no non-defining declaration exists, it falls back to using the defining declaration (i.e., the full function definition). This fallback handles cases where a function has no separate prototype and is defined directly without a prior declaration.

If both the non-defining and defining declarations are NULL, the function reports a fatal error to standard error and aborts execution, as a valid function symbol cannot be resolved in that scenario.

Once the symbol is resolved, the function delegates to the overloaded buildFunctionRefExp that accepts an SgFunctionSymbol pointer to produce the final SgFunctionRefExp node.

Parameters
func_declA pointer to the SgFunctionDeclaration from which the function reference expression is to be built. Must not be NULL. The declaration must have at least one of its non-defining or defining declarations available in the AST with a resolvable symbol.
Returns
A pointer to a newly constructed SgFunctionRefExp node corresponding to the function symbol resolved from the provided declaration.
Warning
If both the non-defining and defining declarations of the provided function declaration are NULL, the function prints a fatal error message to standard error and calls ROSE_ABORT(), terminating the program.
If the resolved symbol cannot be cast to SgFunctionSymbol, behavior is undefined and internal assertions may trigger an abort.
Precondition
func_decl must not be NULL.
At least one of the non-defining or defining declarations associated with func_decl must be non-NULL and have a valid symbol registered in the symbol table.
Postcondition
The returned SgFunctionRefExp is a valid, non-NULL AST node referencing the function symbol resolved from func_decl.
Note
This function was updated on 12/1/2010 (Liao) to handle the case where a function has no prototype declaration and only a defining declaration exists, ensuring correct symbol resolution in such scenarios.
The function internally uses ROSE_ASSERT to enforce non-NULL invariants on intermediate values during symbol resolution.

◆ buildFunctionRefExp() [4/6]

SgFunctionRefExp * SageBuilder::buildFunctionRefExp ( const SgName & name,
const SgType * funcType,
SgScopeStatement * scope )

Builds a function reference expression node for a function identified by name and type.

This function constructs an SgFunctionRefExp AST node representing a reference to a function with the given name and function type. It first validates that the provided type is a non-null SgFunctionType. If a scope is not provided, the top of the current scope stack is used.

The function attempts to locate the corresponding SgFunctionSymbol by searching the parent scopes starting from the given scope. If no symbol is found, which can occur when a function call is being inserted before any prototype or declaration exists in the AST, the function automatically synthesizes a non-defining function declaration and inserts it into the global scope. For Fortran and Jovial languages, an SgProcedureHeaderStatement is generated; for all other languages, a standard SgFunctionDeclaration is generated. The synthesized declaration is given an extern storage modifier. After this insertion, the symbol lookup is retried and is expected to succeed.

Note that automatic declaration synthesis is only supported for regular (non-member) functions. Member function types will trigger an assertion failure in this fallback path.

The resulting SgFunctionRefExp node has its source position set to indicate it was introduced by a transformation.

Parameters
nameThe name of the function to reference. This is used for symbol lookup and, if necessary, for constructing a synthetic function declaration.
funcTypeThe type of the function. Must be a non-null SgFunctionType (or a subtype). This type is used both for symbol lookup disambiguation and as the type of the resulting reference expression.
scopeThe scope from which to begin the symbol lookup. If NULL, the top of the current scope stack is used. Must resolve to a non-null scope after defaulting.
Returns
A pointer to a newly created SgFunctionRefExp node referencing the resolved function symbol with the specified function type. The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-null.
Warning
If no existing symbol is found and the function type represents a member function, an assertion failure will be triggered. Automatic declaration synthesis is only supported for non-member functions.
If no existing symbol is found and automatic synthesis is attempted but the symbol still cannot be resolved after insertion, an assertion failure will be triggered.
Precondition
funcType must not be NULL and must be castable to SgFunctionType.
If scope is NULL, the scope stack must be non-empty so that a valid default scope can be obtained.
If the symbol is not found and a synthetic declaration must be created, the function type must not be a member function type.
Postcondition
The returned SgFunctionRefExp is non-null and has its source position marked as a transformation.
If no prior declaration existed, a non-defining function declaration with extern storage is inserted into the global scope, and the corresponding symbol is registered.
Note
This function is intended for use during AST construction and transformation. When inserting function calls before any prototype exists, the automatic declaration synthesis provides a fallback mechanism, but callers should be aware that this modifies the global scope of the AST.
Template functions are not yet handled in the automatic declaration synthesis path. A TODO exists in the implementation to address this case in the future.

◆ buildFunctionRefExp() [5/6]

SgFunctionRefExp * SageBuilder::buildFunctionRefExp ( const SgName & name,
SgScopeStatement * scope )

Builds a function reference expression node for a function identified by name within a given scope.

This function constructs an SgFunctionRefExp AST node by looking up the function symbol corresponding to the provided name, starting from the given scope and traversing parent scopes as needed. If no scope is provided, the top of the current scope stack is used.

When the function symbol cannot be found, the implementation currently aborts with an error message indicating that this code path is unsupported. Historically, this fallback was intended to handle rare cases where a function call is inserted before any prototype exists, by synthesizing a non-defining function declaration with an assumed integer return type and an empty parameter list, marked with extern storage. This fallback path has been disabled and will trigger a fatal error via ROSE_ABORT() if reached.

Once a valid function symbol is located, the function delegates to the overloaded buildFunctionRefExp(SgFunctionSymbol*) to construct the actual reference expression node, and then sets a single source position marker on the result to indicate it was generated by a transformation.

Parameters
nameThe name of the function for which a reference expression is to be built. This name is used to perform a symbol lookup in the provided scope and its parent scopes.
scopeA pointer to the scope statement in which to begin the symbol lookup. If NULL, the top of the internal scope stack is used as the starting scope. Must not be NULL after defaulting to the scope stack top.
Returns
A pointer to a newly constructed SgFunctionRefExp node representing a reference to the named function. The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-NULL upon successful completion.
Warning
If the function symbol cannot be found in any parent scope, the implementation will call ROSE_ABORT() and terminate the program. The fallback path that previously synthesized a declaration has been intentionally disabled.
This function should not be used in contexts where the function symbol may not yet exist in the scope hierarchy. Ensure that the function has been declared before attempting to build a reference expression for it.
Precondition
The name parameter must correspond to a function that has already been declared and whose symbol is accessible from the provided scope or one of its ancestor scopes.
If scope is NULL, the internal scope stack maintained by SageBuilder must be non-empty so that a valid default scope can be obtained.
Postcondition
The returned SgFunctionRefExp node is non-NULL and has a source position set to indicate it was produced by a transformation.
The returned node is associated with the function symbol found during lookup.
Note
The fallback mechanism for creating a synthetic function declaration when no symbol is found has been disabled as of a refactoring that updated the API to require an SgTemplateArgumentPtrList parameter. Any attempt to reach that code path will result in program termination.
Source position information is set on the resulting node using setOneSourcePositionForTransformation, which marks it as a compiler-generated transformation rather than a node derived from user source code.

Builds a function reference expression node from a given function symbol.

This function constructs a new SgFunctionRefExp AST node using the provided SgFunctionSymbol. The resulting node represents a reference to a named function within the ROSE intermediate representation. After construction, the node is assigned a transformation source position via setOneSourcePositionForTransformation, indicating that this node was introduced by a program transformation rather than parsed from original source code. An assertion is performed to ensure the node was successfully allocated before it is returned.

The returned SgFunctionRefExp node has been allocated, initialized with the provided symbol, and assigned a transformation source position. The node is ready to be inserted into the AST.
Note
The second argument to the SgFunctionRefExp constructor is passed as NULL, meaning no explicit type is provided at construction time; the type is expected to be derived from the associated function symbol. This function is part of the SageBuilder interface, which provides utilities for programmatically constructing ROSE AST nodes during source-to-source transformations.

SgFunctionType * SageBuilder::buildFunctionType ( SgType * return_type,

Builds an SgFunctionType node from a return type and a parameter list.

This function constructs an SgFunctionType by first deriving an SgFunctionParameterTypeList from the provided SgFunctionParameterList, then delegating to the overloaded buildFunctionType that accepts an SgFunctionParameterTypeList directly. If the resulting SgFunctionType already owns a different argument list (e.g., because an equivalent type was found in the type table and reused), the locally created SgFunctionParameterTypeList is deleted to avoid memory leaks. This design ensures that function types are deduplicated and that ownership of the parameter type list is handled correctly depending on whether the type was newly created or retrieved from an existing entry.

return_typeA pointer to the SgType representing the return type of the function. Must not be null.
argListA pointer to the SgFunctionParameterList representing the formal parameters of the function. Must not be null, as enforced by an internal assertion.

A pointer to the constructed or retrieved SgFunctionType node corresponding to the given return type and parameter list.
Warning
If return_type is null, behavior is undefined. Ensure that a valid SgType pointer is passed for the return type.
Precondition
argList must be a non-null pointer to a valid SgFunctionParameterList node.
return_type should point to a valid, previously constructed SgType node.
Postcondition
The returned SgFunctionType reflects the specified return type and the parameter types derived from argList.
If the function type already existed in the type table, the intermediate SgFunctionParameterTypeList created internally is deleted and set to null to prevent memory leaks.
Note
This function is an overload that accepts an SgFunctionParameterList for convenience. Internally it converts the parameter list to an SgFunctionParameterTypeList before constructing the function type.
The deduplication of SgFunctionType nodes is handled by the underlying overloaded buildFunctionType that takes an SgFunctionParameterTypeList, which may return a pre-existing type from the type table rather than creating a new one.

◆ buildFunctionType() [2/2]

SgFunctionType * SageBuilder::buildFunctionType ( SgType * return_type,
SgFunctionParameterTypeList * typeList )

Builds or retrieves a SgFunctionType node representing a function type with the given return type and parameter type list.

This function constructs a SgFunctionType AST node corresponding to a function type defined by a specified return type and a list of parameter types. It makes use of the global function type table (SgFunctionTypeTable) to avoid creating duplicate type nodes. Before allocating a new SgFunctionType, the function computes a mangled name from the return type and the parameter type list using SgFunctionType::get_mangled(), then queries the global type table for an existing entry under that name.

If a matching SgFunctionType is found in the global type table, it is returned directly without allocating a new node. If no match is found, a new SgFunctionType is allocated, its argument list is set to the provided typeList (replacing any pre-existing argument list to avoid memory leaks), and the new type is inserted into the global function type table before being returned.

The function relies on the global function type table being accessible via SgNode::get_globalFunctionTypeTable(). This design ensures that function types are canonicalized across the AST, so that structurally identical function types share a single SgFunctionType node.

Parameters
return_typePointer to the SgType representing the return type of the function type being built. Must not be NULL.
typeListPointer to the SgFunctionParameterTypeList representing the ordered list of parameter types for the function type. Must not be NULL.
Returns
A pointer to an existing or newly created SgFunctionType node that corresponds to the specified return type and parameter type list.
Warning
If the global function type table is not initialized or is inaccessible, the function will trigger an assertion failure. Callers must ensure the ROSE infrastructure has been properly initialized before invoking this function.
If a pre-existing argument list is found on a newly created SgFunctionType, it is deleted and replaced with the provided typeList. Callers should not retain pointers to any argument list that may have been previously associated with a freshly constructed SgFunctionType.
Precondition
return_type must not be NULL.
typeList must not be NULL.
The global function type table (accessible via SgNode::get_globalFunctionTypeTable()) must be initialized and non-NULL before this function is called.
Postcondition
The returned SgFunctionType pointer is non-NULL.
The returned SgFunctionType is registered in the global function type table under its mangled name.
If a new SgFunctionType was created, its argument list is set to typeList and typeList's parent is set to the new SgFunctionType.
Note
This function uses a static member function SgFunctionType::get_mangled() to compute the canonical mangled name for the function type, which serves as the lookup key in the global type table.
This function is not directly applicable to SgMemberFunctionType nodes, as the static mangling mechanism used here does not account for member function specifics without additional work.
Ownership of the typeList object is transferred to the newly created SgFunctionType when a new node is built. Callers should not delete or reuse typeList after passing it to this function if a new type is created.

Builds a goto statement node from a label symbol.

This function constructs an SgGotoStatement AST node using a given SgLabelSymbol. The behavior differs depending on the target language:

For Fortran, the function first creates a goto statement with a NULL label statement, then builds an SgLabelRefExp from the provided symbol and attaches it to the goto statement via set_label_expression(). The label reference expression's parent is also set to the newly created goto statement.

For C and C++, the function retrieves the SgLabelStatement associated with the symbol via get_declaration() and delegates to the overloaded buildGotoStatement() that accepts an SgLabelStatement pointer directly.

In both cases, the resulting SgGotoStatement is validated to be non-NULL before being returned.

Precondition
symbol must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid SgLabelSymbol.
For C/C++ code, symbol->get_declaration() must return a non-NULL SgLabelStatement.
Postcondition
The returned SgGotoStatement is non-NULL.
For Fortran, the returned statement contains a valid SgLabelRefExp with its parent set to the goto statement.
For C/C++, the returned statement is linked to the corresponding SgLabelStatement.
Note
This function internally calls SageInterface::is_Fortran_language() to determine the target language and dispatches accordingly. It relies on overloaded versions of buildGotoStatement() and buildLabelRefExp() for the actual node construction.

◆ buildHeader()

PreprocessingInfo * SageBuilder::buildHeader ( const std::string & header_filename,
PreprocessingInfo::RelativePositionType position,
bool isSystemHeader )

Builds a dangling preprocessor include directive node without inserting it into the AST.

This function constructs a PreprocessingInfo object representing a C preprocessor include directive (either a system header or a user header) but does not attach it to any AST node. The caller must subsequently invoke insertHeader() to actually place the generated include directive into the desired location within the AST.

Depending on the value of isSystemHeader, the generated directive will take one of two forms:

  • System header: #include <header_filename>
  • User header: #include "header_filename"

The resulting PreprocessingInfo node is marked as transformation-generated, with line, column, and file offset all set to zero, reflecting that it does not originate from a physical source file. The relative position (before or after the associated AST node) is controlled by the position parameter.

Internally, the function allocates a new PreprocessingInfo object of type CpreprocessorIncludeDeclaration, sets the transformation flag on its file info, and returns the pointer to the caller. The caller is responsible for managing the lifetime of the returned object or ensuring it is properly inserted and managed by the AST infrastructure.

Parameters
header_filenameThe name of the header file to include (e.g., "stdio.h" or "myheader.h"). This string is embedded directly into the generated include directive without further validation.
positionThe relative position of the generated include directive with respect to the AST node it will eventually be attached to. Defaults to PreprocessingInfo::before, meaning the directive will appear before the associated statement or declaration.
isSystemHeaderA boolean flag indicating whether the header should be treated as a system header. If true, angle brackets are used (#include <...>); if false, double quotes are used (#include "..."). Defaults to false.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created PreprocessingInfo object representing the include directive. The returned object is marked as transformation-generated and is not yet attached to any AST node.
Warning
The returned PreprocessingInfo pointer is a dangling node until insertHeader() is called. Failing to insert it into the AST may result in a memory leak or an orphaned node.
The header_filename string is used verbatim in the generated directive. No validation or sanitization is performed on the filename. Providing a malformed or empty filename will produce an invalid include directive.
Precondition
header_filename must be a non-empty, valid header filename string.
The ROSE infrastructure must be properly initialized before calling this function.
Postcondition
A new PreprocessingInfo object of type CpreprocessorIncludeDeclaration is allocated and returned.
The returned object's file info is marked as transformation-generated.
The returned object is not attached to any AST node; insertHeader() must be called separately to integrate it into the AST.
Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface for constructing AST nodes programmatically as part of source-to-source transformations in the ROSE compiler framework.
The position parameter defaults to PreprocessingInfo::before, which places the include directive before the node it is attached to. This is the most common use case when adding new headers at the top of a file or before a declaration.

Postcondition

◆ buildIfStmt() [1/2]

SgIfStmt * SageBuilder::buildIfStmt ( SgExpression * conditional,
SgStatement * true_body,
SgStatement * false_body )

Builds an if-statement AST node from an expression condition and two statement branches.

This inline overload of buildIfStmt accepts an SgExpression pointer as the conditional instead of an SgStatement pointer. It wraps the given expression in an expression statement by calling buildExprStatement internally, then delegates to the primary buildIfStmt overload that takes an SgStatement as its conditional argument.

This convenience overload simplifies construction of if-statements when the condition is available as a raw expression node rather than a pre-wrapped statement node. The resulting SgIfStmt node represents a complete if-statement with an optional else branch.

The true_body parameter represents the block or statement to be executed when the condition evaluates to true. The false_body parameter represents the block or statement to be executed when the condition evaluates to false (the else branch). Passing a null pointer for false_body indicates that no else branch is present.

Parameters
conditionalThe expression to be used as the condition of the if-statement. This expression is automatically wrapped into an expression statement node via buildExprStatement before being passed to the underlying builder. Must not be a null pointer.
true_bodyThe statement or compound statement representing the then-branch of the if-statement, executed when the conditional expression evaluates to true. Must not be a null pointer.
false_bodyThe statement or compound statement representing the else-branch of the if-statement, executed when the conditional expression evaluates to false. May be a null pointer if no else branch is desired.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgIfStmt AST node representing the complete if-statement, including the condition, true branch, and optional false branch.
Precondition
conditional must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgExpression node.
true_body must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgStatement node.
false_body may be null if no else branch is needed; otherwise it must be a valid pointer to an SgStatement node.
Postcondition
The returned SgIfStmt node has its conditional set to an SgExprStatement wrapping the provided expression, its true body set to true_body, and its false body set to false_body (which may be null).
The ownership of the conditional, true_body, and false_body nodes is transferred to the returned SgIfStmt node as child nodes in the AST.
Warning
Passing a null pointer for conditional or true_body results in undefined behavior and may cause a crash or malformed AST node.
The caller must ensure that conditional, true_body, and false_body are not already attached to another parent node in the AST, as sharing AST nodes between multiple parents is not supported and leads to undefined behavior.
Note
This function is an inline convenience overload. For direct construction using an SgStatement as the conditional, use the primary ROSE_DLL_API overload of buildIfStmt that accepts SgStatement* as its first argument.

◆ buildIfStmt() [2/2]

SgIfStmt * SageBuilder::buildIfStmt ( SgStatement * conditional,
SgStatement * true_body,
SgStatement * false_body )

Builds and returns a new SgIfStmt AST node representing an if statement.

This function constructs a new SgIfStmt node from the provided conditional expression, true body, and optional false body statements. It sets the parent pointers of all child nodes to the newly created if statement, applies a single source position marker for transformation tracking, and handles language-specific semantics.

For case-insensitive languages (as determined by SageInterface::is_language_case_insensitive()), the resulting node is marked with case-insensitive semantics.

For Fortran, the function distinguishes between a Block IF statement and a Logical IF statement according to the Fortran 77 standard (Chapters 11.5 to 11.9). If the true body is an SgBasicBlock, an SgFortranDo, or another SgIfStmt, the node is treated as a Block IF statement: the "THEN" keyword flag and the "END IF" statement flag are both set to true. Otherwise, the node is treated as a Logical IF statement and these flags are left unset.

Parameters
conditionalA pointer to the SgStatement representing the conditional expression of the if statement. Must not be NULL.
true_bodyA pointer to the SgStatement representing the body to execute when the condition evaluates to true. Must not be NULL.
false_bodyA pointer to the SgStatement representing the body to execute when the condition evaluates to false (the else branch). May be NULL if no else branch is desired.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgIfStmt node. The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-NULL.
Precondition
conditional must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an SgStatement node.
true_body must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an SgStatement node.
false_body may be NULL or a valid pointer to an SgStatement node.
Postcondition
The returned SgIfStmt node has its conditional, true body, and (if provided) false body child nodes set with their parent pointers pointing back to the new SgIfStmt node.
The source position of the returned node is set for transformation tracking via setOneSourcePositionForTransformation.
For case-insensitive languages, the returned node has case-insensitive semantics enabled.
For Fortran Block IF statements, the "use_then_keyword" and "has_end_statement" flags are set to true on the returned node.
Warning
Passing a NULL pointer for conditional or true_body will trigger an assertion failure and abort the program.
The caller is responsible for ensuring that the provided statement nodes are not already owned by another part of the AST, as setting parent pointers may invalidate existing tree structure.
Note
The distinction between a Fortran Block IF and a Logical IF is determined solely by the type of the true_body node (SgBasicBlock, SgFortranDo, or SgIfStmt triggers Block IF semantics).
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface for programmatic AST construction and is intended for use in ROSE-based source-to-source transformation tools.

◆ buildIfStmt_nfi()

SgIfStmt * SageBuilder::buildIfStmt_nfi ( SgStatement * conditional,
SgStatement * true_body,
SgStatement * false_body )

Constructs and initializes a new SgIfStmt AST node using the "no file info" (nfi) pattern.

This function allocates a new SgIfStmt node on the heap, passing the conditional expression and the true and false body statements directly to the constructor. After allocation, it calls initializeIfStmt to perform the full initialization of the node, including setting up parent pointers and any additional internal state required by the ROSE AST infrastructure. The separation of construction and initialization allows for deferred or staged setup of AST nodes, which is a common pattern in the SageBuilder interface. The "nfi" suffix indicates that this builder variant does not automatically attach source file information to the created node, making it suitable for programmatically generated or transformed code where no original source location is applicable.

Parameters
conditionalA pointer to the SgStatement representing the conditional (test) expression of the if statement. This is the boolean condition evaluated at runtime.
true_bodyA pointer to the SgStatement representing the body of the if statement that is executed when the conditional evaluates to true.
false_bodyA pointer to the SgStatement representing the else branch of the if statement, executed when the conditional evaluates to false. May be null if there is no else branch.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed and initialized SgIfStmt node.
Warning
The returned pointer is heap-allocated. The caller or the enclosing AST is responsible for managing the lifetime of this node to avoid memory leaks.
This function asserts via ROSE_ASSERT that the allocated SgIfStmt pointer is non-null. If memory allocation fails, the assertion will trigger rather than returning a null pointer gracefully.
Precondition
conditional must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgStatement node.
true_body must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgStatement node representing the if-true branch.
false_body may be null if no else branch is needed, or a valid pointer to an SgStatement node otherwise.
Postcondition
The returned SgIfStmt node is fully constructed and initialized via initializeIfStmt.
The conditional, true_body, and false_body are associated with the returned SgIfStmt node as its child components.
No source file information is attached to the created node, consistent with the nfi construction pattern.
Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface, which provides factory functions for programmatic construction of ROSE AST nodes. The nfi variants are intended for use in code generation and transformation contexts where source provenance is not required or not available.
The actual initialization logic is delegated to initializeIfStmt, which handles parent pointer setup and other structural requirements of the ROSE AST.

Builds an imaginary type node in the ROSE abstract syntax tree.

The imaginary type is built by wrapping a given base type within the SgTypeImaginary structure. This function is part of the ROSE SageBuilder interface, which provides factory methods for constructing AST nodes programmatically.

Internally, the function allocates a new SgTypeImaginary object on the heap, passing the provided base type as its argument. Assertions are used to verify that the base type is non-null and that the resulting object is successfully allocated before returning.

base_typeA pointer to the SgType that serves as the base type for the imaginary type being constructed. This parameter must not be NULL. Typically, this would be a floating-point type such as float, double, or long double.

Passing a NULL pointer for base_type will trigger a failed assertion and abort the program. Always ensure the base type is a valid, non-null SgType pointer before calling this function.

Builds an AST node representing a purely imaginary complex value with a long double imaginary part.

This function constructs a new SgComplexVal node in the ROSE abstract syntax tree (AST) that represents a complex number whose real part is zero and whose imaginary part is the specified long double value. Internally, the function creates a SgComplexVal node by passing a NULL real component, a newly constructed SgLongDoubleVal node for the imaginary component, and a SgTypeLongDouble type. The parent pointer of the imaginary value child node is explicitly set to the newly created SgComplexVal node to maintain proper parent-child relationships within the AST. The caller is responsible for integrating the returned node into the AST properly. Failing to attach the node to a valid parent in the AST may result in memory leaks or inconsistent AST structure.

Postcondition
The returned SgComplexVal node has a non-NULL imaginary value child node.
The imaginary value child node's parent pointer is set to the returned SgComplexVal node.
The returned node has its source position information set to indicate a transformation origin.
Note
The real part of the resulting SgComplexVal node is set to NULL, indicating that this node represents a purely imaginary value with no explicit real component.

After construction, the result is asserted to be non-null before being returned.

If kind_expr is non-NULL, it must be a valid, well-formed SgExpression node that is safe to attach to a type node.

The caller is responsible for managing the lifetime of the returned SgTypeInt node within the broader AST memory management scheme used by ROSE.

SgIntVal * SageBuilder::buildIntVal ( int value)

Builds and returns a new SgIntVal AST node representing an integer literal.

This function constructs a new SgIntVal node in the ROSE abstract syntax tree (AST), representing an integer constant with the given numeric value. The node is allocated on the heap, initialized with the provided integer value and an empty string representation, and assigned a default source position suitable for compiler-generated (transformation) nodes. The function asserts that allocation succeeds before returning.

Internally, the function performs the following steps:

  1. Allocates a new SgIntVal node initialized with the given integer value and an empty string for its value string representation.
  2. Asserts that the newly created node is non-null using ASSERT_not_null.
  3. Calls setOneSourcePositionForTransformation to mark the node as a transformation artifact with a synthetic source position.
  4. Returns the fully initialized SgIntVal node.

valueThe integer value to be stored in the newly created SgIntVal AST node.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created and initialized SgIntVal AST node representing the given integer value.
Warning
The caller is responsible for managing the lifetime of the returned SgIntVal node. If the node is not attached to an AST, it must be explicitly deleted to avoid memory leaks.

The ROSE infrastructure must be properly initialized before calling this function.
Postcondition
The returned SgIntVal pointer is non-null.
The returned node has a synthetic source position set via setOneSourcePositionForTransformation, marking it as a transformation node.
The returned node stores the integer value provided by the caller.
Note
The string representation of the integer value stored in the node is initialized to an empty string. If a specific string representation is required (e.g., for pretty-printing), it may need to be set separately after construction.

For negative values, the string is formed by prepending a minus sign to the hexadecimal representation of the absolute value, preserving the sign in the textual form.

A pointer to the newly constructed SgJovialTableStatement AST node representing the Jovial table declaration.
Warning
The returned pointer must not be used if the underlying buildClassDeclarationStatement_nfi helper fails to produce a valid node, as the function asserts the validity of the first non-defining declaration internally.
Precondition
The name parameter should represent a valid, non-empty identifier for the table being declared.
The kind parameter should be a valid SgClassDeclaration::class_types enumeration value appropriate for a Jovial table structure.
Postcondition
The returned SgJovialTableStatement node has source position information set for transformation purposes on both the defining and first non-defining declarations.
The first non-defining declaration of the returned node is guaranteed to be non-NULL.
Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface for constructing Jovial-specific AST nodes. It is intended for use when building or transforming ASTs that involve the Jovial programming language.
Source positions are set using setOneSourcePositionForTransformation, which marks the nodes as compiler-generated transformations rather than original source locations.

◆ buildJovialTableType()

SgJovialTableType * SageBuilder::buildJovialTableType ( const SgName & name,
SgType * base_type,
SgExprListExp * dim_info,
SgScopeStatement * scope )

Builds a Jovial table type along with its required class definition and both defining and nondefining declarations.

This function constructs a complete SgJovialTableType node representing a Jovial table type in the ROSE abstract syntax tree (AST). It performs the following steps:

  1. Derives an internal type name from the provided name. If a base type is supplied, the name is mangled by prepending "_table_of_" to distinguish the table type from the base type. If the dimension information contains subscript expressions, the address of the dim_info node is appended to the mangled name to ensure uniqueness across different table types.
  2. Creates a class declaration statement of kind e_jovial_table using a templated internal builder (buildClassDeclarationStatement_nfi) scoped to the provided scope. Both the defining declaration and its first nondefining declaration are assigned transformation source positions.
  3. Sets the parent of the nondefining declaration to the defining declaration, as required for type declarations in the ROSE IR.
  4. Retrieves the SgJovialTableType from the class declaration and populates it with the base type, dimension information, and rank (number of subscript expressions). The dim_info node's parent is set to the table type, and the nondefining declaration's type is updated to reference the constructed table type.

This function is intended for use when constructing Jovial table types programmatically during AST construction or transformation.

Parameters
nameThe name to associate with the Jovial table type. If a base type is provided, this name is mangled internally to avoid conflicts.
base_typeA pointer to the base SgType of the table. May be NULL if the table type has no base type. When non-NULL, name mangling is applied.
dim_infoA pointer to an SgExprListExp node containing the dimension/subscript expressions that define the shape of the table. Must not be NULL. If the expression list is non-empty, its address is used to further disambiguate the mangled type name.
scopeA pointer to the SgScopeStatement in which the table type declaration is to be placed. Used to correctly scope the generated declarations.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgJovialTableType node, fully initialized with its base type, dimension information, rank, and associated declarations.
Precondition
dim_info must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an SgExprListExp node.
scope should be a valid scope statement appropriate for receiving a class-like declaration.
If base_type is non-NULL, it must be a valid, fully constructed SgType node.
Postcondition
The returned SgJovialTableType has its base type, dimension information, and rank set.
The nondefining declaration's parent is set to the defining declaration.
The nondefining declaration's type is updated to reference the returned table type.
The dim_info node's parent is set to the returned table type.
Both the defining and nondefining declarations have transformation source positions assigned.
Warning
This function uses ROSE_ASSERT to verify internal invariants. If the nondefining declaration or the resulting SgJovialTableType cannot be retrieved, the program will abort at runtime.
The name mangling strategy relies on the memory address of dim_info when subscripts are present. This means type names are not stable across separate compilation runs or invocations where the address may differ.
Note
This function is specific to the Jovial language frontend in ROSE and should not be used for constructing table types in other language contexts.
The rank of the table type is derived automatically from the number of expressions in dim_info at the time of construction.

◆ buildLabelStatement()

SgLabelStatement * SageBuilder::buildLabelStatement ( const SgName & name,
SgStatement * stmt,
SgScopeStatement * scope )

Builds and returns a new SgLabelStatement node with the given label name and optional associated statement.

This function constructs an SgLabelStatement AST node representing a labeled statement in the intermediate representation used by ROSE. The label is identified by the provided SgName, and an optional SgStatement may be associated with it as the labeled target. An optional scope may also be provided to resolve label symbols correctly.

If no scope is provided, the function uses the top of the current scope stack via SageBuilder::topScopeStack(). After creating the label statement node, the function sets a default source position for transformation purposes using setOneSourcePositionForTransformation().

If the associated statement is non-null, its parent pointer is set to the newly created SgLabelStatement to maintain proper parent-child relationships in the AST.

Special handling is applied for Fortran code: SgLabelStatement is used to represent CONTINUE statements in Fortran, and in that context it has no inherent association with a label symbol. The label symbol association for Fortran is deferred to SageInterface::setNumericalLabel(). For non-Fortran languages, fixLabelStatement() is called to properly register the label symbol within the given scope.

Note that the parent of the returned SgLabelStatement is not set by this function. Setting the parent is intentionally deferred until the statement is inserted into the AST, typically via append_statement() or a similar utility.

Parameters
nameThe label name to assign to the new SgLabelStatement. This is used as the identifier for the label in the AST and for symbol table registration in non-Fortran languages.
stmtAn optional pointer to the SgStatement that the label is associated with. Defaults to NULL. If non-null, its parent is set to the new label statement.
scopeAn optional pointer to the enclosing SgScopeStatement used for label symbol fixup in non-Fortran languages. Defaults to NULL, in which case the top of the current scope stack is used.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgLabelStatement node. The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-null.
Precondition
If scope is NULL, the scope stack must be non-empty so that topScopeStack() can return a valid scope.
If stmt is non-null, it must be a valid, allocated SgStatement object.
Postcondition
The returned SgLabelStatement has its source position set for transformation.
If stmt is non-null, stmt->get_parent() returns the newly created SgLabelStatement.
For non-Fortran languages, the label symbol is registered in the provided or inferred scope.
The parent of the returned SgLabelStatement is not set; it must be set by the caller when inserting the statement into the AST.
Warning
For Fortran code, label symbol association is not performed by this function. Callers must use SageInterface::setNumericalLabel() to associate a numerical label symbol with the returned SgLabelStatement in Fortran contexts.
Note
The function uses ROSE_ASSERT to verify that the newly created SgLabelStatement is non-null, providing a runtime check against allocation failure.
Deferring parent assignment until append_statement() or an equivalent call is by design, to allow flexible AST construction workflows.

Builds a label statement node without full initialization (nfi), suitable for use in transformation contexts.

This function constructs a new SgLabelStatement AST node using the provided label name and an optional associated statement. Unlike its fully-initializing counterpart, this "no full initialization" (nfi) variant defers certain setup steps, such as setting the parent pointer, to allow the caller to complete the attachment process later via functions like append_statement() or similar utilities.

The function allocates a new SgLabelStatement on the heap, sets a transformation source position on it, and optionally sets the parent of the associated statement to the newly created label statement. If a scope is provided, fixLabelStatement() is called to properly register the label within that scope's symbol table and perform any necessary fixups.

The parent of the returned SgLabelStatement itself is intentionally left unset at this stage. Callers are responsible for inserting the node into the AST and setting its parent appropriately.

scopeAn optional pointer to the enclosing SgScopeStatement. If provided, fixLabelStatement() is invoked to register the label within the scope. Defaults to NULL.

The parent pointer of the returned SgLabelStatement is not set by this function. Failing to attach the returned node to the AST properly may result in an incomplete or inconsistent AST.

The name parameter must represent a valid, non-empty label name appropriate for the target language being compiled.
If stmt is non-null, it must be a valid, heap-allocated SgStatement node that has not already been assigned a parent, or whose parent reassignment is intentional.
If scope is non-null, it must point to a valid SgScopeStatement that is part of a well-formed AST.

A new SgLabelStatement node is allocated and its source position is set to a transformation position.
If stmt is non-null, stmt->get_parent() returns the newly created SgLabelStatement.
If scope is non-null, the label is registered within the given scope via fixLabelStatement().
The parent of the returned SgLabelStatement is not set; it remains null until the caller attaches it to the AST.

This function is intended for use in AST transformation contexts where deferred parent assignment is necessary. For standard AST construction where full initialization is desired, consider using the fully-initializing variant of buildLabelStatement().
The source position of the new node is set using setOneSourcePositionForTransformation(), marking it as a compiler-generated (transformation) node rather than one derived from user source code.

Builds and returns a new SgLambdaCapture AST node representing a single capture entry in a C++ lambda expression.

This function constructs an SgLambdaCapture node, which models an individual capture clause within a C++ lambda expression. Lambda captures describe how variables from the enclosing scope are made available inside the lambda body, either by value or by reference.

The function allocates a new SgLambdaCapture object on the heap, passing the provided expressions for the captured variable, the source closure variable, and the closure variable as constructor arguments. The first argument to the SgLambdaCapture constructor is set to NULL, which typically corresponds to an optional parent or file-info parameter handled separately. After construction, an assertion verifies that allocation succeeded.

Source position information is then applied to the newly created node via setSourcePosition, which sets default or compiler-generated location data appropriate for builder-constructed nodes.

closure_variableAn SgExpression pointer representing the closure variable as it appears within the lambda body or the generated closure object.

Precondition
capture_variable, source_closure_variable, and closure_variable should be valid SgExpression pointers or NULL, consistent with the intended capture semantics.
Postcondition
The returned SgLambdaCapture node is fully constructed and has its source position information initialized via setSourcePosition.
The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-NULL; an assertion failure will terminate the program if memory allocation fails.
Warning
Passing invalid or dangling SgExpression pointers for any of the expression arguments may lead to undefined behavior or assertion failures during subsequent AST processing.
Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface, which provides factory functions for constructing ROSE AST nodes in a consistent and safe manner.
The first parameter of the SgLambdaCapture constructor is passed as NULL; this is intentional and consistent with the builder pattern used throughout SageBuilder, where parent linkage and file info are set separately after node construction.

This function constructs a new SgMatrixExp AST node representing a matrix expression, typically used in matrix literal syntax (such as that found in MATLAB-style languages supported by ROSE). The provided SgExprListExp node is appended as the first row of the resulting matrix expression. Source position information is set using the transformation source position helper, marking the node as compiler-generated or transformed code rather than originating from user source.

The function allocates a new SgMatrixExp on the heap, sets its source position for transformation tracking, and appends the given expression list as the initial row. An assertion is performed to verify that the allocation succeeded before returning.

Parameters
firstRowA pointer to an SgExprListExp node representing the first row of the matrix expression. This node is appended directly into the newly created SgMatrixExp.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgMatrixExp node with the first row populated.
Precondition
firstRow must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgExprListExp node.
The ROSE AST infrastructure must be properly initialized before calling this function.
Postcondition
The returned SgMatrixExp node contains firstRow as its first appended expression.
The returned node has its source position set to a transformation position.
Warning
The caller is responsible for managing the lifetime of the returned SgMatrixExp node and ensuring it is properly inserted into the AST or deleted to avoid memory leaks.
Note
This function uses SageInterface::setOneSourcePositionForTransformation to mark the created node as a transformation artifact, which is the standard practice for AST nodes generated programmatically rather than parsed from source code.
Only the first row is added by this function. Additional rows must be appended separately after the node is created if a multi-row matrix is needed.

Builds a matrix type node for use in Matlab language constructs.

This function allocates and initializes a new SgTypeMatrix node, which represents the matrix type used in Matlab source code representations within the ROSE compiler infrastructure. The function uses dynamic allocation via the new operator to create the type node and verifies successful allocation before returning the result.

SgTypeMatrix is part of the ROSE abstract syntax tree (AST) type hierarchy and is specifically intended to support Matlab's native matrix data type. This builder function follows the standard ROSE SageBuilder pattern for constructing AST type nodes programmatically.

Returns
A pointer to a newly allocated SgTypeMatrix node representing the Matlab matrix type.
Warning
The caller is responsible for managing the lifetime of the returned SgTypeMatrix object. Improper management may lead to memory leaks if the node is not properly attached to an AST or explicitly deleted.
