The ROSE infrastructure must be properly initialized before calling this function.
Postcondition
A valid, non-null SgTypeMatrix object is allocated and returned. The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-null due to the internal assertion check.
Note
This function is intended for use when constructing or transforming Matlab ASTs within the ROSE framework. It should not be used for C, C++, or Fortran type construction, as SgTypeMatrix is specific to the Matlab language frontend.

◆ buildMemberFunctionCall() [1/2]

SgFunctionCallExp * SageBuilder::buildMemberFunctionCall ( SgExpression * objectExpression,
SgMemberFunctionSymbol * functionSymbol,
SgExprListExp * params )

Builds a member function call expression given an object expression, a member function symbol, and a parameter list.

This function constructs an AST node representing a member function call of the form object.memberFunction(args), where the object and the member function are already known and represented by their respective AST nodes or symbols. It is intended for use when both the variable reference (object expression) and the member function symbol are available, such as when building a call like a.size().

Internally, the function first creates a member function reference expression (SgMemberFunctionRefExp) from the provided function symbol using buildMemberFunctionRefExp, with both the virtual and pointer-to-member flags set to false. It then constructs a dot expression (SgDotExp) combining the object expression and the member function reference. Finally, it wraps the dot expression and the parameter list into a full function call expression (SgFunctionCallExp) using buildFunctionCallExp.

Parameters
objectExpressionA pointer to the SgExpression representing the object on which the member function is to be called (e.g., the variable a in a.size()). Must be a valid, non-null expression node.
functionSymbolA pointer to the SgMemberFunctionSymbol representing the member function to be called (e.g., the symbol for size). Must be a valid, non-null symbol corresponding to an existing member function.
paramsA pointer to an SgExprListExp containing the list of arguments to pass to the member function. May be an empty list for functions that take no arguments, but must not be null.
Returns
A pointer to a newly constructed SgFunctionCallExp node representing the complete member function call expression, including the dot expression and the argument list.
Precondition
objectExpression must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgExpression node.
functionSymbol must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgMemberFunctionSymbol.
params must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgExprListExp node.
Postcondition
The returned SgFunctionCallExp node represents a syntactically correct member function call of the form objectExpression.functionSymbol(params).
The returned node is suitable for insertion into the AST.
Warning
Passing null pointers for any of the parameters results in undefined behavior and may cause a crash or produce a malformed AST node.
Note
This overload is specifically designed for cases where both the object expression and the member function symbol are already known. For cases where only a string name is available, alternative overloads of buildMemberFunctionCall should be used instead.
The member function reference is built with both the virtual dispatch flag and the pointer-to-member flag set to false.

◆ buildMemberFunctionCall() [2/2]

SgFunctionCallExp * SageBuilder::buildMemberFunctionCall ( std::string className,
SgExpression * objectExpression,
std::string functionName,
SgExprListExp * params,
SgScopeStatement * scope )

Builds an AST node representing a member function call expression.

This function constructs an SgFunctionCallExp node that represents a call to a member function of a named class, using a dot expression (object.memberFunction(args)) as the call target. The function performs the following steps internally:

  1. Looks up the class symbol corresponding to the given class name by searching parent scopes starting from the provided scope.
  2. Retrieves the defining declaration of the class and obtains its class definition.
  3. Looks up the member function symbol by name within the class definition's scope.
  4. Builds a member function reference expression (SgMemberFunctionRefExp) from the resolved symbol.
  5. Constructs a dot expression combining the object expression and the member function reference, then wraps it in a function call expression with the provided argument list.

This builder is useful when programmatically generating or transforming code that invokes a member function on an existing object expression, particularly in ROSE-based source-to-source transformation tools.

Parameters
classNameThe name of the class that owns the member function to be called. This name is used to look up the corresponding class symbol in the enclosing scopes.
objectExpressionA pointer to the expression representing the object on which the member function is to be called. This becomes the left-hand side of the generated dot expression.
functionNameThe name of the member function to be called. This is looked up within the class definition's scope.
paramsA pointer to an SgExprListExp node containing the list of argument expressions to be passed to the member function call.
scopeA pointer to the scope statement used as the starting point for symbol lookups of both the class and the member function.
Returns
A pointer to a newly constructed SgFunctionCallExp node representing the member function call expression of the form objectExpression.functionName(params).
Warning
This function uses ROSE_ASSERT to validate intermediate results. If the class symbol, class declaration, class definition, or member function symbol cannot be resolved, the program will abort at runtime. Ensure that all referenced symbols are visible and properly declared before calling this function.
Precondition
className must correspond to a class that is declared and visible in the parent scopes reachable from scope.
objectExpression must be a valid, non-null pointer to an expression node whose type is compatible with the named class.
functionName must correspond to a member function declared within the class identified by className.
params must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgExprListExp node, even if the argument list is empty.
scope must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgScopeStatement that provides the starting context for symbol resolution.
Postcondition
The returned SgFunctionCallExp node is fully constructed and connected to the provided object expression and argument list.
The internal dot expression and member function reference expression are created as child nodes of the returned call expression.
Note
This function only supports member function calls using dot notation. It does not handle arrow notation (pointer-to-object member access) or calls through base class pointers requiring virtual dispatch adjustments at the AST level.
The member function reference is built with both template and virtual flags set to false via the call to buildMemberFunctionRefExp.

◆ buildMemberFunctionRefExp()

SgMemberFunctionRefExp * SageBuilder::buildMemberFunctionRefExp ( SgMemberFunctionSymbol * sym,
bool virtual_call,
bool need_qualifier )

Builds an SgMemberFunctionRefExp node representing a reference to a member function.

This builder function constructs a new SgMemberFunctionRefExp AST node that represents a reference to a member function within the ROSE intermediate representation. The node is initialized with the provided member function symbol, a flag indicating whether the call is virtual, and a flag indicating whether a qualifier is needed. After construction, the node's source position is set using setOneSourcePositionForTransformation to mark it as a compiler-generated transformation node rather than one originating from user source code. An assertion is performed to ensure the node was successfully allocated before it is returned.

Parameters
symPointer to the SgMemberFunctionSymbol that this reference expression will refer to. Must not be null and must represent a valid member function symbol in the current AST context.
virtual_callA boolean flag indicating whether the member function call should be treated as a virtual dispatch. Pass true for virtual calls and false for non-virtual (direct) calls.
need_qualifierA boolean flag indicating whether a class qualifier is required in the generated expression (e.g., ClassName::method). Pass true if the qualifier must appear explicitly.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgMemberFunctionRefExp node. The caller is responsible for inserting this node into the AST at the appropriate location.
Warning
The returned node is heap-allocated. Failing to attach it to the AST or properly manage its lifetime may result in memory leaks. Do not pass a null sym pointer; doing so results in undefined behavior.
Precondition
sym must be a non-null pointer to a valid SgMemberFunctionSymbol that exists within the current AST.
The ROSE AST infrastructure must be properly initialized before calling this function.
Postcondition
The returned SgMemberFunctionRefExp node has its source position set to indicate a compiler-generated transformation.
The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-null (enforced by an internal assertion).
Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface, which provides factory functions for constructing ROSE AST nodes programmatically during source-to-source transformations.
The parent pointer of the newly created node is set to NULL and must be updated when the node is inserted into the AST.

◆ buildMemberFunctionRefExp_nfi()

SgMemberFunctionRefExp * SageBuilder::buildMemberFunctionRefExp_nfi ( SgMemberFunctionSymbol * sym,
bool virtual_call,
bool need_qualifier )

Builds a member function reference expression node without file information.

This function constructs a new SgMemberFunctionRefExp AST node representing a reference to a member function, using the provided member function symbol and associated flags. The suffix "_nfi" indicates that no file information is attached to the resulting node; the source position is explicitly set to null via setOneSourcePositionNull(). The newly created node is allocated on the heap and returned to the caller. An assertion is performed to verify that the allocation succeeded before returning.

The function sets the virtual call flag and the qualifier requirement flag directly on the constructed node. The third constructor argument (the qualifier expression) is passed as NULL, meaning no explicit qualifier expression is attached at construction time.

Parameters
symPointer to the SgMemberFunctionSymbol that the reference expression will refer to. Must not be NULL and must represent a valid member function symbol in the symbol table.
virtual_callA boolean flag indicating whether the member function call should be treated as a virtual dispatch. Pass true for virtual calls and false for non-virtual (direct) calls.
need_qualifierA boolean flag indicating whether an explicit qualifier is required when generating code for this reference expression. Pass true if the qualifier must be emitted, false otherwise.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgMemberFunctionRefExp node with its source position set to null. The caller is responsible for managing the lifetime of the returned object within the AST.
Precondition
sym must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid SgMemberFunctionSymbol.
The ROSE AST infrastructure must be properly initialized before calling this function.
Postcondition
The returned SgMemberFunctionRefExp node has its source position set to null.
The returned node's virtual call flag is set to the value of virtual_call.
The returned node's need_qualifier flag is set to the value of need_qualifier.
The qualifier expression of the returned node is NULL.
Warning
The returned pointer must not be used after the owning AST has been destroyed, as the node's memory is managed by the AST.
Passing a NULL value for sym will result in undefined behavior, as no NULL check is performed on sym before use.
Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface for constructing AST nodes programmatically. The "_nfi" naming convention is used throughout SageBuilder to denote builder functions that do not attach file information to the created node.
The internal ROSE_ASSERT after allocation will abort execution if memory allocation fails, rather than returning NULL.

◆ buildMemberFunctionType() [1/2]

SgMemberFunctionType * SageBuilder::buildMemberFunctionType ( SgType * return_type,
SgFunctionParameterTypeList * typeList,
SgScopeStatement * struct_name,
unsigned int mfunc_specifier )

Builds an SgMemberFunctionType node from a return type, parameter type list, enclosing scope, and member function specifier.

This function constructs an SgMemberFunctionType representing a C++ member function type. It accepts an SgScopeStatement as the enclosing scope, which may be either an SgClassDefinition or an SgDeclarationScope. From this scope, the function resolves the associated class declaration or nonreal declaration to obtain the underlying class type.

Internally, the function performs the following steps:

  1. Validates that both return_type and struct_name are non-null and that struct_name has a valid parent node.
  2. Attempts to cast struct_name to either an SgClassDefinition or an SgDeclarationScope. If neither cast succeeds, an error is reported and execution is aborted.
  3. Resolves the associated declaration statement from the class definition or declaration scope.
  4. Determines the class type from either an SgClassDeclaration or an SgNonrealDecl.
  5. Delegates to the overloaded buildMemberFunctionType() variant that accepts an SgType* for the class type directly, rather than an SgScopeStatement*.

This design ensures that the resulting SgMemberFunctionType is consistent with the global function type table, avoiding duplicate type nodes and resolving subtle C++-specific issues that arise with the build interface, particularly when used with EDG 4.3 and later.

Parameters
return_typeThe return type of the member function. Must not be NULL.
typeListThe list of parameter types for the member function. A NULL value is tolerated but will trigger a warning message.
struct_nameThe enclosing scope statement, expected to be either an SgClassDefinition or an SgDeclarationScope. Must not be NULL and must have a valid parent node.
mfunc_specifierAn unsigned integer encoding member function specifiers such as const, volatile, or virtual qualifiers.
Returns
A pointer to the constructed or looked-up SgMemberFunctionType node representing the member function type.
Warning
If struct_name cannot be cast to either SgClassDefinition or SgDeclarationScope, an error message is printed and the program aborts via ROSE_ABORT().
If typeList is NULL, a warning message is printed to standard output. The function continues execution but the resulting type will have no parameter type information.
If neither an SgClassDeclaration nor an SgNonrealDecl can be resolved from the declaration, the program aborts via ROSE_ABORT().
Precondition
return_type must not be NULL.
struct_name must not be NULL.
struct_name->get_parent() must not be NULL.
struct_name must be castable to either SgClassDefinition or SgDeclarationScope.
The declaration resolved from struct_name must be either an SgClassDeclaration or an SgNonrealDecl.
Postcondition
The returned SgMemberFunctionType is registered in the global function type table and is consistent with any previously built equivalent member function type.
The returned pointer is non-NULL.
Note
This function is a convenience overload that accepts an SgScopeStatement* for the enclosing class scope. It internally resolves the class type and delegates to the overloaded variant that accepts an SgType* directly.
The ref_qualifiers parameter (lvalue/rvalue reference qualifiers) is not used by this function. If ref_qualifiers support is needed, use the appropriate overload.
This function was refactored to delegate to a lower-level buildMemberFunctionType() overload, improving maintainability and fixing subtle type-table consistency issues introduced by the EDG 4.3 front-end connection to ROSE.

◆ buildMemberFunctionType() [2/2]

SgMemberFunctionType * SageBuilder::buildMemberFunctionType ( SgType * return_type,
SgFunctionParameterTypeList * typeList,
SgType * classType,
unsigned int mfunc_specifier )

Builds or retrieves a SgMemberFunctionType node representing a C++ member function type.

This function constructs a SgMemberFunctionType from the given return type, parameter type list, class type, and member function specifier flags. It is a refactored variant of the broader buildMemberFunctionType() family, specifically designed to accept a SgType pointer for the class type rather than a SgClassDefinition, enabling a cleaner separation of concerns.

The function first queries the global function type table (SgFunctionTypeTable) using a mangled name derived from the provided arguments via SgMemberFunctionType::get_mangled(). If a matching type already exists in the table, that cached type is returned directly and any newly allocated type is discarded, ensuring type uniqueness across the AST.

If no matching type is found in the global table, a temporary SgPartialFunctionType is constructed using the return type, class type, and member function specifier. The provided SgFunctionParameterTypeList is attached to this partial type, which is then passed to SgMemberFunctionType::createType() to produce the final SgMemberFunctionType. After creation, the SgPartialFunctionType is cleaned up and deleted. The newly created SgMemberFunctionType is then registered in the global function type table for future reuse.

Parameters
return_typeThe return type of the member function. May be NULL in some contexts, though non-NULL is generally expected for well-formed types.
typeListThe list of parameter types for the member function. Must not be NULL.
classTypeThe class type to which the member function belongs. May be NULL in certain degenerate or template-related contexts.
mfunc_specifierA bitmask of member function specifier flags (e.g., const, volatile, virtual) that characterize the member function type.
Returns
A pointer to the SgMemberFunctionType representing the described member function type. The returned pointer is either a newly created and registered type or an existing type retrieved from the global function type table.
Warning
The returned SgMemberFunctionType pointer must not be deleted by the caller, as it is owned and managed by the global function type table. Deleting it would corrupt the type table and lead to undefined behavior.
If a type with the same mangled name already exists in the global type table, the newly constructed type is deleted internally and the cached type is returned. Callers should not retain raw pointers to intermediate objects created during this process.
Precondition
typeList must not be NULL.
The global function type table (SgNode::get_globalFunctionTypeTable()) must be initialized and non-NULL before this function is called.
Postcondition
The returned SgMemberFunctionType is registered in the global function type table under its mangled name.
The SgFunctionParameterTypeList pointed to by typeList has its parent set to the returned SgMemberFunctionType.
Any temporary SgPartialFunctionType created internally is deleted before the function returns.
Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface for constructing ROSE IR nodes and is intended to be used during AST construction or transformation passes.
The ref_qualifiers parameter present in earlier versions of this function has been removed as of a later refactoring (circa October 2022), and the mfunc_specifier is expected to encode all necessary qualifier information.
For Fortran support, an optional type kind expression is internally set to NULL, as this function targets C++ member function types only.

Builds a modifier type node wrapping a given base type.

This function constructs a new SgModifierType node that wraps the provided base type. It first allocates a new SgModifierType object using the supplied base type, then attempts to insert it into the global type table via SgModifierType::insertModifierTypeIntoTypeTable(). If an equivalent SgModifierType already exists in the type table, the newly allocated object is discarded and the pre-existing type table entry is returned instead. This deduplication mechanism ensures that equivalent modifier types share a single canonical representation within the IR, which is important for type consistency across the AST.

A warning message is printed to standard output if a previously built SgModifierType is reused from the global type table, which may indicate potential issues in contexts involving complex template instantiations or boost-style template patterns.

Parameters
base_typePointer to the SgType that serves as the base type for the modifier type being constructed. Must not be NULL.
Returns
A pointer to the resulting SgModifierType node. This may be a newly allocated object or a pre-existing object retrieved from the global type table. The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-NULL and distinct from base_type.
Warning
If a matching SgModifierType already exists in the global type table, the newly created object is deleted and the existing one is returned. Callers must not retain or use any pointer to the intermediate object created during this call. Reuse of a previously built modifier type may indicate a subtle issue in template-heavy code (e.g., boost template patterns).
Precondition
base_type must not be NULL.
base_type must point to a valid, fully initialized SgType object.
Postcondition
The returned SgModifierType pointer is non-NULL.
The returned SgModifierType pointer is distinct from base_type.
The returned SgModifierType is registered in the global type table.
Note
This function uses the global type table (via SgModifierType::insertModifierTypeIntoTypeTable()) to deduplicate modifier types. The default value of base_type in the original declaration is NULL, but the implementation enforces that a non-NULL value must be provided at the call site.

◆ buildModuleStatement()

SgModuleStatement * SageBuilder::buildModuleStatement ( const SgName & name,
SgScopeStatement * scope )

Builds a Fortran module declaration node in the ROSE AST.

This function constructs an SgModuleStatement representing a Fortran MODULE declaration and inserts it into the AST. Internally, it delegates to the templated helper buildClassDeclarationStatement_nfi using the class kind SgClassDeclaration::e_fortran_module, which handles the creation of both the defining and non-defining declaration nodes. After construction, source position information is set for transformation purposes on both the module statement itself and its first non-defining declaration, ensuring that the generated nodes are properly marked as compiler-generated transformations rather than originating from user source code.

The function asserts that the first non-defining declaration of the resulting module statement is not NULL before applying source position information to it.

Parameters
nameThe name of the Fortran module to be declared. This is used as the identifier for the resulting SgModuleStatement node.
scopeThe enclosing scope in which the module declaration is to be placed. If NULL, the current scope maintained by the SageBuilder infrastructure is used as the default.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgModuleStatement node representing the Fortran module declaration.
Precondition
The name parameter must represent a valid, non-empty Fortran module identifier.
If scope is non-NULL, it must point to a valid and initialized SgScopeStatement node within the current AST.
Postcondition
The returned SgModuleStatement has source position information set for transformation.
The first non-defining declaration of the returned SgModuleStatement is non-NULL and also has source position information set for transformation.
The returned node is inserted into the specified scope or the current default scope if scope is NULL.
Warning
This function uses an internal assertion (ROSE_ASSERT) to verify that the first non-defining declaration is not NULL. If this assertion fails, the program will abort. Ensure that the underlying declaration builder correctly initializes the non-defining declaration.
Note
This function is specific to Fortran module constructs and relies on the SgClassDeclaration mechanism with the e_fortran_module kind to represent Fortran MODULE statements in the ROSE intermediate representation.
Source positions are set using setOneSourcePositionForTransformation, which marks the nodes as compiler-generated transformations rather than nodes originating from parsed source code.

◆ buildMultibyteNopStatement()

SgAsmStmt * SageBuilder::buildMultibyteNopStatement ( int n)

Builds a multi-byte NOP (no-operation) assembly statement of a specified byte length.

This function constructs an inline assembly statement node (SgAsmStmt) representing a multi-byte NOP instruction for x86 architectures. Multi-byte NOPs are used in code generation and optimization contexts where padding of a specific byte length is required without affecting program behavior.

The function supports NOP encodings from 1 to 9 bytes in length. Each encoding is selected via a switch statement based on the requested byte count:

  • 1 byte: the standard "nop" mnemonic
  • 2 bytes: raw byte sequence 0x66, 0x90
  • 3 bytes: "nopl (%eax)"
  • 4 bytes: "nopl 0x01(%eax)"
  • 5 bytes: raw byte sequence 0x0f, 0x1f, 0x44, 0x00, 0x00
  • 6 bytes: raw byte sequence 0x66, 0x0f, 0x1f, 0x44, 0x00, 0x00
  • 7 bytes: raw byte sequence 0x0f, 0x1f, 0x80, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00
  • 8 bytes: raw byte sequence 0x0f, 0x1f, 0x84, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00
  • 9 bytes: raw byte sequence 0x66, 0x0f, 0x1f, 0x84, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00

The raw byte sequences are expressed as ".byte" directives because mnemonic versions of the longer multi-byte NOP forms were found to be unreliable. Each case delegates to buildAsmStatement() to produce the corresponding SgAsmStmt AST node.

If a value outside the range 1 to 9 is provided, the function prints an error message and calls ROSE_ABORT() to terminate execution.

The byte string constants used internally are defined via define macros local to this function's translation unit.

Parameters
nThe desired byte length of the multi-byte NOP instruction. Must be a positive integer in the range 1 through 9 (inclusive).
Returns
A pointer to a newly constructed SgAsmStmt node representing the multi-byte NOP assembly statement of the requested byte length.
Precondition
n must be greater than 0. This is enforced by a ROSE_ASSERT at the start of the function.
n must be in the range 1 to 9 inclusive. Values outside this range cause the function to print an error and abort via ROSE_ABORT().
Postcondition
The returned pointer is non-NULL and points to a valid SgAsmStmt node representing a NOP instruction of exactly n bytes.
Warning
Values of n less than 1 or greater than 9 will cause program termination via ROSE_ABORT(). There is no graceful error recovery for out-of-range inputs.
Note
The multi-byte NOP encodings used here are specific to x86 and x86-64 architectures. Using this function in contexts targeting other architectures may produce incorrect or invalid assembly.
The mnemonic forms of some multi-byte NOPs were found to be unreliable during development, which is why raw ".byte" directive strings are used for encodings of 5 bytes and above (and for the 2-byte case as well).

◆ buildNamespaceAliasDeclarationStatement()

SgNamespaceAliasDeclarationStatement * SageBuilder::buildNamespaceAliasDeclarationStatement ( const SgName & name,
SgNamespaceDeclarationStatement * namespaceDeclaration )

Builds a namespace alias declaration statement node in the AST.

This function constructs a new SgNamespaceAliasDeclarationStatement node that represents a C++ namespace alias declaration of the form:

namespace name = original_namespace;

The newly created node is initialized with the provided alias name and the target namespace declaration. A single source position is assigned to the node to mark it as a transformation (i.e., compiler-generated code rather than code originating from a source file). The parent scope of the new node is set to the scope currently at the top of the SageBuilder scope stack, reflecting the lexical context in which the alias declaration is being introduced.

This function is part of the SageBuilder API, which provides factory functions for programmatically constructing ROSE AST nodes during source-to-source transformation tasks.

Parameters
nameThe alias name to be assigned to the namespace alias declaration. This is the new identifier by which the target namespace will be known within the current scope.
namespaceDeclarationA pointer to the original SgNamespaceDeclarationStatement that the alias refers to. This must be a valid, non-null pointer to an existing namespace declaration in the AST.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgNamespaceAliasDeclarationStatement node. The caller is responsible for ensuring the node is properly integrated into the AST if further manipulation is required.
Warning
The returned node is heap-allocated. Improper management of this node (e.g., failing to attach it to the AST or allowing it to be orphaned) may result in memory leaks or an inconsistent AST state.
Passing a null pointer for namespaceDeclaration results in undefined behavior, as the constructor and subsequent operations do not perform null checks.
Precondition
The SageBuilder scope stack must be non-empty so that topScopeStack() returns a valid enclosing scope to assign as the parent of the new node.
namespaceDeclaration must be a non-null pointer to a valid SgNamespaceDeclarationStatement node already present in the AST.
Postcondition
A new SgNamespaceAliasDeclarationStatement node is created with its name set to the provided alias, its referenced namespace set to namespaceDeclaration, its source position marked as a transformation, and its parent set to the current top scope on the SageBuilder scope stack.
Note
The source position of the created node is set using setOneSourcePositionForTransformation(), which marks the node as compiler-generated rather than originating from user source code.
The parent pointer is set to the top of the SageBuilder scope stack at the time of the call. If the node needs to be inserted into a different scope, the parent pointer should be updated accordingly after the call.

◆ buildNamespaceDeclaration()

SgNamespaceDeclarationStatement * SageBuilder::buildNamespaceDeclaration ( const SgName & name,
SgScopeStatement * scope )

Builds a namespace declaration statement node in the ROSE AST.

This function constructs a new SgNamespaceDeclarationStatement for a namespace identified by the given name, optionally within a specified scope. Internally, it delegates to buildNamespaceDeclaration_nfi() with the anonymous-namespace flag set to false, indicating that the namespace is a named (non-anonymous) namespace. After construction, source position information is set for the defining declaration and its associated first non-defining declaration using setOneSourcePositionForTransformation(), marking both nodes as compiler-generated or transformation-derived rather than originating from a physical source file.

The function asserts that the resulting declaration's first non-defining declaration is not NULL before applying source position information to it, ensuring structural integrity of the generated AST node.

Parameters
nameThe name of the namespace to be declared. This is a reference to an SgName object representing the identifier of the namespace.
scopeA pointer to the SgScopeStatement in which the namespace declaration will be placed. If NULL, the current scope context is used by default.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgNamespaceDeclarationStatement node representing the named namespace declaration, with source position information set for transformation purposes.
Precondition
The name parameter should be a valid, non-empty namespace identifier.
If scope is non-NULL, it must point to a valid and properly initialized SgScopeStatement in the AST.
Postcondition
The returned SgNamespaceDeclarationStatement has its source position set to indicate a compiler-generated transformation.
The first non-defining declaration associated with the returned node is non-NULL and also has its source position set for transformation.
Warning
The function contains a runtime assertion (ROSE_ASSERT) that the first non-defining declaration of the constructed node is not NULL. If this condition is not met, the program will abort.
Note
This function is intended for use in AST transformation and construction contexts where new namespace declarations need to be programmatically introduced. The resulting node is marked as a transformation artifact and will not correspond to any location in the original source file.

◆ buildNamespaceDeclaration_nfi()

SgNamespaceDeclarationStatement * SageBuilder::buildNamespaceDeclaration_nfi ( const SgName & name,
bool unnamednamespace,
SgScopeStatement * scope )

Builds a namespace declaration statement node in the ROSE abstract syntax tree (AST).

This function constructs a new SgNamespaceDeclarationStatement along with its associated SgNamespaceDefinitionStatement, properly wiring together the defining declaration, the non-defining declaration, and the global definition used to accumulate symbols across re-entrant namespace definitions.

The function first checks whether a namespace symbol with the given name already exists in the provided scope. If a matching symbol is found, the existing non-defining declaration is reused and the new namespace definition is linked into the chain of re-entrant namespace definitions via the previousNamespaceDefinition and nextNamespaceDefinition pointers. The global_definition pointer of the new definition is also set to point to the global definition of the existing namespace, ensuring that all re-entrant definitions share a single logical accumulation point for symbols.

If no existing symbol is found, a fresh non-defining declaration is created. A separate global_definition SgNamespaceDefinitionStatement is built and configured as a union of re-entrant namespace definitions. A new SgNamespaceSymbol is inserted into the scope's symbol table. The non-defining declaration is marked as a forward declaration and its parent is set to the given scope.

In both cases, the defining declaration's firstNondefiningDeclaration pointer is set to the non-defining declaration. The fixNamespaceDeclaration helper is called on both the non-defining and defining declarations to finalize their integration into the scope.

Note that for C++ namespaces, the definingDeclaration field is intentionally left NULL, which differs from the treatment of class declarations. Source position information is set to null for the defining declaration via setOneSourcePositionNull.

If the scope parameter is NULL on entry, the function attempts to use the top of the internal scope stack via SageBuilder::topScopeStack(). A warning is printed if the scope remains NULL after this fallback, as symbol table insertion will be skipped.

Parameters
nameThe name of the namespace to be declared.
unnamednamespaceA boolean flag indicating whether this is an unnamed (anonymous) namespace. Pass true for unnamed namespaces, false otherwise.
scopeThe enclosing scope in which the namespace declaration is to be inserted. If NULL, the function falls back to the top of the internal scope stack. A warning is emitted if the scope cannot be resolved.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgNamespaceDeclarationStatement representing the defining declaration of the namespace.
Warning
If scope is NULL and the internal scope stack is also empty, the function will fail an assertion. Callers should ensure a valid scope is available before invoking this function.
For C++ namespaces, the definingDeclaration field of the returned node is always NULL by design. Do not assume it follows the same convention as class declarations.
If the existing namespace symbol's definition does not have a valid global_definition, the function will trigger an assertion failure and print an error message. This indicates an inconsistency in the AST that must be corrected before calling this function.
Precondition
If scope is non-NULL, it must be a valid, fully initialized SgScopeStatement node with a functional symbol table.
If a namespace symbol with the given name already exists in scope, its declaration and associated definition must be non-NULL and properly linked, including a non-NULL global_definition pointer.
Postcondition
The returned SgNamespaceDeclarationStatement has a non-NULL definition and a non-NULL firstNondefiningDeclaration.
The returned declaration's definition has a non-NULL global_definition that points to itself (i.e., global_definition->get_global_definition() == global_definition).
The definingDeclaration of the returned node is NULL.
If scope was non-NULL, a SgNamespaceSymbol for the given name is present in the scope's symbol table (either pre-existing or newly inserted).
The non-defining declaration is marked as a forward declaration via setForward().
Note
This is a "no frills interface" (nfi) builder function, meaning it performs minimal source position setup. The defining declaration's source position is set to null using setOneSourcePositionNull rather than a transformation marker.
Re-entrant namespace definitions (multiple definitions of the same namespace) are linked together through the previousNamespaceDefinition and nextNamespaceDefinition pointer chain on SgNamespaceDefinitionStatement.
The global_definition of a namespace definition is self-referential: it points to itself and serves as the canonical accumulation point for all symbols belonging to the logical namespace across translation units or re-entrant definitions.
The fixNamespaceDeclaration helper is called on both the non-defining and defining declarations when a valid scope is available, to finalize scope and parent linkage.

◆ buildNamespaceDefinition()

SgNamespaceDefinitionStatement * SageBuilder::buildNamespaceDefinition ( SgNamespaceDeclarationStatement * d)

Builds and returns a new SgNamespaceDefinitionStatement node associated with the given namespace declaration.

This function constructs a new SgNamespaceDefinitionStatement AST node intended to represent the body (definition) of a C++ namespace. It accepts a pointer to an existing SgNamespaceDeclarationStatement as the owning declaration. If the provided declaration pointer is non-NULL, the newly created definition node has its parent set to the given declaration, which mirrors the behavior of set_declaration() in this context. If the provided pointer is NULL, the definition node is still created but no parent relationship is established, avoiding a segmentation fault that would otherwise occur if NULL were passed directly to the constructor without this guard. After construction, a single source position is assigned to the result to mark it as a transformation node, and the result is verified to be non-NULL via an assertion.

Parameters
dA pointer to the SgNamespaceDeclarationStatement that owns this namespace definition. May be NULL, in which case the definition is created without a parent declaration. Passing NULL is handled safely within this function, unlike direct construction.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgNamespaceDefinitionStatement node. This pointer is guaranteed to be non-NULL upon return, as enforced by an internal assertion.
Warning
Passing NULL for the declaration parameter results in a namespace definition node with no associated parent declaration. This may lead to incomplete or inconsistent AST structure if the caller does not subsequently set the parent relationship manually.
Precondition
The ROSE infrastructure must be properly initialized before calling this function.
Postcondition
The returned SgNamespaceDefinitionStatement node is non-NULL.
If d is non-NULL, the returned node has its parent set to d.
The returned node has a source position assigned via setOneSourcePositionForTransformation, marking it as a transformation-generated node.
Note
The comment in the implementation notes that the SgNamespaceDefinitionStatement constructor does not guard against a NULL declaration argument and would cause a segmentation fault if NULL were passed directly. This function provides that guard explicitly.
In the context of SgNamespaceDefinitionStatement, set_declaration() and set_parent() refer to the same operation, so calling set_parent(d) is equivalent to associating the definition with its owning declaration.

◆ buildNaryBooleanOp()

SgNaryBooleanOp * SageBuilder::buildNaryBooleanOp ( SgExpression * lhs)

Builds a new SgNaryBooleanOp AST node initialized with a single operand.

This function constructs a new SgNaryBooleanOp node, which represents an n-ary boolean operation in the ROSE Abstract Syntax Tree (AST). The provided left-hand side expression is added as the first operand of the newly created node, and its parent pointer is updated accordingly to maintain proper AST parent-child relationships. After construction, the node's source position information is set to reflect that it was introduced as a compiler-generated transformation rather than originating from user source code.

The resulting node can later be extended with additional operands to represent multi-operand boolean expressions such as logical conjunctions or disjunctions involving more than two operands.

Parameters
lhsA pointer to an SgExpression node that serves as the initial operand of the n-ary boolean operation. This expression is appended to the operand list of the newly created node, and its parent is set to the new SgNaryBooleanOp node.
Returns
A pointer to the newly allocated and initialized SgNaryBooleanOp node containing lhs as its first operand.
Warning
The caller is responsible for managing the lifetime of the returned SgNaryBooleanOp node. Passing a null pointer for lhs will result in undefined behavior, as the function does not perform null checks.
Precondition
lhs must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgExpression node.
lhs should not already be owned by another part of the AST unless the caller intentionally restructures the tree and updates parent pointers accordingly.
Postcondition
The returned SgNaryBooleanOp node contains lhs as its sole operand.
The parent pointer of lhs is set to the newly created SgNaryBooleanOp node.
The source position of the returned node is marked as a transformation (compiler-generated), not corresponding to any location in the original source file.
Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface, which provides factory functions for constructing ROSE AST nodes during source-to-source transformations.
Additional operands can be appended to the returned node after construction by accessing its operand list via get_operands().

This function constructs a new SgNaryBooleanOp node, which represents an n-ary Boolean operation in the ROSE abstract syntax tree (AST). The "nfi" suffix indicates that this is a no-frills interface builder, meaning it performs minimal setup without additional semantic analysis or scope resolution.

The function allocates a new SgNaryBooleanOp object on the heap, appends the provided expression as the first operand in the node's operand list, and sets the parent pointer of the provided expression to the newly created node. Source position information for the result node is set to null using setOneSourcePositionNull, indicating that no source location is associated with this synthetically constructed node.

This builder is typically used when constructing AST nodes programmatically during transformations or code generation passes where source location tracking is not required.

Parameters
lhsA pointer to an SgExpression node that will serve as the initial operand of the n-ary Boolean operation. This expression is appended to the operand list of the new node, and its parent pointer is updated to point to the newly created SgNaryBooleanOp.

A pointer to the newly allocated and partially initialized SgNaryBooleanOp node containing lhs as its first operand.
Warning
The caller is responsible for managing the lifetime of the returned SgNaryBooleanOp node. Failing to properly attach it to the AST or delete it when no longer needed may result in memory leaks.
The provided lhs expression must not be null. Passing a null pointer will result in undefined behavior when the parent pointer is set.

lhs must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgExpression node.

The parent pointer of lhs is set to the returned SgNaryBooleanOp node.
The source position of the returned node is set to null.
Note

◆ buildNaryComparisonOp()

Builds a new SgNaryComparisonOp AST node initialized with a left-hand side expression.

This function constructs a new n-ary comparison operator node (SgNaryComparisonOp) for use in the ROSE abstract syntax tree (AST). An n-ary comparison operator represents a chained comparison expression that can hold multiple operands, as seen in languages such as Python (e.g., a < b < c). The provided left-hand side expression is added as the first operand of the newly created node, and its parent pointer is updated to reference the new node. Source position information is set to indicate that this node was introduced by a transformation rather than originating from source code.

The construction process follows these steps:

  1. Allocates a new SgNaryComparisonOp node.
  2. Appends the given lhs expression to the node's operand list.
  3. Sets the parent of lhs to the newly created node.
  4. Assigns a transformation source position to the node via setOneSourcePositionForTransformation.

lhsA pointer to the SgExpression that serves as the initial (left-hand side) operand of the n-ary comparison operation. This expression is inserted into the operand list of the new node, and its parent is updated accordingly.

A pointer to the newly created SgNaryComparisonOp node containing lhs as its first operand.
Warning
The caller is responsible for managing the lifetime of the returned node within the AST. Passing a null pointer for lhs may result in undefined behavior or a runtime error.
Precondition
lhs must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgExpression node.
lhs should not already be attached to another AST node as a child, or its parent pointer will be overwritten.
Postcondition
The returned SgNaryComparisonOp node contains lhs as its sole operand.
The parent pointer of lhs is set to the returned SgNaryComparisonOp node.
The returned node has its source position marked as a transformation artifact.
Note
Additional operands can be appended to the returned node after construction to build up a full chained comparison expression.
This builder function is part of the SageBuilder interface, which provides factory functions for constructing ROSE AST nodes during program transformation or analysis tasks.

Builds a noexcept operator expression node with an optional expression parameter.

This function constructs an SgNoexceptOp AST node representing the C++ noexcept operator applied to an expression. The noexcept operator determines at compile time whether a given expression can throw exceptions. The function allocates a new SgNoexceptOp node, optionally attaches the provided expression as a child, sets the parent pointer of the expression to the newly created node, marks any left-hand side values within the node, and initializes the source position information to null.

If the expression parameter is non-null, the function sets the parent of the expression to the resulting SgNoexceptOp node and calls markLhsValues to annotate any lvalue sub-expressions appropriately. If the expression is null, the node is created without an operand, which may represent an incomplete or placeholder AST node.

This is the "no-file-info" (nfi) variant of the builder, meaning source position information is explicitly set to null rather than being derived from the current source file context.

Parameters
expA pointer to an SgExpression node to be used as the operand of the noexcept operator. May be NULL, in which case the resulting node will have no operand expression attached.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgNoexceptOp AST node. The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-null, as the function asserts successful allocation.
Warning
The caller is responsible for managing the lifetime of the returned SgNoexceptOp node. Passing an expression that is already owned by another part of the AST may result in incorrect parent-child relationships.
Precondition
If exp is non-null, it must point to a valid, fully constructed SgExpression object that is not already attached to another parent node in the AST.
Postcondition
The returned SgNoexceptOp node has its source position information set to null.
If exp is non-null, exp->get_parent() returns the newly created SgNoexceptOp node.
The returned node is a valid SgNoexceptOp object with a non-null pointer.
Note
This function uses an assertion (ROSE_ASSERT) to verify that the allocation of the SgNoexceptOp node succeeded. If allocation fails, the program will terminate at the assertion.
The "nfi" suffix in the function name stands for "no file info," indicating that source location metadata is not populated from a file context.
The commented-out code in the implementation suggests that type inference from the expression was considered but not included in this version.

◆ buildNondefiningClassDeclaration()

SgClassDeclaration * SageBuilder::buildNondefiningClassDeclaration ( SgName name,
SgScopeStatement * scope )

Builds or retrieves a non-defining class declaration node in the ROSE AST.

This function constructs a non-defining (forward) class declaration for a class identified by the given name within the specified scope. A non-defining declaration is a forward reference to a class that does not contain the class body; it serves as a placeholder so that other AST nodes (such as types) can reference the class before or without its full definition.

The function first checks whether a class symbol with the given name already exists in the provided scope. If such a symbol is found, the existing non-defining declaration is retrieved and its defining declaration link is updated accordingly. If no symbol is found, a new SgClassDeclaration node is created with kind e_class, a new SgClassType is associated with it, its source position is marked as a transformation, and it is registered as its own first non-defining declaration. If a valid scope is provided, the declaration's scope is set and a new SgClassSymbol is inserted into the scope's symbol table. If scope is NULL, the declaration is constructed without scope or symbol table information, supporting bottom-up AST construction workflows where the scope may not yet be known.

The input name must not contain template argument syntax (e.g., it must not be of the form "X<Y>"). This is enforced by an assertion using SageInterface::hasTemplateSyntax(). Note that this function currently contains a diagnostic call to ROSE_ABORT() guarded by a preprocessor if block, which means calling this function in its current state will unconditionally abort execution. This is an intentional development-time guard indicating the function is not yet fully supported or is under active debugging.

Parameters
nameThe name of the class for which a non-defining declaration is to be built or retrieved. Must not contain template argument syntax (e.g., angle-bracket template parameters).
scopeThe scope in which to look up or insert the class symbol. May be NULL to support bottom-up AST construction where the scope is not yet known. If non-NULL, the scope's symbol table is queried and potentially updated.
Returns
A pointer to the SgClassDeclaration node representing the non-defining (forward) class declaration. The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-NULL. If the class symbol already existed in the scope, the existing non-defining declaration is returned with updated links. Otherwise, a newly constructed non-defining declaration is returned.
Warning
This function currently calls ROSE_ABORT() unconditionally within a preprocessor-guarded block (if 1 ... endif), meaning any call to this function will terminate the program. This guard is present for development and debugging purposes and must be removed or conditioned before the function can be used in production.
The input name must not contain template argument syntax. Passing a name such as "X<Y>" will trigger an assertion failure via SageInterface::hasTemplateSyntax().
Precondition
The name parameter must not contain template syntax, as verified by SageInterface::hasTemplateSyntax(name) == false.
If scope is non-NULL, it must point to a valid SgScopeStatement node.
Postcondition
The returned SgClassDeclaration is non-NULL.
The returned declaration's type (get_type()) is non-NULL.
If scope is non-NULL, the returned declaration's scope (get_scope()) is non-NULL and a corresponding SgClassSymbol has been inserted into the scope's symbol table.
The returned declaration's first non-defining declaration link points to itself (if newly created), and its defining declaration link is set to NULL.
Note
Bottom-up AST construction is supported: passing NULL for scope is not treated as an error. In this case, no symbol table entry is created and the declaration's scope is left unset.
The source position of a newly created non-defining declaration is marked as a transformation (via setOneSourcePositionForTransformation()), indicating it is compiler-generated and does not correspond to a location in the original source code.
This function is distinct from the defining class declaration builder. The non-defining declaration acts as a forward reference and does not carry a class definition body.

◆ buildNondefiningClassDeclaration_nfi()

SgClassDeclaration * SageBuilder::buildNondefiningClassDeclaration_nfi ( const SgName & XXX_name,

Builds a non-defining class declaration node in the ROSE AST, optionally as a template instantiation.

This function constructs and initializes a non-defining SgClassDeclaration (or a SgTemplateInstantiationDecl when building a template instantiation) suitable for insertion into the ROSE Abstract Syntax Tree (AST). A non-defining declaration is a forward declaration or a reference to a class that does not contain the class body (definition). This function is the low-level, "no fixup infrastructure" (nfi) variant, meaning it does not invoke the higher-level ROSE fixup passes automatically.

The function performs the following steps:

  1. Validates that the provided name does not already contain template argument syntax.
  2. If buildTemplateInstantiation is true, it constructs a SgTemplateInstantiationDecl node using the name with template arguments appended (computed via appendTemplateArgumentsToName). The template name (without arguments) is stored separately on the resulting node.
  3. If buildTemplateInstantiation is false, it constructs a plain SgClassDeclaration using the name without template arguments.
  4. Sets the source position on the new declaration node.
  5. Initializes the firstNondefiningDeclaration pointer to point to itself, sets the definingDeclaration to NULL, and marks the declaration as a forward declaration.
  6. Sets the structural parent and logical scope of the new declaration.
  7. If a scope is provided, the function looks up any existing class symbol in the scope's symbol table (using lookup_nontemplate_class_symbol with optional template arguments for disambiguation). If a symbol is found, the new declaration reuses the existing type (via SgClassType::createType referencing the firstNondefiningDeclaration from the symbol) and links itself to the previously established firstNondefiningDeclaration and definingDeclaration chain. If no symbol is found, a new SgClassSymbol is created, inserted into the scope's symbol table, and a new SgClassType is created for the declaration.
  8. If buildTemplateInstantiation is true, setTemplateArgumentsInDeclaration is called to attach the template arguments to the new declaration node.
  9. Final consistency assertions are performed, including verifying that the declaration's name matches the expected name with template arguments and, for template instantiation declarations, that the reconstructed name from the template name and arguments is consistent.

The conditional compilation macro DEBUG_NONDEFINING_CLASS_DECLARATION (set to 0 by define in the source) controls verbose diagnostic output during development and debugging. The macro REUSE_CLASS_DECLARATION_FROM_SYMBOL controls an alternative code path that is currently inactive (dead code).

Parameters
XXX_nameThe class name without template argument syntax. Must not contain template argument syntax (e.g., angle brackets with arguments). This is asserted internally via SageInterface::hasTemplateSyntax().
kindThe class type kind (e.g., struct, class, or union), represented as a SgClassDeclaration::class_types enumeration value.
scopeA pointer to the enclosing scope statement in which the declaration logically resides. May be NULL, in which case topScopeStack() is used for the structural parent and no symbol table operations are performed.
buildTemplateInstantiationA boolean flag indicating whether the declaration being built represents a template instantiation. When true, a SgTemplateInstantiationDecl is created and templateArgumentsList must be non-NULL.
templateArgumentsListA pointer to a list of template arguments used to construct the instantiated name and to set template arguments on the resulting declaration. Must be non-NULL when buildTemplateInstantiation is true. May be NULL when buildTemplateInstantiation is false.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed non-defining SgClassDeclaration (or SgTemplateInstantiationDecl) node. The returned pointer is never NULL. The returned declaration has its type, scope, parent, firstNondefiningDeclaration, and definingDeclaration fields initialized appropriately.
Warning
This is a low-level builder function (nfi = no fixup infrastructure). Callers are responsible for ensuring that the resulting AST node is properly integrated into the surrounding AST structure. Incorrect use may result in an inconsistent or invalid AST.
When buildTemplateInstantiation is true, passing a NULL templateArgumentsList will trigger a failed assertion at runtime.
The input name XXX_name must not contain template argument syntax. Passing a name with template syntax (e.g., "Foo<int>") will trigger a failed assertion via SageInterface::hasTemplateSyntax().
The returned declaration node has its definition (get_definition()) set to NULL. It is the caller's responsibility to attach a defining declaration if one is needed.
Precondition
XXX_name does not contain template argument syntax, as verified by SageInterface::hasTemplateSyntax() returning false.
If buildTemplateInstantiation is true, templateArgumentsList must be non-NULL.
If scope is non-NULL, it must be a valid, initialized SgScopeStatement with an accessible symbol table.
Postcondition
The returned SgClassDeclaration pointer is non-NULL.
The returned declaration's get_definition() returns NULL (it is a non-defining declaration).
The returned declaration's get_type() is non-NULL (a SgClassType has been created or reused).
The returned declaration's get_parent() is non-NULL (set to scope or topScopeStack() if scope is NULL).
The returned declaration's firstNondefiningDeclaration is set to either itself (if no prior symbol was found) or to the declaration retrieved from the existing symbol in the scope's symbol table.
If scope is non-NULL and no prior symbol existed, a new SgClassSymbol for the declaration has been inserted into the scope's symbol table under the name with template arguments.
If buildTemplateInstantiation is true, the returned SgTemplateInstantiationDecl has its templateName set to the name without template arguments, and its template arguments are set via setTemplateArgumentsInDeclaration.
Note
This function uses the name with template arguments (computed by appendTemplateArgumentsToName) for symbol table lookups and insertions, ensuring that template instantiations with different argument lists are properly distinguished even when their base names are identical.
The distinction between the structural parent (set via set_parent()) and the logical scope (set via set_scope()) is intentional. The structural parent reflects the AST tree structure, while the logical scope reflects the C++ scoping rules.
The macro DEBUG_NONDEFINING_CLASS_DECLARATION is set to 0 by define and controls optional verbose diagnostic printf output. It can be set to 1 during development to enable tracing of the declaration building process.
For non-template class declarations (buildTemplateInstantiation is false), the name with template arguments defaults to the name without template arguments, allowing uniform use of nameWithTemplateArguments throughout the function.

SgEnumDeclaration * SageBuilder::buildNondefiningEnumDeclaration_nfi ( const SgName & name,

Builds a non-defining enum declaration node in the ROSE AST for a given name and scope.

This function constructs a new SgEnumDeclaration that serves as a non-defining (forward) declaration of an enumeration type. It is analogous in structure to the support provided for SgClassDeclaration non-defining declarations, though the type handling differs.

The function first checks whether an existing SgEnumSymbol for the given name already exists in the provided scope. If one is found, the existing enum type and first non-defining declaration are reused to maintain proper linkage between declarations. A new SgEnumDeclaration node is always created (rather than reusing an existing one) to avoid sharing declaration nodes across multiple uses, which is required for correctness in cases such as repeated forward declarations in the same translation unit.

After constructing the declaration node, the function sets its source position to null, marks it as a forward declaration, and establishes the first non-defining and defining declaration pointers. If no prior symbol exists in the scope, a new SgEnumSymbol is created and inserted into the scope's symbol table. The declaration's scope and parent are both set to the provided scope.

The input name must not contain template argument syntax (e.g., names of the form "X<Y>" are not permitted). This is enforced by an assertion using SageInterface::hasTemplateSyntax.

Parameters
nameThe name of the enumeration type to declare. Must not contain template argument syntax.
scopeThe scope in which the non-defining enum declaration is to be placed. Must not be null.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgEnumDeclaration node representing the non-defining (forward) declaration of the enumeration. The returned pointer is never null.
Precondition
scope must not be null.
The name parameter must not contain template argument syntax (i.e., SageInterface::hasTemplateSyntax(name) must return false).
Postcondition
A valid SgEnumDeclaration node is returned with its forward flag set.
The returned declaration has its firstNondefiningDeclaration pointer set to either itself (if no prior symbol existed) or to the previously registered first non-defining declaration.
If no prior SgEnumSymbol for the given name existed in the scope, a new SgEnumSymbol is inserted into the scope's symbol table.
The returned declaration's scope and parent are both set to the provided scope.
The returned declaration's type is non-null.
A valid SgEnumSymbol for the given name can be found in the scope after the call.
Warning
This function always allocates a new SgEnumDeclaration node. Callers are responsible for ensuring the returned node is properly managed within the AST to avoid memory leaks.
Note
The behavior of this function is intentionally designed to avoid sharing declaration nodes, which is necessary to prevent subtle AST inconsistencies when the same enum is forward-declared multiple times (e.g., as observed in test cases such as test2007_29.C).
The structural scope and the logical scope of the declaration are both set to the same provided scope. Whether C++ semantics allow these to differ is noted as an open question in the implementation.

Builds a non-defining function declaration by cloning the properties of an existing SgFunctionDeclaration node.

This function constructs a new non-defining function declaration based on an existing SgFunctionDeclaration. It extracts the function name, return type, and parameter list from the provided declaration, performs a deep copy of the parameter list, and then delegates to the overloaded buildNondefiningFunctionDeclaration() that accepts individual components. The resulting declaration inherits the linkage specifier and storage modifier (specifically the extern qualifier) from the source declaration.

The function also verifies that the function type derived from the return type and argument list is consistent with the original function type. It checks that the first non-defining declaration pointer is valid, and when a scope is provided, it further asserts that the internal symbol table references remain consistent with the given scope.

The overloaded buildNondefiningFunctionDeclaration() internally checks whether a matching function declaration has already been created by looking up function symbols in the symbol table, preventing duplicate declarations.

Parameters
funcdeclA pointer to the existing SgFunctionDeclaration from which the new non-defining declaration is derived. Must not be NULL.
scopeAn optional pointer to the SgScopeStatement representing the scope in which the new declaration will be placed. If NULL, no scope-based consistency checks are enforced beyond the basic assertions.
decoratorListAn optional pointer to an SgExprListExp containing decorator expressions to be associated with the new function declaration. May be NULL if no decorators are needed.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed non-defining SgFunctionDeclaration node, with linkage and storage modifiers matching those of the input declaration.
Precondition
funcdecl must not be NULL.
The function type of funcdecl must be consistent with its return type and argument list, as verified by findFunctionType().
If scope is non-NULL, the resulting declaration's first non-defining declaration must be consistent with the provided scope's symbol table.
Postcondition
The returned SgFunctionDeclaration has the same linkage as funcdecl.
The returned SgFunctionDeclaration has the same extern storage modifier as funcdecl.
The returned SgFunctionDeclaration has a valid first non-defining declaration pointer.
Warning
Passing a NULL funcdecl will trigger an assertion failure at runtime.
If the function type of funcdecl is inconsistent with its return type and argument list, an assertion failure will occur during the type consistency check.
When scope is non-NULL, inconsistency between the new declaration and the scope's symbol table will trigger an assertion failure.
Note
The parameter list is deep-copied from the source declaration, so modifications to the new declaration's parameter list will not affect the original.
This function does not create a defining declaration; it only produces a forward (non-defining) declaration suitable for use as a prototype or extern reference.

Builds a non-defining function declaration node in the AST.

This function constructs a non-defining function declaration, which represents a forward declaration of a function without its body. It dispatches to the appropriate templated internal builder function based on the current language context and the requested declaration type.

If the current language is Fortran and the enclosing file node is set to output Fortran, the function delegates to the Fortran-specific builder using SgProcedureHeaderStatement as the declaration type.

For non-Fortran languages, the function checks whether a template instantiation declaration is requested. If buildTemplateInstantiation is true, it creates an SgTemplateInstantiationFunctionDecl node and passes the provided template arguments list. Otherwise, a standard SgFunctionDeclaration node is created.

In all cases, the internal templated helper function buildNondefiningFunctionDeclaration_T is used, with the isMemberFunction flag set to false, indicating that the declaration is not a member function.

◆ buildNondefiningFunctionDeclaration_T()

actualFunction * SageBuilder::buildNondefiningFunctionDeclaration_T ( const SgName & XXX_name,
SgType * return_type,
SgFunctionParameterList * paralist,
bool isMemberFunction,
SgScopeStatement * scope,
SgExprListExp * decoratorList,
unsigned int functionConstVolatileFlags,

Builds a non-defining function declaration AST node for a variety of function declaration types, including regular functions, member functions, template functions, and template instantiations.

This is a templated builder function that constructs a non-defining (forward) function declaration node in the ROSE Abstract Syntax Tree (AST). The template parameter actualFunction determines the concrete IR node type to be constructed, which may be one of the following: SgFunctionDeclaration, SgMemberFunctionDeclaration, SgTemplateFunctionDeclaration, SgTemplateMemberFunctionDeclaration, SgTemplateInstantiationFunctionDecl, SgTemplateInstantiationMemberFunctionDecl, or SgProcedureHeaderStatement.

The function performs the following major steps:

  1. Argument validation: If scope is null, the top of the scope stack is used. The return type and parameter list must be non-null.
  2. Name handling: The input name is separated into a base name (without template arguments) and a name with template arguments appended (for template instantiations). Template argument syntax is appended to the name only when building a template instantiation.
  3. Function type construction: A SgFunctionType or SgMemberFunctionType is built from the return type and parameter list, depending on whether the function is a member function.
  4. Symbol table lookup: The scope is searched for an existing function symbol matching the name and type. For template functions, the template parameter list is also used in the lookup. If a symbol is found in a different global scope, it is inserted into the current scope.
  5. Declaration construction:
    • If no existing symbol is found, a new actualFunction node is created, a new symbol of the appropriate type is created and inserted into the scope's symbol table, and the declaration is set as its own first non-defining declaration.
    • If an existing symbol is found (i.e., this is a second or later prototype), the function type is reused from the previously declared function, a new actualFunction node is created, and the first non-defining declaration and defining declaration pointers are set from the previously found declaration.
  6. Template argument and parameter setup: If building a template instantiation, template arguments are set on the declaration. If building a template declaration, template parameters are set.
  7. Parameter list setup: The provided parameter list is attached to the function declaration, and the scope of each parameter is set to the enclosing scope.
  8. Source position: Source position information is set on the declaration and all its children using setSourcePositionAtRootAndAllChildren.
  9. Fortran special handling: For Fortran language output, the subprogram kind (subroutine or function) is set based on the return type, and the forward declaration is hidden from the code generator.
  10. Storage modifier: The storage modifier (e.g., static) is applied to the declaration modifier before symbol insertion.
  11. Restrict modifier: If the functionConstVolatileFlags includes the restrict flag, the restrict modifier is set on the declaration.
  12. Modification flags: All nodes in the newly built declaration are unmarked as modified, to reflect that they represent parsed (not transformed) code.

The function uses assertions extensively to verify internal consistency of the AST, including symbol table integrity, scope linkage, and declaration chain correctness.

Parameters
XXX_nameThe name of the function to be declared. May be null for compiler-generated constructors of unnamed classes, structs, or unions in C++.
return_typeThe return type of the function. Must be non-null.
paralistThe parameter list for the function declaration. Must be non-null.
isMemberFunctionA boolean flag indicating whether the function is a member function. If true, a member function type is constructed; otherwise, a plain function type is constructed.
scopeThe scope in which the function declaration is to be placed. If null, the top of the SageBuilder scope stack is used. Must resolve to a non-null scope.
decoratorListAn optional list of decorator expressions. May be null. Currently not used directly in the construction logic but accepted as part of the interface.
functionConstVolatileFlagsBit flags encoding const, volatile, and restrict qualifiers for member function types. Uses values from SgMemberFunctionType flag enumerations.
templateArgumentsListA pointer to the list of template arguments, required when building a template instantiation (i.e., when actualFunction is SgTemplateInstantiationFunctionDecl or SgTemplateInstantiationMemberFunctionDecl). Must be non-null for template instantiations.
templateParameterListA pointer to the list of template parameters, used when building a template declaration or performing symbol table lookups for template functions. May be null for non-template functions.
smThe storage modifier to apply to the function declaration (e.g., static, extern). Uses values from SgStorageModifier::storage_modifier_enum.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed non-defining function declaration node of type actualFunction. The returned node is marked as a forward declaration, has its scope, parent, parameter list, and source position set, and is registered in the scope's symbol table. The returned pointer is never null.
Warning
This function performs numerous internal assertions (ROSE_ASSERT, ASSERT_not_null, ASSERT_require) that will abort the program if AST consistency conditions are violated. Callers must ensure that all required inputs are valid and consistent.
For template instantiations, templateArgumentsList must be non-null. Passing null for this parameter when building a template instantiation will trigger an assertion failure.
The storage modifier (sm) must be set before the symbol is inserted into the scope's symbol table. This is handled internally, but callers should be aware that the modifier affects symbol visibility.
If the function name contains template argument syntax (e.g., "X<Y>"), a warning may be emitted under debug builds. Conversion operator names such as "operator std::auto_ptr_ref<_Tp1>" are known to trigger this condition.
For Fortran language output, the returned declaration is hidden from the code generator (i.e., it will not appear in unparsed output). This is intentional, as Fortran prototype declarations are used internally by ROSE.
Precondition
return_type must be non-null.
paralist must be non-null.
If scope is null, SageBuilder::topScopeStack() must return a non-null scope.
If actualFunction is a template instantiation type, templateArgumentsList must be non-null.
The actualFunction template parameter must be one of the supported IR node types: SgFunctionDeclaration, SgMemberFunctionDeclaration, SgTemplateFunctionDeclaration, SgTemplateMemberFunctionDeclaration, SgTemplateInstantiationFunctionDecl, SgTemplateInstantiationMemberFunctionDecl, or SgProcedureHeaderStatement.
Postcondition
The returned function declaration node is a non-defining (forward) declaration, marked via setForward().
The returned node has its firstNondefiningDeclaration pointer set to a valid non-null declaration (either itself or a previously existing non-defining declaration).
The returned node's scope is set to the resolved scope argument.
The returned node's parent is set to the resolved scope argument.

This function is a convenience overload that constructs a non-defining member function declaration in the ROSE abstract syntax tree (AST). A non-defining declaration is a forward declaration that announces the existence of a member function without providing its implementation body. Internally, this overload delegates to the more general form of buildNondefiningMemberFunctionDeclaration, supplying default values for the decorator list (NULL), member function modifiers (set to zero, indicating no special modifiers such as virtual, static, or const), a flag indicating the function is not a constructor (false), and a template argument list (NULL). Builds a non-defining member function declaration node in the ROSE AST.

This function constructs either a standard non-defining member function declaration (SgMemberFunctionDeclaration) or a template instantiation member function declaration (SgTemplateInstantiationMemberFunctionDecl), depending on the value of the buildTemplateInstantiation flag.

Internally, the function delegates to the templated helper buildNondefiningFunctionDeclaration_T, parameterized on the appropriate AST node type. The isMemberFunction argument is always set to true in both branches to indicate that the declaration belongs to a class scope. The storage modifier is set to the default value (SgStorageModifier::e_default) in both cases.

After the declaration node is created, the function performs the following additional setup steps:

  1. Retrieves the SgCtorInitializerList associated with the result and asserts it is non-null.
  2. Sets both the defining declaration and the first non-defining declaration of the SgCtorInitializerList to itself, as required by AST consistency tests.
  3. Verifies that the associated class declaration (get_associatedClassDeclaration) is non-null. The scope parameter must point to a valid SgScopeStatement that is an SgClassDefinition when the associated class declaration needs to be resolved.
If buildTemplateInstantiation is true, templateArgumentsList should be a valid non-null pointer to the relevant template arguments.
The paralist parameter must be a valid, pre-constructed SgFunctionParameterList.
The return_type parameter must be a valid, non-null SgType pointer.
