Builds a nondefining procedure header statement for a Fortran subprogram declaration.

This function constructs a nondefining SgProcedureHeaderStatement node, which represents a forward or external declaration of a Fortran subprogram (such as a subroutine or function) without providing its body. It is intended for use in the ROSE compiler infrastructure when building the abstract syntax tree (AST) for Fortran code.

Internally, the function delegates to the templated helper buildNondefiningFunctionDeclaration_T instantiated with SgProcedureHeaderStatement. This helper handles the creation of the declaration node, the association with the enclosing scope, and the management of the function symbol table entry. The function symbol is always set to reference the first nondefining declaration encountered, even when multiple nondefining declarations exist.

If the provided scope is null, the function falls back to the top of the current scope stack via SageBuilder::topScopeStack(). After construction, the subprogram kind (e.g., subroutine, function, or program) is set on the resulting node using set_subprogram_kind().

The function enforces that the resulting node is a valid SgProcedureHeaderStatement and that its first nondefining declaration pointer is properly initialized before returning.

Parameters
nameThe name of the procedure being declared.
return_typeA pointer to the SgType representing the return type of the procedure. Must not be null.
param_listA pointer to the SgFunctionParameterList describing the formal parameters of the procedure. Must not be null.
kindAn enumeration value of type SgProcedureHeaderStatement::subprogram_kind_enum specifying whether the subprogram is a subroutine, function, program, or another Fortran subprogram variant.
scopeA pointer to the SgScopeStatement representing the enclosing scope in which the declaration is to be placed. If null, the top of the current scope stack is used automatically.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgProcedureHeaderStatement node representing the nondefining procedure header declaration. The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-null and to have a valid first nondefining declaration.
Precondition
return_type must not be null.
param_list must not be null.
If scope is non-null, it must be a valid and properly initialized SgScopeStatement within the current AST.
The SageBuilder scope stack must be non-empty if scope is null, so that topScopeStack() can provide a valid fallback scope.
Postcondition
The returned SgProcedureHeaderStatement is a nondefining declaration node with its subprogram kind set to the value specified by kind.
The first nondefining declaration pointer of the returned node is non-null.
The declaration is registered in the symbol table of the resolved scope.
Warning
This function is intended for use with Fortran AST construction. Using it in the context of C or C++ AST building may produce unexpected or invalid results.
Passing a null return_type or null param_list will trigger an assertion failure and abort execution.
Note
A new nondefining declaration node is always created, even if a symbol with the same name already exists in the target scope. The function symbol in the symbol table will continue to reference the first nondefining declaration that was originally registered.
The created declaration is not a defining declaration; it does not include a function body. A separate defining declaration must be constructed if the subprogram body is required.

Builds a non-defining template class declaration node in the ROSE AST.

This function constructs a non-defining SgTemplateClassDeclaration node, which represents a forward declaration of a template class (or struct or union) without an associated class body definition. It is intended for use during bottom-up or top-down AST construction when a forward reference to a template class is required.

The function performs the following major steps:

  1. If the provided scope is NULL, the function attempts to retrieve the current top scope from the scope stack maintained by SageBuilder.
  2. The template name is split into two forms: one without template specialization arguments (the base template name) and one with any specialization arguments appended. The latter is used for symbol table lookups and node naming.
  3. The function queries the given scope for an existing SgClassSymbol (specifically a SgTemplateClassSymbol) matching the name with specialization arguments and the provided template parameter and specialization argument lists.
  4. If a matching symbol is found in the scope, a new SgTemplateClassDeclaration is constructed using the existing class type from the symbol. The new node is linked to the first non-defining declaration obtained from the symbol, its template parameters and specialization arguments are initialized, and the forward flag is set. A non-real declaration scope (SgDeclarationScope) is attached if the new node is itself the first non-defining declaration.
  5. If no matching symbol exists, a brand new SgTemplateClassDeclaration is created with a NULL class type and NULL definition. The node is designated as its own first non-defining declaration. A new SgClassType is created and associated with the node after the scope is set. A new SgTemplateClassSymbol is constructed and inserted into the scope's symbol table using the name with specialization arguments. Template parameters are also initialized in the declaration via setTemplateParametersInDeclaration().
  6. In both branches, template specialization arguments are set via setTemplateSpecializationArgumentsInDeclaration(), the template name (without specialization arguments) is stored, the forward flag is set, and source position information is applied to the node.
  7. Consistency assertions are performed throughout, including checks on the parent, scope, type, symbol table entry, and template name fields of the resulting node.

The suffix _nfi indicates this is a "non-frontend interface" builder function, meaning it is intended for programmatic AST construction rather than being called during frontend parsing.

Parameters
XXX_nameThe base name of the template class, without any template specialization arguments. This name is used to derive both the plain template name and the name with specialization arguments appended.
kindThe class kind (e.g., class, struct, or union) as defined by SgClassDeclaration::class_types. This determines the syntactic category of the template class declaration being built.
scopeThe scope in which the template class declaration is to be placed. If NULL, the function will attempt to use the top of the current SageBuilder scope stack. A warning is printed if scope remains NULL after this fallback.
templateParameterListA pointer to the list of template parameters for the template class declaration. Must not be NULL. The list is copied into the new declaration node.
templateSpecializationArgumentListA pointer to the list of template specialization arguments. Must not be NULL. Used to form the specialized name and to initialize the specialization argument list on the declaration node.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgTemplateClassDeclaration node representing the non-defining (forward) template class declaration. The returned node is guaranteed to be non-NULL, to have its type set, its forward flag set, its template name set, and its first non-defining declaration pointer initialized. The parent pointer of the returned node will be NULL and must be set by the caller.
Warning
If scope is NULL and the scope stack is also empty, a warning message is printed and symbol table operations are skipped. The resulting node may be incomplete and require additional setup by the caller.
The parent pointer of the returned node is explicitly asserted to be NULL upon return. The caller is responsible for setting the parent after inserting the node into the AST.
This function does not insert the returned declaration into any statement list or parent scope body. The caller must perform this step as part of AST construction.
Precondition
templateParameterList must not be NULL.
templateSpecializationArgumentList must not be NULL.
If scope is non-NULL, it must be a valid, initialized SgScopeStatement node.
The name XXX_name must be a valid, non-null SgName.
Postcondition
The returned SgTemplateClassDeclaration has its forward flag set.
The returned node has a non-NULL SgClassType associated with it.
The returned node has its templateName set to the name without specialization arguments.
The returned node has its firstNondefiningDeclaration pointer set.
If scope is non-NULL, a corresponding SgTemplateClassSymbol has been inserted into the scope's symbol table (if one did not already exist).
The parent pointer of the returned node is NULL.
Template argument parent pointers within the declaration are correctly set.
Note
This function supports bottom-up AST construction, where the scope may not be known at the time of declaration building. In such cases, scope-related operations (symbol table insertion, type creation) are deferred or skipped.
The function calls testTemplateArgumentParents() at multiple points to validate the integrity of template argument parent linkages in the AST.
For template class specializations, the specialization arguments are appended to the class name using appendTemplateArgumentsToName() and this augmented name is used for all symbol table operations, while the plain name is stored separately as the template name.
The function uses ROSE_ASSERT extensively to enforce invariants. Violations will cause an assertion failure at runtime.

Specifically, it checks that if the new declaration does not directly appear in the symbol table, it is not the first non-defining declaration, and that the first non-defining declaration does appear in the symbol table. The ROSE AST infrastructure must be properly initialized before calling this function.

The returned SgTemplateFunctionDeclaration pointer is non-NULL.
The returned declaration has a valid first non-defining declaration set (i.e., get_firstNondefiningDeclaration() returns a non-NULL value).

Builds a non-defining template member function declaration node in the ROSE IR.

This function constructs a new SgTemplateMemberFunctionDeclaration node representing a non-defining (i.e., forward) declaration of a template member function. It delegates the core construction to the templated helper buildNondefiningFunctionDeclaration_T, specifying that the declaration is a member function and using a default storage modifier.

After construction, the function performs the following additional setup steps:

  1. Looks up the corresponding template member function symbol in the given scope using the function name, its type, and the template parameter list. An assertion failure occurs if no such symbol is found, ensuring symbol table consistency.
  2. Retrieves the SgCtorInitializerList associated with the new declaration and sets both its defining declaration and first non-defining declaration pointers to itself, satisfying AST consistency requirements enforced by AstConsistencyTests.
  3. Verifies that the first non-defining declaration of the result has a valid symbol in the symbol table.
  4. If the result is not itself the first non-defining declaration, asserts that its own symbol table lookup returns NULL, which is the expected behavior for subsequent non-defining declarations.
  5. Performs an additional symbol table lookup assertion (conditionally compiled under BUILDER_MAKE_REDUNDANT_CALLS_TO_SYMBOL_TABLE_LOOKUP) to further validate symbol table integrity.
  6. Optionally checks for unintended AST transformations via detectTransformations_local when compiled with BUILDER_MAKE_REDUNDANT_CALLS_TO_DETECT_TRANSFORAMTIONS and the source position classification mode is not set to transformation mode.

The SgCtorInitializerList of the result must be non-NULL; an assertion will fire if it is not present, indicating a malformed IR node.

return_type must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an SgType node.

  6. Sets the child scope's parent to the new declaration and attaches it as the nonreal declaration scope.

scope must not be NULL.

A new SgNonrealDecl node is allocated and returned.
A SgNonrealSymbol corresponding to the declaration is inserted into scope.

The returned declaration has a valid child SgDeclarationScope, either the one provided or a newly allocated compiler-generated one.

◆ buildOpaqueType()

SgType * SageBuilder::buildOpaqueType ( std::string const name,
SgScopeStatement * scope )

Builds an opaque type with a given name within a specified scope.

This function creates or retrieves an opaque type identified by a string name, which is useful during program transformation when the full details of a type are unknown, such as when interfacing with an external runtime library whose internal types are opaque to the transformation tool.

The function first checks whether a typedef symbol with the given name already exists in the provided scope. If no such symbol is found, a new SgTypedefDeclaration is created using a placeholder base type (int), a corresponding SgTypedefType is created and associated with the declaration, and a new SgTypedefSymbol is inserted into the scope's symbol table. The declaration is prepended to the scope's statement list and marked so that it is hidden from the code generator (i.e., it will not be emitted during unparsing). If a typedef symbol with the given name already exists in the scope, the existing declaration and its associated type are reused, avoiding duplicate creation.

The resulting SgTypedefType represents the opaque type and can be used in subsequent AST construction or transformation steps.

Parameters
nameThe string name to assign to the opaque typedef type. This name is used both to look up any existing typedef symbol in the scope and to name the newly created SgTypedefDeclaration if no existing symbol is found.
scopeA pointer to the SgScopeStatement in which the opaque type should be created or looked up. The new typedef declaration, if created, is prepended to this scope and its symbol is inserted into this scope's symbol table.
Returns
A pointer to the SgTypedefType representing the opaque type. The returned pointer is either a newly created SgTypedefType or an existing one retrieved from the scope's symbol table. The pointer is guaranteed to be non-null upon successful return.
Warning
The base type used for the underlying typedef declaration is a placeholder int type. The opaque type is intended to be used only symbolically; its underlying representation should not be relied upon for type-accurate transformations.
The created typedef declaration is hidden from the unparser by unsetting the code generation output flag on its file info. This means the declaration will not appear in the generated output code, which is the intended behavior for opaque types used internally during transformation.
Precondition
scope must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgScopeStatement. An assertion failure will occur if scope is null.
name must be a non-empty string that is a valid C/C++ identifier suitable for use as a typedef name.
Postcondition
If no typedef symbol named name existed in scope prior to the call, a new SgTypedefDeclaration is prepended to scope, a new SgTypedefSymbol is inserted into scope's symbol table, and a new SgTypedefType is created and returned.
If a typedef symbol named name already existed in scope, the existing SgTypedefType associated with that symbol's declaration is returned without modifying the scope.
The returned SgTypedefType pointer is guaranteed to be non-null.
Note
This function is intended for use during AST transformation, particularly when building interfaces to runtime libraries whose internal types are not fully known. It avoids duplicate type creation by checking the scope's symbol table before constructing new AST nodes.
The symbol table is accessed exclusively through the SgScopeStatement interface, consistent with ROSE's design conventions for symbol table management.

◆ buildOpaqueVarRefExp()

SgVarRefExp * SageBuilder::buildOpaqueVarRefExp ( const std::string & name,
SgScopeStatement * scope )

Builds an opaque variable reference expression for a given variable name within a scope.

This function constructs an SgVarRefExp node representing a variable reference, even when the variable may not have been explicitly declared in the AST. The term "opaque" refers to the fact that the variable may not be formally declared in the source being processed, yet a valid reference expression is still needed for AST construction purposes.

The function first attempts to locate an existing variable symbol with the given name by searching the parent scopes starting from the provided scope using lookupVariableSymbolInParentScopes(). If a matching symbol is found, it reuses that symbol to build the variable reference expression directly via buildVarRefExp().

If no existing symbol is found, a fake variable declaration of integer type is created internally using buildVariableDeclaration(). This fake declaration is attached to the given scope as its parent, but its file information is marked to suppress output during code generation. The first variable symbol from this fake declaration is then used to build and return the variable reference expression.

This approach allows tools and transformations to refer to variables by name without requiring a fully resolved declaration in the AST, which is useful in situations such as code generation, transformation, or when referencing externally defined variables.

Parameters
nameThe name of the variable for which an opaque reference expression is to be built.
scopeThe scope in which to search for or create the variable symbol. If NULL, the top of the current scope stack is used as the default scope.
Returns
A pointer to an SgVarRefExp node representing the variable reference. The returned pointer is never NULL provided the scope is valid.
Warning
This function creates a fake variable declaration internally when no existing symbol is found. The fake declaration is not intended to appear in generated code and is suppressed via file info flags. Misuse may lead to inconsistencies in the AST if the fake declaration is inadvertently traversed or modified.
The fake variable declaration created internally is given an integer type regardless of the actual type of the variable being referenced. This may cause type-related issues if the resulting AST is analyzed for type correctness.
Precondition
If scope is non-NULL, it must point to a valid and initialized SgScopeStatement node.
If scope is NULL, the scope stack maintained by SageBuilder must be non-empty so that topScopeStack() returns a valid scope.
Postcondition
The returned SgVarRefExp is associated with a valid SgVariableSymbol, either one found in the existing scope hierarchy or one created from a fake variable declaration.
If a fake variable declaration was created, its file info is configured to suppress output during code generation, and its parent is set to the resolved scope.
Note
This function is intended for use in AST construction scenarios where a variable reference is needed but the variable may not have a formal declaration accessible through normal symbol lookup. It is considered a workaround and should be used with caution.
The internal implementation was updated to use lookupVariableSymbolInParentScopes() instead of the more general lookupSymbolInParentScopes() to improve correctness when dealing with template parameters and template arguments.

SgPragmaDeclaration * SageBuilder::buildPragmaDeclaration ( const string & name,

Builds and returns a new SgPragmaDeclaration AST node with the given pragma string.

This function constructs a pragma declaration node suitable for insertion into the ROSE Abstract Syntax Tree (AST). It creates an SgPragma node from the provided name string, wraps it in an SgPragmaDeclaration, and sets up the necessary internal linkage including defining and first non-defining declaration pointers, as well as parent-child relationships.

If no scope is provided (i.e., scope is NULL), the function falls back to the top of the current scope stack via SageBuilder::topScopeStack(). Source position information is set for transformation nodes on both the SgPragma and the SgPragmaDeclaration to mark them as compiler-generated transformations rather than originating from user source.

The parent of the resulting SgPragmaDeclaration is set to the resolved scope, ensuring consistency in the AST hierarchy. Note that unlike class declarations and enum declarations, pragma declarations can have their parent set directly.

nameThe pragma string content (the text following the #pragma directive) used to initialize the SgPragma node.
scopeA pointer to the enclosing SgScopeStatement in which the pragma declaration will be placed. If NULL, the top of the current scope stack is used instead.

A pointer to the newly constructed SgPragmaDeclaration node, with all internal fields and parent-child relationships properly initialized.
Precondition
If scope is non-NULL, it must point to a valid SgScopeStatement object.
If scope is NULL, the scope stack managed by SageBuilder must be non-empty so that topScopeStack() can return a valid scope.
Postcondition
The returned SgPragmaDeclaration has its defining declaration and first non-defining declaration pointers set to itself.
The SgPragma node is set as the child (parent pointer points to the SgPragmaDeclaration) of the returned declaration.
The returned SgPragmaDeclaration has its parent set to the resolved scope.
Source position information is marked for transformation on both the SgPragma and the SgPragmaDeclaration nodes.
Warning
If both the provided scope and the top of the scope stack are NULL, the resulting SgPragmaDeclaration will have a NULL parent, which may violate AST consistency requirements and trigger assertion failures.
The caller is responsible for inserting the returned node into the AST at the appropriate location; this function only constructs and initializes the node.
Note
This function uses ROSE_ASSERT to verify that both the SgPragma and SgPragmaDeclaration objects are successfully allocated after construction.
Unlike class and enum declarations, pragma declarations support having their parent pointer set directly, so this function sets result->set_parent(scope) unconditionally when a valid scope is available.

Builds a defining SgProcedureHeaderStatement node for a Fortran or Jovial procedure declaration.

This function constructs a defining procedure header statement AST node suitable for representing Fortran or Jovial subprogram declarations, including subroutines, functions, and block data subprograms. It delegates the core construction work to the templated helper buildDefiningFunctionDeclaration_T, then sets the subprogram kind on the resulting node.

The function enforces consistency between the subprogram kind and the return type: subroutine and block data subprograms must have a void return type, while function subprograms may have any valid return type. If an unrecognized subprogram kind is provided, the function logs an error and aborts execution.

The firstNondefDecl parameter is required and must not be null. It is passed directly to the underlying declaration builder to link the defining declaration with its corresponding non-defining (forward) declaration.

kindThe subprogram kind enumeration value indicating whether the procedure is a subroutine, a function, or a block data subprogram. Accepted values are e_subroutine_subprogram_kind, e_function_subprogram_kind, and e_block_data_subprogram_kind. Any other value causes an error and abort.
scopeAn optional pointer to the enclosing SgScopeStatement in which the procedure is declared. May be nullptr, in which case scope resolution is handled internally by the underlying builder.
firstNondefDeclA pointer to the first non-defining declaration of this procedure. Must not be null. Used to link the defining declaration to its forward declaration counterpart.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgProcedureHeaderStatement node representing the defining declaration of the procedure. The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-null.
Warning
If the kind parameter is neither e_subroutine_subprogram_kind, e_block_data_subprogram_kind, nor e_function_subprogram_kind, the function logs an error message and calls ROSE_ABORT(), terminating the program.
Passing a non-void returnType when kind is e_subroutine_subprogram_kind or e_block_data_subprogram_kind will trigger an assertion failure.
Precondition
firstNondefDecl must not be null.
When kind is e_subroutine_subprogram_kind or e_block_data_subprogram_kind, returnType must be equal to the result of buildVoidType().
name must be a valid, non-null, null-terminated C-style string.
params must be a valid, non-null SgFunctionParameterList pointer.
Postcondition
The returned SgProcedureHeaderStatement node has its subprogram kind set to the value specified by the kind parameter.
The returned pointer is non-null and represents a fully constructed defining procedure header statement linked to firstNondefDecl.

This function is intended for use with Fortran and Jovial language frontends. It is not designed for C or C++ procedure declarations.
The underlying construction is performed by the templated helper function buildDefiningFunctionDeclaration_T instantiated for SgProcedureHeaderStatement, with the isMemberFunction flag set to false.

SgProcedureHeaderStatement * SageBuilder::buildProcedureHeaderStatement ( const SgName & name,

Builds a Fortran procedure header statement node in the AST.

This function constructs an SgProcedureHeaderStatement node representing a Fortran subprogram (subroutine, function, or related procedure kind) within the Abstract Syntax Tree (AST). It first resolves the target scope, defaulting to the top of the scope stack if none is provided. It then constructs or retrieves the appropriate function type and searches the given scope for an existing symbol matching the procedure name and type.

If no existing symbol is found, a new non-defining declaration of type SgProcedureHeaderStatement is created using a templated builder helper. If a matching symbol already exists, its associated declaration is reused. The resulting non-defining declaration is verified to be an SgProcedureHeaderStatement and confirmed to be its own first non-defining declaration before being forwarded to an overloaded version of buildProcedureHeaderStatement that accepts a pre-existing non-defining declaration.

This two-step approach ensures that the non-defining and defining declarations are properly linked in the AST, which is required for correct Fortran semantic representation.

Warning
The returned pointer must not be null; internal assertions will abort execution if the constructed node cannot be cast to SgProcedureHeaderStatement or if the non-defining declaration invariant is violated.

return_type must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgType node.
parameter_list must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgFunctionParameterList node.
If scope is non-null, it must be a valid SgScopeStatement in the current AST.
The scope stack must be non-empty if scope is null, so that topScopeStack() returns a valid scope.
Postcondition
An SgProcedureHeaderStatement node exists in the AST under the resolved scope.
If no prior symbol existed for the given name and type, a new non-defining declaration has been inserted into the scope.
The returned node's first non-defining declaration is itself, satisfying the AST structural invariant for non-defining declarations.
Note
This function is specific to Fortran AST construction and relies on Fortran-specific node types such as SgProcedureHeaderStatement and its associated subprogram_kind_enum.
The actual construction of the defining declaration and its linkage to the non-defining declaration is delegated to the overloaded variant of buildProcedureHeaderStatement that accepts an SgProcedureHeaderStatement pointer as an additional argument.

This function constructs a new SgPythonGlobalStmt node, which corresponds to a Python global statement in the ROSE abstract syntax tree (AST). It iterates over the provided list of SgInitializedName pointers and appends each name to the newly created statement node. After populating the names, it sets a single source position on the node to mark it as a transformation artifact, indicating that this node was synthetically introduced rather than parsed from original source code.

This builder function follows the standard SAGE builder pattern used throughout the SageBuilder interface: allocate the node, populate its children or attributes, set source position information for transformation, and return the completed node.

Warning
The caller is responsible for ensuring that the returned node is properly inserted into the AST. Failing to do so may result in memory leaks or an inconsistent AST structure.

The parameter names must be a valid, initialized SgInitializedNamePtrList. Each pointer contained in the list must be a non-null, valid SgInitializedName pointer that is already part of a consistent AST context or is otherwise properly initialized.

A new SgPythonGlobalStmt node is allocated and returned with all names from the input list appended to it.
The source position of the returned node is set to indicate a transformation, as applied by setOneSourcePositionForTransformation.

This function is intended for use when building or transforming Python-language ASTs within the ROSE compiler framework. It is not applicable to C or C++ AST construction.
The source position set by setOneSourcePositionForTransformation marks the node as compiler-generated, which may affect how downstream analysis passes and code generation treat this node.

Builds an AST node representing a Python print statement.

This function constructs a new SgPythonPrintStmt node, which corresponds to the Python 2 print statement syntax. The print statement in Python 2 supports an optional destination expression (using the chevron syntax, e.g. "print >> dest, values") and a list of expressions to be printed.

The function allocates a new SgPythonPrintStmt object using the provided destination and value list. If either the destination or the value list is non-null, the parent pointer of that child node is set to the newly created statement node to maintain proper parent-child relationships in the AST. After construction, a single source position is assigned to the node to indicate that it was introduced by a transformation rather than parsed from source code.

Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgPythonPrintStmt AST node. The caller is responsible for managing the lifetime of this node within the AST.
Warning
This function is intended for use with Python 2 AST construction. Python 3 does not have a print statement; instead, print is a built-in function. Using this builder for Python 3 ASTs may produce incorrect or unsupported AST structures.
Precondition
If dest is non-null, it must be a valid, heap-allocated SgExpression node that is not already owned by another AST node, as its parent pointer will be reassigned.
If values is non-null, it must be a valid, heap-allocated SgExprListExp node that is not already owned by another AST node, as its parent pointer will be reassigned.
Postcondition
The returned SgPythonPrintStmt node has its source position set to reflect a transformation origin.
If dest is non-null, dest->get_parent() returns the newly created SgPythonPrintStmt node.
If values is non-null, values->get_parent() returns the newly created SgPythonPrintStmt node.
Note
This builder follows the standard SageBuilder convention of using setOneSourcePositionForTransformation to mark synthesized nodes, distinguishing them from nodes parsed directly from source files.

Builds a new SgRangeBasedForStatement AST node using raw (non-frontend-interface) construction.

This function constructs a range-based for statement node (SgRangeBasedForStatement) in the ROSE abstract syntax tree (AST). It accepts the individual components that make up a C++11 range-based for loop and assembles them into a properly linked AST node.

The function allocates a new SgRangeBasedForStatement on the heap, initializes its source position to null via setOneSourcePositionNull, and then sets the parent pointer of each non-null child node to point to the newly created statement. This parent-linking step is essential for maintaining the integrity of the AST hierarchy.

The suffix _nfi (no frontend interface) indicates that this builder does not rely on the frontend parsing infrastructure and is intended for programmatic AST construction. Because the scope of child nodes is the SgRangeBasedForStatement itself, the statement node must be created before its children are fully constructed. As a result, some child arguments (such as initializer, range, and body) are permitted to be NULL at the time of the call, allowing deferred attachment of children.

end_declarationA pointer to the SgVariableDeclaration representing the end iterator declaration generated for the range-based for loop. May be NULL.
not_equal_expressionA pointer to the SgExpression representing the loop continuation condition (typically a not-equal comparison between begin and end iterators). May be NULL.
increment_expressionA pointer to the SgExpression representing the increment operation applied to the begin iterator at each loop iteration. May be NULL.
bodyA pointer to the SgStatement representing the body of the range-based for loop. May be NULL if not yet constructed at call time.

Warning
The caller is responsible for ensuring that child nodes passed as arguments are not simultaneously owned by another parent in the AST, as this function unconditionally sets the parent of each non-null child to the new statement node.

If any child pointer is non-NULL, it must point to a valid, fully allocated AST node of the appropriate type.
No child node passed as an argument should already have a parent set to a different AST node, as this function will overwrite the parent pointer.
Postcondition
The returned SgRangeBasedForStatement node is non-NULL.
The source position of the returned node is set to null (via setOneSourcePositionNull).
Each non-null child node has its parent pointer set to the returned SgRangeBasedForStatement node.
Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface for programmatic AST construction in ROSE. It is designed to support scenarios where child nodes must be constructed after the parent statement node, such as when resolving scoping dependencies during AST transformation or generation.
The internal assertion (ROSE_ASSERT) verifies that the allocation of the new node succeeded and that the result is non-NULL.

SgModifierType * SageBuilder::buildRestrictType ( SgType * base_type)

Builds a restrict-qualified modifier type wrapping a given base type.

This function constructs an SgModifierType node that applies the C/C++ restrict qualifier to the provided base type. The restrict qualifier is commonly used with pointer types to indicate that the pointer is the only means by which the referenced object is accessed, enabling certain compiler optimizations.

The function validates that the supplied base type is one of the permitted kinds: a pointer type (SgPointerType), a reference type (SgReferenceType), an array type (SgArrayType), a typedef type (SgTypedefType), or an existing modifier type (SgModifierType). If the base type does not satisfy any of these conditions, an error message is printed and the program is aborted.

Internally, the function allocates a new SgModifierType, sets its restrict modifier flag via setRestrict(), and then attempts to insert the new type into the global ROSE type table using SgModifierType::insertModifierTypeIntoTypeTable(). If an equivalent type already exists in the type table, the newly created node is deleted and the pre-existing type from the table is returned instead. This ensures type uniqueness within the AST.

base_typeA pointer to the base SgType upon which the restrict modifier is applied. Must be a pointer, reference, array, typedef, or modifier type. Must not be NULL.

Warning
If the base type is not a pointer, reference, array, typedef, or modifier type, the function prints an error message and calls ROSE_ABORT(), terminating the program. Callers must ensure the base type satisfies one of these constraints before invoking this function.
Precondition
base_type must not be NULL.
base_type must be an instance of SgPointerType, SgReferenceType, SgArrayType, SgTypedefType, or SgModifierType.
Postcondition
The returned SgModifierType has its restrict modifier flag set.
The returned type is registered in the global ROSE type table, ensuring uniqueness of the restrict-qualified type for the given base type.
Note
The type table insertion guarantees that duplicate restrict types are not created. If an equivalent type already exists, the newly allocated node is freed and the canonical type from the table is returned.
Support for typedef types and modifier types as valid base types was added incrementally to handle cases such as those demonstrated in test2014_77.c, test2012_03.c, and related test files.

◆ buildShortValHex()

SgShortVal * SageBuilder::buildShortValHex ( short v)

Builds an SgShortVal AST node representing a short integer value formatted as a hexadecimal literal.

This function constructs a new SgShortVal node in the ROSE abstract syntax tree (AST) using the provided short integer value. The internal string representation of the value is formatted in hexadecimal notation. For non-negative values, the hex string is produced directly via StringUtility::intToHex. For negative values, the absolute value is converted to hexadecimal and a leading minus sign is prepended to form the string representation.

After construction, the node is verified to be non-null via an assertion, and its source position information is initialized using setOneSourcePositionForTransformation, marking it as a compiler-generated transformation node rather than one derived from original source.

This function is part of the SageBuilder interface, which provides factory functions for programmatically constructing AST nodes during source-to-source transformation tasks.

Parameters
vThe short integer value to be represented by the constructed AST node. Both positive and negative short values are supported. The value is stored internally along with its hexadecimal string representation.
Returns
A pointer to a newly allocated SgShortVal node representing the given short integer value with a hexadecimal string form. The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-null.
Warning
The caller is responsible for managing the lifetime of the returned SgShortVal node. Improper handling may result in memory leaks if the node is not properly inserted into an AST or explicitly deleted.
Precondition
The value v must be a valid short integer within the range representable by the short type on the target platform.
Postcondition
The returned SgShortVal node is non-null, contains the provided value v, and has its source position set to reflect a compiler-generated transformation.
Note
The hexadecimal string representation is computed by casting the value to unsigned int before passing it to StringUtility::intToHex. For negative values, the negation is applied prior to the cast to obtain the magnitude. This means the string representation uses the absolute value in hex with a leading minus sign, rather than a two's complement representation.

◆ buildSourceFile() [1/2]

SgSourceFile * SageBuilder::buildSourceFile ( const std::string & inputFileName,
const std::string & outputFileName,
SgProject * project,
bool clear_globalScopeAcrossFiles )

Builds and returns an SgSourceFile node representing a C/C++ source file within a given ROSE project.

This function constructs an SgSourceFile AST node by delegating to the lower-level buildFile() function, which performs the primary parsing and AST construction. After the file is built, a secondary pass is performed over the source file via secondaryPassOverSourceFile() to attach token stream information, preprocessing directives, and comments in a manner consistent with token-based unparsing support.

The function also performs the following additional steps:

  1. It iterates over the existing file list in the provided SgProject to detect whether the newly built file corresponds to a previously processed file (identified by matching file names). This is relevant when a source file is built a second time, for example during outlining to a separate file or when constructing a dynamic library.
  2. It calls fixupSourcePositionFileSpecification() to update the source position file specification in all IR nodes of the newly built file so that they refer to the output file name rather than the input file name.
  3. It ensures that the global scope's isModified flag is reset to false upon completion. This is important for the correct operation of simpleFrontierDetectionForTokenStreamMapping() when a second file is constructed from the same original source.

The function asserts that the returned SgFile pointer is non-null, that it can be safely cast to an SgSourceFile, and that the resulting source file has a valid global scope.

Note that several code paths guarded by if 0 preprocessor blocks exist within the implementation for debugging and experimental purposes; these are inactive in normal builds.

Parameters
inputFileNameThe path to the input source file to be read and parsed.
outputFileNameThe path to the output file that the resulting SgSourceFile will represent. Source position information in the AST is updated to reflect this file name.
projectA pointer to the SgProject node to which the newly built SgSourceFile will be added. Must not be NULL.
clear_globalScopeAcrossFilesA boolean flag indicating whether the global scope should be cleared across files during construction. Defaults to false.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgSourceFile node. This pointer is guaranteed to be non-null and to have a valid global scope upon return.
Warning
The caller must ensure that the provided SgProject pointer is valid and non-null. Passing a null project pointer will result in assertion failures or undefined behavior.
This function resets the isModified flag on the global scope to false before returning. Any modifications made to the global scope during construction will not be reflected in the isModified state after this function returns.
When the same input file is built a second time (e.g., for outlining or dynamic library generation), care must be taken to avoid redundant collection of comments and CPP directives. The function contains logic to detect this case but does not automatically prevent all forms of redundant processing.
Precondition
project must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized SgProject node.
inputFileName must refer to a readable source file accessible on the file system.
outputFileName must be a valid file path string.
Postcondition
The returned SgSourceFile is a member of the file list of the provided SgProject.
The returned SgSourceFile has a non-null global scope (get_globalScope() != NULL).
Source position file specifications within the returned SgSourceFile's AST nodes have been updated to reflect outputFileName.
The global scope's isModified flag is set to false.
A secondary pass over the source file has been completed, attaching preprocessing information and token stream data.
Note
This function calls secondaryPassOverSourceFile() rather than attachPreprocessingInfo() in order to properly support token-based unparsing.
The function is part of the SageBuilder interface for programmatically constructing and manipulating ROSE ASTs.
The clear_globalScopeAcrossFiles parameter is forwarded directly to buildFile() and controls whether the global scope is cleared when processing multiple files.

Builds and returns a new SgSourceFile node associated with the given project.

This function provides a simplified API for constructing a new SgSourceFile AST node that is intended to have statements added to it programmatically and then unparsed (i.e., written out as source code). Parses a string containing a C/C++ statement and constructs the corresponding AST node.

This function uses the AstFromString parser infrastructure to convert a plain text string representation of a C/C++ statement into a fully constructed ROSE AST SgStatement node. Internally, it sets up the parser context by assigning the input character pointer and the enclosing scope node to the AstFromString global state variables, then invokes afs_match_statement() to perform the parse.

If parsing succeeds, the resulting parsed node is retrieved from AstFromString::c_parsed_node and cast to an SgStatement via isSgStatement. If parsing fails, an error message is printed to standard error and the program is aborted via ROSE_ABORT().

The implementation relies on the AstFromString module, whose source is located in src/frontend/SageIII/astFromString/AstFromString.h and the corresponding .C file. The AstFromString module uses global state variables such as c_char, c_sgnode, and c_parsed_node to communicate between the caller and the parser.

A pointer to the newly constructed SgStatement AST node corresponding to the parsed statement. The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-NULL if the function returns normally.
Warning
If the input string cannot be parsed as a valid statement within the given scope, this function prints an error message to standard error and calls ROSE_ABORT(), terminating the program. It does not return in that case.
This function modifies global state in the AstFromString module (AstFromString::c_char, AstFromString::c_sgnode, AstFromString::c_parsed_node). It is not thread-safe and should not be called concurrently from multiple threads.
Precondition
scope must not be NULL.
The string s must represent a syntactically valid C/C++ statement that can be parsed in the context of the provided scope.
The AstFromString parser infrastructure must be properly initialized and available at the time of the call.

Note

This function is intended for use in AST construction scenarios where a statement must be synthesized programmatically from source text, such as in code transformation or instrumentation passes.

Builds a template class declaration node (both defining and non-defining) in the ROSE IR.

This function constructs an SgTemplateClassDeclaration for a given template class, handling both the defining declaration and the non-defining (forward) declaration as required by the ROSE intermediate representation. It is the low-level "no frills" implementation (nfi) that performs the core construction work.

The function proceeds through the following major steps:

  1. If the provided scope is NULL, the top of the scope stack is used as the effective scope.
  2. Two name variants are computed from the input name: one without template specialization arguments (the base template name) and one with template specialization arguments appended, using appendTemplateArgumentsToName(). The latter is used as the declaration name throughout.
  3. A defining declaration (defdecl) is constructed. If a non-defining declaration is provided and it already has an associated defining declaration, that existing defining declaration is reused rather than creating a duplicate. Otherwise, a new SgTemplateClassDeclaration is allocated with a freshly built SgTemplateClassDefinition.
  4. The template parameter list and template specialization argument list are assigned to the defining declaration. The template name (without specialization arguments) is also set.
  5. A non-defining declaration (nondefdecl) is resolved. If the input nonDefiningDecl is NULL, the function first looks up an existing symbol in the scope. If found, the existing declaration is linked to the new defining declaration. If not found, a new non-defining SgTemplateClassDeclaration is allocated, its template parameters and specialization arguments are initialized, source position information is set, and a new SgTemplateClassSymbol is inserted into the scope's symbol table.
  6. The defining declaration's firstNondefiningDeclaration pointer is set to the non-defining declaration, and the template specialization arguments are set on the defining declaration.
  7. The SgClassType is shared between the non-defining and defining declarations so that the defining declaration does not hold a distinct type object.
  8. Several consistency assertions are performed at the end to verify the integrity of the constructed declaration pair, including checks on scope, type, parent, template name, and template argument parent relationships.

templateParameterList must not be NULL.

◆ buildTemplateInstantiationTypedefDeclaration_nfi()

SgTemplateInstantiationTypedefDeclaration * SageBuilder::buildTemplateInstantiationTypedefDeclaration_nfi ( SgName & name,
SgType * base_type,
SgScopeStatement * scope,
bool has_defining_base,
SgTemplateTypedefDeclaration * templateTypedefDeclaration,
SgTemplateArgumentPtrList & templateArgumentsList )

Builds a new SgTemplateInstantiationTypedefDeclaration node for a template typedef instantiation.

This function constructs and initializes a SgTemplateInstantiationTypedefDeclaration AST node representing the instantiation of a template typedef declaration. It is the "no front-end interaction" (nfi) variant, meaning it performs bottom-up construction without invoking the ROSE front-end parser.

The function proceeds through the following major steps:

  1. Validates that the provided base_type and scope are non-null.
  2. Derives both a name without template arguments and a name with template arguments appended, using the helper function appendTemplateArgumentsToName.
  3. Checks the given scope for a pre-existing SgTemplateTypedefSymbol matching the name-with-template-arguments. If one is found, the corresponding existing SgTemplateInstantiationTypedefDeclaration is returned immediately without creating a duplicate node.
  4. Determines the parent scope symbol by walking up to the enclosing declaration statement, if one exists.
  5. Allocates a new SgTemplateInstantiationTypedefDeclaration, supplying the name with template arguments, the base type, a null typedef type, the base declaration, the parent scope symbol, the originating template typedef declaration, and the template argument list.
  6. Sets the template name (without arguments) on the new node.
  7. Explicitly creates a new SgTypedefType via SgTypedefType::createType and attaches it to the declaration, since the constructor no longer performs this step automatically.
  8. Configures the first non-defining and defining declaration pointers, and nullifies source position information via setOneSourcePositionNull.
  9. Computes the mangled name and registers the template arguments on the declaration via setTemplateArgumentsInDeclaration.
  10. Creates a new SgTemplateTypedefSymbol for the declaration and inserts it into the scope's symbol table under the name with template arguments.
  11. Sets the scope and parent pointers on the declaration node.

Conditional debug output is available when the preprocessor macro DEBUG__SageBuilder__buildTemplateInstantiationTypedefDeclaration_nfi is defined, printing intermediate values such as names, pointer addresses, and class names to standard output.

scopePointer to the SgScopeStatement representing the scope into which the new declaration is to be inserted. Must not be NULL.

templateTypedefDeclarationPointer to the originating SgTemplateTypedefDeclaration from which this instantiation is derived. Must not be NULL.
templateArgumentsListReference to the list of SgTemplateArgument pointers representing the template arguments for this instantiation. Used to form the full name and to register arguments on the declaration.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgTemplateInstantiationTypedefDeclaration node, or a pointer to an existing node if a matching symbol was already present in the given scope. The returned pointer is never NULL.
Warning
If a SgTemplateTypedefSymbol with the name-with-template-arguments already exists in the scope at the time of symbol insertion (after the initial pre-existence check), an error message is printed to standard output and an assertion failure is triggered. This indicates an internal consistency error in the AST construction process.
The typedef type (SgTypedefType) is not set by the SgTemplateInstantiationTypedefDeclaration constructor; it must be created explicitly afterward. This function handles that step, but callers should be aware of this non-standard construction pattern if modifying or extending the function.
Precondition
base_type must not be NULL.
scope must not be NULL.
scope->get_parent() must not be NULL if scope is non-null.
templateTypedefDeclaration must not be NULL.
If a pre-existing SgTemplateTypedefSymbol is found in scope for the given name with template arguments, its associated declaration must be a valid SgTemplateInstantiationTypedefDeclaration.

The returned SgTemplateInstantiationTypedefDeclaration has a non-null SgTypedefType attached via get_type().
The returned declaration's firstNondefiningDeclaration points to itself.
The returned declaration's definingDeclaration is NULL.
A SgTemplateTypedefSymbol for the name with template arguments is present in the given scope's symbol table (either pre-existing or newly inserted).
The returned declaration's scope and parent are set to the provided scope.
Source position information on the returned declaration is set to null via setOneSourcePositionNull.

Bottom-up construction of this node type is not fully supported in all contexts; the function asserts that a non-null scope is provided and does not handle the case where scope is absent.
The has_defining_base parameter is accepted for interface consistency but is not directly referenced in the current implementation body.
The mangled name is computed and stored internally but is not returned directly; it is used as part of the declaration setup.
Debug tracing can be enabled at compile time by defining the preprocessor macro DEBUG__SageBuilder__buildTemplateInstantiationTypedefDeclaration_nfi.

  2. The parent scope symbol is resolved from the enclosing scope's parent declaration, if one exists, to handle certain corner cases in C++ template scoping.

  6. The declaration is marked as its own firstNondefiningDeclaration, and its definingDeclaration is set to NULL, as required for AST consistency.

If scope is non-NULL, scope->get_parent() must not be NULL.

The declaration node's type must be NULL prior to the call to SgTypedefType::createType.

  6. Sets the source position of the declaration node itself to null.

The source positions of the returned declaration node and its associated SgVariableDefinition are set to null.

Builds and returns a new SgThrowOp AST node representing a C++ throw expression.

This function constructs a new SgThrowOp node for use in the ROSE abstract syntax tree (AST). It supports both throw expressions with an operand and re-throw expressions (where the operand may be NULL). When a non-NULL operand is provided, the type of the throw operation is derived from the operand's type via get_type(). If the operand is NULL (as in a bare re-throw statement), the type is also set to NULL.

After construction, if the operand is non-NULL, markLhsValues() is called on the result to properly annotate left-hand-side value information within the subtree. The source position of the resulting node is set using setOneSourcePositionForTransformation() to indicate that this node was introduced by a transformation rather than parsed from source. If the operand is non-NULL, its parent pointer is updated to point to the newly created SgThrowOp node.

An assertion is made to confirm that the resulting node was successfully allocated before returning.

Parameters
operand_iA pointer to the SgExpression representing the operand of the throw expression. This parameter is allowed to be NULL, which corresponds to a re-throw statement (i.e., a bare "throw;" with no operand).
throwKindAn enumeration value of type SgThrowOp::e_throw_kind that specifies the kind of throw operation being represented (e.g., a normal throw or a re-throw).
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgThrowOp AST node. The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-NULL (enforced by an internal assertion).
Warning
The caller is responsible for managing the lifetime of the returned SgThrowOp node and integrating it correctly into the AST. Improper use may lead to memory leaks or dangling pointers if the node is not properly attached to the AST.
Precondition
If operand_i is non-NULL, it must be a valid, fully constructed SgExpression node with a valid type accessible via get_type().
Postcondition
The returned SgThrowOp node has its source position marked as a transformation.
If operand_i is non-NULL, its parent pointer is set to the returned SgThrowOp node.
If operand_i is non-NULL, markLhsValues() has been applied to the returned node.
Note
A NULL operand_i is explicitly supported and corresponds to a C++ re-throw expression (a standalone "throw;" statement). This is a deliberate design choice and not an error condition.

◆ buildTryStmt() [1/2]

SgTryStmt * SageBuilder::buildTryStmt ( SgBasicBlock * try_body,
SgBasicBlock * finally_body )

Builds an SgTryStmt node representing a try statement, primarily intended for use with Java.

This function constructs an SgTryStmt abstract syntax tree (AST) node from the provided try body and an optional finally body. It is designed for use in the context of Java try-finally constructs within the ROSE compiler framework.

When an SgTryStmt is allocated, its constructor automatically preallocates an SgCatchStatementSeq for the internal field p_catch_statement_sequence_root. Because of this internal allocation, callers must not use set_catch_statement_seq_root() to assign a catch statement sequence after construction, as doing so would leave the constructor-allocated object dangling and cause a memory leak or undefined behavior.

The function sets the parent pointer of the try body to the newly created SgTryStmt node. If a finally body is provided, it is attached to the try statement and its parent pointer is similarly set. Source position information is also initialized on the resulting node using setSourcePosition().

Parameters
try_bodyA pointer to the SgBasicBlock representing the body of the try block. Must not be NULL.
finally_bodyA pointer to the SgBasicBlock representing the body of the finally block. May be NULL if no finally block is present, in which case no finally body is attached to the resulting try statement.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgTryStmt node with the try body (and optionally the finally body) attached and parent pointers properly set.
Warning
Do not use set_catch_statement_seq_root() on the returned SgTryStmt node. The constructor preallocates an SgCatchStatementSeq internally, and replacing it via that setter will leave the originally allocated object dangling, resulting in a memory leak or undefined behavior.
Precondition
try_body must not be NULL. An assertion failure will occur if a NULL pointer is passed.
try_body must be a valid, fully constructed SgBasicBlock node.
If finally_body is non-NULL, it must be a valid, fully constructed SgBasicBlock node.
Postcondition
The returned SgTryStmt node has its try body set and the try body's parent pointer points to the returned SgTryStmt.
If finally_body was non-NULL, the returned SgTryStmt has its finally body set and the finally body's parent pointer points to the returned SgTryStmt.
The returned SgTryStmt has default source position information initialized.
Note
This function is primarily intended for building Java try-finally constructs. For try-catch constructs, additional handling of the preallocated SgCatchStatementSeq is required through the appropriate ROSE API.

SgTryStmt * SageBuilder::buildTryStmt ( SgStatement * body,

Builds a try statement node in the ROSE abstract syntax tree.

This function constructs an SgTryStmt node representing a C++ try statement, associating it with a body statement and up to five optional catch clauses. The body statement is required and must not be NULL; its parent pointer is set to the newly created try statement. Source position information is initialized for the try statement and, if present, for its internal catch statement sequence root node. Each non-NULL catch option statement is appended to the try statement in order from catch0 through catch4. Catch clauses that are NULL are silently skipped, allowing callers to supply fewer than five handlers without padding.

The function uses internal ROSE builder utilities (setSourcePosition) to assign default source position metadata to the constructed nodes, ensuring that the resulting AST nodes carry valid source location information. Assertions are used throughout to verify structural invariants of the constructed AST nodes.

Parameters
bodyThe body statement of the try block. Must not be NULL. Its parent pointer will be set to the newly created SgTryStmt node.
catch0The first catch option statement to append. May be NULL, in which case it is ignored.
catch1The second catch option statement to append. May be NULL, in which case it is ignored.
catch2The third catch option statement to append. May be NULL, in which case it is ignored.
catch3The fourth catch option statement to append. May be NULL, in which case it is ignored.
catch4The fifth catch option statement to append. May be NULL, in which case it is ignored.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgTryStmt node with the body and all non-NULL catch clauses attached.
Precondition
body must not be NULL; a failed assertion will terminate the program if it is.
Each non-NULL catch parameter must point to a valid, properly initialized SgCatchOptionStmt node.
Postcondition
The returned SgTryStmt node has its body's parent pointer set to itself.
Source position information is initialized for the SgTryStmt node and, if the catch statement sequence root exists without source position data, for that root node as well.
All non-NULL catch option statements have been appended to the try statement in the order catch0, catch1, catch2, catch3, catch4.
Warning
The function supports a maximum of five catch clauses. If more than five catch handlers are needed, additional handlers must be appended manually after the function returns.
Passing a NULL body will trigger an assertion failure and terminate the program. Callers must ensure the body is a valid, non-NULL pointer.
Note
If the catch statement sequence root already has valid start and end of construct source position pointers, the function will not overwrite them. An assertion verifies consistency between the start and end positions in this case.

SgTupleExp * SageBuilder::buildTupleExp ( const std::vector< SgExpression * > & elts)

Builds a tuple expression node populated with a list of sub-expressions.

This function constructs an SgTupleExp AST node and populates it with the provided vector of SgExpression pointers. It first creates an empty SgTupleExp node by calling the no-argument overload of buildTupleExp(), then appends each expression from the supplied vector to the node's internal expression list using appendExpressionList(). This is a convenience overload that allows callers to initialize a tuple expression with multiple elements in a single call, rather than constructing an empty node and appending elements manually.

Parameters
eltsA constant reference to a vector of SgExpression pointers representing the elements to be included in the tuple expression. Each pointer in the vector must be a valid, non-null SgExpression node. The order of elements in the vector determines their order in the resulting tuple.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgTupleExp node containing all the expressions from the input vector as its child elements.
Precondition
Each SgExpression pointer in the elts vector must be non-null and must point to a valid, properly initialized SgExpression node.
The SageBuilder infrastructure must be properly initialized before calling this function.
Postcondition
The returned SgTupleExp node contains exactly the expressions provided in elts, in the same order, as its child expression list.
The parent pointers of the child expressions are updated to reference the newly created SgTupleExp node.
Warning
Passing null pointers within the elts vector results in undefined behavior and may cause crashes or corrupt the AST.
The caller is responsible for ensuring that the returned SgTupleExp node is properly inserted into the AST to avoid memory leaks or dangling nodes.
Note
This function is an overload of buildTupleExp() that accepts a pre-assembled vector of expressions. For building an empty tuple expression, use the no-argument overload buildTupleExp() directly.
Ownership of the expression nodes in elts is transferred to the resulting SgTupleExp node upon insertion; callers should not delete or reuse these nodes independently after this call.

Builds an SgTupleExp node containing up to ten expression elements.

This function constructs a new SgTupleExp AST node representing a tuple expression, which is commonly used in languages such as Python that support tuple literals. Up to ten SgExpression pointers may be provided as elements of the tuple. Each non-null expression argument is appended to the tuple in order using appendExpression. Arguments that are null pointers are silently skipped and do not contribute an element to the resulting tuple. After all elements are appended, the source position of the new node is set to a default transformation position via setOneSourcePositionForTransformation, marking the node as compiler-generated rather than originating from user source code.

Parameters
elt1Pointer to the first expression element to include in the tuple, or null if no first element is desired.
elt2Pointer to the second expression element to include in the tuple, or null if no second element is desired.
elt3Pointer to the third expression element to include in the tuple, or null if no third element is desired.
elt4Pointer to the fourth expression element to include in the tuple, or null if no fourth element is desired.
elt5Pointer to the fifth expression element to include in the tuple, or null if no fifth element is desired.
elt6Pointer to the sixth expression element to include in the tuple, or null if no sixth element is desired.
elt7Pointer to the seventh expression element to include in the tuple, or null if no seventh element is desired.
elt8Pointer to the eighth expression element to include in the tuple, or null if no eighth element is desired.
elt9Pointer to the ninth expression element to include in the tuple, or null if no ninth element is desired.
elt10Pointer to the tenth expression element to include in the tuple, or null if no tenth element is desired.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgTupleExp node. The returned pointer is never null; the function asserts successful allocation internally.
Precondition
Each non-null expression pointer passed as an argument must point to a valid, fully constructed SgExpression node that is not already attached as a child of another AST node, to avoid ownership conflicts in the AST.
Postcondition
The returned SgTupleExp node contains, as children, all non-null expression arguments in the order they were provided.
The source position of the returned node is set to a transformation position, indicating it was generated rather than parsed from source.
Warning
Passing the same SgExpression pointer for more than one argument will result in the same node being appended multiple times, which may produce an invalid AST with shared child nodes.
This function supports a maximum of ten tuple elements. If more elements are required, consider building the SgTupleExp node manually and appending additional expressions using appendExpression.
Note
Null pointer arguments are silently ignored; callers do not need to provide all ten arguments if fewer elements are needed. Trailing arguments default to null if not specified, provided appropriate default argument declarations are available in the header.
The source position is marked as a transformation, which is appropriate for AST nodes introduced by program transformation tools rather than those parsed directly from user source code.

◆ buildTupleExp_nfi() [1/2]

SgTupleExp * SageBuilder::buildTupleExp_nfi ( )

Builds and returns a new, empty SgTupleExp AST node with a null source position.

This function allocates a new SgTupleExp node on the heap using the "no file info" (nfi) convention, meaning that the source position information is explicitly set to null rather than being derived from a real source location. This is typically used when constructing synthetic or compiler-generated tuple expressions that do not correspond to any specific location in the original source code.

The function follows the standard SageBuilder nfi pattern: it allocates the node, asserts that allocation succeeded, sets the source position to null via setOneSourcePositionNull, and then returns the newly constructed node.

Returns
A pointer to the newly allocated SgTupleExp node with a null source position. The caller is responsible for managing the lifetime of this node, typically by inserting it into the AST, which will then take ownership.
Warning
The returned pointer must not be used after the owning AST has been destroyed, as the memory will be freed along with the rest of the AST. Failing to insert the returned node into the AST may result in a memory leak.
Precondition
The ROSE infrastructure must be properly initialized before calling this function.
Postcondition
A valid SgTupleExp node is returned with its source position set to null.
The returned node contains no child expressions (empty tuple).
Note
The "nfi" suffix in the function name stands for "no file info," indicating that the constructed node is not associated with any particular source file location. This distinguishes it from builder variants that accept source position information as parameters.
An assertion is performed immediately after allocation to guard against memory allocation failures.

base_type must be a valid, non-null pointer to an existing SgType node.
name must be a non-empty string representing a valid C/C++ identifier.
If scope is non-null, it must point to a valid SgScopeStatement node already present in the AST.
Postcondition

The returned node is fully initialized and suitable for insertion into the AST at the specified scope.
Warning
Passing a null base_type may result in undefined behavior or an assertion failure within the underlying buildTypedefDeclaration_nfi() function.

◆ buildTypedefDeclaration_nfi()

SgTypedefDeclaration * SageBuilder::buildTypedefDeclaration_nfi ( const std::string & name,
SgType * base_type,
SgScopeStatement * scope,
bool has_defining_base )

Builds a non-frontend-interface (nfi) SgTypedefDeclaration AST node for a typedef declaration.

This function constructs a new SgTypedefDeclaration node representing a C/C++ typedef declaration and inserts the corresponding typedef symbol into the given scope's symbol table. It is intended for bottom-up AST construction within the ROSE compiler infrastructure.

The function performs the following steps:

  1. Validates that the provided base type is non-null.
  2. Resolves the scope to the top of the scope stack if no explicit scope is provided.
  3. Strips pointer, reference, and typedef layers from the base type to obtain the underlying named type, and retrieves its associated declaration (base_decl) if applicable.
  4. Determines the parent scope symbol by examining the parent of the scope node. For Ada discriminated types and certain edge cases, this step is conditionally skipped or adjusted. This logic is guarded by the ifndef ROSE_USE_CLANG_FRONTEND preprocessor directive.
  5. Allocates a new SgTypedefDeclaration node with the given name, base type, base declaration, and parent scope symbol.
  6. Sets the scope and parent of the new declaration node before creating the associated SgTypedefType, because the type creation may depend on the scope being set in order to produce a unique mangled name (particularly relevant for template typedefs).
  7. Configures the declaration as a non-defining declaration by setting firstNondefiningDeclaration to itself and definingDeclaration to NULL, consistent with AST consistency requirements.
  8. Sets all source position information to null via setOneSourcePositionNull.
  9. If the base declaration is a class declaration, sets the parent pointer of the defining or non-defining class declaration as appropriate, based on the has_defining_base flag. This handles nested typedef cases such as "typedef struct Frame { int x; } st_frame;".
  10. Creates a new SgTypedefSymbol wrapping the new declaration and inserts it into the scope's symbol table under the given name.
Parameters
nameThe name of the typedef being declared.
base_typeThe underlying type that the typedef aliases. Must not be NULL.
scopeThe scope in which the typedef declaration is to be inserted. If NULL, the top of the current scope stack is used.
has_defining_baseIndicates whether the base type has a defining declaration (e.g., a struct defined inline within the typedef). When true, the parent pointer of the defining class declaration is set to the new typedef declaration node if it has not already been set. When false, the non-defining class declaration's parent pointer is set instead.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgTypedefDeclaration node, which has been inserted into the given scope's symbol table.
Warning
Bottom-up construction for SgTypedefDeclaration nodes is not fully supported in all contexts. Callers should ensure that the scope and base type are fully constructed before calling this function.
The Ada language frontend has special handling for discriminated types and may not set the declaration link for Ada typedef declarations. The behavior under the Clang frontend is also conditionally compiled out via the ifndef ROSE_USE_CLANG_FRONTEND guard.
Sharing of base declarations across multiple files can occur when the base type's declaration is retrieved from a named type. This may cause issues when the typedef has a defining declaration for a base type in multiple translation units.
Precondition
base_type must not be NULL.
If scope is NULL, the scope stack must be non-empty so that topScopeStack() returns a valid scope.
If scope is non-NULL, scope->get_parent() must not be NULL (except in Ada discriminated type contexts).
For non-Ada, non-Clang builds, if the parent of the scope is a declaration statement, that declaration must have a valid firstNondefiningDeclaration.
Postcondition
A new SgTypedefDeclaration node is allocated and configured as a non-defining declaration with its firstNondefiningDeclaration pointing to itself and its definingDeclaration set to NULL.
The new declaration's scope and parent are set to the resolved scope.
The new declaration's associated SgTypedefType is created and attached.
All source position fields of the new declaration are set to null.
A new SgTypedefSymbol is created and inserted into the resolved scope's symbol table under the given name.
If the base declaration is a class declaration, the appropriate defining or non-defining class declaration's parent pointer is set to the new typedef declaration node if it was previously unset.
Note
The scope must be set on the declaration before SgTypedefType::createType is called, because the type creation relies on the mangled name of the declaration, which in turn requires the scope to be established. This is especially important for SgTemplateTypedefDeclaration nodes.
This function does not perform full AST post-processing. Callers may need to invoke AstPostProcessing() or resetParentPointers() separately if additional parent pointer fixups are required.
The suffix _nfi indicates that this builder does not use the frontend interface and is intended for programmatic AST construction rather than parsing.

The function allocates a new SgTypeIdOp node using the provided operand expression and operand type, asserts that allocation succeeded, and then assigns a transformation source position to the resulting node to indicate it was introduced programmatically rather than parsed from source code.

SgTypeOfType * SageBuilder::buildTypeOfType ( SgExpression * base_expression,
