Builds a GNU typeof operator node in the ROSE IR.

This function constructs an SgTypeOfType node representing the GNU typeof operator, which yields the type of a given expression or type at compile time. The construction strategy varies depending on the nature of the inputs provided:

  1. If base_expression is a function parameter reference expression (SgFunctionParameterRefExp), the SgTypeOfType node is created directly via the new operator, passing the expression and a NULL type argument. The base_type is then set explicitly on the resulting node.
  2. If base_expression is non-NULL but is not an SgFunctionParameterRefExp, the node is created using SgTypeOfType::createType with the expression and a NULL type argument. This path uses the type system's internal deduplication and caching mechanism.
  3. If base_expression is NULL, base_type must be non-NULL. In this case, SgTypeOfType::createType is called with the base_type directly, and the resulting node's base type is verified to match the provided base_type.

In all cases, if base_expression is non-NULL, its parent pointer is set to the newly created SgTypeOfType node. The function uses a compile-time debug flag (DEBUG_TYPEOF_TYPE) controlled by a define to enable diagnostic output during development.

Parameters
base_expressionPointer to the expression whose type is to be queried using the typeof operator. May be NULL if base_type is provided instead. If non-NULL, its parent pointer will be updated to point to the resulting SgTypeOfType node.
base_typePointer to the base type to be used when base_expression is NULL or when the result node requires an explicit base type assignment. Must be non-NULL if base_expression is NULL.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgTypeOfType node representing the GNU typeof operator. The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-NULL.
Precondition
At least one of base_expression or base_type must be non-NULL. If base_expression is NULL, then base_type must be non-NULL.
Postcondition
The returned SgTypeOfType pointer is non-NULL and represents a valid typeof type node in the ROSE IR.
If base_expression is non-NULL, its parent pointer is set to the returned SgTypeOfType node.
Warning
Passing both base_expression and base_type as NULL will trigger an assertion failure at runtime.
Note
This function supports the GNU typeof extension, which is not part of standard C or C++. The behavior when base_expression is an SgFunctionParameterRefExp differs from the general case because such expressions require direct allocation rather than going through the type system's createType factory, which may deduplicate or cache types.
The internal debug flag DEBUG_TYPEOF_TYPE can be enabled at compile time via the define directive to print diagnostic information about the expression and type pointers being processed.

◆ buildTypeTraitBuiltinOperator()

SgTypeTraitBuiltinOperator * SageBuilder::buildTypeTraitBuiltinOperator ( SgName functionName,
SgNodePtrList parameters )

Builds an AST node representing a builtin type trait operator expression.

This function constructs a new SgTypeTraitBuiltinOperator node, which represents compiler-builtin type trait operators used in C++ (and extensions thereof). Type trait operators are special compiler extensions increasingly common in modern versions of GNU and other compilers. They typically accept types as arguments and are used to query properties of types at compile time (for example, __is_pod, __has_trivial_constructor, and similar constructs).

The function allocates a new SgTypeTraitBuiltinOperator node initialized with the provided function name, then iterates over the supplied parameter list, appending each parameter node to the internal argument list of the newly created operator node. Each parameter node's parent pointer is updated to point to the newly created operator node, maintaining proper parent-child relationships within the AST.

This builder is part of the SageBuilder interface, which provides factory functions for constructing ROSE AST nodes in a consistent and correct manner.

Parameters
functionNameThe name of the builtin type trait operator to be represented (e.g., __is_pod, __has_trivial_destructor). This name is stored directly in the resulting AST node.
parametersA list of SgNode pointers representing the arguments (typically types) passed to the type trait operator. Each node in this list is added to the operator node's argument list, and its parent pointer is set to the newly created operator node.
Returns
A pointer to the newly allocated and initialized SgTypeTraitBuiltinOperator node representing the specified builtin type trait operator with its arguments. The caller is responsible for ensuring this node is properly inserted into the AST.
Warning
The returned pointer is heap-allocated. Improper management of this node (e.g., failing to insert it into the AST or failing to let the AST memory pool manage it) may result in memory leaks.
Each node in the parameters list will have its parent pointer modified to point to the newly created operator node. Passing nodes that are already part of another AST subtree without proper detachment may corrupt the existing AST structure.
Precondition
functionName must be a valid, non-empty SgName representing the name of a compiler-builtin type trait operator.
Each element in the parameters list must be a valid, non-null SgNode pointer.
Postcondition
The returned SgTypeTraitBuiltinOperator node is non-null and contains all nodes from the parameters list as its arguments.
The parent pointer of each node in the parameters list is set to the returned SgTypeTraitBuiltinOperator node.
Note
This function was introduced to support compiler extensions required for implementing type traits in C++, which are used with increasing frequency in newer versions of GNU and other compilers.
The SgTypeTraitBuiltinOperator node is allocated using the new operator and is expected to be managed by the ROSE AST memory pool after insertion into the AST.

Constructs a new unary expression node of the specified type with the given operand.

This function template creates a new AST (Abstract Syntax Tree) node representing a unary expression. The type parameter T determines the specific kind of unary expression to construct (for example, SgMinusOp, SgNotOp, or any other unary expression class derived from SgExpression). The function allocates a new instance of T, passing the provided operand and a NULL second argument to the constructor, which is the conventional pattern for unary expression nodes in the ROSE framework.

If the operand is non-NULL, the function sets the operand's parent pointer to the newly created expression node and calls markLhsValues() to properly annotate any left-hand side value information on the result. This step is required because markLhsValues() internally asserts that the operand is not NULL.

After construction, the function calls SageInterface::setOneSourcePositionForTransformation() on the result to assign a default source position, marking the node as a transformation artifact rather than original source code.

Parameters
operandA pointer to the SgExpression node that serves as the operand of the unary expression. May be NULL, in which case parent-setting and lvalue marking are skipped.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed unary expression node of type T. The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-NULL, as enforced by an internal assertion.
Precondition
The type parameter T must be a unary expression class whose constructor accepts an SgExpression pointer as its first argument and a NULL pointer as its second argument.
If operand is non-NULL, it must be a valid, well-formed SgExpression node.
Postcondition
The returned node is a valid, heap-allocated instance of T.
If operand is non-NULL, operand->get_parent() returns the newly created node.
The returned node has a default transformation source position assigned.
Warning
The caller is responsible for managing the lifetime of the returned node. Failing to attach it to the AST or explicitly delete it may result in memory leaks.
markLhsValues() internally asserts that the operand is non-NULL; this is safely guarded by the NULL check in this function, but callers should be aware of this constraint when extending or modifying this function.
Note
This is a generic helper intended to reduce code duplication when building various kinds of unary expression nodes in the ROSE AST builder interface. Specialized builder functions for individual unary operators typically delegate to this template.

◆ buildUnaryExpression_nfi()

T * SageBuilder::buildUnaryExpression_nfi ( SgExpression * operand)

Builds a unary expression node of the specified type without file information.

This is a generic template function that constructs a new unary expression AST node of type T, which must be a subclass of SgExpression representing a unary operation. The suffix "_nfi" stands for "no file information", indicating that the source position is set to a default or null state rather than being derived from actual source file locations.

The function allocates a new node of type T, assigns the provided operand as its child expression, and sets the parent pointer of the operand back to the newly created node to maintain proper parent-child relationships in the AST. If the operand is non-null, the function also invokes markLhsValues() to correctly annotate left-hand-side value information on the expression. The source position of the resulting node is initialized via SageInterface::setSourcePosition(), and the need-parenthesis flag is set to false by default.

Template Parameters
TThe type of the unary expression node to be created. Must be a concrete subclass of SgExpression that accepts a unary expression constructor taking an SgExpression pointer and a NULL second argument.
Parameters
operandA pointer to the SgExpression that serves as the operand of the unary expression. May be NULL, in which case parent-setting and lvalue marking are skipped.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created unary expression node of type T. The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-null, as the function asserts successful allocation.
Warning
The caller is responsible for managing the lifetime of the returned node and integrating it into the AST appropriately. Failing to attach the returned node to the AST may result in memory leaks or dangling references.
The type parameter T must be a unary expression class whose constructor accepts (SgExpression*, SgExpression*) or a compatible signature. Using an incompatible type will result in a compilation error or undefined behavior.
Precondition
If operand is non-null, it must be a valid, properly initialized SgExpression node. Passing a partially constructed or corrupted expression node may lead to undefined behavior.
Postcondition
The returned node of type T is fully constructed with its operand set and parent pointer of the operand updated to point to the new node (if operand is non-null).
The source position of the returned node is initialized via SageInterface::setSourcePosition().
The need-parenthesis flag of the returned node is set to false.
If operand is non-null, lvalue annotations are applied to the returned node via markLhsValues().
Note
This function is intended for internal or low-level AST construction where file information is not yet available or not required. For building unary expressions with proper source location information, consider using the corresponding builder functions that accept file information parameters.
The function uses ROSE_ASSERT to verify that memory allocation for the new node succeeded. In builds where assertions are disabled, a failed allocation may not be detected immediately.

◆ buildUnknownType()

SgTypeUnknown * SageBuilder::buildUnknownType ( )

Builds and returns an SgTypeUnknown node representing an unknown type in the ROSE AST.

This function constructs a new SgTypeUnknown instance by invoking the static factory method SgTypeUnknown::createType(). The SgTypeUnknown type is used within the ROSE compiler framework to represent types that cannot be resolved or are otherwise unrecognized during AST construction or transformation. This is useful in scenarios where a placeholder type is needed, such as when processing code with incomplete type information or when building synthetic AST nodes that do not yet have a fully determined type.

The function asserts that the resulting pointer is non-null before returning, ensuring that type creation succeeded. If the assertion fails, the program will terminate, indicating an internal error in the type creation mechanism.

Returns
A pointer to a newly created SgTypeUnknown node. The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-null upon successful return.
Precondition
The ROSE infrastructure must be properly initialized before calling this function, as it relies on internal type creation mechanisms provided by the SgTypeUnknown class.
Postcondition
A valid SgTypeUnknown object has been created and its pointer returned. The returned object is managed by the ROSE memory pool and should not be manually deleted by the caller.
Warning
The caller should not attempt to free or delete the returned pointer, as the lifetime of the SgTypeUnknown node is managed internally by the ROSE AST memory management system.
Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface, which provides factory functions for constructing ROSE AST nodes. SgTypeUnknown is typically used as a placeholder and may not be valid in all contexts where a fully resolved type is required.

Builds an SgUnsignedLongLongIntVal AST node using a numeric value and its string representation, without file information.

This function constructs a new SgUnsignedLongLongIntVal node, which represents an unsigned long long integer literal value in the ROSE abstract syntax tree (AST). The suffix "_nfi" stands for "no file information", indicating that the resulting node will have its source position set to null rather than being associated with any particular location in a source file. This is typical for compiler-generated or synthetic AST nodes that do not correspond to any specific location in user source code.

Internally, the function allocates a new SgUnsignedLongLongIntVal object using the provided numeric value and string representation, asserts that the allocation succeeded (i.e., the pointer is not null), and then calls setOneSourcePositionNull to clear any source position information from the node before returning it.

Parameters
vThe unsigned long long integer value to be stored in the AST node.
strA string representation of the integer literal, as it appeared or should appear in source code (e.g., "42ULL"). This is stored alongside the numeric value in the node.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgUnsignedLongLongIntVal AST node initialized with the given value and string, and with its source position information set to null.
Warning
The caller is responsible for managing the lifetime of the returned SgUnsignedLongLongIntVal pointer. Failing to properly insert the node into the AST or to manage its memory may result in memory leaks.
Precondition
The string parameter str should be a valid textual representation of an unsigned long long integer literal, consistent with the numeric value v.
Postcondition
The returned SgUnsignedLongLongIntVal node is fully initialized with the provided value and string representation.
The source position of the returned node is set to null, meaning it carries no file or line information.
The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-null; the function will assert and abort if memory allocation fails.
Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface, which provides factory functions for constructing ROSE AST nodes. Nodes created with "_nfi" variants are commonly used when generating synthetic code transformations where no original source location is applicable.
The string representation str is stored in the node separately from the numeric value v and may be used during unparsing to reproduce the original or intended textual form of the literal.

◆ buildUpcRelaxedType()

SgModifierType * SageBuilder::buildUpcRelaxedType ( SgType * base_type)

Builds a UPC relaxed modifier type wrapping a given base type.

This function constructs a new SgModifierType node that applies the UPC relaxed access modifier to the provided base type. In Unified Parallel C (UPC), the relaxed qualifier indicates that accesses to shared data do not require strict memory consistency guarantees, allowing the compiler and runtime to reorder or overlap memory operations for improved performance.

Internally, the function allocates a new SgModifierType wrapping the given base type, sets its UPC access modifier to e_upc_relaxed, and then attempts to insert the newly created type into the global type table via SgModifierType::insertModifierTypeIntoTypeTable(). If an equivalent type already exists in the type table, the pre-existing type is returned and the newly allocated type is deleted to avoid duplication in the AST type pool. This deduplication ensures that structurally identical types share a single representation in the ROSE intermediate representation.

Parameters
base_typeA pointer to the SgType that serves as the base type for the UPC relaxed modifier type. Must not be NULL.
Returns
A pointer to an SgModifierType representing the UPC relaxed qualified version of the given base type. The returned pointer may refer to a pre-existing type from the type table if an equivalent type was already registered.
Warning
The caller must not delete the returned SgModifierType pointer, as it is owned and managed by the ROSE type table infrastructure.
If base_type is NULL, an assertion failure will be triggered at runtime. Always provide a valid, non-NULL base type.
Precondition
base_type must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid SgType node that has already been properly initialized and is part of the AST.
Postcondition
The returned SgModifierType is registered in the global ROSE type table with its UPC access modifier set to e_upc_relaxed.
If a newly allocated SgModifierType was found to be a duplicate of an existing entry in the type table, the duplicate is deleted and the canonical type table entry is returned instead.
Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface for constructing UPC-specific AST nodes. It is intended for use when building or transforming ASTs that involve UPC shared memory qualifiers.
The UPC relaxed qualifier is distinct from the UPC strict qualifier. Use buildUpcStrictType() when strict memory consistency semantics are required.

A layout value of -1 conventionally indicates that no explicit block size was specified (i.e., plain "shared" without a block size qualifier).

Internally, the function allocates a new SgModifierType, configures its UPC modifier to mark the type as shared, and sets the layout field. The newly constructed type is then inserted into the global type table via SgModifierType::insertModifierTypeIntoTypeTable(). If an equivalent type already exists in the type table, the newly allocated node is deleted and the pre-existing canonical type is returned instead, ensuring type uniqueness within the AST.

If base_type is NULL, an assertion failure will be triggered at runtime. Always provide a valid, non-NULL base type.

◆ buildUpcStrictType()

SgModifierType * SageBuilder::buildUpcStrictType ( SgType * base_type)

Builds a UPC strict modifier type wrapping a given base type.

This function constructs a new SgModifierType node that applies the UPC strict access modifier (e_upc_strict) to the provided base type. UPC (Unified Parallel C) strict memory access semantics enforce ordering constraints on shared memory accesses, ensuring that all shared memory operations are visible to other threads in the order they were issued.

Internally, the function allocates a new SgModifierType using the supplied base type, then sets the UPC access modifier to e_upc_strict via the modifier's accessor methods. The newly created type is then inserted into the global type table using SgModifierType::insertModifierTypeIntoTypeTable. If an equivalent type already exists in the type table, the duplicate is deleted and the pre-existing canonical type is returned instead. This deduplication step ensures that the IR maintains a single canonical representation for each unique type.

base_typeA pointer to the SgType that will serve as the base type for the newly created UPC strict modifier type. Must not be NULL.

Warning
Passing NULL as base_type will trigger an assertion failure and abort the program. Always ensure that base_type is a valid, non-NULL SgType pointer before calling this function.
Precondition
base_type must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid SgType node.
Postcondition
The returned SgModifierType has its UPC access modifier set to e_upc_strict and is registered in the global type table.
If a duplicate type was created during the call, it has been deleted and the canonical type from the type table is returned.
Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface for constructing AST nodes related to UPC (Unified Parallel C) language extensions.
The returned pointer should not be manually deleted by the caller, as the type table manages the lifetime of canonical type nodes.

Builds and returns a new SgVariableDeclaration AST node for a variable with the given name, type, optional initializer, and scope.

This function constructs a new SgVariableDeclaration node in the ROSE abstract syntax tree (AST), representing a variable declaration with the specified name, type, optional initializer expression, and enclosing scope. If no scope is provided, the function retrieves the current top of the scope stack via SageBuilder::topScopeStack().

The function handles several special cases and performs a number of fixup operations:

Fortran parameter handling: When building a variable declaration in a Fortran context, the function checks whether the declared name corresponds to an existing function parameter symbol in the enclosing procedure definition. If such a symbol is found, the default SgInitializedName created for the new declaration is replaced with the one from the function parameter list. The parent pointer of the parameter's SgInitializedName is updated from the SgFunctionParameterList to the new SgVariableDeclaration, and the associated SgVariableDefinition is relinked accordingly. The old default SgInitializedName is deleted to maintain AST consistency. In this case, no new symbol is added to the scope because the parameter symbol already exists under the function definition.

For non-Fortran parameters, fixVariableDeclaration() is called to properly register the declaration and its symbol in the given scope.

Source position information is set on the declaration and all its children using setSourcePositionAtRootAndAllChildren(), and the SgVariableDefinition child node receives explicit source position marking via setOneSourcePositionForTransformation() to ensure correct behavior during deep copy operations (addressing a known bug related to SgVariableDefinition file info).

After construction, unsetNodesMarkedAsModified() is called on the resulting declaration to reset any modification flags introduced during the building process.

The declaration modifier's access modifier is set to default (equivalent to public) by default; this is ignored by the unparser for most languages supported by ROSE.

nameThe name of the variable to declare. Must not be a null SgName.
typeThe type of the variable. Must not be NULL.
varInitAn optional initializer for the variable. May be NULL if no initialization is needed.
scopeThe enclosing scope statement in which the variable is declared. If NULL, the top of the current scope stack is used.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgVariableDeclaration node, with source position information set and modification flags cleared.
Precondition
name.is_null() must return false; the variable name must be valid and non-null.
type must not be NULL.
If scope is NULL, the SageBuilder scope stack must be non-empty so that topScopeStack() returns a valid scope.
If operating in a Fortran context and the name matches a function parameter, the enclosing SgFunctionDefinition must have a valid symbol table entry for that parameter.
Postcondition
The returned SgVariableDeclaration has its firstNondefiningDeclaration set to itself.
Source position information is set on the declaration and all its child nodes.
If the scope is non-NULL and the declaration is not a Fortran parameter replacement, the variable symbol is registered in the given scope.
The SgVariableDefinition associated with the declaration has valid start and end of construct source position pointers.
Nodes marked as modified during construction are unset before the declaration is returned.

The declaration modifier defaults to public access, which may not be appropriate for all languages or contexts; callers may need to adjust the access modifier after construction.

The Fortran parameter handling addresses the requirement that Fortran subroutine and function parameters have corresponding variable declarations in the function body, and their symbols must reside under SgFunctionDefinition rather than the function body block.
Bug 119 is addressed by explicitly setting source position on SgVariableDefinition, since AstQuery-based traversal used by setSourcePositionForTransformation() does not reach all child nodes.

◆ buildVariableDeclaration_nfi()

SgVariableDeclaration * SageBuilder::buildVariableDeclaration_nfi ( const SgName & name,
SgType * type,
SgInitializer * varInit,
SgScopeStatement * scope,
bool builtFromUseOnly,
SgStorageModifier::storage_modifier_enum sm )

Builds a new SgVariableDeclaration AST node, reusing existing symbols and initialized names when appropriate.

This function constructs an SgVariableDeclaration node for a variable with the given name, type, optional initializer, and scope. It is the non-frontend-interface (nfi) variant, meaning it is intended for use during AST construction or transformation rather than during direct frontend parsing.

The function performs the following steps:

  1. If no scope is provided, the top of the SageBuilder scope stack is used.
  2. The current scope is queried for an existing variable symbol matching the given name.
  3. If no symbol exists, a fresh SgVariableDeclaration is created with the given name, type, and optional initializer. If the builtFromUseOnly flag is set, the declaration is marked accordingly to indicate it was constructed from a use-site reference rather than a definition.
  4. If a symbol already exists, the function determines whether the associated variable declaration was previously built from a use-only context (i.e., its builtFromUseOnly flag is true). In that case, the existing SgVariableDeclaration is reused, its builtFromUseOnly flag is cleared, and its parent is reset to NULL in preparation for reinsertion into the AST.
  5. If the existing declaration cannot be reused (e.g., it was not built from use-only), a new SgInitializedName is constructed or borrowed, depending on whether the parent of the existing initialized name is a scope statement. The new or borrowed SgInitializedName is linked to the original via set_prev_decl_item(), and a new SgVariableDeclaration is built around it.
  6. Source position information is set on the SgInitializedName and the SgVariableDeclaration.
  7. The firstNondefiningDeclaration pointer is set to the newly created declaration itself.
  8. The storage modifier is applied using the provided sm parameter.
  9. For named variables, fixVariableDeclaration() is called to register the symbol in the scope. For anonymous variables (e.g., anonymous bit fields), the parent is set directly to the top of the scope stack.
  10. Source positions on the SgVariableDefinition and SgVariableDeclaration are set to null (transformation-style positions).
  11. The isModified flags on the newly constructed subtree are cleared via unsetNodesMarkedAsModified().
Parameters
nameThe name of the variable to declare. May be an empty string for anonymous declarations such as anonymous bit fields.
typePointer to the SgType representing the type of the variable. Must not be NULL.
varInitOptional pointer to an SgInitializer to associate with the variable. May be NULL if no initializer is needed.
scopePointer to the SgScopeStatement in which the variable is declared. If NULL, the top of the SageBuilder scope stack is used.
builtFromUseOnlyBoolean flag indicating whether this declaration is being built from a use-site reference rather than an explicit definition. When true, the resulting SgVariableDeclaration is marked with set_builtFromUseOnly(true).
smThe storage modifier enum value to apply to the declaration's storage modifier.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed or reused SgVariableDeclaration node. The returned node will have its firstNondefiningDeclaration set to itself and its parent set appropriately. The node will never be NULL.
Warning
If a variable symbol already exists in scope, the behavior depends on whether the associated declaration was built from use-only. Incorrect reuse of SgInitializedName nodes across multiple declarations may lead to subtle AST inconsistencies. Callers should ensure that the scope and symbol state are consistent before invoking this function.
For anonymous bit fields (empty name string), the parent of the declaration is set directly to the top of the scope stack. If the scope stack is empty or not being used, this may result in an assertion failure or an incorrect parent pointer.
Precondition
type must not be NULL.
If scope is NULL, the SageBuilder scope stack must be non-empty so that topScopeStack() returns a valid SgScopeStatement pointer.
The SgVariableDeclaration being built must not already have a parent node set (i.e., get_parent() == NULL) prior to insertion into the AST.
Postcondition
The returned SgVariableDeclaration has its firstNondefiningDeclaration pointer set to itself.
The storage modifier of the returned declaration is set to the value specified by sm.
Source position information on the SgVariableDefinition and SgVariableDeclaration nodes is initialized to null (transformation-style).
The isModified flags on all nodes in the returned subtree are cleared.
For named variables, the variable symbol is registered in the given scope via fixVariableDeclaration().
Note
This function is the non-frontend-interface (nfi) variant of buildVariableDeclaration and is intended for use in AST construction and transformation contexts rather than during frontend parsing.
The define DEBUG_BUILD_VARIABLE_DECLARATION controls verbose diagnostic output within this function. It is set to 0 by default and can be enabled locally for debugging.
When a variable symbol already exists and the associated declaration was not built from use-only, a new SgInitializedName is created (or borrowed from the parent scope statement) and linked to the original via set_prev_decl_item() to maintain the declaration chain.
For variables declared inside conditional expressions (e.g., inside SgIfStmt), the parent of the SgInitializedName may be a scope statement rather than an SgVariableDeclaration. This case is handled by reusing the existing SgInitializedName directly.

Builds an SgVariableDefinition IR node without file information inference (nfi).

This function constructs a new SgVariableDefinition node and connects it into the Abstract Syntax Tree (AST). It is refactored from the ROSETTA grammar statement code originally found in SgVariableDeclaration::append_variable(). The function handles two cases depending on whether the parent variable declaration node has associated file information:

If the declaration node has valid file information (via get_file_info()), a deep copy of that file information is made and assigned to the newly created SgVariableDefinition node. Additionally, if the declaration has an end-of-construct position, a copy of that is also created and attached to the definition node.

If the declaration node does not have file information, the SgVariableDefinition is constructed using a simpler constructor that does not require file position data.

If the type associated with init_name is a function type (i.e., isSgFunctionType returns non-null), the function returns NULL without creating any node, since variable definitions for function types are not applicable in this context.

initPointer to an SgInitializer node representing the optional initializer expression for the variable. May be NULL if the variable is declared without an initializer.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgVariableDefinition node if the variable type is not a function type and construction succeeds. Returns NULL if the type of init_name is an SgFunctionType.
Warning
The caller is responsible for ensuring that the returned SgVariableDefinition node is properly integrated into the surrounding AST structure. Failing to do so may result in an inconsistent or malformed AST.
Internal assertions (ROSE_ASSERT) will abort execution if decl or init_name are NULL, or if memory allocation for the new nodes fails.

decl must not be NULL.
init_name must not be NULL.
init may be NULL; a NULL value indicates no initializer is associated with the variable definition.
Postcondition
If the type of init_name is not a function type, a valid SgVariableDefinition node is returned with its file information and optional end-of-construct position properly set and parented.
If the type of init_name is a function type, NULL is returned and no new IR nodes are created.
Note
This function is intended for internal use within the SageBuilder interface. The "nfi" suffix in the function name stands for "no file information inference", indicating that file position data is copied directly from the provided declaration node rather than being inferred or synthesized automatically.
The newly created SgVariableDefinition node connects init_name and init into the AST as part of its construction, establishing parent-child relationships within the IR.

SgVarRefExp * SageBuilder::buildVarRefExp ( const SgName & name,

Builds a variable reference expression (SgVarRefExp) for a variable with the given name in the specified scope.

This function constructs an SgVarRefExp AST node representing a reference to a variable identified by the provided name. It first resolves the target scope: if the caller passes NULL for the scope parameter, the function falls back to the top of the current scope stack maintained by SageBuilder.

Once the scope is determined, the function attempts to locate a matching variable symbol by calling lookupVariableSymbolInParentScopes(), which traverses the scope hierarchy upward from the given scope. This approach correctly handles nested scopes and parent-scope visibility.

If a matching symbol is found, it is cast to SgVariableSymbol and used directly to construct the SgVarRefExp node. If no matching symbol is found, the function creates a placeholder SgInitializedName with an unknown type and a corresponding SgVariableSymbol. This placeholder mechanism is intended to support a deferred post-processing phase that can later resolve the symbol to its correct declaration and type. The placeholder initialized name is assigned the provided scope as both its scope and parent.

After constructing the SgVarRefExp, the function sets a single source position for transformation tracking purposes and verifies that the resulting node and its associated variable symbol's declaration are non-NULL via assertions.

Parameters
nameThe name of the variable for which a reference expression is to be built. This is used to look up the corresponding variable symbol in the scope hierarchy.
scopeThe scope in which to search for the variable symbol. If NULL, the function uses the top of the SageBuilder scope stack. The scope is expected to be a valid SgScopeStatement or NULL. Note that for C++, qualified names may indicate different scopes, so the provided scope should be the correct one when known.
Returns
A pointer to a newly constructed SgVarRefExp node referencing the resolved or placeholder variable symbol. The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-NULL.
Warning
If no variable symbol is found in the scope hierarchy, a placeholder symbol with an unknown type is created. This placeholder must be resolved during a subsequent post-processing phase; using the resulting AST node before that resolution may produce incorrect or incomplete results.
For C++ code, qualified names may indicate variables in different scopes. Callers should ensure the correct scope is provided to avoid unintended symbol resolution.
Precondition
The name parameter must represent a valid, non-empty variable name string.
If scope is non-NULL, it must point to a valid SgScopeStatement node within the AST.
If scope is NULL, the SageBuilder scope stack must be non-empty so that a valid fallback scope can be obtained.
Postcondition
The returned SgVarRefExp is non-NULL and has a valid SgVariableSymbol attached.
The SgVariableSymbol associated with the returned SgVarRefExp has a non-NULL declaration (SgInitializedName).
A source position for transformation is set on the returned SgVarRefExp node.
Note
This function uses lookupVariableSymbolInParentScopes() rather than lookupSymbolInParentScopes() to correctly handle template parameters and template arguments during symbol resolution.
When a placeholder symbol is created due to a failed lookup, the SgInitializedName is assigned SgTypeUnknown as its type. The buildInitializedName() helper does not set the scope automatically, so this function explicitly sets both the scope and parent of the placeholder initialized name.

This is useful when constructing synthetic AST nodes that do not correspond to any specific location in a source file, such as nodes introduced during code transformation or generation.

The function allocates a new SgVoidVal object on the heap, asserts that the allocation succeeded, sets its source position to null, and returns the resulting pointer.

Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgVoidVal node with null source position information. The caller is responsible for managing the lifetime of the returned object within the context of the ROSE AST.
Warning
The returned pointer is heap-allocated. Improper management of this pointer outside of the ROSE AST infrastructure may result in memory leaks or dangling references.
Precondition
Sufficient heap memory must be available to allocate a new SgVoidVal object.
Postcondition
The returned SgVoidVal node has null source position information as set by setOneSourcePositionNull.
The returned pointer is non-null; an assertion failure will terminate the program if allocation fails.
Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface for constructing ROSE AST nodes without file information. For nodes that require source position data, consider using the corresponding builder function that accepts file information parameters.

Builds a volatile-qualified modifier type wrapping a given base type.

This function constructs a new SgModifierType node that applies the volatile qualifier to the provided base type. Internally, it allocates a new SgModifierType object, sets its volatile modifier flag via the constVolatile modifier interface, and then attempts to insert the resulting type into the global type table using SgModifierType::insertModifierTypeIntoTypeTable().

If an equivalent volatile-qualified modifier type already exists in the type table, the newly allocated SgModifierType is deleted and the pre-existing canonical type from the table is returned instead. This ensures that structurally identical types are represented by a single shared node within the AST, preserving type uniqueness.

Warning
Passing a NULL pointer for base_type will trigger an assertion failure and abort the program. Always ensure the base type is a valid, non-NULL SgType pointer before calling this function.
Precondition
base_type must not be NULL.
base_type must point to a valid, fully constructed SgType node within the ROSE IR.
Postcondition
The returned SgModifierType has its volatile modifier flag set.
The returned SgModifierType is registered in the global type table, ensuring type uniqueness across the AST.
If a duplicate type was detected during insertion, the intermediate SgModifierType object is deleted and the canonical instance from the type table is returned.
Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder interface, which provides factory functions for constructing ROSE AST nodes.
The type table insertion mechanism guarantees that only one canonical SgModifierType node exists for any given combination of base type and modifier flags, preventing redundant type nodes in the AST.

◆ buildWhileStmt()

SgWhileStmt * SageBuilder::buildWhileStmt ( SgStatement * condition,
SgStatement * body,
SgStatement * else_body )

Builds a while statement (while loop) AST node from a condition, body, and optional else body statement.

This function constructs a new SgWhileStmt node representing a while loop in the ROSE abstract syntax tree (AST). It accepts a condition statement, a body statement, and an optional else body statement (used to support Python-style while-else constructs).

Two overloads are provided: the primary overload accepts an SgStatement as the condition, while the inline overload accepts an SgExpression and internally wraps it in an expression statement via buildExprStatement before delegating to the primary overload.

The function performs the following steps:

  • Asserts that both the condition and body are non-null.
  • Allocates a new SgWhileStmt node with the provided condition and body.
  • If the current language uses case-insensitive symbol table semantics (as determined by SageInterface::is_language_case_insensitive()), sets the case-insensitive flag on the resulting node.
  • Calls setOneSourcePositionForTransformation to assign a source position appropriate for compiler-generated (transformation) nodes.
  • Sets the parent pointer of the condition and body to the newly created SgWhileStmt.
  • If an else body is provided (non-null), attaches it to the SgWhileStmt and sets its parent pointer accordingly. This else body is a Python-specific feature that allows a block of code to execute when the while loop condition becomes false without a break statement having been encountered.

The resulting while statement node encapsulates the loop condition, the loop body, and an optional else body (used in languages such as Python that support while-else constructs). When building from an expression, the expression is automatically promoted to a statement to satisfy the AST node requirements.

Parameters
conditionThe condition of the while loop. In the primary overload, this is an SgStatement representing the loop condition. In the inline overload, this is an SgExpression that will be wrapped into an SgExprStatement automatically. Must not be null.
bodyThe body of the while loop, represented as an SgStatement. This statement is executed repeatedly as long as the condition evaluates to true. Must not be null.
else_bodyAn optional else body statement, defaulting to NULL. When provided, this statement is executed after the while loop exits normally (i.e., without a break). This parameter is primarily relevant for languages that support while-else semantics (e.g., Python). Pass NULL if no else body is needed.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgWhileStmt AST node representing the while loop. The returned pointer is guaranteed to be non-null.
Precondition
condition must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgStatement node.
body must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgStatement node.
If else_body is non-null, it must be a valid pointer to an SgStatement node.
The ROSE AST infrastructure must be properly initialized before calling this function.
Postcondition
A new SgWhileStmt node is created and returned.
The parent pointer of condition is set to the returned SgWhileStmt.
The parent pointer of body is set to the returned SgWhileStmt.
If else_body is non-null, it is attached to the returned SgWhileStmt and its parent pointer is set accordingly.
The returned SgWhileStmt has a source position assigned suitable for transformation-generated nodes.
Parent pointers of the condition, body, and else_body (if non-null) are updated to point to the newly created SgWhileStmt node.
Warning
The condition and body parameters must not be null; the function will trigger an assertion failure (via ROSE_ASSERT) if either is null.
The else_body parameter is a Python-specific feature. Providing a non-null else_body in a non-Python context may produce unexpected behavior or an invalid AST for other languages.
Passing a null pointer for condition or body may result in undefined behavior or an improperly formed AST node.
The else_body parameter is only meaningful in language contexts that support while-else constructs. Providing a non-null else_body when generating C or C++ code may produce invalid or unexpected output.
Note
The else body support was added to handle a Python-specific language feature where a while loop may have an associated else clause.
Case-insensitive symbol table semantics are applied to the resulting node when the current language requires it, as determined by SageInterface::is_language_case_insensitive().
The inline overload is a convenience wrapper that accepts an SgExpression for the condition and converts it to an SgExprStatement using buildExprStatement before calling the primary overload.
Ownership of the passed AST nodes is transferred to the newly created SgWhileStmt node; callers should not attempt to free these nodes independently after passing them to this function.

◆ clearScopeStack()

void SageBuilder::clearScopeStack ( )

Clears all entries from the scope stack used during AST construction.

This function removes all elements from the internal scope stack maintained by the SageBuilder module. The scope stack is a global data structure used during the construction of the Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) to track the current nesting of scopes, such as namespaces, classes, and function bodies. Calling this function resets the stack to an empty state, effectively discarding any scope context that has been accumulated.

This is typically called at the end of a build session or when reinitializing the builder state to ensure no stale scope information persists between independent AST construction operations.

Warning
Calling this function while an AST construction is in progress may result in undefined behavior or malformed AST nodes, as scope context required for correct node placement will be lost.
This function operates on a global shared data structure. In multi-threaded environments, external synchronization must be provided to avoid race conditions.
Precondition
The SageBuilder module must have been initialized prior to calling this function.
Postcondition
The internal scope stack is empty and contains no scope entries.
Note
After calling this function, any subsequent calls to scope-dependent SageBuilder functions will require the scope stack to be repopulated before use, typically via pushScopeStack().

Converts a SourcePositionClassification enum value to its corresponding string representation.

This function is intended primarily as a debugging utility to obtain a human-readable string name for a given SourcePositionClassification enumeration value. It uses a switch statement to map each known enumerator to its exact symbolic name as a string. If an unrecognized value is passed, the function prints an error message to standard output and aborts execution via ROSE_ABORT().

The supported enumeration values and their string mappings are:

e_sourcePositionError maps to "e_sourcePositionError" e_sourcePositionDefault maps to "e_sourcePositionDefault" e_sourcePositionTransformation maps to "e_sourcePositionTransformation" e_sourcePositionCompilerGenerated maps to "e_sourcePositionCompilerGenerated" e_sourcePositionNullPointers maps to "e_sourcePositionNullPointers" e_sourcePositionFrontendConstruction maps to "e_sourcePositionFrontendConstruction" e_sourcePosition_last maps to "e_sourcePosition_last"

Returns
A string containing the symbolic name of the given SourcePositionClassification enumerator value.
Warning
If the value of scp does not match any of the known enumerators, the function will print an error message and call ROSE_ABORT(), terminating the program. Do not pass uninitialized or out-of-range enum values to this function.
Precondition
The parameter scp must hold a valid, recognized value from the SourcePositionClassification enumeration. Passing an invalid or unrecognized value will result in program termination.
Postcondition
The returned string is a non-empty string exactly matching the symbolic name of the enumerator corresponding to scp, provided scp is a valid enumerator.

Checks whether the scope stack maintained by SageBuilder is empty.

This function queries the internal scope stack used by the SageBuilder module to manage the current nesting of scopes during AST construction. The scope stack is a global data structure that tracks the active scope context as new AST nodes are built. This function provides a simple way to determine whether any scopes are currently on the stack, which is useful for validation, debugging, or ensuring that all opened scopes have been properly closed after a series of AST construction operations.

Returns
