◆ errorCheckingTargetAST()

void SageBuilder::errorCheckingTargetAST ( SgNode * node_copy,
SgNode * node_original,
SgFile * targetFile,
bool failOnWarning )

Performs error and consistency checking on a copied AST node relative to a target file and its original counterpart.

This function validates that a copied AST node and its associated structural elements (such as scopes, first non-defining declarations, and defining declarations) belong to the expected target file. It is intended to be used during AST transformation and snippet insertion operations to detect inconsistencies that may arise when merging or copying AST fragments from one file context into another.

The function proceeds through several distinct checking phases:

  1. Statement scope checking: If the copied node is an SgStatement with an explicit scope, the function retrieves the enclosing file of that scope and compares it against the provided target file. If the scope's enclosing file does not match the target file, a warning is printed. If failOnWarning is true, the program aborts.
  2. Declaration statement checking: If the copied node is an SgDeclarationStatement, the function checks both the first non-defining declaration and the defining declaration (if present). For each, it retrieves the enclosing file of the copied declaration and compares it to the target file. Mismatches are reported as warnings or notes. If getEnclosingFileNode() returns NULL (which can occur for declarations in external libraries such as Java's java.lang), a note is printed. If failOnWarning is true, the program aborts on any such condition.
  3. Expression type checking: If the copied node is an SgExpression with an explicit type, the function retrieves and asserts the non-NULL existence of that type. No file comparison is performed for expressions in this implementation.

The function uses the copied node (node_copy) rather than the original node (node_original) for file enclosure queries, as this reflects the corrected behavior after earlier bugfixes. The original node is used only for assertions and pointer comparisons where needed.

Internally, the function uses isSgStatement(), isSgDeclarationStatement(), and isSgExpression() to dynamically dispatch on the node type, and uses getEnclosingFileNode() to determine which source file a given node belongs to.

Parameters
node_copyPointer to the copied AST node being validated. Must not be NULL.
node_originalPointer to the original AST node from which the copy was made. Used for assertions and reference comparisons. Must not be NULL.
targetFilePointer to the SgFile representing the target file into which the AST node is being inserted or merged. Used as the reference file for all comparisons.
failOnWarningIf true, the function will call ROSE_ABORT() upon detecting any warning condition, causing the program to terminate. If false, warnings are printed but execution continues.
Warning
If failOnWarning is set to true and any scope, first non-defining declaration, or defining declaration is found to reside outside the target file, the program will abort immediately via ROSE_ABORT(). Use this flag with caution in production transformations.
This function uses ROSE_ASSERT() to enforce several internal invariants. Passing NULL pointers for node_copy or node_original, or nodes with NULL scopes when explicit scopes are expected, will trigger assertion failures.
Precondition
node_copy must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an SgNode in a well-formed ROSE AST.
node_original must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an SgNode corresponding to the original source of node_copy.
targetFile must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an SgFile representing the intended target of the transformation.
If node_copy is an SgStatement with an explicit scope, that scope must be non-NULL.
If node_copy is an SgDeclarationStatement, its get_firstNondefiningDeclaration() must return a valid pointer (NULL is handled with a warning but is not expected in most contexts).
Postcondition
No structural modifications are made to node_copy, node_original, or targetFile by this function.
If failOnWarning is false, the function always returns normally regardless of detected issues.
If failOnWarning is true and a warning condition is detected, the program will have been terminated via ROSE_ABORT() before this function returns.
Note
This function is intended for use during AST snippet insertion and transformation workflows within the SageBuilder infrastructure. It is a diagnostic utility and does not perform any AST repair or modification.
Mismatches in the first non-defining declaration's enclosing file are considered allowable in merged AST scenarios and are reported as notes rather than errors, unless failOnWarning is true.
A NULL return from getEnclosingFileNode() may occur legitimately for declarations originating from external language runtime libraries (e.g., Java's java.lang package) and is handled gracefully with a printed note.

◆ findAssociatedDeclarationInTargetAST()

SgDeclarationStatement * SageBuilder::findAssociatedDeclarationInTargetAST ( SgDeclarationStatement * snippet_declaration,
SgScopeStatement * targetScope )

Finds the corresponding declaration in a target AST that matches a given snippet declaration.

This function locates the declaration in a target Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) that corresponds to a given declaration from a snippet AST. It is designed to support code segregation transformations where declarations from one AST must be matched to their counterparts in another AST that shares no common global scope.

The algorithm works in two phases. In the first phase, the function walks upward from the snippet declaration through its enclosing scopes, recording each named scope encountered along the way until the global scope is reached. All intermediate scopes are required to be named scopes (e.g., class definitions or namespace definitions), since unnamed scopes cannot be matched by name in the target AST.

In the second phase, the function traverses the recorded scope list in reverse order (from global scope downward) and, at each level, looks up the corresponding named scope in the target AST using symbol table lookups. Supported scope types include SgClassDefinition and SgNamespaceDefinitionStatement. SgFunctionDefinition scopes are explicitly rejected with an assertion failure, as they are not expected to appear as enclosing scopes for type declarations.

Once the matching target scope is identified, the function performs a symbol lookup for the snippet declaration itself within that target scope. The following declaration kinds are supported via a switch on the declaration variant:

  • SgClassDeclaration
  • SgTypedefDeclaration
  • SgEnumDeclaration (named enums only; unnamed enums produce a warning and return NULL)
  • SgFunctionDeclaration
  • SgMemberFunctionDeclaration
  • SgTemplateFunctionDeclaration
  • SgTemplateMemberFunctionDeclaration

For function declarations, if the snippet declaration is a defining declaration, the function returns the defining declaration from the target AST rather than the first non-defining declaration.

This function is similar in purpose to findAssociatedSymbolInTargetAST() but was introduced separately to support the requirements of the codeSegregation tool without modifying the behavior of the existing snippet transformation support.

Conditional compilation via the preprocessor macro DEBUG_FIND_ASSOCIATED_DECLARATION controls the emission of diagnostic printf statements throughout the function body. This macro is set to 0 by define and is intended for developer use only.

Parameters
snippet_declarationA pointer to the declaration node in the snippet AST for which a corresponding declaration is to be found in the target AST. Must not be NULL. Must be a named declaration of a supported kind (class, typedef, enum, function, member function, or template function/member function).
targetScopeA pointer to a scope statement node in the target AST. Used to determine the global scope of the target AST and must belong to a different global scope than snippet_declaration. Must not be NULL.
Returns
A pointer to the SgDeclarationStatement in the target AST that corresponds to the given snippet declaration. The returned declaration is guaranteed to belong to a different global scope than snippet_declaration. Returns NULL only in the case of an unnamed enum declaration (with a warning printed to stdout).
Precondition
snippet_declaration must not be NULL.
targetScope must not be NULL.
snippet_declaration and targetScope must belong to different global scopes, as verified by SageInterface::hasSameGlobalScope() returning false.
All scopes between snippet_declaration and the global scope must be named scopes (i.e., isNamedScope() returns true for each).
The target AST must contain declarations with matching names for each scope and for the final declaration itself; otherwise, internal assertions will fail.
The snippet declaration must be of a supported variant type. Unsupported types will trigger ROSE_ABORT().
SgFunctionDefinition must not appear as an intermediate enclosing scope of snippet_declaration; if encountered, ROSE_ABORT() is called.
Postcondition
The returned declaration pointer is non-NULL (except for unnamed enum declarations).
The returned declaration belongs to a different global scope than snippet_declaration.
The name of the returned declaration matches the name of snippet_declaration.
For defining function declarations, the returned declaration is the defining declaration in the target AST.
Warning
Unnamed enum declarations are not fully supported. If snippet_declaration is an SgEnumDeclaration with get_isUnNamed() returning true, a warning is printed and the function proceeds with returnSymbol set to NULL, which will cause the subsequent ROSE_ASSERT(returnDeclaration != NULL) to fail. Do not pass unnamed enum declarations to this function.
If the target AST does not contain a matching symbol for any scope or for the final declaration, internal ROSE_ASSERT() calls will abort the program.
This function calls ROSE_ABORT() if the snippet declaration's variant is not one of the explicitly handled cases in the switch statement.
Note
This function was introduced alongside findAssociatedSymbolInTargetAST() to support the codeSegregation tool. The two functions serve similar purposes but have been kept separate to avoid compromising snippet transformation support.
The DEBUG_FIND_ASSOCIATED_DECLARATION preprocessor macro, when set to a non-zero value, enables verbose diagnostic output via printf statements. It is hardcoded to 0 via define and must be changed at compile time to enable debug output.

◆ findAssociatedSymbolInTargetAST()

SgSymbol * SageBuilder::findAssociatedSymbolInTargetAST ( SgDeclarationStatement * snippet_declaration,
SgScopeStatement * targetScope )

Finds the symbol in a target AST that corresponds to a given declaration from a snippet AST.

This function bridges two separate abstract syntax trees (ASTs): a snippet AST and a target AST. Given a declaration node from the snippet AST and a scope within the target AST, the function locates and returns the symbol in the target AST that corresponds to the same named entity as the snippet declaration.

The algorithm proceeds in two phases:

Phase 1 - Scope chain collection: Starting from the scope that directly contains the snippet declaration, the function walks upward through enclosing named scopes, recording each scope into an ordered list until the global scope is reached. All intermediate scopes must be named scopes (e.g., class definitions or namespace definitions); unnamed or anonymous scopes will trigger an assertion failure.

Phase 2 - Reverse traversal into the target AST: The collected scope list is then traversed in reverse order (from the global scope downward). At each level, the function looks up the corresponding named scope (class or namespace) in the target AST using symbol table queries. This progressively narrows the target scope until the innermost enclosing scope is identified.

Finally, the function resolves the symbol for the snippet declaration itself within the identified target scope. It handles the following declaration kinds via a switch statement:

  • SgClassDeclaration: looks up a class symbol by name.
  • SgTypedefDeclaration: looks up a typedef symbol by name.
  • SgEnumDeclaration: looks up an enum symbol by name (unnamed enums are not supported and will result in a warning and a NULL return value).
  • SgFunctionDeclaration and SgMemberFunctionDeclaration: looks up a function symbol by name.
  • Any other declaration kind causes an assertion abort.

Diagnostic printf statements are conditionally compiled into the function body using if / endif preprocessor guards and may produce output during execution depending on how the source was compiled.

Parameters
snippet_declarationA pointer to the declaration node in the snippet AST whose corresponding symbol is to be found in the target AST. Must not be NULL. Must be one of the supported declaration types: SgClassDeclaration, SgTypedefDeclaration, SgEnumDeclaration, SgFunctionDeclaration, or SgMemberFunctionDeclaration.
targetScopeA pointer to a scope statement within the target AST. Used to determine the global scope of the target AST as the starting point for the reverse traversal. Must not be NULL and must belong to a valid target AST that contains a reachable global scope.
Returns
A pointer to the SgSymbol in the target AST that corresponds to the given snippet declaration. Returns NULL if the snippet declaration is an unnamed enum, as unnamed enums are explicitly unsupported. Returns a valid non-NULL SgSymbol pointer for all other supported declaration types when the corresponding symbol is found.
Warning
Unnamed enum declarations (where SgEnumDeclaration::get_isUnNamed() returns true) are not handled. The function will print a warning message and return NULL in this case.
If an unsupported declaration type is passed as snippet_declaration, the function will call ROSE_ABORT() and terminate the program.
If a SgFunctionDefinition is encountered as an intermediate scope in the scope chain of the snippet declaration, the function treats this as an error and calls ROSE_ABORT().
All intermediate scopes between the snippet declaration and the global scope must be named scopes. Encountering an unnamed scope will trigger a ROSE_ASSERT failure.
All symbol lookups in the target AST are expected to succeed. A failed lookup (returning NULL) will trigger a ROSE_ASSERT failure and abort execution.
Precondition
snippet_declaration must not be NULL and must point to a valid SgDeclarationStatement node within a snippet AST.
targetScope must not be NULL and must be a valid scope node within a target AST that has a reachable global scope accessible via TransformationSupport::getGlobalScope().
All scopes enclosing snippet_declaration up to the global scope must be named scopes (i.e., isNamedScope() returns true for each).
The target AST must contain symbols corresponding to every named scope and to the final declaration present in the snippet AST's scope chain; otherwise assertion failures will occur.
Postcondition
The returned symbol, if non-NULL, belongs to the target AST and has the same name as the corresponding entity in the snippet AST.
The name of the declaration associated with the returned symbol matches the name of snippet_declaration, as verified by internal assertions.
Note
This function is intended to support AST snippet insertion workflows where declarations from an externally constructed snippet AST must be reconciled with an existing target AST.
The function uses TransformationSupport::getGlobalScope() to obtain the global scope of the target AST from the provided targetScope argument.
For enum declarations, the function uses lookupEnumSymbolInParentScopes() rather than a direct scope lookup, to account for enum visibility rules across parent scopes.
Support for SgMemberFunctionDeclaration and SgFunctionDeclaration was added to support the codeSegregation tool.

◆ fixupCopyOfAstFromSeparateFileInNewTargetAst()

void SageBuilder::fixupCopyOfAstFromSeparateFileInNewTargetAst ( SgStatement * insertionPoint,
bool insertionPointIsScope,
SgStatement * toInsert,
SgStatement * original_before_copy )

Fixes up a copied AST subtree from a separate source file after it has been inserted into a new target AST.

When a snippet AST from a separate file is copied and inserted into a target AST, certain structural and symbolic connections become inconsistent. This function traverses both the copy of the snippet and the original snippet in parallel, node by node, and delegates per-node fixup work to fixupCopyOfNodeFromSeparateFileInNewTargetAst() for each corresponding pair of IR nodes.

The function first verifies that the insertion point belongs to the target file and that the copy of the snippet has already been inserted (i.e., its parent traversal leads back to the target file's SgFile node). It also verifies that the original snippet still belongs to a different file than the target.

Structural equivalence between the copy and the original is checked using isStructurallyEquivalentAST(). If the two are not structurally equivalent, a warning is printed and the function returns early without performing any fixup. This situation can arise if transformations were applied to the copy before it was inserted into the target AST, which is not supported.

The parallel traversal uses RoseAst iterators over both the copy and the original. For each pair of corresponding IR nodes, the variant types are compared. If a mismatch is found, an error is reported and the function aborts.

This function temporarily enables forced searching of base classes in symbol tables (via SgSymbolTable::set_force_search_of_base_classes(true)) for the duration of the fixup, and restores the setting to false before returning. This is done to support symbol resolution in languages such as Java where base class symbols may need to be consulted.

Note: The body of this function is conditionally compiled. The parallel traversal and per-node fixup logic are guarded by ifndef USE_CMAKEx, because the required libraries may not be configured when building with CMake.

Parameters
insertionPointThe statement in the target AST at or near which the snippet copy has been inserted. Must not be NULL. Used to determine the enclosing target SgFile node.
insertionPointIsScopeA boolean flag indicating whether the insertion point itself acts as a scope for the inserted statement.
toInsertThe root of the copied snippet AST that has already been inserted into the target AST. Must not be NULL. Its parent traversal must lead to the same SgFile as the insertion point.
original_before_copyThe root of the original snippet AST before copying. Must not be NULL. Its enclosing SgFile must differ from the target file, confirming it still belongs to the snippet's source file.
Precondition
insertionPoint must not be NULL.
toInsert must not be NULL.
original_before_copy must not be NULL.
toInsert must have already been inserted into the target AST such that traversing its parent chain reaches the same SgFile as insertionPoint.
original_before_copy must reside in a different SgFile than the target AST's SgFile.
The copy represented by toInsert must be structurally equivalent to original_before_copy; no transformations should have been applied to the copy prior to insertion.
Postcondition
All IR nodes in the copied snippet AST have been processed for fixup with respect to symbol references and other connections to the target AST.
SgSymbolTable base class search is restored to false.
If structural equivalence fails, no fixup is performed and the function returns early.
Warning
Do not apply transformations to the copy of the snippet before inserting it into the target AST. Doing so may cause structural inequivalence with the original, which will cause this function to skip the fixup and print a warning.
If the variant types of corresponding nodes in the copy and the original do not match during traversal, the function calls ROSE_ABORT() and terminates.
The parallel traversal and fixup logic are conditionally compiled and will be omitted when USE_CMAKEx is define'd, as the required libraries may not be available in that build configuration.
Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder infrastructure for inserting code snippets from separate files into a target AST, a common pattern in ROSE-based source-to-source transformations.
The forced base class symbol search is enabled only for the duration of this call to support Java language semantics and is explicitly disabled before the function returns.

◆ fixupCopyOfNodeFromSeparateFileInNewTargetAst()

void SageBuilder::fixupCopyOfNodeFromSeparateFileInNewTargetAst ( SgStatement * insertionPoint,
bool insertionPointIsScope,
SgNode * node_copy,
SgNode * node_original )

Fixes up a copied IR node from a separate snippet file so that it is internally consistent within the target AST at the specified insertion point.

This function is responsible for reconciling individual ROSE IR nodes that were copied from a snippet AST (originating from a separately compiled file) into a target AST. When code snippets are injected into a target program's AST, the copied nodes may still reference symbols, types, scopes, and declarations that belong to the snippet file rather than the target file. This function corrects those references so that the copied node is fully consistent with the target AST context.

The function operates on a per-node basis and is intended to be called for each node in the copied AST sub-tree. It dispatches on the variant type of node_copy using a switch statement, handling the following IR node kinds individually:

  • SgInitializedName: Updates the type to the target-file equivalent using getTargetFileType(), inserts the appropriate variable or enum field symbol into the target scope, and resets the scope pointer. Special handling is provided for function parameters, enum declarations, catch-option statements, and Java for-each statements.
  • SgVariableDeclaration: No explicit fixup is required at this level since types are stored in the contained SgInitializedName nodes.
  • SgFunctionDeclaration: Resolves the function symbol in the target scope, inserts a new SgFunctionSymbol if necessary, resets the scope of the declaration and its first non-defining declaration, and calls resetDeclaration() to finalize the fixup.
  • SgClassDeclaration: Resolves or inserts the class symbol in the target scope, resets the class type to the target-file equivalent, and calls resetDeclaration().
  • SgEnumDeclaration: Resolves or inserts the enum symbol in the target scope, resets the enum type to the target-file equivalent, and calls resetDeclaration().
  • SgTemplateClassDeclaration: Resets the class type to the target-file equivalent.
  • SgTypedefDeclaration: Resets both the base type and the typedef type to their target-file equivalents, resolves or inserts the typedef symbol, and calls resetDeclaration().
  • SgVarRefExp: Locates the corresponding variable symbol in the target AST (searching parent scopes, the snippet scope, and class definitions for member accesses) and resets the symbol reference in the expression.
  • SgFunctionRefExp: Locates the corresponding function symbol in the target AST and resets the symbol reference in the expression.
  • SgMemberFunctionRefExp: Locates the corresponding member function symbol in the target AST, with fallback searches through class definitions for dot and arrow expressions, and resets the symbol reference in the expression.
  • SgEnumVal: Resets the stored reference to the associated SgEnumDeclaration to the copy belonging to the target AST, using findAssociatedSymbolInTargetAST(). Unnamed enum declarations are not fully supported and produce a warning.
  • SgTryStmt, SgCatchStatementSeq, SgCatchOptionStmt: Recognized but minimally handled; placeholder cases for future implementation.
  • SgJavaPackageStatement: Currently triggers an abort, indicating it is not yet supported.

For all expressions that store an explicit type (hasExplicitType() returns true), the stored type is updated to the target-file equivalent before the switch dispatch.

After the switch dispatch, errorCheckingTargetAST() is called to report any remaining inconsistencies between the fixed-up node and the target AST.

The target file is determined by calling getEnclosingFileNode() on the insertionPoint. The target scope is derived from insertionPoint directly if insertionPointIsScope is true, or from insertionPoint's parent otherwise.

Parameters
insertionPointA pointer to the SgStatement in the target AST at or near which the snippet sub-tree has been inserted. Used to determine the target file and the target scope. Must not be NULL.
insertionPointIsScopeIf true, insertionPoint itself is treated as the target scope (i.e., it is an SgScopeStatement). If false, the parent of insertionPoint is used as the target scope.
node_copyA pointer to the copied IR node (produced by the AST copy mechanism) that requires fixup. This node is already inserted into the target AST sub-tree. Must not be NULL.
node_originalA pointer to the original IR node from the snippet AST. This node remains connected within the snippet file's AST and is used as a reference for resolving symbols and scopes. Must not be NULL.
Warning
This function calls ROSE_ABORT() if a required symbol or scope cannot be resolved, or if an unsupported IR node kind (such as SgJavaPackageStatement) is encountered. Callers must ensure that the target AST has been properly prepared with all required declarations before invoking this function.
Unnamed enum declarations in SgEnumVal nodes are not fully supported. A warning message is printed to stdout and the enum value's declaration reference is not updated in that case.
For SgFunctionRefExp, if the referenced function symbol cannot be found in any parent scope of the target AST, an error message is printed to stderr and the function aborts. The target AST must already contain a visible declaration of the referenced function.
Precondition
insertionPoint must be a valid, non-NULL SgStatement node that is part of the target AST.
node_copy must be a valid, non-NULL SgNode that has already been inserted into the target AST sub-tree via the AST copy mechanism.
node_original must be a valid, non-NULL SgNode that is still connected within the snippet file's AST.
The parent of insertionPoint (or insertionPoint itself, if insertionPointIsScope is true) must be a valid SgScopeStatement in the target AST.
getEnclosingFileNode(insertionPoint) must return a non-NULL SgFile pointer representing the target file.
For SgFunctionRefExp nodes, the referenced function must already have a visible declaration inserted into the target AST before this function is called.
For SgMemberFunctionRefExp nodes, the class containing the referenced member function must already be defined and accessible from the target scope.
Postcondition
node_copy has its scope, type, and symbol references updated to be consistent with the target AST context at insertionPoint.
Any required symbols (variable, function, class, enum, typedef, or enum field) that were not already present in the target scope are inserted into targetScope's symbol table.
errorCheckingTargetAST() has been called on node_copy to report any remaining inconsistencies.
Note
This function is part of the ROSE snippet injection infrastructure in the SageBuilder namespace. It is designed to be called once per node in the copied AST sub-tree, typically from a traversal that visits every node in the copied snippet.
The translationMap mentioned in internal comments is noted as being required only for name-qualified (C++ specific) references and is described as a performance optimization for scope traversal. It is not a parameter of this function.
Several branches of the switch statement contain dead code guarded by if 0 / endif preprocessor directives. These represent earlier implementation approaches that were superseded by the refactored getTargetFileType() and resetDeclaration() helper functions.
Java-specific IR nodes (SgJavaForEachStatement, SgJavaPackageStatement, SgMemberFunctionRefExp in Java calling conventions) receive partial or no support in the current implementation.

◆ fixupSharingSourcePosition()

void SageBuilder::fixupSharingSourcePosition ( SgNode * subtreeRoot,
int new_file_id )

Updates the source position file designations in an AST subtree to support shared IR node unparsing.

This function traverses a given AST subtree rooted at subtreeRoot and modifies the Sg_File_Info objects associated with each SgStatement node found during the traversal. Its primary purpose is to mark statement constructs as shared and to register the provided file identifier (new_file_id) so that the associated language constructs can be correctly unparsed when multiple files reference the same AST nodes.

The function uses an internal local class derived from AstSimpleProcessing to perform a preorder traversal of the subtree. During the traversal, for each SgStatement node whose startOfConstruct physical file ID matches new_file_id, the following actions are taken:

  1. Both the startOfConstruct and endOfConstruct Sg_File_Info objects are marked as shared via setShared().
  2. The new_file_id and the corresponding line numbers are appended to the fileIDsToUnparse and fileLineNumbersToUnparse lists of both the start and end construct Sg_File_Info objects.

Only statements originating from the file identified by new_file_id (based on the physical file ID stored in the Sg_File_Info) are processed. Statements from header files or other included files are skipped.

If subtreeRoot is not an SgStatement, the function prints an error message and calls ROSE_ABORT() to terminate execution.

Parameters
subtreeRootA pointer to the root node of the AST subtree to be processed. Must be a non-null pointer to an SgStatement or a subtype thereof.
new_file_idThe numeric file identifier to be registered in the Sg_File_Info objects of matching statement nodes. Must be a non-negative integer.
Precondition
subtreeRoot must not be NULL.
new_file_id must be greater than or equal to 0.
subtreeRoot must be an SgStatement or a subtype of SgStatement; otherwise the function will abort.
For each processed SgStatement, the sizes of fileIDsToUnparse and fileLineNumbersToUnparse in both the start and end Sg_File_Info objects must be equal before modification.
Postcondition
For all SgStatement nodes in the subtree whose startOfConstruct physical file ID equals new_file_id, both the start and end Sg_File_Info objects are marked as shared.
The new_file_id and corresponding line numbers have been appended to the fileIDsToUnparse and fileLineNumbersToUnparse lists of the affected Sg_File_Info objects.
The sizes of fileIDsToUnparse and fileLineNumbersToUnparse remain equal in all modified Sg_File_Info objects after modification.
Warning
If subtreeRoot is not an SgStatement, the function will print an error message to standard output and call ROSE_ABORT(), terminating the program.
This function only processes nodes of type SgStatement. Non-statement nodes encountered during traversal are silently ignored.
Calling this function with an incorrect new_file_id may cause incorrect unparsing behavior for shared AST nodes.
Note
This function was introduced to handle cases where AST nodes are shared across multiple translation units and the unparsing infrastructure needs to know which file IDs and line numbers are associated with each shared construct.
The traversal is performed in preorder using AstSimpleProcessing::traverse().
Statements located in header files or other files whose physical file ID does not match new_file_id are not modified.

◆ fixupSourcePositionFileSpecification()

void SageBuilder::fixupSourcePositionFileSpecification ( SgNode * subtreeRoot,
const std::string & newFileName )

Updates all Sg_File_Info source position file designations within an AST subtree to reference a new filename.

This function traverses an AST subtree rooted at subtreeRoot and replaces all file identifier references in associated Sg_File_Info objects with those corresponding to newFileName. It is intended to correct or reassign the filename designation recorded in source position information after AST construction or transformation operations that may have introduced nodes attributed to an incorrect or placeholder filename.

The function first determines the original file identifier (originalFileId) from the root node. If the root is an SgFile node, the filename of its start-of-construct Sg_File_Info is directly updated to newFileName, and the resulting new file identifier is retrieved from the global filename-to-ID map. If the root is an SgLocatedNode, the original file identifier is read from its start-of-construct, and the new file identifier is obtained by looking up newFileName in the same map. If the root is neither an SgFile nor an SgLocatedNode, the function reports an error and aborts.

An internal AST traversal class (derived from AstSimpleProcessing) is then instantiated and performs a preorder traversal of the subtree. During traversal, each visited node is handled as follows:

  • For SgLocatedNode instances whose physical file ID matches originalFileId, both the logical and physical file IDs of the start-of-construct and end-of-construct Sg_File_Info objects are updated to new_file_id. Nodes marked as shared are noted but still updated.
  • For SgInitializedName instances whose physical file ID matches originalFileId, both the logical and physical file IDs of the start-of-construct and end-of-construct Sg_File_Info objects are updated.
  • For SgSourceFile instances whose physical file ID matches originalFileId, the logical and physical file IDs of the start-of-construct Sg_File_Info are updated. Note that SgSourceFile does not have an end-of-construct.
  • For SgExpression instances whose operator position physical file ID matches originalFileId, both the logical and physical file IDs of the operator position Sg_File_Info are updated.

Conditional debug output is available via the define DEBUG_FIXUP, which is set to 0 by default and can be enabled at compile time for diagnostic purposes.

subtreeRootPointer to the root SgNode of the AST subtree to be updated. Must be non-null and must be either an SgFile or an SgLocatedNode (or a subtype thereof).
newFileNameThe new filename string to assign to all matching Sg_File_Info objects within the subtree. Must be a non-empty string.
Precondition
subtreeRoot must not be NULL.
newFileName must not be an empty string.
newFileName must already be registered in the global Sg_File_Info filename-to-ID map, or the root must be an SgFile so that registration can be triggered by setting the filename on its start-of-construct.
subtreeRoot must be either an SgFile or an SgLocatedNode; otherwise the function will abort with an error message.
The computed new_file_id must be a non-negative integer upon completion of the ID lookup.
Postcondition
All Sg_File_Info objects within the subtree whose physical file ID matched the original file ID of subtreeRoot will have both their logical and physical file IDs updated to the ID corresponding to newFileName.
The global Sg_File_Info filename-to-ID map will contain an entry for newFileName after this function completes (either pre-existing or created when setting the filename on an SgFile root node).
Warning
If subtreeRoot is neither an SgFile nor an SgLocatedNode, the function will print an error message to standard output and call ROSE_ABORT(), terminating the program.
Nodes whose Sg_File_Info is marked as shared (isShared() == true) are still updated. Callers should be aware that modifying shared Sg_File_Info objects may affect other parts of the AST that reference the same object.
This function uses a preorder AST traversal that visits all nodes in the subtree, including those in nested scopes. Ensure that subtreeRoot is the intended root to avoid unintended modification of file position information in unrelated subtrees.

The internal traversal uses AstSimpleProcessing with a preorder traversal strategy.
The define DEBUG_FIXUP (set to 0) can be changed to 1 at compile time to enable verbose diagnostic output tracing the traversal and file ID assignments.
SgSourceFile nodes do not have an end-of-construct Sg_File_Info; only the start-of-construct is updated for such nodes.

◆ getGlobalScopeFromScopeStack()

SgScopeStatement * SageBuilder::getGlobalScopeFromScopeStack ( )

Retrieves the global scope (SgGlobal) from the internal scope stack.

This function provides access to the global scope stored within the internal scope stack mechanism used by SageBuilder. The scope stack is maintained as an ordered list where the global scope (SgGlobal) is always expected to be the first (front) element, while the currently active scope resides at the back (end) of the list. This function inspects the front of the stack and returns it after verifying that it is indeed a valid SgGlobal node.

The function uses assertions to enforce correctness: it asserts that the scope stack is not empty before attempting to access its front element, and it further asserts that the retrieved scope is a non-null SgGlobal instance. If either assertion fails, the program will terminate with an error, which helps catch misuse or an inconsistent stack state early during development and testing.

Returns
A pointer to the SgScopeStatement representing the global scope (SgGlobal) found at the front of the internal scope stack.
Warning
This function will trigger an assertion failure and terminate the program if the scope stack is empty or if the front element of the stack is not a valid SgGlobal node. Callers must ensure the scope stack has been properly initialized and populated before invoking this function.
Precondition
The internal scope stack (ScopeStack) must be non-empty.
The front element of the scope stack must be a valid, non-null SgGlobal node.
Postcondition
The scope stack is left unmodified; no elements are added or removed.
The returned pointer refers to the SgGlobal node at the front of the scope stack.
Note
The global scope is conventionally placed at the front of the scope stack, while the most recently pushed (innermost) scope resides at the back. This ordering is an invariant of the SageBuilder scope stack mechanism and is relied upon by this function.

◆ getSourcePositionClassificationMode()

SourcePositionClassification SageBuilder::getSourcePositionClassificationMode ( )

Retrieves the current source position classification mode used by SageBuilder.

This function returns the current value of the global SourcePositionClassificationMode setting maintained within the SageBuilder namespace. The source position classification mode controls how source position information is assigned to newly constructed AST (Abstract Syntax Tree) nodes during code generation and transformation. Different classification modes may cause SageBuilder to attach transformation-generated positions, compiler-generated positions, or positions inherited from surrounding source context to newly built nodes.

This accessor is typically used to query the current mode before performing a series of AST construction operations, allowing callers to save and later restore the mode if a temporary change is needed.

Returns
The current SourcePositionClassification enumeration value representing the active source position classification mode in SageBuilder.
Precondition
The SageBuilder module must have been properly initialized prior to calling this function. The SourcePositionClassificationMode global variable must be in a valid, initialized state.
Postcondition
The internal SourcePositionClassificationMode state is not modified by this call.
Note
To change the current mode, use the corresponding setter function setSourcePositionClassificationMode(). Querying and restoring the mode around a block of AST construction calls is a common usage pattern when a temporary mode change is required.
Warning
Calling this function before SageBuilder has been initialized may return an undefined or default-constructed enumeration value. Ensure that SageBuilder initialization has occurred before relying on the returned value.

◆ getTargetFileType()

SgType * SageBuilder::getTargetFileType ( SgType * snippet_type,
SgScopeStatement * targetScope )

Resolves a snippet AST type to its corresponding type in the target AST scope.

This function takes a type originating from a snippet (code fragment) AST and attempts to find or reconstruct the equivalent type within the target AST, rooted at the given target scope. It handles named types (such as class types, typedef types, and enum types) by locating their associated declarations in the target AST, and also reconstructs compound or wrapped types such as pointer types, const-qualified modifier types, and typedef-wrapped types.

The implementation delegates the core named-type resolution to the support function getTargetFileTypeSupport, which performs the actual symbol lookup and type matching within the target scope hierarchy. After resolving the innermost base type, the function iterates over the list of internal (wrapping) types obtained via getInternalTypes() on the snippet type, and reconstructs each wrapper layer in reverse order. Supported wrapper layers include:

  • SgModifierType with a const qualifier, rebuilt using buildConstType.
  • SgTypedefType, resolved recursively via getTargetFileTypeSupport.
  • SgPointerType, rebuilt using buildPointerType.

If the resolved base type is NULL (for example, when the snippet type is a non-named type that is shared and does not require remapping), the function returns NULL without attempting to rebuild any wrapper layers.

The function contains dead code guarded by preprocessor conditionals (the else branch following the active if 1 block). This dead code includes explicit switch-case handling for V_SgClassType, V_SgTypedefType, V_SgEnumType, V_SgJavaParameterizedType, V_SgJavaQualifiedType, and V_SgJavaWildcardType variants, and is retained for historical reference but is not compiled.

Parameters
snippet_typeA pointer to the SgType node from the snippet AST that is to be mapped to the corresponding type in the target AST. Must not be NULL.
targetScopeA pointer to the SgScopeStatement representing the scope within the target AST in which the equivalent type should be located. Must not be NULL.
Returns
A pointer to the SgType in the target AST that corresponds to the input snippet type, including any reconstructed type wrappers (pointer, const modifier, typedef). Returns NULL if the snippet type is a non-named (shared) type that does not require remapping.
Warning
If a modifier type other than const is encountered during wrapper reconstruction, the function will print an error message and call ROSE_ABORT(). Similarly, any unrecognized type variant in the internal type list will trigger ROSE_ABORT().
The Java-specific type variants (SgJavaParameterizedType, SgJavaQualifiedType, SgJavaWildcardType) in the dead code branch are explicitly marked as untested and will call ROSE_ABORT() if reached.
Precondition
snippet_type must not be NULL.
targetScope must not be NULL.
The target AST must contain valid declarations and symbols for all named types referenced by snippet_type, so that symbol lookup within the target scope hierarchy can succeed.
Postcondition
If a non-NULL value is returned, it is a valid SgType pointer belonging to the target AST, with all type wrapper layers (pointer, const, typedef) reconstructed to match the structure of the original snippet type.
If NULL is returned, the snippet type is considered a shared non-named type that does not require remapping, and the caller should not attempt to reset it.
Note
This function was refactored (as of 3/17/2014) to delegate the core type resolution to getTargetFileTypeSupport, separating the unwrapping and rewrapping logic from the named-type lookup logic.
Non-named types (types not derived from SgNamedType) are considered shared across ASTs and are not remapped; in such cases the function returns NULL.
The internal type list is obtained by calling getInternalTypes() on the snippet type. When this list contains more than one element, the outermost wrapper layers are rebuilt in reverse order after the base type is resolved.

◆ getTargetFileTypeSupport()

SgType * SageBuilder::getTargetFileTypeSupport ( SgType * snippet_type,
SgScopeStatement * targetScope )

Resolves a snippet AST type to its corresponding type in the target AST.

This function serves as the inner implementation for getTargetFileType(). It examines a given type from a snippet AST and attempts to locate the equivalent type within the target AST, identified by the provided target scope. The function handles named types (SgNamedType) by inspecting the associated declaration and performing symbol lookups in the target scope's parent scopes. Non-named types are considered shared across ASTs and do not require remapping, so NULL is returned for those cases.

The function dispatches on the variant of the named type using a switch statement, handling the following cases:

  • V_SgClassType: Looks up the class symbol in the target scope's parent scopes using the class declaration name. If not found via a simple parent scope traversal (as may occur with name-qualified types in C++ or Java), it falls back to findAssociatedSymbolInTargetAST() to locate the matching symbol.
  • V_SgTypedefType: Looks up the typedef symbol in the target scope's parent scopes. If not found, falls back to findAssociatedSymbolInTargetAST().
  • V_SgEnumType: Looks up the enum symbol in the target scope's parent scopes. If not found, emits a diagnostic message and returns the original snippet type as a fallback, since the missing enum type represents a violation in the target AST rather than the snippet mechanism.
  • V_SgJavaParameterizedType: Looks up the underlying class symbol for the parameterized Java type. Falls back to findAssociatedSymbolInTargetAST() if not found via simple parent scope lookup.
  • V_SgJavaQualifiedType: Partially handled; returns the original qualified type with diagnostic output. The assertion for this case is currently commented out.
  • V_SgJavaWildcardType: Partially handled; returns the original wildcard type with diagnostic output. Triggers ROSE_ABORT() as this case is not yet fully tested.
  • default: Emits a diagnostic error message and triggers ROSE_ABORT().
Parameters
snippet_typeThe type from the snippet AST that needs to be resolved to an equivalent type in the target AST. Must not be NULL.
targetScopeThe scope statement in the target AST used as the starting point for symbol lookups. Must not be NULL.
Returns
A pointer to the corresponding SgType in the target AST if the input type is a named type and a match is found. Returns NULL if the input type is not a named type, indicating that no remapping is necessary.
Warning
For V_SgJavaWildcardType, the function calls ROSE_ABORT() because this case is not yet fully implemented or tested.
For V_SgJavaQualifiedType, the resolution is incomplete. The function returns the original type and emits a diagnostic message. The corresponding assertion has been commented out intentionally.
For V_SgEnumType, if the enum symbol cannot be found in the target AST, the function falls back to returning the original snippet type rather than asserting. This may indicate an inconsistency in the target AST.
If an unrecognized named type variant is encountered in the switch statement, the function emits a diagnostic error and calls ROSE_ABORT().
Precondition
snippet_type must not be NULL.
targetScope must not be NULL.
For V_SgClassType and V_SgTypedefType cases, the associated symbol must be locatable either through parent scope traversal or via findAssociatedSymbolInTargetAST(). If neither succeeds, an assertion failure will occur.
For V_SgEnumType, the enum declaration must have a non-null name (i.e., get_name().is_null() must return false).
Postcondition
If the input type is a named type and a matching symbol is found in the target AST, the returned SgType pointer refers to a type node owned by the target AST.
If the input type is not a named type, the return value is NULL and no modifications are made.
For all successfully resolved named type cases, the returned type is non-NULL and its associated declaration name matches the name of the original snippet declaration.
Note
This function is intended to be called only from getTargetFileType() and should not be used directly in general code.
Non-named types (e.g., primitive types, pointer types) are considered shared between the snippet and target ASTs and are not remapped by this function.
The function contains several disabled diagnostic ifdef blocks (using preprocessor value 0 guards) that can be re-enabled for debugging purposes during development.
Java-specific type variants (V_SgJavaParameterizedType, V_SgJavaQualifiedType, V_SgJavaWildcardType) have varying levels of completeness in their implementations.

◆ getTemplateArgumentList()

SgTemplateArgumentPtrList * SageBuilder::getTemplateArgumentList ( SgDeclarationStatement * decl)

Retrieves the template argument list from a given declaration statement node.

This function examines the variant type of the provided declaration statement and returns a pointer to the appropriate template argument list, depending on whether the declaration represents a template instantiation or a template declaration (including specializations).

For template instantiation nodes (such as SgTemplateInstantiationDecl, SgTemplateInstantiationFunctionDecl, SgTemplateInstantiationMemberFunctionDecl, and SgTemplateInstantiationTypedefDeclaration), the function returns a pointer to the templateArguments field. For template declaration nodes (such as SgTemplateClassDeclaration, SgTemplateFunctionDeclaration, SgTemplateMemberFunctionDeclaration, SgTemplateVariableDeclaration, SgTemplateTypedefDeclaration, and SgNonrealDecl), the function returns a pointer to the templateSpecializationArguments field (or the equivalent tpl_args field for SgNonrealDecl).

For declaration types that do not participate in template mechanisms, such as SgNamespaceDeclarationStatement, SgNamespaceAliasDeclarationStatement, SgEnumDeclaration, SgVariableDeclaration, SgTypedefDeclaration, SgFunctionDeclaration, SgMemberFunctionDeclaration, SgClassDeclaration, SgProcedureHeaderStatement, SgJovialTableStatement, SgJavaPackageDeclaration, and SgTemplateDeclaration, the function returns NULL.

This function is designed to be called in a general context, particularly as part of name qualification support, where many different types of declarations may be encountered. If an unrecognized declaration variant is encountered, the function prints a diagnostic message and aborts execution.

Parameters
declA pointer to the SgDeclarationStatement node from which the template argument list is to be retrieved. Must not be NULL.
Returns
A pointer to the SgTemplateArgumentPtrList associated with the given declaration, or NULL if the declaration type does not carry a template argument list.
Warning
If an unrecognized declaration variant is passed, this function will print a diagnostic message to standard output and call ROSE_ABORT(), terminating the program. Ensure that only supported declaration types are passed to this function.
Precondition
decl must not be NULL.
decl must be a valid SgDeclarationStatement node with a recognized variant type as handled by the internal switch statement.
Postcondition
The returned pointer, if non-NULL, refers to the internal template argument list of the given declaration node and remains valid as long as the declaration node itself is valid.
Note
This function is intended for use within the ROSE compiler infrastructure and relies on ROSE AST node types and their associated accessor methods. It handles both template declarations and template instantiations uniformly, making it suitable for contexts where the exact declaration kind may not be known in advance.

◆ getTemplateParameterList()

SgTemplateParameterPtrList * SageBuilder::getTemplateParameterList ( SgDeclarationStatement * decl)

Retrieves the template parameter list associated with a given declaration statement node.

This function inspects the variant type of the provided declaration statement and returns a pointer to the corresponding SgTemplateParameterPtrList if the declaration is a template declaration. For non-template declarations such as namespace declarations, enum declarations, variable declarations, typedef declarations, function declarations, class declarations, member function declarations, and their template instantiation counterparts, the function returns NULL. This behavior is intentional, as the function is called in a general context as part of name qualification support, and must gracefully handle many types of declarations without treating non-template cases as errors.

The function uses a switch statement on the variant tag of the declaration node to dispatch to the appropriate handling logic. The following declaration types return a valid pointer to the template parameter list:

  • SgTemplateClassDeclaration
  • SgTemplateFunctionDeclaration
  • SgTemplateMemberFunctionDeclaration
  • SgTemplateVariableDeclaration
  • SgTemplateTypedefDeclaration
  • SgNonrealDecl (via get_tpl_params())
  • SgTemplateDeclaration

The following declaration types return NULL without error:

  • SgNamespaceAliasDeclarationStatement
  • SgNamespaceDeclarationStatement
  • SgEnumDeclaration
  • SgVariableDeclaration
  • SgTypedefDeclaration
  • SgProcedureHeaderStatement
  • SgJovialTableStatement
  • SgJavaPackageDeclaration
  • SgFunctionDeclaration
  • SgMemberFunctionDeclaration
  • SgClassDeclaration
  • SgTemplateInstantiationTypedefDeclaration
  • SgTemplateInstantiationDecl
  • SgTemplateInstantiationFunctionDecl
  • SgTemplateInstantiationMemberFunctionDecl

If an unrecognized declaration variant is encountered, the function prints a diagnostic message and calls ROSE_ABORT() to terminate execution.

Parameters
declA pointer to the SgDeclarationStatement node whose template parameter list is to be retrieved. Must not be NULL.
Returns
A pointer to the SgTemplateParameterPtrList associated with the declaration if it is a recognized template declaration type, or NULL if the declaration is a non-template or template instantiation declaration type that does not carry a template parameter list.
Warning
If the declaration variant is not handled by any of the known cases in the switch statement, the function will print an error message to standard output and call ROSE_ABORT(), terminating the program. Callers must ensure that only supported declaration types are passed to this function.
Precondition
decl must not be NULL. An assertion (ROSE_ASSERT) is enforced at the start of the function to guarantee this.
decl must point to a valid SgDeclarationStatement node within a well-formed ROSE AST.
Postcondition
The returned pointer, if non-NULL, refers to the internal template parameter list of the given declaration node. The caller must not delete or otherwise invalidate this pointer, as it points directly into the AST node's data.
If the declaration is a non-template or template instantiation type, the returned value is NULL and the AST is left unmodified.
Note
This function is intended for use as part of name qualification support in the ROSE framework and is designed to be called in a general context on many types of declarations. It does not modify the AST in any way.
For SgNonrealDecl nodes, the template parameters are accessed via get_tpl_params() rather than get_templateParameters(), which is used for all other template declaration types.

◆ initDiagnostics()

void SageBuilder::initDiagnostics ( )

Initializes the diagnostic logging facility for the SageBuilder module.

This function sets up the diagnostic message stream used by the Rose::SageBuilder namespace. It registers the module-level logging object mlog with the Rose diagnostics infrastructure under the name "Rose::SageBuilder" and attaches a human-readable comment describing its purpose as "building abstract syntax trees".

The function uses a local static boolean flag to ensure that initialization is performed only once, regardless of how many times the function is called. This pattern is a common guard against redundant re-initialization in library startup routines. On the first invocation, the flag is set to true and the registration proceeds; on all subsequent calls, the function returns immediately without performing any work.

This function is typically called during the startup phase of any tool or library component that relies on the SageBuilder subsystem, ensuring that diagnostic messages can be properly routed and filtered through the Rose diagnostics framework.

Precondition
The Rose diagnostics infrastructure must be available and properly configured before this function is called, as it invokes Rose::Diagnostics::initAndRegister internally.
Postcondition
The mlog diagnostic stream for the Rose::SageBuilder module is registered and ready for use. Subsequent calls to this function have no effect.
Note
This function is safe to call multiple times. The internal static flag ensures that the actual initialization logic executes exactly once per program lifetime.
Warning
This function is not thread-safe if called concurrently from multiple threads before initialization has completed. In multi-threaded contexts, external synchronization should be applied around the first call to this function.

◆ inSwitchScope()

bool SageBuilder::inSwitchScope ( )

Determines whether any scope in the current scope stack is a switch statement.

This function iterates over the global ScopeStack maintained by the SageBuilder infrastructure to check whether any currently active scope corresponds to an SgSwitchStatement node. It is primarily used to detect when code is being built inside a switch statement context, which is relevant for suppressing or adjusting certain pragma processing behaviors that are known to be problematic within switch statement scopes.

The function performs a linear scan of the ScopeStack from beginning to end, testing each scope entry using isSgSwitchStatement(). If any entry matches, the function returns true. If no switch statement scope is found after exhausting the entire stack, the function returns false.

Returns
true if at least one scope in the current ScopeStack is an SgSwitchStatement; false otherwise.
Precondition
The ScopeStack must be properly initialized and maintained by the SageBuilder infrastructure prior to calling this function.
Postcondition
The ScopeStack is not modified by this function; it remains in the same state as before the call.
Note
This function was introduced to address issues with pragma processing inside switch statements. Pragma handling may behave incorrectly in switch scopes, and this function provides a way to detect that situation so that callers can take appropriate action.
Warning
This function depends on the global ScopeStack being consistent and up to date. If scopes have been pushed or popped incorrectly, the result may not accurately reflect the actual nesting context.

◆ popScopeStack()

void SageBuilder::popScopeStack ( )

Removes the top scope from the scope stack maintained by SageBuilder.

This function pops the most recently pushed scope off the internal scope stack used by the SageBuilder module. The scope stack is a global data structure that tracks the current nesting of scopes during AST construction. When building an AST programmatically, scopes are pushed onto the stack as they are entered and must be popped when construction of that scope's contents is complete.

Internally, the function asserts that the scope stack is not empty before attempting to remove the top element. This is enforced via a runtime assertion using ASSERT_require. If the stack is empty at the time of the call, the assertion will fail and the program will abort with a diagnostic message.

This function is typically called in conjunction with pushScopeStack() to maintain a balanced scope nesting during AST construction.

Warning
Calling this function when the scope stack is empty will trigger a failed assertion and cause program termination. Always ensure that a corresponding pushScopeStack() call has been made before calling this function.
Precondition
The scope stack must contain at least one scope entry (i.e., it must not be empty).
Postcondition
The top element of the scope stack is removed, and the scope stack contains one fewer entry than before the call.
Note
This function operates on a module-level (global) scope stack within SageBuilder. It is not thread-safe if multiple threads are concurrently modifying the scope stack. Callers are responsible for ensuring proper synchronization in multi-threaded contexts.

◆ pushScopeStack()

void SageBuilder::pushScopeStack ( SgScopeStatement * stmt)

Pushes a scope statement onto the scope stack maintained by SageBuilder.

This function appends the given SgScopeStatement pointer to the end of the internal ScopeStack, which is a global stack used by the SageBuilder interface to track the current active scope during AST construction. The scope stack provides context for builder functions that need to know the enclosing scope when creating new AST nodes. Scopes pushed onto the stack should be popped in the reverse order of their insertion using the corresponding pop function to maintain correct nesting semantics.

The function performs a null-pointer assertion on the provided statement before pushing it, ensuring that only valid, non-null scope statements are added to the stack. If the assertion fails, the program will terminate with an error.

Parameters
stmtA pointer to the SgScopeStatement to be pushed onto the scope stack. Must not be null.
Precondition
stmt must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgScopeStatement node that has already been properly allocated and initialized.
Postcondition
The provided SgScopeStatement pointer is appended to the end of ScopeStack, increasing the stack size by one. The newly pushed scope becomes the current active scope for subsequent SageBuilder operations.
Warning
Passing a null pointer for stmt will trigger an assertion failure and terminate the program. Callers must ensure the pointer is valid before invoking this function.
Scopes pushed onto the stack must be popped in the correct order. Failing to balance push and pop calls may result in incorrect scope resolution during AST construction and lead to malformed ASTs.
Note
This function operates on a global scope stack (ScopeStack) shared across the SageBuilder interface. Care should be taken in multi-threaded or complex construction scenarios to ensure the stack remains in a consistent state.
This function is typically used in conjunction with popScopeStack() to bracket the construction of AST subtrees that belong to a particular scope.

Defines the binary operator node ReplicationOp for use in the ROSE AST.

This macro-generated function constructs a binary operator expression node representing the replication operator, which is a Jovial-specific binary operation. The BUILD_BINARY_DEF macro expands to provide the full definition of the builder function for the ReplicationOp AST node, following the conventions established for binary expression construction within the ROSE compiler infrastructure.

The replication operator is specific to the Jovial programming language and was introduced as part of Jovial language support added around July 2018. The macro BUILD_BINARY_DEF handles the boilerplate of creating the corresponding SgExpression subclass node, linking the left-hand side and right-hand side operands, and assigning the result type.

A new binary operator AST node of type ReplicationOp is created and returned with lhs and rhs set as its operands and t as its type.

This function is generated by the BUILD_BINARY_DEF macro. Direct modification of this function should be done through the macro definition rather than any expanded form.

Warning

This function (or constructor) is generated via the BUILD_BINARY_DEF macro, which expands to provide a standardized binary operator definition for use within the ROSE compiler infrastructure. ReplicationOp represents the Jovial replication operator, which is used in the Jovial programming language to replicate or repeat a value or structure a specified number of times. The macro BUILD_BINARY_DEF automates the boilerplate required to integrate this operator into the abstract syntax tree (AST) node hierarchy, ensuring consistent construction and representation of binary expression nodes.

The Jovial language support was added as part of ongoing frontend extensions to ROSE. This particular operator was introduced to handle Jovial-specific syntax that does not have a direct counterpart in C or C++, requiring a dedicated AST node type.

Parameters

rhsPointer to the right-hand side expression operand of the replication operation.

Precondition
lhs must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgExpression node.
rhs must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgExpression node.
t must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgType node.
Postcondition
A new SgReplicationOp node is created and inserted into the AST with lhs and rhs as its child operands and t as its associated type.
Note
This definition is generated by the BUILD_BINARY_DEF macro. Any changes to the general structure of binary operator construction should be made in that macro rather than in this specific instantiation.
This operator is specific to the Jovial language frontend and may not be applicable or meaningful in the context of other supported languages such as C, C++, or Fortran.
Warning

◆ setSourcePositionClassificationMode()

void SageBuilder::setSourcePositionClassificationMode ( SourcePositionClassification X)

◆ setTemplateArgumentParents()

void SageBuilder::setTemplateArgumentParents ( SgDeclarationStatement * decl)

Sets the parent pointers of template arguments belonging to a declaration to the declaration's first non-defining declaration.

This function iterates over the list of template arguments associated with the given declaration statement and ensures that each template argument's parent pointer is correctly assigned to the first non-defining declaration of the provided declaration node.

The function handles three cases when examining the current parent of each template argument:

  1. If the parent is NULL, the template argument's parent is set to the first non-defining declaration.
  2. If the parent is a scope statement (SgScopeStatement), it means the template argument had its parent set to a scope when it was originally built. In this case, the parent is refined and updated to the first non-defining declaration now that the enclosing declaration has been constructed.
  3. If the parent is already a declaration statement (SgDeclarationStatement), no change is made. A diagnostic message may be printed under the ROSE_DEBUG_NEW_EDG_ROSE_CONNECTION define guard to indicate this condition.
  4. If the parent is none of the above types, a diagnostic error message may be printed under the ROSE_DEBUG_NEW_EDG_ROSE_CONNECTION define guard to flag an unexpected parent type.

After processing all template arguments, the function calls testTemplateArgumentParents() to validate that all parent pointers have been set correctly.

If the declaration has no associated template argument list (i.e., the list pointer is NULL), the function performs no iteration but still invokes testTemplateArgumentParents() for validation.

Parameters
declPointer to the SgDeclarationStatement whose template argument parent pointers are to be set. Must not be NULL.
Precondition
decl must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid SgDeclarationStatement node.
decl->get_firstNondefiningDeclaration() must return a non-NULL pointer when a template argument list is present.
Postcondition
All template arguments in the declaration's template argument list that had a NULL parent or a scope statement as their parent will have their parent pointer set to the first non-defining declaration of decl.
testTemplateArgumentParents() has been called on decl to verify the integrity of the parent assignments.
Warning
Passing a NULL pointer for decl will trigger an assertion failure.
If a template argument's parent is set to an unexpected node type (neither NULL, a scope statement, nor a declaration statement), this may indicate a structural inconsistency in the AST. A diagnostic message is printed only when compiled with the ROSE_DEBUG_NEW_EDG_ROSE_CONNECTION define enabled.
Note
This function is intended for internal use during AST construction to ensure proper parent-child relationships for template argument nodes.
The diagnostic printf statements within this function are conditionally compiled under the ROSE_DEBUG_NEW_EDG_ROSE_CONNECTION preprocessor guard and are not active in standard builds.

Sets the template arguments for a template instantiation declaration node.

This function assigns a provided list of template arguments to a given template instantiation declaration node in the ROSE AST. It is designed to handle any supported type of template instantiation declaration, including class template instantiations, function template instantiations, member function template instantiations, and typedef template instantiations.

The function first retrieves the existing template argument list associated with the declaration using an internal helper. If a valid list is found, it overwrites the existing template arguments with the contents of the provided input list. After updating the arguments, it sets the parent pointers for all template argument nodes to ensure the AST remains consistent. Finally, it verifies the correctness of the parent pointers by calling a validation routine.

Parameters
declA pointer to the declaration statement whose template arguments are to be set. Must be a non-null pointer to one of the supported template instantiation declaration types: SgTemplateInstantiationDecl, SgTemplateInstantiationFunctionDecl, SgTemplateInstantiationMemberFunctionDecl, or SgTemplateInstantiationTypedefDeclaration.
templateArgumentsList_inputA pointer to the list of template arguments to assign to the declaration. Must not be null.
Precondition
decl must not be null.
templateArgumentsList_input must not be null.
decl must be of one of the following variant types: V_SgTemplateInstantiationDecl, V_SgTemplateInstantiationFunctionDecl, V_SgTemplateInstantiationMemberFunctionDecl, or V_SgTemplateInstantiationTypedefDeclaration.
Postcondition
The template argument list of decl is updated to match the contents of templateArgumentsList_input, if the declaration's internal template argument list is non-null.
All template argument nodes within decl have their parent pointers correctly set.

Warning
This function uses ROSE_ASSERT to enforce preconditions. Passing a null pointer for either argument, or a declaration of an unsupported type, will trigger an assertion failure and abort execution.
Note
If the internal template argument list retrieved from the declaration is null, the assignment step is skipped, but parent pointer validation is still performed.
This function is intended for internal use within the SageBuilder interface when constructing or modifying template instantiation nodes in the ROSE AST.

◆ setTemplateNameInTemplateInstantiations()

void SageBuilder::setTemplateNameInTemplateInstantiations ( SgFunctionDeclaration * func,
const SgName & name )

Sets the template name on a function declaration node if it represents a template instantiation.

When constructing or modifying the ROSE AST, function declarations that are template instantiations carry two distinct name-related pieces of information: the full function name (which may include template arguments) and a separate template name (which does not include template arguments). This function checks whether the given SgFunctionDeclaration node is either a SgTemplateInstantiationFunctionDecl or a SgTemplateInstantiationMemberFunctionDecl, and if so, assigns the provided name as the template name on that node, provided the template name has not already been set.

The design assumes that the input name is already stripped of template arguments. Rather than attempting to parse and remove template argument syntax from a fully qualified name (which is error-prone for complex cases such as "X<Y<Z>> operator X&()" or "X<Y<Z>> operator>()"), the caller is expected to supply the bare template name directly. Template arguments are then appended separately by other parts of the infrastructure.

For member function template instantiations, the template name is set via set_templateName on the SgTemplateInstantiationMemberFunctionDecl node. For non-member function template instantiations, the template name is set via set_templateName on the SgTemplateInstantiationFunctionDecl node, and an assertion verifies that the supplied name does not already contain template syntax.

If the given function declaration is not a template instantiation of either kind, this function performs no operation.

Parameters
funcA pointer to the SgFunctionDeclaration node to be examined and potentially updated. Must not be NULL. The node may be either a regular function declaration (in which case this function is a no-op) or a template instantiation function or member function declaration.
nameThe template name to assign, provided without template arguments. This value is used directly as the template name on the instantiation node. For non-member function instantiations, the name must not contain template syntax (i.e., angle-bracket argument lists).
Precondition
func must not be NULL.
name should not contain template argument syntax (angle-bracket lists) when the target node is a non-member function template instantiation, as enforced internally by an assertion on hasTemplateSyntax.
If func is a template instantiation node, its template name should either be unset (null) or already correctly assigned; this function only sets the name when it is currently null.
Postcondition
If func is a SgTemplateInstantiationMemberFunctionDecl and its template name was null, the template name is now set to the provided name.
If func is a SgTemplateInstantiationFunctionDecl and its template name was null, the template name is now set to the provided name.
In both template instantiation cases, the template name on the node is guaranteed to be non-null upon return.
Warning
Passing a name that contains template argument syntax for a non-member function template instantiation will trigger an internal assertion failure, as the function enforces that template syntax is absent from the stored template name.
Note
This function is intended for internal use during AST construction and transformation within the SageBuilder interface. It addresses a specific requirement that template instantiation nodes maintain a clean template name separate from the full instantiated function name.
The distinction between member and non-member template instantiation handling is enforced by mutually exclusive assertions: exactly one of the two instantiation pointer types will be non-NULL when the node is identified as a template instantiation.

◆ setTemplateParameterParents()

void SageBuilder::setTemplateParameterParents ( SgDeclarationStatement * decl)

Sets the parent pointers of template parameters belonging to a declaration to the declaration's first non-defining declaration node.

This function iterates over the template parameter list associated with the given declaration statement and ensures that each template parameter's parent pointer is correctly assigned to the first non-defining declaration of the provided declaration.

For each template parameter in the list, the function checks whether the parent pointer is NULL or currently set to an SgScopeStatement. In either case, the parent is updated to point to the first non-defining declaration. This refinement is necessary because template parameters may have had their parent pointers initially set to a scope when they were first constructed, and this function corrects that assignment once the enclosing declaration has been fully built.

After updating parent pointers, the function calls testTemplateParameterParents() to validate the correctness of the resulting parent assignments.

Parameters
declA pointer to the SgDeclarationStatement whose template parameter parent pointers are to be set. Must not be NULL. The declaration must have a valid first non-defining declaration accessible via get_firstNondefiningDeclaration().
Precondition
decl must not be NULL.
decl->get_firstNondefiningDeclaration() must return a non-NULL pointer.
Postcondition
All template parameters in the template parameter list of decl that had a NULL parent or a parent of type SgScopeStatement will have their parent pointer set to the first non-defining declaration of decl.
testTemplateParameterParents(decl) is called to verify the integrity of the parent assignments.
Warning
If decl is NULL, the function will trigger an assertion failure.
If decl->get_firstNondefiningDeclaration() returns NULL, the function will trigger an assertion failure.
Note
If the declaration has no template parameter list (i.e., getTemplateParameterList() returns NULL), the function performs no modifications and proceeds directly to the validation step via testTemplateParameterParents().
Template parameters whose parents are already set to a non-scope, non-NULL node other than an SgScopeStatement are left unchanged.

void SageBuilder::setTemplateParametersInDeclaration ( SgDeclarationStatement * decl,
