Sets the template parameters for a template declaration node in the AST.

This function assigns a list of template parameters to a given template declaration statement within the ROSE abstract syntax tree (AST). It supports the following types of template declarations: SgTemplateClassDeclaration, SgTemplateFunctionDeclaration, SgTemplateMemberFunctionDeclaration, and SgTemplateVariableDeclaration.

The function first retrieves the existing template parameter list from the declaration node. If a template parameter list is already present, it is overwritten with the contents of the provided input list via a deep copy assignment. After updating the list, the parent pointers of all template parameters are updated by calling setTemplateParameterParents to ensure the AST remains consistent. Finally, testTemplateParameterParents is called to verify the correctness of the parent pointer assignments.

Parameters
declA pointer to the SgDeclarationStatement node representing a template declaration. Must be one of the supported template declaration variant types: SgTemplateClassDeclaration, SgTemplateFunctionDeclaration, SgTemplateMemberFunctionDeclaration, or SgTemplateVariableDeclaration.
templateParameterList_inputA pointer to the SgTemplateParameterPtrList containing the template parameters to be assigned to the declaration. Must not be NULL.
Precondition
decl must point to a valid SgDeclarationStatement of one of the supported template declaration variant types (V_SgTemplateClassDeclaration, V_SgTemplateFunctionDeclaration, V_SgTemplateMemberFunctionDeclaration, or V_SgTemplateVariableDeclaration).
templateParameterList_input must not be NULL.
Postcondition
If the declaration node already contains a template parameter list, it is replaced with the contents of templateParameterList_input.
The parent pointers of all template parameters in the declaration are set correctly to point to the declaration node.
The integrity of template parameter parent pointers is verified via testTemplateParameterParents.
Warning
This function will trigger an assertion failure (via ROSE_ASSERT) if templateParameterList_input is NULL or if decl is not one of the supported template declaration variant types.
Note
If the declaration node does not yet have an associated template parameter list (i.e., getTemplateParameterList returns NULL), the function will skip the assignment step but will still call testTemplateParameterParents for validation.

void SageBuilder::setTemplateSpecializationArgumentsInDeclaration ( SgDeclarationStatement * decl,

Sets the template specialization arguments on a supported template declaration node.

This function assigns a list of template specialization arguments to a given template declaration node in the ROSE IR (Intermediate Representation). It retrieves the existing template argument list associated with the declaration and overwrites it with the contents of the provided input list. After updating the argument list, it sets the parent pointers for all template arguments to ensure the AST remains consistent. A final validation step is performed to confirm that all template argument parent pointers are correctly established.

The function supports the following declaration types:

  • SgTemplateClassDeclaration
  • SgTemplateFunctionDeclaration
  • SgTemplateMemberFunctionDeclaration
  • SgTemplateVariableDeclaration

If the declaration's internal template argument list pointer is non-null, the assignment is performed by dereferencing and copying the input list. Parent pointer fixup is then applied via a call to setTemplateArgumentParents(), and correctness is verified via testTemplateArgumentParents().

Parameters
declA pointer to the SgDeclarationStatement representing a template declaration whose specialization arguments are to be set. Must be one of the four supported template declaration variant types.
templateSpecializationArgumentsList_inputA pointer to the SgTemplateArgumentPtrList containing the template specialization arguments to be assigned to the declaration. Must not be NULL.
Warning
This function will trigger an assertion failure if templateSpecializationArgumentsList_input is NULL.
This function will trigger an assertion failure if decl is not one of the four supported template declaration variant types (SgTemplateClassDeclaration, SgTemplateFunctionDeclaration, SgTemplateMemberFunctionDeclaration, or SgTemplateVariableDeclaration).
Precondition
decl must be a non-null pointer to a valid SgDeclarationStatement of one of the four supported template declaration variant types.
templateSpecializationArgumentsList_input must be a non-null pointer to a valid SgTemplateArgumentPtrList.
Postcondition
If the declaration's internal template argument list is non-null, it will contain a copy of the elements from templateSpecializationArgumentsList_input.
All template argument nodes associated with the declaration will have their parent pointers correctly set.
The template argument parent pointers will have been validated by testTemplateArgumentParents().
Note
If the declaration's internal template argument list pointer is NULL, no assignment is performed, though parent pointer validation is still executed.
This function is intended for use during AST construction or transformation when template specialization information must be explicitly attached to a template declaration node.

◆ testTemplateArgumentParents()

void SageBuilder::testTemplateArgumentParents ( SgDeclarationStatement * decl)

Validates that all template arguments associated with a declaration have non-null parent pointers.

This function inspects the template argument list of a given declaration statement and verifies that every template argument in that list has a valid (non-null) parent node set in the AST. If any template argument is found to have a null parent, an error message is printed to standard output and an assertion failure is triggered. This function is intended as a diagnostic and correctness-checking utility during AST construction or transformation, particularly in contexts where template declarations are being processed.

Internally, the function retrieves the template argument list via a helper function getTemplateArgumentList. If the list is non-null, it iterates over each SgTemplateArgument pointer in the list and checks the result of get_parent(). It also asserts that the first non-defining declaration of the given declaration is non-null, as part of additional consistency checking introduced for template argument parent validation.

Note that a previously enforced constraint requiring a strict one-to-one mapping between EDG template argument pointers and SgTemplateArgument nodes was relaxed (commented out) to allow reuse of SgTemplateArgument objects while maintaining the mapping from EDG internal representations.

Parameters
declA pointer to the SgDeclarationStatement whose template arguments are to be validated. Must not be null.
Precondition
decl must be a non-null pointer to a valid SgDeclarationStatement node.
If decl has a non-null template argument list, each SgTemplateArgument in that list must have a non-null parent pointer set in the AST; violation results in an assertion failure.
decl->get_firstNondefiningDeclaration() must return a non-null pointer for any declaration that has a non-empty template argument list.
Postcondition
All template arguments in the declaration's template argument list have been confirmed to have non-null parent pointers, or an assertion failure has been raised.
Warning
This function uses ROSE_ASSERT to enforce correctness conditions. If any template argument has a null parent, the program will terminate with an assertion failure after printing a diagnostic error message.
Note
This function is primarily a debugging and validation utility and is not intended for use in production code paths where performance is critical.
The constraint that SgTemplateArgument objects must have parents set to the first non-defining declaration was previously enforced but has since been relaxed to allow reuse of SgTemplateArgument instances across multiple declarations.

◆ testTemplateParameterParents()

void SageBuilder::testTemplateParameterParents ( SgDeclarationStatement * decl)

Validates that all template parameters of a declaration node have non-null parent pointers set correctly.

This function iterates over the template parameter list associated with the given declaration statement and checks that each template parameter has a valid (non-null) parent node assigned. If any template parameter is found with a null parent, an error message is printed to standard output and an assertion failure is triggered.

Additionally, the function checks whether each template parameter's parent matches the first non-defining declaration of the given declaration node. A mismatch is noted internally but is not treated as a fatal error, since template parameters may be shared (cached) across multiple declarations. This caching mechanism was introduced to support pointer equality tests for template parameters in symbol table handling, analogous to the approach previously used for template arguments.

If the declaration has no associated template parameter list (i.e., getTemplateParameterList() returns NULL), the function exits without performing any checks.

Parameters
declPointer to the declaration statement whose template parameter parents are to be validated. Must not be NULL.
Precondition
decl must be a non-null pointer to a valid SgDeclarationStatement node.
Each template parameter in the declaration's template parameter list must have a non-null parent pointer; violation causes an assertion failure.
The first non-defining declaration of decl must be non-null if a template parameter list is present.
Postcondition
All template parameters in the list have been verified to have non-null parent pointers.
Warning
If a template parameter is found with a null parent pointer, the function prints a diagnostic message and triggers an assertion failure via ROSE_ASSERT, which may abort the program.
Note
Template parameters may be shared (cached) across multiple declarations as of a specific ROSE commit. As a result, the parent of a template parameter is not guaranteed to be the first non-defining declaration of the given decl, and such mismatches are tolerated without error.
The diagnostic message for parent mismatches is conditionally compiled out via a if 0 / endif preprocessor guard and will not appear in normal builds. It was suppressed because it generated excessive output for certain C++11 test cases.

◆ topScopeStack()

SgScopeStatement * SageBuilder::topScopeStack ( )

Returns the top-most scope statement from the current scope stack.

This function retrieves the scope statement at the top of the internal scope stack (ScopeStack) maintained by the SageBuilder infrastructure. The scope stack is used during AST construction to track the currently active enclosing scopes, allowing builder functions to associate newly created nodes with the correct containing scope.

If the scope stack is empty, the function returns a null pointer rather than attempting to access an undefined back element, which would result in undefined behavior. When the stack is non-empty, the function retrieves the topmost SgScopeStatement pointer via ScopeStack.back(). As a diagnostic step, if the retrieved scope pointer is non-null, class_name() is called on it to verify the object is well-formed and accessible; this is primarily a compatibility check introduced for certain versions of the GNU 4.0.x compiler toolchain where other versions of g++ behave correctly without it.

Returns
A pointer to the SgScopeStatement at the top of the scope stack, or nullptr if the scope stack is empty.
Precondition
The ScopeStack global or module-level container must be properly initialized before this function is called.
Postcondition
The scope stack is not modified; this function is a read-only query of the current top element.
Warning
Callers must check the returned pointer for null before dereferencing it, as an empty scope stack will cause this function to return nullptr.
Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder scope management utilities. The internal call to class_name() on the retrieved scope is a defensive compatibility measure and does not affect the returned value or the state of the scope stack.

◆ unparseTemplateArgumentToString()

SgName SageBuilder::unparseTemplateArgumentToString ( SgTemplateArgument * templateArgument)

Converts a template argument node into its string representation.

This function produces a human-readable string form of a given SgTemplateArgument AST node by invoking the node's own unparseToString() method with a specially configured SgUnparse_Info context. The unparsing context is set to target C++ language output and is configured to suppress the emission of class and enumeration definitions, ensuring that only the template argument expression or type name is rendered rather than any associated definitions. Additionally, the context is configured to use generated names for nested template arguments, which helps produce stable, canonical string representations suitable for debugging and diagnostic purposes.

Internally, an SgUnparse_Info object is heap-allocated, configured, and then deleted after the unparsing operation completes. This function is noted as being functionally redundant with SgTemplateArgument::unparseToStringSupport(), but is retained as a convenience wrapper within the SageBuilder interface.

Parameters
templateArgumentA pointer to the SgTemplateArgument node to be converted to a string. Must not be NULL.
Returns
An SgName object containing the string representation of the given template argument.
Warning
This function asserts that templateArgument is not NULL. Passing a NULL pointer will trigger a failed assertion and terminate the program.
Precondition
templateArgument must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an SgTemplateArgument node that is part of a well-formed AST.
Postcondition
The returned SgName contains the unparsed string form of the template argument as it would appear in C++ source code, with class and enum definitions suppressed and generated names used for nested template arguments.
Note
This function allocates and immediately frees an SgUnparse_Info object internally. The caller is not responsible for any memory management related to this object. The function is primarily intended for debugging and diagnostic use.
